short_description: Computes the Thorin measure whose positivity is equivalent to the Riemann Hypothesis, from Pólya's integral for Xi in certified ball arithmetic, and proves that finite positivity tests on the heat trace cannot decide it; with hitting times, friable approximants, the reciprocal zeta function and Lee Yang theory.
description:
The Riemann Hypothesis can be restated as the positivity of a measure, the Thorin measure of a ratio of values of Riemann's Xi function. This book computes that measure from Pólya's integral for Xi, without primes or a list of zeros, in certified ball arithmetic, and asks what such computations can and cannot teach about the zeros.

A certified zero off the critical line would refute the hypothesis, but no finite computation can prove it. From the zeros verified up to height 3 × 10^12 the book certifies that the derivatives of the heat trace have the predicted signs up to order 1.16 × 10^25, and proves that such finite positivity tests cannot settle it: a perturbation of Xi with the same zeros below a large height, and zeros off the line above it, passes them. No proof of the hypothesis is claimed.

New results: the reciprocal Xi function at x to the power p is hyperbolically completely monotone exactly when the absolute value of p is at most one minus twice the largest zero angle over pi; at the basepoint one the Thorin density is certified smallest at the origin, so the shifted clock is a stable variable plus a generalized gamma convolution; between the basepoints one half and one the shifted clocks are almost generalized gamma convolutions, unconditionally; the clock of Pólya's Bessel function is the hitting time of an explicit diffusion; adjacent real zeros of a polynomial cannot meet under the backward heat flow before an explicit time; and the Pólya law lies within 2 × 10^-6 in total variation of the ferromagnetic laws of Lee and Yang, a distance that is zero exactly under the hypothesis.

Later chapters read the programme through Pólya's papers on the zeros of entire functions (the Pólya Schur form of the hypothesis, Turán inequalities, a certificate that the two sided reciprocal Xi density is log concave and lies within 1.6 × 10^-10 of a Pólya frequency function of every order), Yoshida's Hermitian form of Weil's explicit formula and Zhu's compact windows (a damped Weil criterion, least eigenvalues and an uncertainty barrier), Dedekind zeta functions and the Linnik constant, friable approximants of Xi after Miyatake (truncations of Riemann's theta series to integers built from the first few primes, which agree with Xi to an exponentially small amount and yet leave the real line) with the cosh ladder, the zeros of entire functions in the work of Haseo Ki read through the Thorin programme, and hitting times of the reciprocal Xi law (Kent's formula, Jensen and extreme value hitting times, a universal three halves stable limit for prime side hitting times, and what the reciprocal Xi function proves). The October 2026 claims of a zero free half plane Re s > 7/8 for all L functions, and the later preprints that lower the constant slightly, are not refereed: the book states only conditional consequences (a principal signal for zeta, the sliver and Mertens estimate, the Thorin property at every basepoint above 7/8), credited to their authors.

The scripts and data files behind the tables and figures are in the book's repository https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh, listed in code/README.md.

chapters.title: Introduction and foundations
chapters.summary:
This chapter states the Riemann Hypothesis (RH) as a positivity condition. For the completed zeta function $\xi$, put $G(u)=\xi(\frac12+\sqrt{u})/\xi(\frac12)$; the reciprocal $1/G$ is the clock. RH holds exactly when the clock is the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution (GGC), whose Thorin measure is then the sum of unit atoms at the squared ordinates of the zeros. This is the Thorin condition. Its equivalent forms are sign conditions: $G'/G$ is a Stieltjes transform, the heat trace of the zeros is completely monotone, the Thorin density $\rho_\varepsilon(\theta)=\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(\frac12+\varepsilon+i\theta)$ is nonnegative at every resolution $\varepsilon>0$ (Lagarias's criterion), Weil's explicit formula functional is positive, and the clock is hyperbolically completely monotone (HCM). The chapter introduces the Hadamard product, the Pólya kernel and density, van Dantzig pairs, the Poisson smoothing of the zeros (the Cauchy flow) and the sine squared lemma, which gives the Thorin density from the primes. It treats GGCs for computation: the Bondesson hierarchy, diagnostics of the Thorin condition and the sinh clock benchmark. It explains why computation can measure but not prove the Thorin condition.

#### From the literature

The Thorin representation of generalized gamma convolutions (Thorin 1977; Bondesson 1992); extended GGCs (Thorin 1978); the HCM characterization of GGC Laplace transforms (Bondesson 1992); Lagarias's criterion (Lagarias 1999); Weil's explicit formula (Weil 1952); Pólya's integral for $\xi$ (Pólya 1926); van Dantzig pairs (Lukacs 1968) and their link with RH (Konstantopoulos, Patie and Sarkar 2024); the Bessel hitting time form of $\xi$ (Biane, Pitman and Yor 2001, after Williams 1990); the verification of RH to height $3\times10^{12}$ (Platt and Trudgian 2021).

#### New results

The chapter restates the rigidity and shifted clock theorems of Polson (2026), proves the sine squared lemma of Polson (2017) again, and adds one open question on positivity on a single line.

- [Rigidity of the clock, a GGC if and only if RH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#rigidity_clock_ggc_iff_rh) (Proposition 1.2.1, page 10; proved): The clock, the reciprocal of the normalised completed zeta function in the variable $u=s^2$, is the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution exactly when the Riemann Hypothesis holds, and then its Thorin measure is the sum of unit atoms at the squared ordinates of the zeros. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Shifted clock is a GGC to the right of every zero](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#shifted_clock_ggc_right_of_every_zero) (Theorem 1.2.2, page 14; proved): To the right of every zero of the completed zeta function, in particular at every basepoint $\alpha\ge 1$, the shifted clock is the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution with an explicit positive Thorin density, and it is one exactly when $\alpha$ is at least the supremum of the real parts of the zeros. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Positivity of the Thorin density on one line, open question](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#one_line_positivity_exclusion_open) (Remark 1.2.4, page 15; open): It is not known, without assuming the Riemann Hypothesis, whether nonnegativity of the real part of the logarithmic derivative of the completed zeta function on a single vertical line excludes zeros to the right of that line. New in this book.
- [The variable Z sqrt(2T) of the van Dantzig pair is self decomposable with no hypothesis, with an explicit canonical function](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#self_decomposability_of_z_sqrt_2t_and_its_canonical_function_for_the_clock) (Result 1.3.2, page 18; proved): With no hypothesis, $Z\sqrt{2T}$ (standard normal $Z$ independent of the clock $T$) is self decomposable, with canonical function $k(r)=\sum_je^{-r\sqrt{a_j}}$ obtained by subordinating the Lévy measure of $T$ to the heat kernel; it is an extended generalised gamma convolution exactly when RH holds. New in this book.

#### Key terms

Riemann Hypothesis, RH, Riemann xi function, completed zeta function, Thorin condition, Thorin measure, generalized gamma convolution, generalised gamma convolution, GGC, clock, rigidity theorem, Pólya kernel, Polya kernel, heat trace, van Dantzig pair, Cauchy flow, sine squared lemma, Bondesson class, HCM, Lagarias criterion, sinh clock

chapters.title: Evaluating the Xi function
chapters.summary:
This chapter asks how to evaluate the Riemann xi function $\xi$ and its derivative at complex arguments, the raw material for computing the Thorin density at every resolution. The Pólya route applies the trapezoid rule to Pólya's integral $\Xi(\theta)=\int\Phi(u)\cos(\theta u)\,du$. It needs neither primes nor zeros and is spectrally accurate because the Pólya kernel $\Phi$ is analytic in the strip $|\operatorname{Im}u|<\pi/4$. The evaluator is two fixed polynomials in Arb ball arithmetic; below height 200 it gives about 60 correct digits and recovers the 79 zeros, with the count read from the argument principle. Cancellation costs about $0.341\,\theta$ digits at height $\theta$; tilting the contour into the strip reduces the loss to about $\delta\theta/\log 10$ digits and gives 25 digits of the Thorin density at height 5000. The chapter compares the route with the Riemann Siegel formula, the Odlyzko Schönhage algorithm and Turing's method, resolves the Lehmer pair near height 7005, reads the count $N(1000)=649$ from the Thorin mass, and ends with a worked computation from the theta series to the first zero. Ball radii certify rounding only, so the results are computed, not certified.

#### From the literature

Pólya's integral for $\xi$ (Pólya 1926); the exponentially convergent trapezoid rule (Trefethen and Weideman 2014); Arb ball arithmetic (Johansson 2017); the Riemann Siegel formula (Siegel 1932; Gabcke 1979); Gram points and Gram's law (Gram 1903), Rosser's rule (Rosser, Yohe and Schoenfeld 1969) and their failures (Brent 1979; Trudgian 2011); Backlund's count (Backlund 1918; Hutchinson 1925); Turing's method (Turing 1953; Lehman 1970; Trudgian 2011); the Odlyzko Schönhage algorithm (Odlyzko and Schönhage 1988); the Lehmer pair (Lehmer 1956); the verification of RH to height $3\times10^{12}$ (Platt and Trudgian 2021).

#### New results

The tilted Pólya representation is new in the book. Digit counts, timings and zero counts are computed, with ball arithmetic certifying rounding only.

- [Tilted Pólya representation of xi and its derivative](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#tilted_polya_representation_of_xi) (Proposition 2.1.1, page 29; proved): Moving the line of integration of Pólya's integral into the strip of analyticity of the Pólya kernel gives exact integral formulas for $\xi$ and $\xi'$ on a line at distance $\delta$ from the edge of the strip, with kernel bounds of order $\delta^{-5/2}$. New in this book.

#### Key terms

Riemann xi function, Pólya route, Polya route, Pólya kernel, trapezoid rule, spectral accuracy, tilted contour, ball arithmetic, Arb, Riemann Siegel formula, Odlyzko Schönhage algorithm, Gram points, Rosser's rule, Turing's method, Backlund's method, argument principle, zero counting, Lehmer pair, Thorin density, Thorin mass

chapters.title: The Thorin measure at finite resolution
chapters.summary:
This chapter asks what finite computations of the Thorin density $\rho_\varepsilon$, the Poisson smoothing of the zeros of $\xi$, can establish about the Riemann Hypothesis. On the window below height 200, where the 79 zeros are known, it measures the distance from the computed Thorin measure to the discrete measure demanded by RH. Raw total variation is maximal, matched total variation sits at a numerical floor of about $3.7\times10^{-9}\varepsilon$, and cell distance, mass defect and heat trace error vanish linearly in the resolution $\varepsilon$. The chapter proves the first order mass defect, closed form signatures of an off line zero, a Littlewood identity, and a zero density identity that counts the zeros to the right of any line from the cumulative Thorin mass (at $\varepsilon=\frac12$, Backlund's count with the vertical side on $\operatorname{Re}s=1$). It shows that the sine squared lemma and Selberg's smoothed explicit formula give the Thorin density from the primes only at a cost exponential in $1/\varepsilon$, and explains why a finite computation can refute RH by certifying a zero off the line but cannot measure a distance to RH.

#### From the literature

Lagarias's criterion (Lagarias 1999); the argument principle count, the Riemann von Mangoldt formula and Littlewood's lemma (see Titchmarsh 1986); Backlund's method (Backlund 1918) and Turing's method (Turing 1953; Lehman 1970; Trudgian 2011); Selberg's smoothed explicit formula (Selberg 1946); Weil's positivity criterion (Weil 1952); zero density estimates (Ingham 1940); the verification of RH to height $3\times10^{12}$ (Platt and Trudgian 2021). The sine squared lemma is an earlier result of Polson (2017); the canonical measure of $\log\xi$ that the sine squared decomposition uses and the square root law for a displaced zero are earlier results of Polson (2026).

#### New results

The propositions below are new in the book. The tables of distances, masses and counts at height 200 are computed, not certified.

- [Mass defect of the Thorin measure on a window](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#thorin_mass_first_order_defect) (Proposition 3.2.2, page 48; proved): When every zero up to height $\Theta$ lies on the critical line, the Thorin mass of the window $(0,\Theta^2]$ equals the zero count $N(\Theta)$ minus $(\varepsilon/\pi)\,\Xi'(\Theta)/\Xi(\Theta)$ up to a remainder of order $\varepsilon^2$. New in this book.
- [Signatures of an off line zero in the Thorin density](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#off_line_zero_signatures) (Proposition 3.3.1, page 50; proved): The effect of an off line pair of zeros on the Thorin density is computed in closed form: a displacement that keeps the count has total variation $\frac{3\sqrt{3}}{4\pi}(\delta/\varepsilon)^2$ per displaced zero to leading order for $\delta<\varepsilon$, an omitted pair has total variation $\frac4\pi\arcsin(\varepsilon/\delta)$, and a displaced zero has negative mass $\frac1\pi\arcsin(\varepsilon/\delta)$, the last two for $\delta>\varepsilon$; the quadratic growth of the first is the square root law of Polson (2026). New in this book.
- [Littlewood identity for the cumulative Thorin mass](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#littlewood_identity_thorin_mass) (Proposition 3.4.1, page 54; proved): The cumulative Thorin mass at resolution $\varepsilon$ is $\pi^{-1}$ times the derivative in $\varepsilon$ of the integral of $\log|\xi|$ along the line $\operatorname{Re}s=\frac12+\varepsilon$, which links the mass to the integral of $\log|\xi|$ on the critical line. New in this book.
- [Zero density identity from the Thorin mass](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#zero_density_identity_thorin_mass) (Proposition 3.4.2, page 54; proved): The cumulative Thorin mass at resolution $\varepsilon$ plus a short horizontal correction equals the zero count $N(T)$ minus twice the number of zeros to the right of the line $\operatorname{Re}s=\frac12+\varepsilon$, and at $\varepsilon=\frac12$ it is Backlund's unconditional count of $N(T)$. New in this book.

#### Key terms

Thorin density, Thorin mass, resolution, Poisson smoothing, Cauchy kernel, total variation, matched total variation, cell distance, mass defect, Richardson extrapolation, off line zero, square root law, Littlewood identity, zero density, argument principle, Backlund count, Turing's method, Selberg explicit formula, sine squared lemma, variogram, Weil criterion

chapters.title: Weak limits, hyperbolic complete monotonicity and a Bosch type theorem
chapters.summary:
Can closure of generalized gamma convolutions (GGC) under weak limits, or Bondesson's characterization of GGC Laplace transforms as hyperbolically completely monotone (HCM) functions, settle the Riemann Hypothesis (RH) without locating zeros? For the reciprocal Xi function (the clock) the chapter recalls (Polson 2017) that the Cauchy flow of Thorin measures converges vaguely to the measure of the zeros on the critical line whether or not RH holds, so weak closure cannot reach RH, and shows that HCM of the clock is RH in other forms (Stieltjes and Pick function conditions, HCM of the de Bruijn Newman deformation at every positive time). An elasticity criterion for HCM functions transfers Bosch's method for powers of the half Cauchy law: the clock composed with x^p is HCM exactly when |p| is at most one minus twice the largest zero angle over pi, with RH the extreme case, and unconditionally for |p| within about 10^-13 of one, by the verification of RH to height 3 times 10^12. Further results: the Thorin density of this family, a natural boundary argument with the Dedekind eta function, a first gap condition for the Mellin variable W (under RH and further hypotheses), and open questions.

#### From the literature

Closure of generalized gamma convolutions under convergence in law (Thorin 1977; Bondesson 1992); Bondesson's theorem that a Laplace transform is a GGC transform if and only if it is HCM (Bondesson 1992; James, Roynette and Yor 2008); Bondesson's representation of HCM functions (Bondesson 1992); Bosch's theorem on powers of the half Cauchy law (Bosch 2015); the proof of Bondesson's conjecture on stable densities (Bosch and Simon 2016); Lagarias's criterion for RH (Lagarias 1999); the de Bruijn Newman constant (de Bruijn 1950; Newman 1976), nonnegative (Rodgers and Tao 2020), at most 0.22 (Polymath 2019) and at most 0.2 (Platt and Trudgian 2021); Lamperti's stable ratio density (Lamperti 1958); the Mellin representation of xi (Biane, Pitman and Yor 2001); Pólya's gap theorem (Pólya 1923, 1929).

#### New results

- [RH as a weak limit criterion for generalized gamma convolutions](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#rh_iff_clock_is_weak_limit_of_ggc_transforms) (Corollary 4.1.2, page 63; proved): The Riemann Hypothesis holds if and only if the reciprocal Xi function is the pointwise limit of Laplace transforms of generalized gamma convolutions on a set of points with an accumulation point in the positive half line. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [The reciprocal Xi function is HCM if and only if RH holds](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#reciprocal_xi_hcm_iff_rh) (Corollary 4.1.3, page 64; proved): The reciprocal Xi function with basepoint alpha at least one is hyperbolically completely monotone (HCM) unconditionally, and with basepoint one half (the clock) it is HCM if and only if the Riemann Hypothesis holds; the equivalence for the clock is noted in versions 21 and 23 of Polson's arXiv paper 1708.02653, and both parts follow from Polson (2026) by Bondesson's theorem. New in this book.
- [Deformed reciprocal Xi function is HCM exactly for t at least Lambda](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#deformed_reciprocal_xi_hcm_iff_time_at_least_lambda) (Corollary 4.2.5, page 71; proved): The reciprocal Xi function deformed by the de Bruijn Newman heat flow to time t is HCM exactly when t is at least the de Bruijn Newman constant, so RH is equivalent to HCM for every positive t. New in this book.
- [Question: for which beta is the density of W^beta HCM](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#question_hcm_powers_of_mellin_variable_w) (Question 4.2.7, page 72; open): The book asks for which powers beta the density of W to the power beta is HCM, where W is the positive variable with Mellin transform Xi(0)/Xi(z). New in this book.
- [Question: does HCM of W^beta for a single beta imply RH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#question_single_power_hcm_implies_rh) (Question 4.2.8, page 72; open): The book asks whether HCM of the density of W to the power beta for one single beta already implies the Riemann Hypothesis. New in this book.
- [Elasticity criterion for HCM functions (Bondesson's representation restated as a Pick condition)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#elasticity_criterion_for_hcm_functions) (Theorem 4.3.2, page 73; proved): A positive function on the half line is HCM exactly when it extends to a zero free analytic function off the negative axis whose elasticity is a Pick function; this restates Bondesson's representation of HCM functions, with a direct proof of sufficiency. New in this book.
- [Bosch type theorem for the reciprocal Xi function](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#reciprocal_xi_power_hcm_threshold) (Theorem 4.3.5, page 75; proved): The reciprocal Xi function composed with the power x to the p is HCM exactly when the absolute value of p is at most one minus twice the largest zero angle over pi, so RH is the extreme case p equal to one. New in this book.
- [Equivalent forms of RH: HCM of all powers, Pick elasticity](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#rh_iff_hcm_of_all_powers_below_one_and_pick_elasticity) (Corollary 4.3.6, page 76; proved): The Riemann Hypothesis is equivalent to HCM of the reciprocal Xi function composed with x to the p for every p of absolute value below one, to the elasticity of the reciprocal Xi function being a Pick function, and to an angular sign condition on xi prime over xi. New in this book.
- [Unconditional HCM range for the reciprocal Xi function composed with a power](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#reciprocal_xi_power_hcm_unconditional_range) (Corollary 4.3.7, page 76; proved): From the verification of RH to height 3 times 10^12, the reciprocal Xi function composed with x to the p is HCM for all p of absolute value at most one minus 1/(3 pi times 10^12), which exceeds one minus 1.1 times 10^-13. New in this book.
- [Stieltjes sign of minus the logarithmic derivative of the clock outside a thin parabolic region](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#stieltjes_sign_of_clock_outside_parabolic_region) (Theorem 4.3.9, page 77; proved): From the verification of RH to height 3 times 10^12, minus the logarithmic derivative of the reciprocal Xi function has the sign of a Stieltjes function at every point of the upper half plane outside an explicit thin parabolic region. - [Question: HCM exponent of the deformed reciprocal Xi function for negative time](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#question_hcm_exponent_deficit_negative_heat_time) (Question 4.3.11, page 79; open): The book asks how fast one minus the HCM exponent of the deformed reciprocal Xi function tends to zero as the heat time rises to zero from below, assuming RH. - [Refined first gap conjecture for sums of Laplace variables](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#question_first_gap_conjecture_refined) (Question 4.3.29, page 90; open): The book asks whether, for e to the power of a sum of independent Laplace variables over frequencies lambda_n, the HCM threshold of the powers is exactly the first gap lambda_2 minus lambda_1 when the first gap is the largest or the characteristic function decays faster than any exponential. New in this book.

chapters.title: The heat trace, the arithmetic and the limits of finite information
chapters.summary:
How much of the Thorin condition on the reciprocal Xi function (RH) follows from sign conditions on the heat trace W(t), the sum of exp(-a_j t) over the zeros of the Riemann xi function, and what can finite information not decide? Using only the verification of RH to a finite height (Platt and Trudgian 2021) and Weil's explicit formula for the primes, the chapter proves that W is positive and decreasing (Polson 2026), so the clock is infinitely divisible and self decomposable; sketches the proof (Polson 2017) that the derivatives of W alternate in sign up to order 10^17; and proves, by a window theorem, that they do so up to order 1.16 times 10^25 (positivity of the Williamson measures) and that W is completely monotone on (0, 1.29]. Positive semidefinite Hankel matrices of the derivatives at one time are equivalent to RH, the numbers of negative eigenvalues of Hankel matrices of Stieltjes moments tend to the number of quadruples of zeros off the critical line, and RH is equivalent to nonnegativity of a Gaussian smoothing of the zeros. A perturbation of xi with four off line zeros passes finite heat trace tests, and a certified zero of a Mellin transform of the Pólya density closes the Bernstein Pick route. The chapter also defines the Thorin functional from the primes and compares zero spacings with GUE statistics.

#### From the literature

Weil's explicit formula (Weil 1952); self decomposability of laws with a nonincreasing W(t) in the Lévy density W(t)/t (Sato 1999) and unimodality (Yamazato 1978); Mase's theorem on indecomposable factors (Mase 1975) and Linnik's class I_0 (Linnik 1964); Williamson's theorem on k monotone functions (Williamson 1956); Hermite's count of nonreal roots by Hankel forms (Hermite 1856), with Grommer (1914), Chebotarev (1928) and Baricz and Štampach (2018); Hutchinson's early verification of zeros (Hutchinson 1925); the explicit Riemann von Mangoldt formula (Hasanalizade, Shen and Wong 2022); solutions of the van Dantzig problem (Konstantopoulos, Patie and Sarkar 2024); pair correlation (Montgomery 1973) and spacings (Odlyzko 1987); zero density estimates (Ingham 1940; Guth and Maynard 2026).

#### New results

- [Complete asymptotic expansion of the heat trace W(t) at t = 0 with the coefficients d_n and b_k, and the logarithmic divergence of the clock](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#small_time_expansion_of_heat_trace_w_at_the_origin_with_euler_number_coefficients) (Result 5.1.1, page 94; proved): With no hypothesis, $W(t)$ has the asymptotic expansion $\frac{\log(1/t)-\gamma_E-4\log2-2\log\pi}{8\sqrt{\pi t}}+\sum d_nt^n+\sum b_kt^{k-1/2}$ as $t\downarrow0$, with $d_0=\frac78$; the two term case is in Polson 2017, and the integral of $W(t)/t$ from $\tau$ diverges so the clock has infinitely many jumps. New in this book.
- [The clock is infinitely divisible and self decomposable, unconditionally](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#clock_infinitely_divisible_and_self_decomposable) (Theorem 5.1.1, page 95; proved): Using only the verification of RH below height 1000, the heat trace is positive and decreasing, so the clock is the Laplace transform of an infinitely divisible, self decomposable law with Lévy density W(t)/t, with the numerical inequalities of the proof certified in ball arithmetic. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Truncation error of the residues of the reciprocal clock when the product over zeros is cut after K factors](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#truncation_error_of_residues_of_reciprocal_xi_product_over_first_zeros) (Proposition 5.1.2, page 97; proved): For simple zeros, the residue of the truncated product at the pole $-a_k$ differs from the true residue by the factor $\prod_{j>K}(1-a_k/a_j)$, which under RH is close to one exactly for $\gamma_k\le(\gamma_K/\log\gamma_K)^{1/2}$ and not beyond. New in this book.
- [Hankel positivity of the heat trace at one time is equivalent to RH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#hankel_positivity_at_one_time_iff_rh) (Theorem 5.1.3, page 98; proved): At any single time t, positive semidefiniteness of the two Hankel matrices of derivatives of the heat trace, equivalently of Weil's quadratic form on the span of r^m exp(-r^2 t/2), is equivalent to RH. First stated in Polson (2017, version 24 of 2026), On Hilbert's 8th problem, arXiv:1708.02653.
- [RH is equivalent to boundedness of the heat trace of the zeros on a vertical line](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#rh_equivalent_to_boundedness_of_heat_trace_on_vertical_line) (Theorem 5.1.4, page 98; proved): The Riemann Hypothesis holds if and only if the heat trace $v\mapsto W(\sigma+iv)$ of the zeros is bounded on the real line, for one, equivalently every, $\sigma>0$. New in this book.
- [Positive definite Hankel blocks of the heat trace up to size 3 x 10^7](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#heat_trace_hankel_blocks_positive_definite_to_size_3e7) (Theorem 5.1.5, page 100; proved): If every zero of xi below height 20000 N (1 + log N)^(1/2) lies on the critical line, the leading N by N Hankel blocks of the derivatives of the heat trace are positive definite at every time, and the verification of RH to height 3 times 10^12 gives this unconditionally for every N up to 3 times 10^7. First stated in Polson (2017, version 24 of 2026), On Hilbert's 8th problem, arXiv:1708.02653.
- [Derivative signs of the heat trace up to order 10^17](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#heat_trace_derivative_signs_to_order_1e17) (Theorem 5.1.6, page 100; proved): Using only the verification of RH below height 10^12, the derivatives of the heat trace alternate in sign, (-1)^k W^(k)(t) > 0, for every t > 0 and every order k up to 10^17. First stated in Polson (2017, version 24 of 2026), On Hilbert's 8th problem, arXiv:1708.02653.
- [Hankel matrices of Stieltjes moments count the zeros off the critical line (eigenvalue form of the Grommer and Chebotarev criterion)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#hankel_inertia_counts_zeros_off_critical_line) (Theorem 5.1.7, page 102; proved): In an eigenvalue form of the classical determinant criterion of Grommer (1914) and Chebotarev (1928), the numbers of negative eigenvalues of the Hankel matrices of the Stieltjes moments of the heat trace are nondecreasing in the matrix size and tend to the number of distinct zeros of xi to the right of the critical line in the upper half plane, so RH holds if and only if they are all zero. New in this book.
- [Heat trace completely monotone on (0, 1.29]; every order up to t = 0.019](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#heat_trace_completely_monotone_near_origin) (Theorem 5.1.9, page 105; proved): Every derivative of the heat trace of order at least one alternates in sign for t up to 0.019 using no information on the zeros, and with the verification of RH below height 10^12 the heat trace is completely monotone on (0, 1.29], with the numerical inequalities of the proof certified in ball arithmetic. New in this book.
- [Heat trace derivative along a ray is the Gaussian smoothing of the zeros](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#heat_trace_derivative_along_ray_is_gaussian_smoothing_of_zeros) (Proposition 5.1.10, page 109; proved): For u at least 2 and k equal to u^2 t, not necessarily an integer, the k th derivative of the heat trace (defined by its sum over the zeros), divided by an explicit factor, equals the Gaussian smoothing of the zeros at resolution 1/(2 sqrt t) up to an explicit relative error on each zero within u/2 of u and an explicit remainder, with no hypothesis on the zeros. New in this book.
- [RH is equivalent to nonnegativity of the Gaussian smoothing of the zeros](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#rh_iff_gaussian_smoothing_of_zeros_nonnegative) (Proposition 5.1.11, page 110; proved): The Riemann Hypothesis holds if and only if the Gaussian smoothing of the zeros of xi, a sum of Gaussian bumps in complexified ordinates, is nonnegative for every real centre and every resolution. New in this book.
- [There is no Gaussian smoothing criterion for RH on a line with real part alpha above one half](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#no_gaussian_criterion_on_vertical_line_alpha_above_one_half_under_rh) (Proposition 5.1.12, page 110; conditional on The Riemann Hypothesis: every nontrivial zero of the Riemann zeta function has real part $\frac12$): Under RH the Gaussian smoothing of the zeros shifted to the line $\operatorname{Re}s=\alpha$ with $\frac12<\alpha<1$ takes negative values for some $u$ and $t$, so positivity of the Gaussian smoothing cannot be a criterion for RH on that line. New in this book.
- [Derivative signs of the heat trace up to order 1.16 x 10^25](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#heat_trace_derivative_signs_to_order_1e25) (Theorem 5.1.13, page 112; proved): From the verification of RH to height 3 times 10^12, every derivative of the heat trace alternates in sign, equivalently the Williamson measures are positive, up to order 1.16 times 10^25, with the numerical inequalities of the proof certified in ball arithmetic. New in this book.
- [Compound Poisson defect of the off line zeros: the clock plus an independent compound Poisson variable is a GGC](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#heat_trace_compound_poisson_defect_of_off_line_zeros) (Theorem 5.1.14, page 113; proved): Unconditionally, the heat trace of the zeros of xi is the Laplace transform of a Thorin measure minus an explicit nonnegative remainder carried by the off line zeros, so the clock plus an independent compound Poisson variable of rate below $10^{-12}$ (a bound certified in ball arithmetic from the verification of RH to height $3\times10^{12}$ and an explicit zero counting bound) is a generalized gamma convolution, and the remainder vanishes exactly when RH holds, that is, when the heat trace is completely monotone. New in this book.
- [Heat trace of the zeros of xi is completely monotone on (0, 1.70] and has the right sign at every order up to 1.52e25 (certified)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#heat_trace_completely_monotone_up_to_time_1_70_and_order_1_52e25_certified) (Theorem 5.1.16, page 115; proved): Unconditionally, the heat trace of the zeros of xi is completely monotone on $(0,1.70]$ and its derivatives have the alternating signs for all times $t>0$ and every order up to $1.70(H-23)^2>1.52\times10^{25}$ with $H=3\times10^{12}$, proved with a ball arithmetic computation (certified) of the numerical inequalities for the orders above $1.16\times10^{25}$. New in this book.
- [Four off line zeros that pass the finite heat trace tests](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#off_line_perturbation_passing_finite_heat_trace_tests) (Theorem 5.2.1, page 117; proved): Moving a close pair of zeros of xi on the critical line to four zeros at distance one quarter off the line gives an even entire function whose heat trace still passes the finite tests (infinite divisibility, self decomposability, log convexity, and at large heights positive Hankel blocks and derivative signs up to order 10^17). First stated in Polson (2017, version 24 of 2026), On Hilbert's 8th problem, arXiv:1708.02653.
- [A pair of zeros off the line at the height of a line zero: its contribution to the density at resolution epsilon is positive exactly when epsilon is below d over sqrt 3 or above d](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#pair_of_zeros_off_the_line_at_the_ordinate_of_a_line_zero_is_positive_for_resolution_below_d_over_sqrt_3_or_above_d) (Proposition 5.2.2, page 121; proved): The zeros $\frac12$ and $\frac12\pm d$ at one ordinate contribute to $\pi\rho_\varepsilon$ a rational function that is positive at every $\theta$ if and only if $\varepsilon<d/\sqrt3$ or $\varepsilon>d$; so when every off line zero shares its ordinate with a line zero and the distances have a positive infimum $d_0$, the density is positive on every line with $0<\varepsilon<d_0/\sqrt3$ although zeros lie to the right of it. New in this book.
- [Certified zero of a Mellin transform closes the Bernstein Pick route to RH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#bernstein_pick_route_closed_by_certified_zero) (Theorem 5.2.3, page 123; proved): A certified simple zero of the meromorphically continued Mellin transform M of the Pólya density near -8.494 + 2.938i gives the canonical interpolant of the moment ratios a nonreal pole, so no Bernstein interpolant is a complete Bernstein function and the Bernstein Pick route to RH is closed. First stated in Polson (2017, version 24 of 2026), On Hilbert's 8th problem, arXiv:1708.02653.
- [Local model for the first failing derivative order of the heat trace near an off line quadruple](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#first_failing_derivative_order_local_model_off_line_quadruple) (Proposition 5.2.4, page 123; proved): To leading order, if two consecutive zeros of xi on the line are replaced by an off line quadruple at distance $\delta$ from the line and height $g$, with $\Delta$ the larger gap to the nearest line zeros and $\delta\ll\Delta\ll g$, the first derivative order at which a sign fails, for the heat trace restricted to the quadruple and its two neighbouring zeros on the line, is $k^*=\omega^*g^2/(2\delta\Delta)$, about $\frac\pi4g^2/(\delta\Delta)$, at a time depending on $\delta$ and $\Delta$ only; the comparison of this time with the seven certified failure times of the book's table, within 0.20 to 2.76 per cent, is a computation. New in this book.

#### Key terms

Riemann Hypothesis, RH, heat trace, Thorin measure, Thorin condition, reciprocal Xi function, clock, infinitely divisible, self decomposable, completely monotone, Williamson measure, k monotone, Hankel matrix, Stieltjes moments, Weil explicit formula, Gaussian smoothing of the zeros, van Dantzig pair, Pólya density, verification of RH, Bernstein Pick route, spacing of zeros, GUE, cell distance

chapters.title: The reciprocal zeta function
chapters.summary:
This chapter asks whether the zeros, the primes and the gamma factor of the Riemann zeta function assemble into a Thorin measure, that is, whether the reciprocal zeta function, in the clock variable, is a generalized gamma convolution (GGC) or at least infinitely divisible. From the Dirichlet series and Euler product it computes Thorin type measures of an Euler factor and, under the Riemann Hypothesis (RH), of the normalised reciprocal zeta function, the signed measure $dM$ with $M-1$ the argument function $S(\sqrt t)$, and from the Weierstrass product that of the gamma factor. The Lai and Vere-Jones identity gives the Vere-Jones representation by hyperbolic secants and sawtooth measures, and an explicit canonical function (heat trace) that yields a criterion for RH. The sine squared lemma and the Meixner law show that the reciprocal gamma factor is a GGC after a stable tilt, and the floor of the reciprocal Xi function, whose infinite divisibility follows from Polson (2026), is a GGC exactly when RH holds.

#### From the literature

- the Thorin representation of generalized gamma convolutions (Thorin 1977; Bondesson 1992)
- the hyperbolic secant law as a Brownian exit time and a GGC, and its gamma powers $C_t$ with Laplace transform $(\cosh\sqrt{2\lambda})^{-t}$ (Biane, Pitman and Yor 2001)
- the Meixner hypergeometric law and the completeness problem for dilates of the hyperbolic secant (Lai and Vere-Jones 1979)
- the Riemann von Mangoldt formula (see Titchmarsh 1986) and the explicit formula (Weil 1952), in its heat trace form (Polson 2026)
- the local Riemann Hypothesis for Mellin transforms of even Hermite functions (Bump, Choi, Kurlberg and Vaaler 2000), rederived here with no priority claimed, and Meixner Pollaczek expansions of $\Xi$ (Kuznetsov 2008; Romik 2021)
- Williamson's theorem on $n$ monotone functions (Williamson 1956)
- the verification of RH to height $3\times10^{12}$ (Platt and Trudgian 2021) and a bound for the zero count (Hasanalizade, Shen and Wong 2022)
- infinite divisibility and self decomposability of the reciprocal Xi function (Polson 2026)

#### New results

The results below first appeared in Part IX of Polson (2026), five of them corrected or sharpened here; the two sine squared lemmas are from Polson (2017).

- [Thorin type density of an Euler factor](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#euler_factor_thorin_type_density) (Proposition 6.1.2, page 138; proved): The Euler factor $1-qe^{-\lambda\sqrt s}$ is zero free on the cut plane and has an explicit Thorin type density, a cosine series of both signs. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Lai and Vere-Jones identity (the exponential as a Möbius sum of hyperbolic secants)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#lai_vere_jones_identity) (Proposition 6.1.3, page 139; proved): The exponential $e^{-x}$ equals a Möbius weighted sum of the dilates $\operatorname{sech}(mx)$ of the hyperbolic secant, which expands the Dirichlet series of the reciprocal zeta function in hyperbolic secants; the book names it after Lai and Vere-Jones, who posed the completeness of these dilates as an open problem. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Vere-Jones representation of the reciprocal zeta function by hyperbolic secants](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#vere_jones_representation_reciprocal_zeta) (Theorem 6.1.5, page 139; proved): Where the Dirichlet series converges absolutely, $1/\zeta(\frac12+\sqrt s)$ equals $1$ plus an explicit Möbius weighted series of hyperbolic secants $\operatorname{sech}(\sqrt s\log N)$, each the Laplace transform of a Brownian exit time and a GGC with atomic Thorin measure. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Logarithmic twin of the Lai and Vere-Jones identity (the exponential as a sum of logarithms with Dirichlet eta weights)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#exponential_as_eta_weighted_sum_of_log_blocks) (Proposition 6.1.6, page 140; proved): The exponential $e^{-x}$ equals $\sum_{m\ge1}d_m\log(1+e^{-mx})$ with weights $d_m$ bounded by $1$ whose Dirichlet series is $1/\eta(1+v)$ for Dirichlet's eta function $\eta$, the logarithmic twin of the Lai and Vere-Jones identity. Corrects a statement of Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Sawtooth Thorin measure of a Vere-Jones block](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#sawtooth_thorin_measure_of_vere_jones_block) (Lemma 6.1.7, page 140; proved): The function $2/(1+e^{-\lambda\sqrt s})$ has the signed Thorin type measure formed by unit atoms at the squares of the odd multiples of $\pi/\lambda$ minus the density $\lambda/(4\pi\sqrt t)$, a sawtooth measure. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Vere-Jones representation of log zeta by sawtooth blocks](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#vere_jones_representation_log_zeta) (Theorem 6.1.8, page 141; proved): Where the Dirichlet series converges absolutely, $\log\zeta(\frac12+\sqrt s)$ is an explicit absolutely convergent series of the blocks $\log(1+N^{-\sqrt s})$ with weights from Dirichlet's eta function, and its derivative is a sum of Stieltjes transforms with poles on sawtooth lattices. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Thorin type measure of the normalised reciprocal zeta function under RH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#thorin_measure_normalised_reciprocal_zeta_under_rh) (Theorem 6.1.10, page 142; conditional on The Riemann Hypothesis: every nontrivial zero of the Riemann zeta function has real part $\frac12$): Under RH the normalised reciprocal zeta function has the signed Thorin type measure $dM$, unit atoms at the squared ordinates of the zeros plus the density of the gamma factor, with $M-1$ the argument function $S(\sqrt t)$, so it is not a GGC even under RH. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Canonical function of the normalised reciprocal zeta function, prime and zero forms](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#canonical_function_normalised_reciprocal_zeta) (Theorem 6.1.11, page 143; proved): With no hypothesis, $-\varphi'/\varphi$ is the Laplace transform of the canonical function $w(x)=e^{x/4}-P(x)$, explicit in the primes, which by the arithmetic form of the heat trace (Weil's explicit formula; Polson 2026, Theorem 4.4) equals the heat trace over the zeros minus the heat trace of their smooth count. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Theta function series for the canonical function w](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#theta_series_for_canonical_function_reciprocal_zeta) (Proposition 6.1.13, page 144; proved): The canonical function $w$ equals $e^{x/4}$ plus an absolutely convergent series of Jacobi theta functions, one for each prime power, with the weights $B_N$ of the Vere-Jones representation. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Sawtooth expansion of the argument function after Gaussian averaging, under RH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#sawtooth_expansion_argument_function_gaussian_average) (Corollary 6.1.14, page 145; conditional on The Riemann Hypothesis: every nontrivial zero of the Riemann zeta function has real part $\frac12$): Under RH the Gaussian average of the argument function $S$ equals $(e^{x/4}-1)/x$ plus the $B_N$ weighted Gaussian averages of sawtooth functions, which makes the sawtooth expansion of $S$ rigorous after Gaussian averaging. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Criterion for RH from the canonical function w](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#rh_criterion_from_canonical_function) (Theorem 6.1.15, page 145; proved): RH is equivalent to the function $w$, explicit in the primes, being the Laplace transform of a real signed measure $m$ on $[0,\infty)$ with $\int|m|(dt)/(1+t)<\infty$, and the measure is then $dM$. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Thorin measure of the gamma factor as a renormalised product of Poisson kernels](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#thorin_measure_of_the_gamma_factor) (Theorem 6.2.1, page 147; proved): The gamma factor $\Gamma(\frac14+\frac{\sqrt s}2)\pi^{-\sqrt s/2}/\Gamma(\frac14)$ is a renormalised infinite product with signed Thorin type measure $-\theta'(\sqrt t)/(2\pi\sqrt t)\,dt$, a series of Poisson kernels of widths $2n+\frac12$ with flat compensators. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Closed form heat trace over the zeros and formal Thorin measure of the reciprocal Xi function](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#heat_trace_closed_form_and_formal_thorin_measure_of_reciprocal_xi) (Theorem 6.2.3, page 149; proved): The heat trace $W(x)$ over the zeros has an explicit absolutely convergent closed form, the polar term, a theta series over prime powers and complementary error functions over the poles of the gamma factor, equivalently the Laplace transform of a formal Thorin measure of the reciprocal Xi function. Corrects a statement of Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Sine squared lemma (Polson 2017, Lemma 1)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#sine_squared_lemma_polson_2017) (Lemma 6.2.4, page 150; proved): A Lévy representation of $\log f$ gives, through the kernel $2\sin^2$, a Lévy representation in the variable $s^2/2$ of the tilted reciprocal $f(\alpha)/f(\alpha+s)$, by a linear positivity preserving map of the Lévy measure. First stated in Polson (2017, version 24 of 2026), On Hilbert's 8th problem, arXiv:1708.02653.
- [Sine squared lemma in the variable s = u squared (Polson 2017, Lemma 1)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#sine_squared_lemma_clock_variable) (Lemma 6.2.5, page 151; proved): In the variable $s=u^2$ a Lévy measure $\tilde\mu$ of $\log f$ gives the Thorin density $\frac{1}{2\pi\sqrt t}\int2\sin^2(\frac{x\sqrt t}2)\tilde\mu(dx)$ of the tilted reciprocal $f(0)/f(\sqrt s)$, so a positive $\tilde\mu$ gives a GGC; this restates Lemma 1 of Polson (2017) with a proof by subordination. First stated in Polson (2017, version 24 of 2026), On Hilbert's 8th problem, arXiv:1708.02653.
- [Reciprocal zeta to the right of the line Re z = 1 is a GGC after a stable tilt](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#reciprocal_zeta_right_of_line_one_tilted_ggc) (Proposition 6.2.6, page 152; proved): For $\beta>1$ the function $\zeta(\beta)/\zeta(\beta+\sqrt s)$ times the tilt $e^{\sqrt s\,\zeta'(\beta)/\zeta(\beta)}$ is a GGC transform with the explicit nonnegative Thorin density $\frac{1}{2\pi\sqrt t}\sum\Lambda(n)n^{-\beta}\,2\sin^2(\frac{\sqrt t\log n}2)$. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Positive Thorin density of a shifted Vere-Jones block](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#shifted_vere_jones_block_positive_thorin_density) (Proposition 6.2.7, page 152; proved): After a shift of the basepoint by $\alpha>0$ and an explicit stable tilt, the reciprocal of the block $1+e^{-\lambda\sqrt s}$ has a positive Poisson kernel Thorin density, which tends to the lattice of atoms of the sawtooth measure as $\alpha\downarrow0$. Corrects a statement of Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Divergence of the cosine Lévy series of the Vere-Jones blocks](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#cosine_levy_series_of_vere_jones_blocks_diverges) (Proposition 6.2.9, page 154; proved): The cosine Lévy forms of the sawtooth blocks cannot be summed with the weights $B_N$, because for every $x>0$ the series $\sum_NB_NK_{U_{\log N}}(x)$ diverges. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [The Meixner density of the gamma factor is not a Pólya frequency function of infinite order](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#meixner_density_not_polya_frequency_function) (Proposition 6.2.10, page 154; proved): The Meixner density $|\Gamma(\frac14+\frac{i\tau}2)|^2/(2^{3/2}\pi^{3/2})$ of the gamma factor, with characteristic function $\operatorname{sech}(v)^{1/2}$, is not a Pólya frequency function of infinite order, because by Schoenberg's theorem the reciprocal $\cosh(v)^{1/2}$ of its characteristic function would have to be entire. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Bernstein function of the gamma factor: theta derivative and Meixner score](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#gamma_factor_bernstein_function_and_meixner_score) (Proposition 6.2.11, page 155; proved): The function $\psi(\frac14+\frac\lambda2)-\psi(\frac14)$ is a Bernstein function whose boundary values on the imaginary axis have real part $2(\theta'(\tau)-\theta'(0))$ and imaginary part the Meixner score $-\frac{d}{d\tau}\log p(\tau)$. Corrects a statement of Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [The reciprocal gamma factor is a GGC after a stable tilt](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#tilted_reciprocal_gamma_factor_is_ggc) (Theorem 6.2.12, page 155; proved): After the stable tilt $e^{-c\sqrt s}$ with $c=\zeta'(\frac12)/\zeta(\frac12)$, the reciprocal of the gamma factor is a GGC transform with the explicit nonnegative Thorin density $(\theta'(\sqrt t)-\theta'(0))/(2\pi\sqrt t)$. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Factorisation of the Pólya autocorrelation through the Meixner law](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#polya_autocorrelation_meixner_factorisation) (Proposition 6.2.14, page 158; proved): The autocorrelation of the Pólya kernel is a fourth order differential operator applied to the Fourier transform of $p|\zeta|^2$ on the critical line, formally the Meixner characteristic function convolved with a positive measure on the lattice $\{\log(m/n)\}$, and the lattice sum diverges because of the pole of $\zeta$. Corrects a statement of Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Splitting of the canonical function of the floor of the reciprocal Xi function, and GGC if and only if RH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#floor_reciprocal_xi_infinitely_divisible_ggc_iff_rh) (Theorem 6.2.15, page 159; proved): With no hypothesis the canonical function $W(x)+c/(2\sqrt{\pi x})$ of the floor $e^{-c\sqrt s}\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt s)$ is the sum of the function $w$, explicit in the primes and proved positive with certified interval enclosures and the verification of RH to height $50$, and a completely monotone archimedean part, which reproves that the floor is infinitely divisible (this also follows from Theorem A of Polson 2026); the floor is a GGC if and only if RH holds. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Derivative signs of the canonical function of the floor to order ten billion, a separate proof (Williamson measures)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#floor_canonical_function_derivative_signs_to_order_1e10) (Theorem 6.2.17, page 161; proved): The canonical function $k$ of the floor satisfies $(-1)^nk^{(n)}(y)>0$ for all $y>0$ and every $n\le10^{10}$, proved by a two range argument from the verification of RH to height $3\times10^{12}$, a bound for the zero count and one certified interval enclosure, which gives positive Williamson measures; the signs to order $10^{17}$ follow from Polson (2017, version 24 of 2026), and to order $1.16\times10^{25}$ from the book's heat trace estimates. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.

#### Key terms

reciprocal zeta function, Thorin measure, generalized gamma convolution, generalised gamma convolution, GGC, infinite divisibility, canonical function, heat trace, Riemann Hypothesis, RH, Lai and Vere-Jones identity, hyperbolic secant, sawtooth measure, Meixner Pollaczek polynomials, local Riemann Hypothesis, sine squared lemma, stable tilt, floor of the reciprocal Xi function

chapters.title: Infinite divisibility and truncations of the reciprocal zeta function
chapters.summary:
This chapter asks where the normalised reciprocal zeta function $\varphi(s)=\zeta(\frac12)/((1-4s)\zeta(\frac12+\sqrt s))$ sits among infinitely divisible laws, and how far truncations of the Biane Pitman Yor lattice go towards the Riemann Hypothesis (RH). Unconditionally, and certified in interval arithmetic, it proves that the canonical function $w$ is positive, so that $\varphi$ is the Laplace transform of an infinitely divisible law with Lévy density $w(x)/x$, which is not self decomposable, not in the Bondesson class and not a generalized gamma convolution (GGC). It reads the Vere-Jones weights as necklace polynomials, extends the canonical function across the critical strip, and states the Laguerre Pólya class and the Lee and Yang property in Thorin measure terms. For simple zeros $\rho$, zeros of the truncated lattice transforms converge to $\rho/2$ at rate $1/n$: the one sided Conjecture T is false, while the symmetrised Conjecture S is proved above explicit heights for $n\le24$ and $n=32,36$ and only checked numerically below them. It also proves Weil positivity on the Bernstein cone and reads the de Bruijn Newman flow as a path of GGCs.

#### From the literature

Thorin measures and generalized gamma convolutions (Thorin 1977; Bondesson 1992), closed under independent products (Bondesson 2015); unimodality of self decomposable laws (Yamazato 1978); Selberg's central limit theorem for $S(t)$ (Selberg 1946); verification of RH to height 50 (Backlund 1918) and $3\times10^{12}$ (Platt and Trudgian 2021); simplicity of the first $1.5\times10^9$ zeros (van de Lune, te Riele and Winter 1986); an explicit Riemann von Mangoldt bound (Hasanalizade, Shen and Wong 2022); necklace polynomials (Metropolis and Rota 1983); Pólya's theory of real zeros (Pólya 1926), Cardon's theorems (Cardon 2004, 2005), zeros of $\xi(s+a)+\xi(s-a)$ for $a\ge\frac12$ (Lagarias 2005), the Lee and Yang theorem (Lee and Yang 1952), Newman's characterization of Lee and Yang spins (Newman 1974); the Biane Pitman Yor identity (Biane, Pitman and Yor 2001; Williams 1990); Weil's criterion (Weil 1952; Bombieri 2000); the de Bruijn Newman constant (de Bruijn 1950; Newman 1976; Rodgers and Tao 2020; Polymath 2019; Platt and Trudgian 2021).

#### New results

Most results below first appeared in Part IX of Polson (2026); uncertified numerical checks are not catalogued.

- [The normalised reciprocal zeta function is infinitely divisible](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#reciprocal_zeta_infinitely_divisible_unconditional) (Theorem 7.1.1, page 166; proved): Without any hypothesis on the zeros, the normalised reciprocal zeta function is the Laplace transform of an infinitely divisible law with Lévy density $w(x)/x$, because its canonical function $w$ is positive; the proof is certified with the verification of the Riemann Hypothesis to height 50 and interval enclosures. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Negative bias of the Gaussian smoothed prime number theorem error](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#gaussian_smoothed_prime_number_theorem_error_negative_bias) (Proposition 7.1.2, page 167; proved): The error of the prime number theorem, smoothed with a Gaussian weight in $\log y$, has a definite negative bias, about $-0.343\,(\pi x)^{-1/2}$ at large $x$, whereas a pointwise bound on the error of size $\sqrt y\log^2y$, even the one that the Riemann Hypothesis implies, controls it only up to order $x$. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [The reciprocal zeta function in the Bondesson hierarchy: not self decomposable, not a GGC](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#reciprocal_zeta_bondesson_hierarchy_classification) (Theorem 7.1.3, page 168; proved): The normalised reciprocal zeta function is infinitely divisible but not self decomposable, not in the Bondesson class and not a mixture of exponentials, hence not a generalised gamma convolution, with no hypothesis on the zeros. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Density of the reciprocal zeta law at the origin](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#reciprocal_zeta_density_rises_from_origin) (Theorem 7.1.4, page 170; proved): The density of the law with Laplace transform equal to the normalised reciprocal zeta function starts at $-\zeta(\frac12)/4$ with the positive slope $-\zeta(\frac12)/16$, so it is not monotone, not log convex and not completely monotone. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [The reciprocal zeta law is not a sum, product or limit of GGC variables](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#reciprocal_zeta_law_not_built_from_ggc_operations) (Corollary 7.1.6, page 171; proved): The random variable with Laplace transform equal to the normalised reciprocal zeta function is not a sum, a product or a weak limit of independent generalised gamma convolution variables. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [The GGC class is not closed under the harmonic mean](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#ggc_class_not_closed_under_harmonic_mean) (Proposition 7.1.7, page 171; proved): The harmonic mean of two independent standard exponential variables has an explicit density and is not a generalised gamma convolution, so the class of generalised gamma convolutions is not closed under harmonic means of independent variables. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Vere-Jones weights of the zeta function are necklace polynomials](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#vere_jones_weights_are_necklace_polynomials) (Theorem 7.1.8, page 173; proved): A 2 adic variant of the cyclotomic identity of Metropolis and Rota factors $1/(1-qy)$ into factors $1+y^n$ with necklace polynomial exponents, which makes the Vere-Jones weights of the zeta function at prime powers necklace polynomials at $p^{-1/2}$; the authors have not found the identity stated in this form, but it may well be known in the combinatorics of necklaces. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Sign rule for the necklace weights of the zeta function](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#necklace_weights_sign_rule) (Proposition 7.1.9, page 173; proved): At $q=p^{-1/2}$ the necklace exponent $b_{2^a}$ is positive, and for odd $n>1$ the exponent $b_n$ is nonzero with sign $(-1)^{\omega(n)}$, where $\omega(n)$ counts the distinct prime factors of $n$. Corrects a statement of Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Lévy representation of the reciprocal zeta function across the critical strip](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#levy_representation_reciprocal_zeta_across_critical_strip) (Theorem 7.1.12, page 176; proved): For each $\sigma$ in $(0,1)$ the shifted reciprocal zeta function has an explicit canonical function $w_\sigma$ in three equivalent forms, with the asymptotic $\zeta'(\sigma)/\zeta(\sigma)$ over $2\sqrt{\pi x}$, and it is infinitely divisible with Lévy density $w_\sigma(x)/x$ whenever $w_\sigma$ is nonnegative, a positivity that the chapter proves only for $\sigma=\frac12$. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [The shifted reciprocal zeta function is never a GGC on a line of the strip](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#shifted_reciprocal_zeta_never_ggc_on_the_strip) (Proposition 7.1.13, page 177; proved): On every line $\sigma$ in $(0,1)$ the shifted reciprocal zeta function is not a generalised gamma convolution and, if infinitely divisible, not self decomposable, because the factor that removes the pole makes its canonical function increase at the origin. Corrects a statement of Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Laguerre Pólya class as integer atom GGCs](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#laguerre_polya_class_integer_atom_ggc) (Proposition 7.1.15, page 180; proved): A real even entire function $G$ of order below 2 lies in the Laguerre Pólya class exactly when $G(0)/G(i\sqrt s)$ is the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution whose Thorin measure has integer masses at the squared zeros. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Lee and Yang single spin laws as integer atom GGCs](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#lee_yang_property_integer_atom_ggc) (Proposition 7.1.16, page 181; proved): A symmetric law with Gaussian moments of all orders has the Lee and Yang property exactly when the reciprocal of its moment generating function at $\sqrt s$ is the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution with integer atoms at the squared zeros of its characteristic function. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Random harmonic series and the strip of the Pólya kernel](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#random_harmonic_series_matches_polya_kernel_strip) (Proposition 7.1.17, page 182; proved): The random harmonic series $H_\kappa$ has a double exponential tail whose leading constant equals that of the Pólya kernel exactly at $\kappa^*=6.61845\ldots$, and its density is analytic in the strip $|\operatorname{Im}t|<\pi/4$, the strip of analyticity of the Pólya kernel. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [The reciprocal Xi transform is a harmonic mean of Brownian exit time transforms](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#reciprocal_xi_transform_harmonic_mean_of_brownian_exit_time_transforms) (Proposition 7.1.23, page 187; proved): The Laplace transform of the clock, the reciprocal Xi function, is the harmonic mean over the Pólya density of the Laplace transforms $1/\cosh(x\sqrt s)$ of scaled Brownian exit times, so by Jensen's inequality it is at most the Laplace transform of the corresponding scale mixture. New in this book.
- [A harmonic mean of two GGC transforms that is not a Laplace transform of a positive measure](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#harmonic_mean_of_two_ggc_transforms_not_a_laplace_transform) (Example 7.1.24, page 188; counterexample, proved): The harmonic mean of the Laplace transforms $(1+s)^{-2}$ and $(1+2s)^{-2}$ of two generalized gamma convolutions (GGC) is $1/(1+3s+\frac52s^2)$, whose inverse transform $2e^{-0.6t}\sin(0.2t)$ is negative on $(5\pi,10\pi)$, so a harmonic mean of GGC transforms need not be the Laplace transform of a positive measure. New in this book.
- [A two point scale mixture of Gamma(2) that is infinitely divisible and not a GGC](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#gamma_two_scale_mixture_infinitely_divisible_but_not_ggc) (Example 7.1.25, page 188; counterexample, proved): A scale mixture of a Gamma(2) variable by an independent variable equal to $1$ or to a positive $\lambda\ne1$ with probability one half each is infinitely divisible but not a generalized gamma convolution, because its Laplace transform has nonreal zeros. New in this book.
- [The clock is not a Gamma scale mixture, for any shape](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#clock_is_not_a_gamma_scale_mixture) (Theorem 7.1.26, page 188; proved): The clock is not a scale mixture of Gamma($a$) laws for any shape $a>0$, because the Laplace transform of such a mixture is at least a constant times $s^{-a}$ for large $s$, while that of the clock is at most a constant times $e^{-x\sqrt s}$ for every $x>0$. New in this book.
- [First order expansion of the zeros of the truncated lattice transforms](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#truncated_lattice_zeros_first_order_expansion) (Proposition 7.2.2, page 190; proved): Near each simple zero $\rho$ of $\xi$ the truncated transform $F_n$ has exactly one zero, equal to $\rho/2+\kappa(\rho)/n+O(n^{-2})$ for large $n$, with an explicit constant $\kappa(\rho)$. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Displacement constant of the truncated zeros in terms of Hardy's function](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#truncated_lattice_displacement_formula_hardy_function) (Theorem 7.2.3, page 191; proved): For a simple zero on the critical line, the real and imaginary parts of the displacement constant $\kappa(\rho)$ are given in closed form by the derivative of Hardy's function $Z$ and the number $e^{i\theta(\gamma)}\zeta(\frac52+i\gamma)$. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Conjecture T is false for large n](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#conjecture_t_false_truncated_zeros_right_of_the_line) (Corollary 7.2.4, page 192; counterexample, proved): Conjecture T, that no truncated lattice transform $F_n$ has a zero with real part above $\frac14$, is false: for all large $n$ there is such a zero near $\rho_{213}/2$, certified with a ball arithmetic enclosure of the displacement constant. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Symmetrised truncations: symmetry, limit and persistence of simple zeros on the line](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#symmetrised_truncations_symmetry_and_limit) (Proposition 7.2.6, page 193; proved): The symmetrised truncations $K_n$ are symmetric about the line $\operatorname{Re}w=\frac14$, converge to $4\xi(2w)$, and keep every simple zero of $\xi(2w)$ on the line as a zero exactly on the line for all large $n$. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Real rooted symmetrised truncations for infinitely many n imply the Riemann Hypothesis](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#symmetrised_truncations_real_rooted_implies_rh) (Theorem 7.2.7, page 193; proved): If for infinitely many $n$ all zeros of the symmetrised truncation $K_n$ in the strip $0<\operatorname{Re}w<\frac12$ lie on the line $\operatorname{Re}w=\frac14$, then the Riemann Hypothesis holds. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Single term bound: no off line zeros of the symmetrised truncation above explicit heights](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#symmetrised_truncations_single_term_bound_explicit_heights) (Theorem 7.2.8, page 195; proved): A single term bound shows that for $n=1$ to $6$, $8$ and $10$ the symmetrised truncation $K_n$ has no zero off the line in the strip above explicit heights $Y_n$ between $4.81$ and $21232$, which are obtained by evaluating the explicit bounds numerically. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Conjecture S for n up to 6 and n = 8 above explicit heights](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#conjecture_s_small_n_above_explicit_heights) (Corollary 7.2.9, page 195; proved): Conjecture S is proved for $n=1$ to $6$ and $n=8$ above the explicit heights of the single term bound, which are evaluated numerically, and below those heights it is only checked numerically by floating point argument principle counts. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Torus bound for the symmetrised truncations](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#symmetrised_truncations_torus_bound) (Theorem 7.2.10, page 196; proved): Explicit inequalities on the extremes of the Dirichlet polynomial $P_n$ and its logarithmic derivative over the torus of prime phases imply that the symmetrised truncation $K_n$ has no zero off the line $\operatorname{Re}w=\frac14$ in the strip $0<\operatorname{Re}w<\frac12$ at a given height or above. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Conjecture S for n up to 24, 32 and 36 above explicit thresholds](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#conjecture_s_above_explicit_thresholds_n_to_36) (Corollary 7.2.11, page 197; proved): Conjecture S is proved for $n=7$, $9$ to $24$, $32$ and $36$ above explicit height thresholds by torus bounds certified in ball arithmetic, and below the thresholds it is only checked numerically; with the small $n$ results it covers every $n\le24$ and $n=32,36$. Corrects a statement of Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Thorin positivity of R is Weil's criterion](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#thorin_positivity_of_reciprocal_xi_is_weil_criterion) (Proposition 7.2.13, page 201; proved): The reciprocal Xi function $R$ is the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution exactly when Weil's distribution is positive definite, by combining Polson's rigidity theorem with Weil's criterion, so Thorin positivity of $R$ is Weil's criterion in other coordinates and gives no new criterion. Corrects a statement of Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Weil positivity on the Bernstein cone](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#weil_positivity_on_bernstein_cone) (Theorem 7.2.14, page 202; proved): Unconditionally, Weil's functional $\sum_\rho\hat h(\gamma_\rho)$ is positive for every test function $\hat h$ that is a Laplace transform in $r^2$ of a nonnegative weight under an integrability condition, including Thorin type products, $\operatorname{sech}(cr)$ and $(1+r^2/a)^{-m}$; it integrates the positivity of the heat trace of the zeros (Polson 2026, Theorem A), for which the book gives a second proof certified with the verification of RH to height 50 and interval enclosures. Corrects a statement of Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
