- [The de Bruijn Newman flow as a path of GGCs](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#debruijn_newman_flow_ggc_path) (Theorem 7.2.15, page 204; proved): For every $t$ at least the de Bruijn Newman constant, $R_t=H_t(0)/H_t(2i\sqrt s)$ is the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution with atoms at the squared half zeros of $H_t$, so it is a GGC for every $t\ge0.2$ unconditionally, and the Riemann Hypothesis holds exactly when $R_t$ is a GGC for arbitrarily small $t>0$. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [No GGC multiplier can create the positivity of R](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#no_ggc_multiplier_can_create_positivity) (Proposition 7.2.16, page 204; proved): Multiplying $R$ by the Laplace transform of any generalised gamma convolution gives a generalised gamma convolution exactly when the Riemann Hypothesis holds, so no such multiplier can manufacture the positivity; for the normalised reciprocal zeta function only one direction holds for every multiplier. Corrects a statement of Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Conjecture S for infinitely many n](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_conjecture_s_for_infinitely_many_n) (Problem 7.1, page 206; open): The book asks for a proof that the symmetrised truncations $K_n$ have all their zeros in the strip $0<\operatorname{Re}w<\frac12$ on the line $\operatorname{Re}w=\frac14$ for infinitely many $n$, which would imply the Riemann Hypothesis. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Torus method beyond n = 36](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_torus_method_beyond_n_36) (Problem 7.2, page 206; open): The book asks for an extension of the torus bound for the symmetrised truncations with narrower bands around $x=\frac54$, and for the first $n$ at which the torus function $P_n$ has zeros with $x\ge\frac54$. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [From finite order to all orders for the floor](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_finite_order_to_all_orders_n_monotonicity_of_the_floor) (Problem 7.3, page 206; open): The book asks whether the argument that proves $(-1)^nk^{(n)}(y)>0$ for the canonical function $k$ of the floor of the reciprocal Xi function up to order $10^{10}$ extends to every order, which would imply the Riemann Hypothesis; the signs are already known to order $10^{17}$ (Polson 2017, version 24 of 2026) and, by the book's heat trace estimates, to order $1.16\times10^{25}$. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Beyond the Bernstein cone](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_largest_cone_of_unconditional_weil_positivity) (Problem 7.4, page 207; open): The book asks for the largest cone of test functions, closed under the operations that preserve the Thorin structure, on which Weil positivity can be proved unconditionally, and for how far such a cone can localise in height. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Deforming the binary product](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_deforming_the_binary_product) (Problem 7.5, page 207; open): The book asks where and how the positivity of the interference pattern of arithmetic progressions in the pseudo spectral trace formula can fail along the path from the binary product at $\sigma=0$ to the critical line. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Regularising the autocorrelation of the Pólya kernel](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_regularising_the_autocorrelation_of_the_polya_kernel) (Problem 7.6, page 207; open): The book asks for the regularised form of the Meixner characteristic function convolved with the positive lattice measure $\mathcal A$, and whether it has a Thorin or Lee and Yang structure in $v$. Corrects a statement of Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Unimodality of w and of the density f](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_unimodality_of_the_canonical_function_and_density) (Problem 7.7, page 207; open): The book asks for proofs that the canonical function $w$ of the normalised reciprocal zeta function and the density $f$ of its law are unimodal, which is supported only by numerical evidence. Corrects a statement of Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Infinite divisibility across the strip](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_levy_density_positive_on_every_line_of_the_strip) (Problem 7.8, page 207; open): The book asks whether $w_\sigma(x)>0$ for every $\sigma$ in $(0,1)$ and every $x>0$, that is whether the shifted reciprocal zeta function is infinitely divisible on every vertical line of the critical strip. New in this book.
- [Meixner Pollaczek truncations with real zeros](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_meixner_pollaczek_truncations_real_rooted) (Problem 7.9, page 208; open): The book asks for a weighting of the coefficients of the symmetric Meixner Pollaczek expansion of $(\tau^2+\frac14)Z(\tau)$, or a Jensen type construction from them, whose polynomials are real rooted with zeros converging to the ordinates of the zeta zeros. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Nyman Beurling criterion and the sech expansion](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_nyman_beurling_and_the_sech_expansion) (Problem 7.10, page 208; open): The book asks how the completeness question of Lai and Vere-Jones for dilates of $\operatorname{sech}$ relates to the Nyman Beurling criterion, and whether the sech expansion of $1/\zeta(\frac12+\sqrt s)$ has an $L^2$ version on the boundary. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
- [Product representations of the law of R](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_product_representation_of_the_reciprocal_xi_law) (Problem 7.11, page 208; open): The book asks whether the compensation in the formal deconvolution of the reciprocal zeta law into the reciprocal Xi law can be absorbed into a product of independent generalised gamma convolution variables, since an unconditional representation of that kind would prove the Riemann Hypothesis. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.

#### Key terms

reciprocal zeta function, infinite divisibility, Lévy density, canonical function, self decomposable, Bondesson class, generalized gamma convolution, generalised gamma convolution, GGC, Thorin measure, necklace polynomials, Vere-Jones weights, Laguerre Pólya class, Lee Yang property, Biane Pitman Yor, Conjecture S, symmetrised truncations, Weil criterion, Weil positivity, Bernstein cone, de Bruijn Newman constant, Riemann Hypothesis, RH

chapters.title: Probability, hitting times and other criteria
chapters.summary:
What else does the Pólya density compute about the Riemann Hypothesis (RH)? The clock $1/G$ of Riemann's xi function is the Laplace transform of a random variable $T$, self decomposable with no hypothesis on the zeros and a generalized gamma convolution (GGC) exactly when RH holds, and the Pólya route computes its law with no zero as input. The chapter studies this clock variable (hazard rate, Kent approximants, Monte Carlo through Williams' representation), proves that it is not a Brownian first passage time to an independent random level, and computes a curved Brownian boundary for it from the Volterra equation. It computes the Keiper Li coefficients, reads Li's criterion as positivity of the Thorin functional, and follows the de Bruijn Newman flow to the collisions of zeros, with a Hankel test and collision time bounds in terms of Laguerre's quantity suggested by Biane's free convolution with a semicircle law. It then evaluates the Dedekind eta kernel, Dirichlet $L$ functions and Ramanujan's $\Delta$, recovers zeros by nonnegative deconvolution, and treats Pólya's Bessel function $K_{i\theta/2}(2\pi)$, for which the Thorin programme holds as theorems. No proof of RH is claimed.

#### From the literature

- Kent's eigenvalue expansion of hitting times (Kent 1980) and Krein's inverse spectral theory (Dym and McKean 1976).
- Williams' Bessel hitting time representation of $\xi$ (Williams 1990; Biane, Pitman and Yor 2001); Talbot inversion (Talbot 1979).
- Tangent approximation and inverse problem for first passage boundaries (Roberts and Shortland 1995; Ekström and Janson 2016).
- Li's criterion (Li 1997), Keiper's coefficients (Keiper 1992), Bombieri and Lagarias (1999), Lagarias's positivity criterion (Lagarias 1999).
- The de Bruijn Newman constant (de Bruijn 1950; Newman 1976), $\Lambda\ge0$ (Rodgers and Tao 2020), $\Lambda\le0.2$ (Platt and Trudgian 2021), Lehmer pair bounds (Csordas, Smith and Varga 1994).
- Free convolution with a semicircle law (Biane 1997); Pólya's Bessel function (Pólya 1926); Biane's dictionary of hitting times and spectral measures, with corrected constants, and the Liouville operator of the zeros, going back to Titchmarsh (Biane 2009); Hecke's converse theorem (Hecke 1936).
- Generalised gamma convolutions and the Bondesson class (Bondesson 1992).

#### New results

Tables of computed values are numerical.

- [Möbius series for the density of the clock with no hypothesis, with terms g_n a convolution of one fixed function with a first passage kernel](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#mobius_series_for_clock_density_converges_absolutely_for_every_t) (Proposition 8.1.1, page 210; proved): With no hypothesis the density $f$ of the clock equals $\sum_n\mu(n)n^{-1/2}g_n(t)$, $g_n=g_1*q_{\log n}$, an absolutely convergent series (faster than any power of $n$) whose terms are bounded through an erfc factor; $g_1$ grows like $2\xi(\frac12)e^{t/4}$, so for large $t$ the series rests on the prime number theorem, and for small $t$ it converges very fast. New in this book.
- [Lower tail of the clock: P(T at most y) is at most exp of minus (log 1/y) squared over 16 y, so the density vanishes to infinite order at the origin](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#clock_lower_tail_chernoff_bound_density_vanishes_to_infinite_order_at_origin) (Result 8.1.1, page 211; proved): With no hypothesis $P(T\le y)\le\exp\{-(1+o(1))(\log\frac1y)^2/16y\}$ as $y\downarrow0$, by Chernoff's bound with $\log G(u)\sim\frac{\sqrt u}4\log u$ optimised at $\sqrt u\approx\log(1/y)/4y$; so the density vanishes to infinite order at the origin. New in this book.
- [RH holds if and only if the density of the clock is a Pólya frequency function of infinite order](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#rh_equivalent_to_clock_density_being_polya_frequency_function_of_infinite_order) (Proposition 8.1.2, page 211; proved): RH is equivalent to the density $f$ of the clock being a Pólya frequency function of infinite order, the one sided form of the two sided criterion: under RH $f$ is the density of $\sum_\gamma e_\gamma/\gamma^2$, and conversely Schoenberg's theorem forces $G$ to have only real zeros. New in this book.
- [The clock is not a Brownian first passage time to an independent random level](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#clock_not_first_passage_time_to_random_level) (Proposition 8.2.1, page 217; proved): The clock variable of the Riemann xi function is not, for any constant drift and any independent random level, the first passage time of Brownian motion with that drift to that level, and the proof uses no hypothesis on the zeros. New in this book.
- [Keiper Li coefficients as values of the Thorin functional](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#keiper_li_coefficients_as_thorin_functional) (Proposition 8.3.1, page 224; proved): With no hypothesis on the zeros, each Keiper Li coefficient is the Thorin functional of the zeros paired with an explicit rational function that is nonnegative on the positive axis, so Li's criterion is nonnegativity of that functional on the cone spanned by these functions. New in this book.
- [Critical point lower bound for the collision time of zeros under the backward heat flow](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#backward_heat_flow_critical_point_collision_bound) (Theorem 8.4.6, page 238; proved): While all zeros stay real and simple, a gap between two zeros of a real polynomial cannot close under the backward heat flow before the time one over Laguerre's quantity at the critical point of the gap, and z squared minus a squared attains the bound. New in this book.
- [Biane form lower bound for the collision time of zeros under the backward heat flow](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#backward_heat_flow_biane_form_collision_bound) (Theorem 8.4.8, page 239; proved): While all zeros of a real polynomial stay real and simple, a gap between two adjacent zeros cannot close under the backward heat flow before the time one over the minimum of Laguerre's quantity over the gap, a bound at least as strong as the one from the critical point and attained by z squared minus a squared. New in this book.
- [Local lower bound for the closing of a gap with a correction from the nonreal zeros](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#backward_heat_flow_local_bound_nonreal_zeros) (Theorem 8.4.11, page 240; proved): For the minimum m of Laguerre's quantity over a gap between real zeros, the upper right Dini derivative is at most one plus an explicit correction, computed from the nonreal zeros, times m squared, which bounds the time at which the gap closes from below. New in this book.
- [Lower bound for the closing of a gap from the quantity delta, with no knowledge of the nonreal zeros](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#backward_heat_flow_delta_collision_bound) (Corollary 8.4.12, page 241; proved): A quantity delta computed from the function and its first four derivatives at the minimiser of Laguerre's quantity over a gap between real zeros controls the growth of that minimum under the backward heat flow, and when delta stays at most zero until the collision the gap cannot close before Biane's time, one over the initial minimum of Laguerre's quantity, even when nonreal zeros are present. New in this book.
- [Upper bound (deadline) for the closing time of a gap between real zeros](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#backward_heat_flow_collision_deadline) (Theorem 8.4.13, page 241; proved): If the share Q of the other zeros and the sum W over the nonreal zeros stay below constants rho and W bar for which 3 rho plus the square root of 9 rho squared plus 6 W bar is less than the initial minimum of Laguerre's quantity over a gap between two real zeros, the gap closes, by a collision of one of its bounding zeros with another zero, no later than an explicit logarithmic time. New in this book.
- [Deadline for the closing of a gap in terms of the quantity kappa](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#backward_heat_flow_collision_deadline_kappa_form) (Corollary 8.4.14, page 242; proved): The deadline for the closing of a gap holds with six times the bound on W replaced by the largest negative part of a quantity kappa, computed from the function at the minimiser and the two zeros bounding the gap, and this form is never weaker. New in this book.
- [Control of the nonreal zeros of the de Bruijn Newman function at negative times](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#nonreal_zeros_control_along_backward_heat_flow) (Problem 8.1, page 245; open): No bound is known, computed from the de Bruijn Newman function at time zero, for how far its nonreal zeros travel at negative times or how close to a gap between real zeros they come, and such control would make the lower and upper bounds for the closing time of a gap unconditional statements about that function. New in this book.
- [Shielding deficit identity for a pair of adjacent real zeros of the de Bruijn Newman function (Newton 2026, Zenodo)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#shielding_deficit_identity_for_adjacent_real_zeros_of_de_bruijn_newman_function) (Theorem 8.4.15, page 247; proved): A telescoping identity (Newton 2026, Zenodo) expresses the shielding deficit of a pair of adjacent real zeros as a sum over the exterior gaps of the relative deviations of those gaps from the pair's gap, when all zeros are real and the exterior zeros tend to infinity. New in this book.
- [Consequences of the shielding deficit identity: lattice, truncated lattice, single enlarged gap, one sided bound and monotonicity of the smallest gap (Newton 2026, Zenodo)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#shielding_deficit_consequences_lattice_tail_single_gap_and_smallest_gap_does_not_shrink) (Corollary 8.4.16, page 247; proved): Five consequences of the shielding deficit identity: the lattice has zero deficit, a truncated lattice with $R$ exterior zeros per side has deficit $2/(R+1)$, a single enlarged gap contributes $\delta/(j(j+\delta))$, the positive part of the deficit is at most $g^{-1}\sum_j j^{-2}$ times the excess of the exterior gaps over $g$, and a smallest gap of a configuration does not shrink forward in time. New in this book.
- [The de Bruijn Newman function as a Gaussian average and the reciprocal transform of the tilted clock as a Gaussian smoothing of xi](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#tilted_kernel_gaussian_average_and_reciprocal_tilted_clock_gaussian_smoothing) (Proposition 8.4.17, page 248; proved): For $t>0$ the de Bruijn Newman function $H_t$ is the Gaussian average $\mathbb{E}H_0(z+i\sqrt{2t}Z)$ of $H_0$, and $1/R_t(\sigma^2)$, the reciprocal of the Laplace transform of the tilted clock when $t$ is at least the de Bruijn Newman constant, is the Gaussian smoothing of $\xi(\frac12+\sigma)$ with variance $t/2$, normalised at $\sigma=0$. New in this book.
- [Large tilt of the clock: the limit is twice the Brownian exit time](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#large_tilt_limit_of_the_clock_twice_brownian_exit_time) (Proposition 8.4.18, page 249; proved): As the tilt $t\to\infty$, the tilted clock divided by the square of the mode $u_t$ of the tilted kernel converges in law to twice the exit time of Brownian motion from $(-1,1)$, its Laplace transform tends to $1/\cosh(2\sqrt s)$, and $u_t$ times the $j$th positive zero of $H_t$ tends to $\pi(j-\frac12)$. New in this book.
- [Gaussian smoothing of a reciprocal GGC transform is again one](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#gaussian_smoothing_of_reciprocal_ggc_transform_is_again_one) (Theorem 8.4.19, page 250; proved): Gaussian smoothing in the variable $\sqrt s$ of the reciprocal of the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution (GGC) with discrete Thorin measure and no drift is again the reciprocal of such a transform, the Thorin atoms obey, while they are simple, the motion equation of the de Bruijn Newman flow, and the mean of the GGC satisfies $\frac{d}{d\lambda}\mathbb{E}S_\lambda=(\mathbb{E}S_\lambda)^2-\frac32\operatorname{Var}S_\lambda$. New in this book.
- [Concentration of the Laguerre expressions at the origin along the whole de Bruijn Newman flow, with positivity of $L_{n,t}$ on every window for large $n$ (Newton 2026, Zenodo)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#laguerre_expression_central_second_moment_vanishes_uniformly_along_de_bruijn_newman_flow) (Theorem 8.4.20, page 252; proved): For the probability measures $\mathbb{E}_{n,t}$ defining the Laguerre expressions $L_{n,t}$ of the de Bruijn Newman function, the second moment of the centred variable tends to zero uniformly in $0\le t\le\frac12$, so for every $X$ the expression $L_{n,t}(x)$ is positive on $|x|\le X$ for all large $n$, uniformly in $t$ (Newton 2026, Zenodo); the index is not effective. New in this book.
- [Compact uniform asymptotic of the Laguerre ratio $k_nL_{n+1,t}(x)/L_{n,t}(x)$ along the whole de Bruijn Newman flow (Newton 2026, Zenodo)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#uniform_asymptotic_of_laguerre_ratio_one_eighth_log_n_squared_on_every_window) (Theorem 8.4.22, page 253; proved): For every $X$, uniformly in $0\le t\le\frac12$ and $|x|\le X$, the ratio $k_nL_{n+1,t}(x)/L_{n,t}(x)$ equals $c_n(t)(1+o(1))=\frac18(\log n)^2(1+o(1))$ (Newton 2026, Zenodo), the second equality using the Lambert centring proposition, whose proof in the book is a sketch. New in this book.
- [Local Rouché criterion for backward persistence of an adjacent pair of real simple zeros of the de Bruijn Newman function (Newton 2026, Zenodo)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#local_rouche_criterion_for_backward_persistence_of_a_pair_of_real_zeros_of_de_bruijn_newman_function) (Proposition 8.4.25, page 255; proved): If an explicit integral $\psi_Y(\sigma)$ is smaller than the minimum of $|H_{t_*}|$ on a contour around an adjacent pair of real simple zeros, then the pair stays real and simple for the backward time $\sigma$ and the gap shrinks by at most $2r$ (Newton 2026, Zenodo). New in this book.
- [Obstruction at height: the absolute value Rouché criterion certifies only backward steps of size $O(e^{-\delta a})$ at a real zero $a$ of the de Bruijn Newman function (Newton 2026, Zenodo, mechanism corrected)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#no_fixed_step_rouche_criterion_certifies_backward_persistence_at_every_height_for_de_bruijn_newman_function) (Proposition 8.4.26, page 256; proved): No criterion of the form $\psi_Y(\sigma)<m$ certifies a fixed backward step $\sigma>0$ at every height, since $\min_\Gamma|H_{t_*}|$ decays like $e^{-\delta a}$ while $\psi_Y(\sigma)\ge\psi_0(\sigma)>0$ does not decay; the step such a criterion can certify at height $a$ is $O(e^{-\delta a})$ (Newton 2026, Zenodo, with the mechanism corrected in the book). New in this book.
- [Max representation of the L function of Ramanujan's Delta](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#max_representation_of_ramanujan_delta_l_function) (Theorem 8.5.2, page 262; proved): The completed L function of Ramanujan's cusp form Delta is the expectation of an incomplete gamma function at the random point 2 pi M*, where M* is a maximum of independent exponential variables, a representation with no signs. New in this book.
- [Gamma mixture and mixed Poisson forms of L values of Delta](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#gamma_mixture_and_mixed_poisson_forms_of_delta_l_values) (Corollary 8.5.3, page 263; proved): For real s above minus 11/2 the L value of Ramanujan's Delta is the probability that a gamma variable exceeds 2 pi M*, and at the points s equal to k minus 11/2 it is a mixed Poisson probability. New in this book.
- [L values of Delta and chi12 as infinitely divisible probabilities](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#delta_and_chi12_l_values_as_infinitely_divisible_probabilities) (Proposition 8.5.7, page 268; proved): By Kristiansen's theorem on Gamma(2) mixtures and the theorem of Goldie and Steutel on exponential mixtures, the L values of Ramanujan's Delta at real s between minus 11/2 and minus 7/2 and of the character chi12 at real s between 0 and 4 are probabilities that an infinitely divisible variable exceeds one. New in this book.
- [Laplace transform of the maximum M1 of exponentials in closed form](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#laplace_transform_of_max_of_exponentials_m1_closed_form) (Proposition 8.5.8, page 268; proved): The Laplace transform of the maximum of independent exponential variables with rates 2 pi n is an explicit ratio of a sine and a cosine, equal to an infinite product over the numbers b_n = pi (n squared minus 1)/12. New in this book.
- [Rényi type decomposition of the maximum M1 of exponentials](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#renyi_type_decomposition_of_max_of_exponentials_m1) (Corollary 8.5.9, page 269; proved): The maximum of independent exponential variables with rates 2 pi n is a sum of independent exponential variables whose rates are b_{6k-1} or b_{6k+1} with explicit probabilities p_k that decrease to one half. New in this book.
- [Lévy density and Bondesson function of the maximum M1](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#levy_density_and_bondesson_function_of_max_of_exponentials_m1) (Proposition 8.5.11, page 271; proved): The Lévy density of the maximum M1 has an explicit theta function form with stated behaviour at zero and infinity, and its Bondesson function N_1 is nonnegative and grows like a constant times the square root of z. New in this book.
- [Thorin measure of M1 as a difference of two GGC Thorin measures](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#thorin_measure_of_m1_difference_of_two_ggc_thorin_measures) (Theorem 8.5.12, page 271; proved): The maximum M1 plus an independent GGC Z has the law of a second GGC S, so the signed Thorin measure of M1 is the difference of two positive measures with unit atoms. New in this book.
- [Certified zeros of the Laplace transform of the maximum M* of exponentials](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#certified_zeros_of_laplace_transform_of_max_of_exponentials_m_star) (Proposition 8.5.13, page 273; proved): Certified in ball arithmetic: the Laplace transform of M* changes sign in each of 25 gaps between its poles, and has exactly one zero near each of ten nonreal points, so it has zeros off the real axis. New in this book.
- [The maximum M* of exponentials is not in the Bondesson class](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#max_of_exponentials_m_star_not_in_bondesson_class) (Corollary 8.5.14, page 274; proved): The maximum of independent exponential variables with 24 variables of each rate 2 pi n is not in the Bondesson class and so is not a GGC, because its Laplace transform has nonreal zeros. New in this book.
- [Open question on infinite divisibility of maxima of exponentials](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_infinite_divisibility_of_maxima_of_exponentials) (Question 8.5.15, page 275; open): Is every maximum of independent exponential variables infinitely divisible, and in particular is the maximum M* with 24 variables of each rate 2 pi n? New in this book.
- [Open question on real zeros of cosh kernels with exponential multipliers](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_real_zeros_of_cosh_kernel_with_exponential_multiplier) (Question 8.5.16, page 277; open): For which parameters does the Fourier transform of the kernel exp(-a cosh u) times an exponential multiplier have only real zeros, a form shared by the kernels of Ramanujan's Delta, chi12 and the conductor 11 curve? New in this book.
- [Pólya kernel of an imaginary quadratic field](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#polya_kernel_of_imaginary_quadratic_field) (Theorem 8.5.17, page 280; proved): The completed Dedekind zeta function of an imaginary quadratic field is the two sided Laplace transform of an even doubly exponentially decaying kernel, which is positive exactly when a one variable function is positive on a finite interval, in particular for the discriminants minus 3, minus 4, minus 7 and minus 8. New in this book.
- [Pólya kernel of an imaginary quadratic field takes negative values when 2 and 3 are inert](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#polya_kernel_takes_negative_values_when_two_and_three_inert) (Theorem 8.5.18, page 282; proved): For every negative fundamental discriminant d congruent to 5 modulo 24 the Pólya kernel of Q(sqrt d) takes negative values, by an explicit evaluation of a finite sum with a bounded tail, and there are infinitely many such d. New in this book.
- [Open question on the density of positive Pólya kernels](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_density_of_positive_polya_kernels_imaginary_quadratic) (Question 8.5.19, page 282; open): Does the proportion of imaginary quadratic fields with a positive Pólya kernel tend to a limit, is the limit positive, and is the kernel positive for infinitely many fields in which 2 and 3 split? New in this book.
- [Open question on positivity criteria for real quadratic fields](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_positivity_criterion_polya_kernel_real_quadratic) (Question 8.5.20, page 283; open): Is there a criterion for positivity of the Pólya kernel of the Dedekind zeta function of a real quadratic field or a field of higher degree that is as simple as the one for imaginary quadratic fields? New in this book.
- [Lévy form of the Dirichlet beta function at basepoints from one](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#levy_form_of_dirichlet_beta_function_from_basepoint_one) (Proposition 8.5.23, page 286; proved): The logarithm of the completed Dirichlet beta function at every basepoint alpha at least one has a Lévy form whose signed Lévy measure is an explicit positive gamma density plus prime power atoms of both signs. New in this book.
- [Thorin measure of the Dirichlet beta function from basepoint one](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#thorin_measure_of_dirichlet_beta_function_from_basepoint_one) (Proposition 8.5.24, page 288; proved): For every basepoint alpha at least one the reciprocal of the completed Dirichlet beta function is the Laplace transform of a GGC with a positive explicit Thorin density, and, by Lagarias's criterion, GRH for chi4 is equivalent to the positivity of that density at every alpha above one half. New in this book.
- [Termwise positivity thresholds for the Dirichlet beta function and chi12](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#termwise_positivity_thresholds_dirichlet_beta_and_chi12) (Proposition 8.5.25, page 289; proved): Bounding the prime weights by their absolute values gives a positive Thorin density exactly for basepoints above 2.2823106368 for the Dirichlet beta function and above 1.8348743295 for chi12, thresholds located by bisection with certified signs. New in this book.
- [No bound from the sizes of the prime weights beats the absolute values](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#no_bound_from_prime_weight_sizes_beats_absolute_values_kronecker) (Proposition 8.5.26, page 290; proved): By Kronecker's theorem no lower bound for the real part of L'/L of the Dirichlet beta function better than minus the sum of the absolute weights holds at all large heights, and the height from which the termwise bound works grows like e to the power 2/(alpha minus 1). New in this book.
- [Thorin density of the Dirichlet beta function as a difference over the Gaussian field](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#thorin_density_of_dirichlet_beta_as_difference_over_gaussian_field) (Proposition 8.5.27, page 291; proved): On every vertical line the Thorin density of the Dirichlet beta function is the difference of the Thorin densities of the Dedekind zeta function of Q(i) and of Riemann's xi function, and the canonical measures subtract in the same way. New in this book.
- [GRH for chi4 and domination of Thorin densities over Q(i)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#grh_chi4_iff_gaussian_field_thorin_density_dominates_xi) (Corollary 8.5.28, page 291; conditional on Part (iii) assumes the Riemann hypothesis for the Riemann zeta function; parts (i) and (ii) hold without any hypothesis): GRH for chi4 is equivalent to the Thorin density of the Dedekind zeta function of Q(i) dominating that of Riemann's xi at every basepoint, and for alpha at least one the GGC of Q(i) is the sum of independent GGCs for xi and for the Dirichlet beta function. New in this book.
- [Open question on a coupling construction over the Gaussian primes](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_coupling_construction_over_gaussian_primes) (Question 8.5.29, page 292; open): Is there a construction of the GGC attached to Q(i) from the Gaussian primes themselves that persists below the basepoint one? New in this book.
- [Thorin mass of the Dirichlet beta function as an argument](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#thorin_mass_of_dirichlet_beta_as_argument_of_completed_function) (Proposition 8.5.30, page 293; proved): On a vertical line the cumulative Thorin mass of the Dirichlet beta function is the argument of the completed function divided by pi, with an asymptotic expansion that becomes the zero counting formula at the centre and a limit that counts the zeros on the critical line. New in this book.
- [GRH for chi4 and monotonicity of the argument of the completed function](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#grh_chi4_iff_argument_of_completed_function_nondecreasing) (Corollary 8.5.31, page 294; proved): GRH for chi4 is equivalent to the argument of the completed Dirichlet beta function being nondecreasing on every line to the right of the centre, and without any hypothesis it can fall only in short windows around zeros off the line, none below height 2.5 times 10^7 by Platt's verification. New in this book.
- [The half kernel of the Dirichlet beta function is not a gamma mixture](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#half_kernel_of_dirichlet_beta_not_a_gamma_mixture) (Proposition 8.5.32, page 295; proved): The half kernel of the Dirichlet beta function is not a positive mixture of gamma densities of any shape, and the theta function eta(ix) cubed is not completely monotone. New in this book.
- [Open question on a reciprocal side representation from the eta product](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_reciprocal_side_representation_from_eta_product) (Question 8.5.33, page 296; open): Can the complete monotonicity of the reciprocal of the eta cube theta function, and of the reciprocal eta product for chi12, be turned into a positive representation on the reciprocal side in the spirit of Thorin? New in this book.
- [Laplace transform of Bessel hitting times with curvature](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#laplace_transform_of_bessel_hitting_times_with_curvature) (Proposition 8.7.6, page 306; proved): The hitting time of radius a by the radial Brownian motion on the three dimensional space form of curvature kappa has an explicit Laplace transform, is a GGC with equally spaced Thorin atoms shifted by minus kappa/2, and is an exponential tilt of the flat case. The flat case is classical (Ciesielski and Taylor 1962), and for kappa < 0 the process is the Bessel process of dimension three with drift (Salminen and Vallois 2007), the norm of a three dimensional Brownian motion with drift, where the formula also follows from the Cameron Martin formula; the formula for the whole family, its Thorin measure and its reading as an exponential tilt are the book's. New in this book.
- [Exact quantisation rule for the zeros of Pólya's Bessel function](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#exact_quantisation_rule_for_zeros_of_polya_bessel_function) (Proposition 8.7.8, page 309; proved): The positive zeros of nu maps to K_{i nu}(2 pi) are exactly the solutions of an explicit phase equation, so their counting function is the integer part of a smooth function with an explicit asymptotic expansion. New in this book.
- [Index side Thorin measure of Pólya's Bessel function](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#index_side_thorin_measure_of_polya_bessel_function) (Theorem 8.7.9, page 311; proved): For Pólya's Bessel function the reciprocal K_0(2 pi)/K_{sqrt u}(2 pi) is, without any hypothesis, the Laplace transform of the GGC whose Thorin atoms are the squares of the positive zeros of nu maps to K_{i nu}(2 pi). New in this book.
- [Clock of Pólya's Bessel function as a hitting time of an explicit diffusion](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#clock_of_polya_bessel_function_hitting_time_of_explicit_diffusion) (Theorem 8.7.10, page 313; proved): The index side clock of Pólya's Bessel function, the GGC with Thorin atoms at the squares of the positive zeros of nu maps to K_{i nu}(2 pi), is the clock of a hitting time of a level by an explicit diffusion, planar Brownian motion killed at rate one half and Doob transformed by K_0. New in this book.
- [Sine squared forms of the Bessel clock, the drifted clock and Pólya's clock](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#sine_squared_forms_of_bessel_clock_drifted_clock_and_polya_clock) (Proposition 8.7.13, page 316; proved): The Laplace exponents of the sum of two Bessel hitting times, of the drifted first passage time and of Pólya's clock have sine squared forms whose kernels are the classical Planck and Macdonald measures and, for Pólya's clock, a completely monotone wave trace of a selfadjoint operator. New in this book.
- [Klein Gordon criterion for real zeros](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#klein_gordon_criterion_for_real_zeros) (Theorem 8.7.14, page 317; proved): If an even positive kernel is the boundary value of a solution of a Klein Gordon equation with a real potential bounded below, with the stated decay and nonvanishing conditions, then every zero of its Fourier transform is real and its square is a Dirichlet eigenvalue. New in this book.
- [De Bruijn Newman constant of Pólya's function is finite](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#de_bruijn_newman_constant_of_polya_function_is_finite) (Proposition 8.7.15, page 318; proved): The Gaussian deformations of Pólya's Bessel function have only real zeros exactly from a finite time Lambda_P at most zero onward, by an argument of Newman, so its de Bruijn Newman constant is not minus infinity, contrary to a conjecture of the first author's earlier note. New in this book.
- [A property that survives Gaussian damping cannot imply real zeros](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#gaussian_damping_property_cannot_imply_real_zeros) (Proposition 8.7.16, page 322; proved): No property of even positive kernels that implies real zeros and survives a fixed Gaussian damping can hold for Riemann's kernel Phi, for Pólya's asymptote or for the Bessel kernel, which excludes a family of constructions with room to spare, using the theorems of Rodgers and Tao and of Newman. New in this book.
- [Open question on a diffusion for the clock of the Riemann xi function](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_diffusion_for_clock_of_riemann_xi_function) (Question 8.7.17, page 323; open): Is there, without assuming RH, a diffusion on a half line with an entrance boundary whose hitting time of a level has the Laplace transform of the clock of Riemann's xi function scaled by four? New in this book.
- [Open question on a Klein Gordon extension of Pólya's kernel](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_klein_gordon_extension_of_polya_kernel) (Question 8.7.18, page 324; open): Does the kernel of Riemann's xi function, rescaled, admit a Klein Gordon extension with a real potential asymptotic to e^{2x}, which would imply RH? New in this book.
- [Open question on the de Bruijn Newman constants of Pólya's functions](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_de_bruijn_newman_constants_of_polya_functions) (Question 8.7.19, page 324; open): What are the de Bruijn Newman constants of Pólya's Bessel function and of his function Xi star, at what height do the first nonreal zeros appear, and do they appear through collisions of real zeros? New in this book.
- [Open question on a family joining the two clocks](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_family_joining_the_two_clocks) (Question 8.7.20, page 324; open): Is there a one parameter family of laws joining the drifted first passage time and the sum of two Bessel hitting times, each member with a reciprocal symmetry encoding a functional equation, along which the index side Thorin measure can be followed? New in this book.

#### Key terms

Riemann Hypothesis, Riemann xi function, clock variable, generalized gamma convolution, generalised gamma convolution, GGC, Thorin measure, Pólya density, Polya density, hitting time, first passage time, Keiper Li coefficients, Li criterion, de Bruijn Newman constant, Lehmer pair, Laguerre inequality, Hankel matrix, free convolution, semicircle law, Dedekind eta function, nonnegative deconvolution, backward heat flow, collision of zeros, inverse first passage problem, maximum of independent exponential variables, Bondesson class.

chapters.title: The basepoint one
chapters.summary:
This chapter works out the shifted clock $T_\alpha$ of the reciprocal Xi function at the basepoint $\alpha=1$, the random variable with Laplace transform $\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+\sqrt u)$ for the completed Riemann zeta function $\xi$. It asks what the Thorin measure and the law of $T_1$ are, whether the Thorin density comes from the sine squared lemma, and whether $T_1$ is a hitting time to which Kent's theorem applies. The Thorin measure of this generalized gamma convolution (GGC) is the Poisson smoothing of the zeros by Cauchy kernels, positive with no hypothesis because no zero lies on $\operatorname{Re}s=1$ (the threshold theorem of Polson 2026 at $\alpha=1$). The chapter derives a Lévy form of $\log\xi(1+s)$, proves with no hypothesis (using ball arithmetic and explicit zero counts) that the Thorin density is smallest at the origin, giving an independent positive stable one half summand, and shows that this minimum at every height on every line with real part between one half and one is equivalent to the Riemann Hypothesis (RH). It certifies the heat trace from the primes and represents every shifted clock $T_\alpha$ with $\alpha>\frac12$ as a subordinated hitting time of sticky Brownian motion.

#### From the literature

- $2\xi(s)$ as the Mellin transform of a sum of two Bessel hitting times (Williams 1990; Biane, Pitman and Yor 2001)
- generalized gamma convolutions (Thorin 1977; Bondesson 1992); Kent's theorem on diffusion hitting times, with Krein's inverse spectral theory (Kent 1980; Dym and McKean 1976)
- the complete Riemann zeta distribution (Nakamura 2015); Lagarias's positivity criterion for RH (Lagarias 1999)
- sticky Brownian motion (Itô and McKean 1965); inverse first passage (Anulova 1980; Ekström and Janson 2016)
- verification of RH to $3\times10^{12}$ (Platt and Trudgian 2021) and of GRH for the characters modulo 4 and 12 (Platt 2016); explicit zero counts (Hasanalizade, Shen and Wong 2022; Bennett, Martin, O'Bryant and Rechnitzer 2021) and bounds for $\psi(y)-y$ (Büthe 2018; Broadbent, Kadiri, Lumley, Ng and Wilk 2021; Johnston and Yang 2023)

#### New results

- [Levy density of the Barnes beta law as a Gaussian mixture whose mixing law has Mellin transform xi(2q+2) (after Ostrovsky)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#ostrovsky_barnes_beta_laws_as_gaussian_mixture_with_mellin_transform_xi) (Remark 9.1.1, page 331; computed): The companion $C_2$ of $S_2$ has $\mathbb{E}e^{-uC_2}=\operatorname{sech}^2\sqrt{2u}$ and Mellin transform $\frac{2^{2q+2}-1}{q+1}(\frac2\pi)^{q+1}\xi(2q+2)$, checked numerically at four points, so the Lévy density of the Barnes beta law (Ostrovsky) is a Gaussian mixture whose mixing law has Mellin transform $\xi(2q+2)$. New in this book.
- [Compensated sine squared formula at the basepoint one](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#compensated_sine_squared_formula_basepoint_one) (Proposition 9.1.3, page 333; proved): At the basepoint one the Thorin density equals an explicit digamma expression plus a compensated sine squared sum over the primes, and the limit exists by the prime number theorem. New in this book.
- [De la Vallée Poussin's zero free region from the Thorin density: the two frequency inequality 4Z(y)+Z(2y) at most 8 c_alpha](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#de_la_vallee_poussin_inequality_in_thorin_form_from_sine_squared_lemma) (Proposition 9.1.4, page 334; proved): The prime part $Z(\alpha,y)$ of the Thorin density of $\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+\sqrt u)$ satisfies $0\le Z\le2c_\alpha$ and $4Z(\alpha,y)+Z(\alpha,2y)\le8c_\alpha$, and a zero $\beta_0+i\gamma_0$ then satisfies $1-\beta_0\ge c/\log\gamma_0$ for large $\gamma_0$, de la Vallée Poussin's classical zero free region read through the Thorin density. New in this book.
- [Thorin property of the reciprocal Xi function for basepoint at least 5.4962 from the sine squared lemma alone, with no information on the zeros](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#reciprocal_xi_is_ggc_for_basepoint_at_least_5_4962_by_sine_squared_lemma_alone) (Proposition 9.1.5, page 335; proved): For $\alpha\ge\alpha_0=5.4962215670\ldots$, the root of an explicit increasing function $D$, the function $u\mapsto\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+\sqrt u)$ is the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution, proved from the sine squared lemma alone without any information on the zeros. New in this book.
- [Thorin condition with the prime part dropped: the sign of m(alpha) changes at alpha_1 = 3.5747764, computed in floating point and not proved on [alpha_1, alpha_0)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#floating_point_thorin_condition_below_alpha_0_with_threshold_alpha_1_3_5748) (Remark 9.1.6, page 335; computed): Dropping the prime part $Z\ge0$ from the Thorin density leaves $m(\alpha)=\min_y\{P+A\}+D(\alpha)$, which changes sign at $\alpha_1=3.5747764\ldots$, below $\alpha_0=5.4962$; this is computed in floating point at sampled points, not proved on $[\alpha_1,\alpha_0)$, and no bound on the primes uniform in $y$ goes below $\alpha_1$ because $\inf_yZ(\alpha,y)=0$. New in this book.
- [Unconditional GGC property of the reciprocal Xi function in the fourth root variable, compensated by the first power sum, with explicit Thorin density from the heat trace](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#heat_trace_weighted_reciprocal_xi_in_fourth_root_is_ggc_with_absolutely_continuous_thorin_measure) (Proposition 9.1.7, page 336; proved): Unconditionally, the function $\Psi(s)=\frac{\xi(\frac12+s^{1/4})}{\xi(\frac12)}e^{-p_1\sqrt s}$ is the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution whose Thorin measure has an explicit density built from the heat trace $W$, and under RH it equals the Weierstrass product $\prod_{\gamma>0}(1+\sqrt s/\gamma^2)e^{-\sqrt s/\gamma^2}$. New in this book.
- [The square root is forced: xi(alpha)/xi(alpha+q) is not the Laplace transform of a positive measure in q for any alpha](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#reciprocal_xi_not_laplace_transform_of_positive_measure_in_q_so_clock_variable_is_u_equals_q_squared) (Remark 9.1.8, page 337; proved): For every real $\alpha$, $q\mapsto\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+q)$ is not $\int e^{-qt}\mu(dt)$ for a positive measure $\mu\ne0$ on any half plane, because it decays faster than $e^{-qT}$ for every $T$; so the clock starts at the variable $u=q^2$. New in this book.
- [Barnes beta law of Ostrovsky with Lévy density sech squared over 4t: Mellin transform by Barnes G, GGC form with an explicit Thorin density, and zeros of the Mellin transform of that density](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#barnes_beta_law_with_levy_density_sech_squared_has_thorin_density_from_zeta_at_2w) (Proposition 9.1.9, page 337; proved): For the Barnes beta law $\mathfrak b=e^{-Y_{\mathfrak b}}$ of Ostrovsky (Lévy density $\operatorname{sech}^2(t/4)/4t$), $\mathbb{E}\mathfrak b^q$ is a ratio of Barnes $G$ functions, $\mathbb{E}\mathfrak b^{\sqrt s}e^{\sqrt s}$ is the reciprocal of a GGC transform with Thorin density $\frac1{2\pi\sqrt z}-\frac1{\sinh2\pi\sqrt z}>0$, and the Mellin transform of that density is $-4(2\pi)^{-2w}(1-2^{-2w})\Gamma(2w)\zeta(2w)$. New in this book.
- [Lévy form of the completed zeta function at the basepoint one](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#levy_form_of_xi_at_basepoint_one) (Proposition 9.1.10, page 338; proved): The logarithm of $\xi(1+s)/\xi(1)$ has an explicit Lévy form whose drift is the sum of the reciprocals of the zeros and whose signed Lévy measure consists of a gamma density, a pole term and prime atoms, the compensated integral converging by the prime number theorem. New in this book.
- [Minimum of the Thorin density at the origin and stable summand at the basepoint one](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#thorin_density_minimum_at_origin_basepoint_one) (Proposition 9.1.11, page 340; proved): With no hypothesis on the zeros, certified with the first 1800 zeros in ball arithmetic and explicit zero counts above height 2000, the Thorin density of the shifted clock at the basepoint one is smallest only at the origin, so the clock is the sum of an independent positive stable one half variable and a generalized gamma convolution. New in this book.
- [Minimum at the origin and stable summand at every basepoint from one](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#thorin_density_minimum_at_origin_every_basepoint_from_one) (Proposition 9.1.12, page 343; proved): The same minimum at the origin and the same splitting into a positive stable one half summand and a generalized gamma convolution hold at every basepoint at or above one, certified with ball arithmetic and explicit zero counts above height 2000. New in this book.
- [Lévy form below the basepoint one and zero free half planes](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#levy_form_below_basepoint_one_and_zero_free_half_plane) (Proposition 9.1.13, page 345; proved): Below the basepoint one the Lévy form of $\xi$ converges and gives a positive Thorin density when all zeros lie to the left of the basepoint, and conversely its validity at a basepoint forces a zero free half plane to the right of it. New in this book.
- [Comparison of the Thorin density across vertical lines](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#thorin_density_ratio_comparison_across_vertical_lines) (Theorem 9.1.15, page 349; proved): The ratio of the real part of the logarithmic derivative of a completed function on a vertical line to the distance of that line from the critical line is nonincreasing as the line moves right, under a hypothesis on the zeros to the right of the critical line that holds under RH, for lines at distance at least $1/\sqrt2$ from the critical line, and below the verified height. New in this book.
- [Explicit lower bound of the Thorin density by comparison with the Euler product](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#explicit_lower_bound_of_thorin_density_by_comparison_with_euler_product) (Corollary 9.1.16, page 349; proved): On a line to the right of one the Euler product and the digamma function give an explicit lower bound for the real part of the logarithmic derivative of a completed zeta or Dirichlet L function, and under the comparison hypothesis the bound, multiplied by the ratio of the distances of the lines from the critical line, holds on every line to the left and is of order a positive multiple of the logarithm of the height. New in this book.
- [Minimum of the Thorin density at the origin and its equivalence with RH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#thorin_density_minimum_at_origin_below_one_equivalent_to_rh) (Theorem 9.1.18, page 350; proved): RH, respectively GRH for the Dirichlet L function of the character modulo 4 or modulo 12, is equivalent to the Thorin density of the corresponding completed function on every line with real part between one half and one being smallest at the origin and only there, a property certified in ball arithmetic with no hypothesis up to the verified height. New in this book.
- [Certified positivity of the heat trace at the basepoint one](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#heat_trace_at_basepoint_one_positive_certified_from_primes) (Proposition 9.1.24, page 358; proved): The heat trace of the shifted clock at the basepoint one is certified positive at every time, with an explicit lower bound, from the primes up to ten million and published explicit bounds for Chebyshev's error, in ball arithmetic. New in this book.
- [No Brownian first passage to a random level at the basepoint one](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#no_brownian_first_passage_to_random_level_at_basepoint_one) (Proposition 9.2.1, page 359; proved): The shifted clock at the basepoint one is not the first passage time of a Brownian motion with drift to a random level independent of the motion. New in this book.
- [Subordination of the tilted centre clock at the basepoint one](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#basepoint_one_clock_subordination_of_tilted_centre_clock) (Theorem 9.2.2, page 360; proved): The shifted clock at the basepoint one is the exponentially tilted centre clock run through the inverse local time of a sticky Brownian motion, equivalently the tilted clock plus a Brownian first passage time to a level proportional to it. New in this book.
- [Kent string hitting time of the shifted clock at the basepoint one under RH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#basepoint_one_clock_kent_string_hitting_time_under_rh) (Corollary 9.2.3, page 361; conditional on the Riemann Hypothesis (every nontrivial zero of the Riemann zeta function has real part one half) and the simplicity of every nontrivial zero): Assuming RH and simple zeros, the tilted centre clock is a Kent hitting time of a Krein string with spectrum the squared moduli of the zeros, and the shifted clock at the basepoint one is the first hitting time of a level by this string diffusion run on the local time of a sticky Brownian motion. New in this book.
- [Subordination of the centre clock at every basepoint above the centre](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#shifted_clock_subordination_every_basepoint_above_centre) (Theorem 9.2.5, page 365; proved): For every basepoint above the centre the shifted clock exists with no hypothesis on the zeros and is a Brownian hitting time built from the tilted centre clock, with a stable one half tail, and, by the threshold theorem of Polson 2026, it is a generalized gamma convolution exactly when no zero lies to the right of the basepoint. New in this book.
- [Lévy measure and self decomposability of the shifted clock](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#shifted_clock_levy_measure_and_self_decomposability) (Corollary 9.2.6, page 366; proved): The shifted clock at every basepoint above the centre is infinitely divisible and self decomposable, with an explicit Lévy measure obtained from that of the centre clock. New in this book.

#### Key terms

basepoint one, shifted clock, reciprocal Xi function, completed zeta function, Thorin measure, Thorin density, generalized gamma convolution, generalised gamma convolution, GGC, Lévy form, Levy form, sine squared lemma, Cauchy kernel, positive stable law, subordination, sticky Brownian motion, Kent's theorem, hitting time, first passage time, Wald's identity, heat trace, zero free half plane, Riemann Hypothesis, GRH

chapters.title: The critical strip and Riesz's criterion
chapters.summary:
This chapter asks how much of the unconditional structure of the reciprocal Xi function at the basepoint one survives inside the critical strip of the Riemann zeta function, and what it says about Riesz's criterion for the Riemann Hypothesis (RH). Its objects are the basepoint clocks $T_\alpha$, with Laplace transform $\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+\sqrt u)$, and their Thorin measures. On the real axis the reciprocal of $\xi$ is the characteristic function of an infinitely divisible normal scale mixture, an extended generalised gamma convolution (EGGC) exactly when no zero lies to the right of the basepoint. RH is equivalent to complete monotonicity of the Poisson trace of the zeros, and zero free half planes become completeness of translates of the Pólya kernel. Riesz's criterion becomes the statement that every $T_\alpha$ with $\alpha>\frac12$ is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC), and $1/\zeta(2k)$ is a Laplace transform value of the clocks. The squarefree integers, with Dirichlet series $\zeta(s)/\zeta(2s)$, give criteria for RH from exponentially and Gamma(2) smoothed counts, a Mertens function representation and a threshold at Gamma shape two. The chapter proves no new zero free region.

#### From the literature

- Thorin representation of generalised gamma convolutions (Thorin 1977, 1978; Bondesson 1992).
- Wiener's closure theorem (Wiener 1932; Kac 1965; Korevaar 1965); Salem's equivalent of RH (Salem 1953).
- Riesz's criterion (Riesz 1916) and its companion (Hardy and Littlewood 1916); Lagarias's positivity criterion (Lagarias 1999); the Nyman Beurling criterion (Nyman 1950; Beurling 1955; Báez Duarte 2003).
- Euler's formulae for $\zeta(2n)$ from Cauchy variables (Bourgade, Fujita and Yor 2007).
- RH verified to height $3\times10^{12}$ (Platt and Trudgian 2021).
- Squarefree integers: Math StackExchange question 2063166 (2016), the conditional exponent 7/22 (Baker and Pintz 1985), Lazarević's inequality (Lazarević 1966), integer and fractional parts (Steutel and Thiemann 1989), Ingham's method (1942); a mean square criterion the chapter calls presumably folklore.

#### New results

New in the book; the squarefree material and the Poisson trace conditions are from unpublished notes of Nicholas Polson.

- [Reciprocal Xi function on the real axis as a normal scale mixture](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#reciprocal_xi_real_axis_normal_scale_mixture) (Proposition 10.1.1, page 370; proved): For every basepoint $\alpha\ge\frac12$, $\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+|u|)$ is the characteristic function of a symmetric, unimodal, infinitely divisible law with no hypothesis on the zeros, which has a Cauchy tail when $\alpha>\frac12$. New in this book.
- [Thorin form of the reciprocal Xi function and the EGGC criterion](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#reciprocal_xi_thorin_form_and_eggc_criterion) (Theorem 10.1.2, page 372; proved): When every zero of $\zeta$ has real part less than the basepoint $\alpha>\frac12$ (always for $\alpha\ge1$), the characteristic function $\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+|u|)$ has an explicit Thorin form with the positive density $\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(\alpha+i\theta)/\pi$, and for $\frac12<\alpha<1$ the law is an extended generalised gamma convolution exactly when there is no zero to the right of $\alpha$. New in this book.
- [EGGC property of the reciprocal Xi law across the critical strip](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#eggc_property_across_the_critical_strip) (Theorem 10.1.3, page 374; proved): For $\frac12<\alpha<1$ the law $Y_\alpha$ is an extended generalised gamma convolution exactly when $\zeta$ has no zeros with real part above $\alpha$, and with no hypothesis its characteristic function is that of an extended generalised gamma convolution times a remainder $\mathcal{E}_{\alpha,T_0}(u)$ with $|\log\mathcal{E}_{\alpha,T_0}(u)|\le4(|u|+u^2)\log T_0/T_0$, where $T_0\ge2$ is a height up to which all zeros lie on the critical line. New in this book.
- [Complete monotonicity of the Poisson trace is equivalent to RH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#poisson_trace_completely_monotone_iff_rh) (Corollary 10.1.4, page 377; proved): RH holds exactly when the Poisson trace $\sum_ke^{-y\sqrt{a_k}}$ of the zeros is completely monotone (the same equivalence for the heat trace was shown earlier by Polson 2026), and for $\alpha\ge1$ the corresponding trace is completely monotone with no hypothesis and decays like $b_\alpha/(\pi y)$. New in this book.
- [Unconditional range of the complete monotonicity conditions of the Poisson trace](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#poisson_trace_derivative_conditions_hold_below_verified_height) (Theorem 10.1.6, page 379; proved): If all zeros up to height $H$ lie on the critical line, the derivative conditions $(-1)^nK^{(n)}(y)>0$ of the Poisson trace $K$ hold at every $0<y<\pi$ and every order $n<H(\pi-y)$; with $H=3\times10^{12}$ this covers all orders below $4.24\times10^{11}$ for $y\le3$. New in this book.
- [Quasi Riemann hypothesis version of the range of the Poisson trace conditions: y below 4 pi over 3 and n below 4 pi T_0 over 3 under (Q_{7/8})](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#rectangle_theorem_for_poisson_trace_remains_valid_under_quasi_rh_at_seven_eighths_with_range_four_pi_over_three) (Remark 10.1.7, page 379; conditional on The quasi Riemann hypothesis $(\mathrm Q_{7/8})$ of the book, which rests on the unrefereed half plane of OpenAI (2026); the variant with Liu's claimed half plane $\operatorname{Re}s>0.874957$ rests on an unrefereed claim as well): The rectangle uses that $\varphi_k$ and $\delta_k$ have the same sign; under $(\mathrm Q_{7/8})$, $\Delta=\frac38$ and the range of the Poisson trace theorem becomes $0<y<\frac{4\pi}3$ and $n<\frac{4\pi}3T_0=1.26\times10^{13}$; Liu's claimed half plane would give $y<4.1893$. New in this book.
- [Positive definite and bounded forms of the Poisson trace criterion for RH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#poisson_trace_positive_definite_and_bounded_forms_of_rh) (Proposition 10.1.8, page 380; proved): RH is equivalent to positive definiteness of $y\mapsto K_{1/2}(x+iy)$ for every $x>0$, and to boundedness of $y\mapsto K_{1/2}(x+iy)$ on $[0,\infty)$ for some $x>0$, where $K_{1/2}$ is the Poisson trace of the zeros. New in this book.
- [Small y asymptotics of the Poisson trace and Pólya's trace](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#poisson_trace_versus_polya_trace_small_y_asymptotics) (Proposition 10.1.9, page 382; proved): As $y\to0+$ the Poisson trace of the zeros of $\zeta$ and the trace of the zeros of Pólya's Bessel function $K_{i\theta/2}(2\pi)$ have the same main term and their difference tends to $\frac98$, with a refined second term under RH. New in this book.
- [Explicit obstruction and approximation cost for translates of the tilted Pólya kernel](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#tilted_polya_kernel_translates_obstruction_and_approximation_cost) (Proposition 10.1.10, page 384; proved): For translates of the tilted Pólya kernel $\Phi_\alpha$ the book proves an explicit obstruction at the centre (no finite combination approximates $g\in L^1(\mathbb{R})$ with $L^1$ error below $\sup_\gamma|\hat g(\gamma)|$, over the ordinates $\gamma$ of the zeros on the critical line) and, where the translates are dense, an explicit cost of approximation (a combination within $\delta$ of $g$ has coefficient sum at least $(|\hat g(\gamma)|-\delta)/|\xi(\alpha+i\gamma)|$ for every ordinate $\gamma$ of a zero of $\zeta$); the density criteria (dense exactly when $\zeta$ has no zeros on the line $\operatorname{Re}s=\alpha$; dense for every $\alpha>\frac12$ exactly when RH holds) restate Wiener's closure theorem (Wiener 1932). New in this book.
- [Pólya kernel analogue of Salem's criterion](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#polya_kernel_analogue_of_salem_criterion) (Corollary 10.1.11, page 386; proved): RH holds if and only if, for every $\frac12<\alpha<1$, the convolution equation with the tilted Pólya kernel $\Phi_\alpha$ has no bounded nonzero solution; at the centre $\cos(\gamma y)$ solves it for every ordinate $\gamma$ of a zero on the critical line. New in this book.
- [Twisted Riesz function and the basepoint form of Riesz's criterion](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#twisted_riesz_function_and_basepoint_riesz_criterion) (Proposition 10.2.1, page 390; proved): Twisting Riesz's function by $(x/n^2)^{ih}$ changes the Gamma factor of its Mellin transform to $\Gamma(1-s+ih)/\zeta(2s)$ and keeps the criterion: $\zeta$ has no zeros with real part above $\alpha$ exactly when $R_h(x)=O(x^{\alpha/2+\delta})$ for every $\delta>0$. New in this book.
- [The Riesz function as an average over the centre clock](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#riesz_function_as_centre_clock_average) (Proposition 10.2.4, page 392; proved): With no hypothesis, Riesz's function is minus the expectation of an alternating series in the centre clock whose terms decay like $e^{-4k^2T}$ instead of $1/(k-1)!$. New in this book.
- [Riesz coefficients as values of GGC Laplace transforms](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#riesz_coefficients_as_ggc_laplace_values) (Proposition 10.2.5, page 393; proved): For $\alpha\in[\frac12,1]$, $1/\zeta(2k)$ is an explicit multiple of the Laplace transform of the basepoint clock $T_\alpha$ at $(2k-\alpha)^2$, in particular of the centre clock at $\alpha=\frac12$ and of the basepoint one clock at $\alpha=1$, and at $\alpha=1$ it is $\kappa_k$ times the exponential of minus a Thorin integral, with no hypothesis on the zeros. New in this book.
- [GGC form of Riesz's criterion](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#riesz_criterion_as_ggc_property_of_basepoint_clocks) (Theorem 10.2.7, page 395; proved): Riesz's growth condition at exponent $\alpha/2$ is equivalent to each clock $T_{\alpha'}$ with $\alpha'>\alpha$ being a generalised gamma convolution, to positivity of $\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)$ on the lines to the right of $\alpha$, and to convergence of a compensated sine squared sum over the primes; for $\alpha=\frac12$, RH holds exactly when every $T_\alpha$ with $\alpha>\frac12$ is a GGC. New in this book.
- [Closed form constant of the squarefree reciprocal sum over number fields](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#squarefree_reciprocal_sum_closed_form_constant) (Proposition 10.3.1, page 403; proved): Over a number field $K$ of degree $n\ge2$ the sum of $\mu(\mathfrak a)^2/N(\mathfrak a)$ over the integral ideals of norm at most $x$ equals $\frac{c_K}{\zeta_K(2)}(\log x+C_K)+O(x^{-1/n}\log x)$ with the explicit constant $C_K=\gamma_K-2\zeta_K'(2)/\zeta_K(2)$, $\gamma_K$ the Euler Kronecker constant of $K$. New in this book.
- [Squarefree Dirichlet series as a gamma factor times a ratio of Pólya moment generating functions](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#squarefree_dirichlet_series_as_gamma_factor_times_polya_ratio) (Proposition 10.3.3, page 405; proved): The squarefree Dirichlet series $\zeta(s)/\zeta(2s)$ equals an explicit gamma factor times $\mathbb{E}\,e^{(s-1/2)X}/\mathbb{E}\,e^{(2s-1/2)X}$ for the Pólya variable $X$, which continues the series to every $s$ with $\xi(2s)\ne0$. New in this book.
- [Squarefree constant as a combination of two tilted Pólya means](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#squarefree_constant_as_difference_of_tilted_polya_means) (Theorem 10.3.5, page 405; proved): The constant $C$ of the squarefree reciprocal sum is an elementary part plus $b_1-2b_2$, a combination of the means of the Pólya variable tilted at the basepoints one and two, which is an absolutely convergent sum over the zeros with no hypothesis. New in this book.
- [Dedekind zeta clock is a GGC if and only if RH holds for the field](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#dedekind_clock_is_ggc_iff_rh_for_dedekind_zeta) (Proposition 10.3.6, page 407; proved): For a number field $K$ with $\zeta_K(\frac12)\ne0$, the reciprocal of the normalised completed Dedekind function is the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution exactly when all nontrivial zeros of $\zeta_K$ lie on the critical line, with Thorin measure the sum of point masses at the squared ordinates; this is the number field form of the rigidity theorem of Polson 2026. New in this book.
- [Squarefree constant of a number field through the zeros of its Dedekind zeta function](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#squarefree_constant_of_a_number_field_through_zeros) (Theorem 10.3.7, page 407; proved): For a number field $K$ the constant $C_K$ is an explicit elementary term $A_K$ plus an absolutely convergent sum over the zeros of its Dedekind zeta function, and under the Riemann Hypothesis for $\zeta_K$ that sum is a combination of two Stieltjes transform values of the Thorin measure. New in this book.
- [Exponentially and Gamma(2) smoothed squarefree counts are equivalent to RH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#smoothed_squarefree_counts_equivalent_to_rh) (Theorem 10.3.9, page 410; proved): RH holds if and only if the squarefree count smoothed by an exponential law, or by a Gamma(2) law, with mean $x$ equals $6x/\pi^2+O(x^{1/4+\varepsilon})$ for every $\varepsilon>0$, and under RH with simple zeros an explicit formula with exponentially damped terms at the zeros holds. New in this book.
- [Lower bound for the squarefree error of the order of the fourth root of x](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#squarefree_error_lower_bound_order_fourth_root_of_x) (Corollary 10.3.11, page 413; proved): With no hypothesis the squarefree error $\Delta(x)$ satisfies $\limsup\Delta(x)/x^{1/4}\ge0.1004$ and $\liminf\Delta(x)/x^{1/4}\le-0.1004$, so the order $x^{1/4}$ cannot be lowered, and the Gamma(2) smoothed error has the same property with constant $9.94\times10^{-5}$. New in this book.
- [Squarefree count at a Gamma(n) random point under RH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#squarefree_gamma_n_smoothing_bound_under_rh) (Proposition 10.3.12, page 414; conditional on the Riemann Hypothesis): Under RH, the expected squarefree count at a Gamma($n$) random point of mean $x$ is $6x/\pi^2+O(x^{1/4+\varepsilon}n^{1/8+\varepsilon})$, uniformly in $n\ge1$. New in this book.
- [Gamma(2) smoothed squarefree error as a positive average of the Mertens function](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#gamma2_smoothed_squarefree_error_as_mertens_average) (Theorem 10.3.15, page 416; proved): The squarefree count smoothed by a Gamma(2) law of mean $x$ equals $6x/\pi^2$ minus half the expected Mertens function at the random point $\sqrt{x\mathcal{V}_2/2}$, where the density $f_2$ of $\mathcal{V}_2$ is explicit and positive by Lazarević's inequality. New in this book.
- [Gamma smoothing threshold, shape two](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#gamma_smoothing_threshold_shape_two) (Theorem 10.3.18, page 418; proved): The signed density that mixes the Mertens function in the Gamma($\nu$) smoothed squarefree error is nonnegative exactly for the shapes $\nu\in(0,2]$, the obstruction above two being the trivial zero of $\zeta$ at $-2$. New in this book.
- [Pointwise bound for the squarefree error under RH (open)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#squarefree_error_pointwise_bound_under_rh_open) (Question 10.3.19, page 420; open): The book asks for a proof, under RH, that the squarefree count has error $O(x^{1/4+\varepsilon})$, and records forms equivalent to it or sufficient for it. New in this book.
- [Sharpening the lower bound constant for the squarefree error (open)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#squarefree_error_fejer_constant_and_unboundedness_open) (Question 10.3.20, page 420; open): The book asks whether a Fejér kernel over many zeros improves the constant $0.1004$ in the lower bound for the squarefree error, and whether $\limsup|\Delta(x)|/x^{1/4}$ is infinite. New in this book.

#### Key terms

Riesz criterion, Riemann hypothesis, critical strip, reciprocal Xi function, basepoint clock, Thorin measure, generalised gamma convolution, generalized gamma convolution, GGC, extended generalised gamma convolution, EGGC, normal scale mixture, Poisson trace, complete monotonicity, Wiener closure theorem, Salem criterion, Pólya kernel, Möbius function, squarefree integers, square free numbers, Mertens function, Gamma smoothing, Dedekind zeta function, Nyman Beurling criterion

chapters.title: Infinite divisibility, the eta analogue and almost generalised gamma convolutions
chapters.summary:
What can be said about the Thorin measure of the reciprocal Xi function without a zero free half plane? The centre clock is self decomposable and unimodal with no hypothesis, and the tilted Pólya variable is quasi infinitely divisible above the basepoint one and not at it. The Upsilon transform and the Bercovici Pata bijection give the clock a free counterpart, and RH holds exactly when the clock is the Upsilon image of an infinitely divisible law. A Wiener gamma integral and a Riemann Ornstein Uhlenbeck process realise the laws as processes. A Dedekind eta analogue treats the Dirichlet L function of the real character modulo 12, whose completed function has no pole. The almost GGC theorem uses zero density estimates to show, with no hypothesis, that every shifted clock is a generalized gamma convolution up to a defect carried by the zeros to its right, whose Cauchy kernels carry a vanishing fraction of the mass of the others, with a power saving; the verification of RH to height $3\times10^{12}$ bounds the defect explicitly. The last section treats Pakes's Lambert law, Urbanik's classes ($L_2$ but not $L_3$) and a criticality filter.

#### From the literature

Self decomposable laws and GGCs (Sato 1999; Bondesson 1992), driving subordinators (Wolfe 1982; Jurek and Vervaat 1983), unimodality (Yamazato 1978), subexponential tails (Embrechts, Goldie and Veraverbeke 1979); quasi infinite divisibility (Lindner, Pan and Sato 2018), proved above the basepoint one by Nakamura (2015); Bessel hitting times (Williams 1990; Biane, Pitman and Yor 2001); Bercovici Pata bijection (Bercovici and Pata 1999), free regular laws (Arizmendi, Hasebe and Sakuma 2013), free self decomposability (Barndorff-Nielsen and Thorbjørnsen 2002), its unimodality (Hasebe and Thorbjørnsen 2016), Upsilon transform (Barndorff-Nielsen and Thorbjørnsen 2004; Barndorff-Nielsen, Maejima and Sato 2006), finite free convolution (Marcus, Spielman and Srivastava 2022); zero density estimates (Ingham 1940; Huxley 1972; Guth and Maynard 2026); verification of RH to $3\times10^{12}$ (Platt and Trudgian 2021); Steutel's conjecture on Gamma(2) scale mixtures (Kristiansen 1994); size biasing theorem (Steutel 1973); nonnegativity of the de Bruijn Newman constant (Rodgers and Tao 2020); the Lambert law as a GGC (Pakes 2011; Kalugin, Jeffrey and Corless 2012) and ladders of self decomposable laws (Pakes 2026); Urbanik's classes (Urbanik 1973).

#### New results

- [Background driving subordinator of the centre clock](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#centre_clock_background_driving_subordinator) (Proposition 11.1.1, page 422; proved): With no hypothesis the centre clock is the integral of $e^{-t}$ against a subordinator whose Lévy density is minus the derivative of the heat trace of the zeros, and RH holds if and only if that density is completely monotone. New in this book.
- [Unimodality of the centre clock and the shifted clocks](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#centre_clock_and_shifted_clocks_unimodal) (Corollary 11.1.2, page 423; proved): The centre clock and every shifted clock with basepoint above one half have unimodal laws, with no hypothesis. New in this book.
- [The tilted Pólya variable at the basepoint one is not quasi infinitely divisible](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#polya_tilt_basepoint_one_not_quasi_infinitely_divisible) (Proposition 11.1.3, page 426; proved): The tilted Pólya variable at the basepoint one, with moment generating function $\xi(1+s)/\xi(1)$, is not quasi infinitely divisible, hence not infinitely divisible. New in this book.
- [Thorin Bernstein form of the shifted clock criterion](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#thorin_bernstein_criterion_for_shifted_clock_exponent) (Proposition 11.1.4, page 429; proved): The Laplace exponent of the shifted clock is a Thorin Bernstein function with no hypothesis when the basepoint is at least one, and for basepoints between one half and one exactly when zeta has no zero to the right of the basepoint, while the exponent of the centre clock is one if and only if RH holds. New in this book.
- [Upsilon image and free counterpart of the centre clock](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#upsilon_image_and_free_counterpart_of_centre_clock) (Theorem 11.2.3, page 440; proved): With no hypothesis the Upsilon image of the centre clock is a generalised gamma convolution with an explicit Thorin measure and its Bercovici Pata counterpart is a freely self decomposable unimodal law carried by a half line $[c,\infty)$ with $c>0$, and RH holds if and only if the clock is itself the Upsilon image of an infinitely divisible law. New in this book.
- [RH holds if and only if a freely infinitely divisible law nu_xi with free cumulant transform log xi(1/2)/xi(1/2+sqrt(-z)) exists](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#rh_equivalent_to_existence_of_freely_infinitely_divisible_law_with_cumulant_transform_log_xi_ratio) (Proposition 11.2.4, page 442; proved): RH holds exactly when the function $\mathcal{C}_\xi(z)=\log\{\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt{-z})\}$ is the free cumulant transform of a freely infinitely divisible probability measure, which under RH is $\Lambda_{\rm BP}(\mu_0)$, with compact support, free cumulants $m_{n-1}/n$ and free Lévy measure $N(y^{-1/2})dy/y$. New in this book.
