chapters.title: Yoshida's Hermitian forms, Weil positivity and the Thorin programme
chapters.summary:
Can Yoshida's Hermitian form of Weil's explicit formula on a window be read inside the Thorin programme for the Riemann Hypothesis (RH), and does it give a path to RH? The heat trace of the zeros and every rung $T_k=(-1)^kW^{(k)}$ of its ladder are diagonal values of the form on Hermite Gaussian vectors, and if RH fails every rung beyond a finite order fails and RH is positivity of the odd rungs. The tent coefficient is the sine squared lemma summed over the zeros, and Yoshida's matrix is, up to signs, a Löwner matrix of an odd meromorphic function, a Pick function exactly when RH holds. Damped at a basepoint $\alpha$ to the right of every zero, the form is a Fourier multiplier with symbol $\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}\xi'/\xi(\alpha+i\tau)$, which gives a sharp lower bound for its least eigenvalue on every window, $2\xi'(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha)$ unconditionally for $\alpha\ge1$ and under RH for $\frac12<\alpha<1$. An uncertainty barrier limits what prime side computations of the tent coefficient detect above the verified height. The chapter does not prove RH.

#### From the literature

- Yoshida's Hermitian forms of Weil's explicit formula on a window (Yoshida 1992), as the first author reads it, unchecked
- the explicit formula and the positivity criterion for RH (Weil 1952; Bombieri 2000); a short window reproved by Connes and Consani (2021, attribution unverified); certified positivity on one window with prime powers (Zhu 2026)
- RH as positivity of the tent coefficient, classical in substance (Landau's theorem, Widder 1941, on a Riesz mean as in Ingham 1932), Landau's zero sum formula (Landau 1912), Löwner's theorem on Pick functions (Löwner 1934; Donoghue 1974)
- Lagarias's criterion for xi (Lagarias 1999), RH as monotonicity of $|\xi(\sigma+i\tau)|$ in $\sigma$ (Sondow and Dumitrescu 2010), de Bruijn's bound for the de Bruijn Newman constant (de Bruijn 1950; normalisation of Rodgers and Tao 2020)
- RH verified to $3\times10^{12}$ (Platt and Trudgian 2021), explicit zero counting bounds (Hasanalizade, Shen and Wong 2022), the Vinogradov Korobov zero free region (Vinogradov 1958; Korobov 1958), the Davenport Heilbronn function (Davenport and Heilbronn 1936)

#### New results

Every theorem is proved, with its hypotheses stated, except a double precision computation of the tent coefficient up to level 47.48; the five problems are open.

- [Ladder rungs are diagonal values of Weil's form on Hermite Gaussians](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#ladder_rungs_are_diagonal_values_of_weil_form_on_hermite_gaussians) (Proposition 17.2.1, page 643; proved): Weil's Hermitian form on the Hermite Gaussian vector of order $k$ and width $x$ equals twice the rung $T_k(x)$ of the ladder of the heat trace of the zeros, and the heat trace $W(x)$ is half the value of the form on the Gaussian itself. New in this book.
- [If RH fails every large rung of the ladder fails: RH is positivity of the odd rungs](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#rh_is_positivity_of_odd_ladder_rungs_and_every_large_rung_fails) (Theorem 17.3.1, page 644; proved): The orders $k$ for which the rung $T_k$ of the ladder is nonnegative form an initial segment, and if RH fails every rung beyond some finite order takes a negative value, so RH is equivalent to nonnegativity of the rungs of any fixed infinite set of orders, in particular of the odd rungs, that is of Weil's form on odd Hermite Gaussians. New in this book.
- [Where the rungs fail: saddle point location for an off line zero](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#saddle_point_location_of_failing_ladder_rungs_for_an_off_line_zero) (Proposition 17.3.2, page 645; proved): If RH fails, a saddle point computation shows that for every large $k$ the rung $T_k$ is negative at a point $x=k/y_k$ with $y_k$ within $O(1/k)$ of $\gamma_*^2-\delta_*^2$ for an off line zero that maximises $\log\sec\theta$, with no explicit bound for the order $k$. New in this book.
- [The tent coefficient of Yoshida's matrix: zero side, prime side and residue series](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#tent_coefficient_zero_side_prime_side_and_residue_series) (Proposition 17.6.1, page 649; proved): The tent coefficient $D(x)$ of Yoshida's matrix is the zero sum $\sum_\rho4\sin^2(\gamma_\rho x/2)/\gamma_\rho^2$, under RH it is $8\int\sin^2(x\sqrt t/2)\,t^{-1}\,U(dt)$ for the Thorin measure $U$, and it has an explicit prime side expression, a Riesz mean of $\Lambda(n)n^{-1/2}$ plus an archimedean term given in closed form and by a residue series. New in this book.
- [Yoshida's matrix is a Löwner matrix, and RH is the Pick property of one function](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#yoshida_matrix_is_a_lowner_matrix_and_rh_is_the_pick_property) (Theorem 17.7.1, page 654; proved): Yoshida's matrix of Weil's form on a window of half length $a$ is, up to a sign change, $2/a$ times the Löwner matrix of an odd meromorphic function $g_a$ built from the zeros (under RH $g_a(\nu)=\nu\,\mathcal{S}_a(-\nu^2)$ for the Stieltjes transform $\mathcal{S}_a$ of the Thorin measure weighted by $2\sin^2(a\sqrt t)$), and RH holds if and only if $g_a$ is a Pick function, for any one $a>0$. New in this book.
- [The damped Yoshida form is a Fourier multiplier with symbol Re xi'/xi over pi](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#damped_yoshida_form_is_a_fourier_multiplier_with_symbol_xi_log_derivative) (Proposition 17.8.1, page 656; proved): For a basepoint $\alpha\ge\sigma_{\max}$ with no zero on the line $\operatorname{Re}s=\alpha$, the damped Yoshida form of a function supported in a window is the integral of $|\widehat\varphi|^2$ against the positive density $\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(\alpha+i\tau)$, a sum of Poisson kernels of the zeros. New in this book.
- [Positivity of the damped Yoshida forms: basepoints beyond the zeros, and RH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#damped_yoshida_forms_are_positive_semidefinite_for_basepoints_beyond_the_zeros_and_rh_equivalence) (Theorem 17.8.3, page 657; proved): The damped Yoshida form is positive semidefinite for every basepoint $\alpha\ge\sigma_{\max}$, hence unconditionally for $\alpha\ge1$, RH holds if and only if it is positive semidefinite for every $\alpha>\frac12$, and the supremum of the half lengths $a$ for which it is positive semidefinite on the smooth functions supported in $[-a,a]$ is nondecreasing in $\alpha$. New in this book.
- [Sharp coercivity of the damped Yoshida forms on every window](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#sharp_coercivity_of_damped_yoshida_forms_by_the_minimum_of_xi_log_derivative) (Theorem 17.8.5, page 658; proved): For $\alpha\ge\sigma_{\max}$ with no zero on the line $\operatorname{Re}s=\alpha$, the least eigenvalue of the damped Yoshida form on a window of half length $a$ is at least $2\inf_\tau\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(\alpha+i\tau)$ and tends to it as $a\to\infty$; this infimum is $\xi'(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha)$ under RH and unconditionally for $\alpha\ge1$, RH is equivalent to the bound $2\xi'(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha)$ for all $\alpha\in(\frac12,1]$ and all windows, and the constant vanishes linearly as $\alpha\downarrow\frac12$. New in this book.
- [Unconditional sharp coercivity of the damped Yoshida form at alpha equal to 1](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#unconditional_sharp_coercivity_of_the_damped_yoshida_form_at_basepoint_one) (Corollary 17.8.8, page 660; proved): With no hypothesis on the zeros, the damped Yoshida form at $\alpha=1$ satisfies $\langle\varphi,\varphi\rangle_1\ge(2+\gamma_E-\log4\pi)\|\varphi\|^2$ on every window, and this constant, about $0.0461914$, cannot be enlarged for all windows. New in this book.
- [Uncertainty barrier for the tent coefficient above the verified height](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#uncertainty_barrier_for_the_tent_coefficient_above_the_verified_height) (Proposition 17.9.1, page 663; proved): If all zeros up to height $H$ lie on the critical line, the zeros above $H$ change the tent coefficient $D(x)$ by at most $8\cosh^2(x/4)\sum_{\gamma>H}\gamma^{-2}$, which is below $1.184\times10^{-11}\cosh^2(x/4)$ for $H=3\times10^{12}$, a bound that grows like $e^{x/2}$ and concerns the tent coefficient only. New in this book.
- [Computed positivity of the tent coefficient up to level 47.48 from the verification of RH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#tent_coefficient_computed_positive_up_to_level_47_from_the_verified_height_and_1700_zeros) (Proposition 17.9.2, page 663; computed): A computation in double precision (a branch and bound, then a grid with a Lipschitz bound), not a ball arithmetic certificate, shows from the first 1700 zeros and the verification of RH to height $3\times10^{12}$ alone that the tent coefficient $D(x)$ is positive for $0.05\le x\le47.48$, so that a prime side computation of $D$ at these levels cannot produce a negative value. New in this book.
- [Open problem: the symbol inequality Re xi'/xi at least xi'/xi(alpha) below the line alpha equal to 1](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_symbol_inequality_for_xi_log_derivative_below_basepoint_one) (Problem 17.1, page 665; open): Determine the region of lines $\operatorname{Re}s=\alpha<1$ and heights $\tau$ above the verified height $3\times10^{12}$ in which $\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(\alpha+i\tau)>\xi'(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha)$ can be proved with no hypothesis and with explicit constants, the Vinogradov Korobov region being the natural target. New in this book.
- [Open problem: a prime side proof of the symbol inequality at alpha equal to 1](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_prime_side_proof_of_the_symbol_inequality_at_basepoint_one) (Problem 17.2, page 666; open): Prove, from Mertens type information on the primes and not through the zeros, the inequality $\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(1+i\tau)\ge\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(1)$ in its form as a bound for the prime sum $\sum_n\Lambda(n)n^{-1}\cos(\tau\log n)$. New in this book.
- [Open problem: what does Löwner positivity on the lattice of one window say about the zeros](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_lowner_positivity_of_yoshida_form_on_the_lattice_of_a_single_window) (Problem 17.3, page 666; open): Decide what positivity of Yoshida's form on a single window, that is of the Löwner matrix of $g_a$ on the lattice $\frac\pi a\mathbb{Z}$, implies about the location of the zeros, an answer that grows with $a$ quantifying Yoshida's threshold $a_0$. New in this book.
- [Open problem: the orders of the first failing rung and of Yoshida's window threshold for one off line pair](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_orders_of_the_first_failing_rung_and_of_the_window_threshold_for_one_off_line_pair) (Problem 17.4, page 666; open): Determine, for a single off line pair of zeros, the order of the first failing ladder rung $K_0$ and of Yoshida's window threshold $a_0$ in terms of the height and displacement of the pair, and compare them with the displacement and with the de Bruijn Newman constant. New in this book.
- [Open problem: zero density estimates and the barrier, and a barrier for windows](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_zero_density_sharpening_of_the_barrier_and_barriers_for_windows) (Problem 17.5, page 666; open): Sharpen the barrier level of the tent coefficient with explicit zero density estimates, decide whether any prime side computation of the tent coefficient at feasible levels can exclude off line zeros above the verified height, and decide whether windows of corresponding length can see such a zero. New in this book.

#### Key terms

Yoshida, Hermitian form, Weil positivity, Weil criterion, explicit formula, Riemann Hypothesis, RH, xi function, Hermite Gaussian, heat trace, ladder, tent coefficient, sine squared lemma, Löwner matrix, Loewner matrix, Pick function, damped form, basepoint, Fourier multiplier, coercivity, least eigenvalue, uncertainty barrier, Thorin programme, Thorin program, de Bruijn Newman constant

chapters.title: Zhu's compact windows and the Landau Widom horizon
chapters.summary:
This chapter reads Xuefeng Zhu's 2026 preprint on Weil positivity in compact windows in the language of Thorin measures. The question is how far Weil's criterion for the Riemann Hypothesis, positivity of Weil's quadratic form on test functions supported in every window [-a,a], can be certified by finite computation, and what a window says about the height of the zeros. The objects are the least eigenvalue of the form, the prime comb in its symbol and the Thorin measure of the clock of the Xi function. The methods are a dictionary that makes the form, under RH, a sampling functional of the Thorin measure on Paley Wiener functions, Zhu's test function through a truncated reciprocal Xi transform, the Landau Widom horizon, and damping to a basepoint alpha. It proves the dictionary and a two parameter bound for the least eigenvalue of the damped form (conditional on RH below 1), reproves its coercivity for basepoints above 1 from the Euler product, and computes least eigenvalues and a detection experiment with a hypothetical off line quadruple of zeros. The passage from windows to heights is a heuristic. Four problems are open. Nothing here proves RH.

#### From the literature

- Weil's explicit formula and criterion (Weil 1952; Bombieri 2000); positivity on windows with 2a at most log 2 (Yoshida 1992), proved again by other methods (Connes and Consani 2021).
- Zhu (2026): a finite reduction of positivity on a window, a computer assisted certificate on [-0.8, 0.8], the upper bound exp(-a e^a) for the least even eigenvalue under RH for large a, the barrier for pointwise comb certificates and the Landau Widom decay law, a conjecture fitted to computed bounds.
- Positivity on each window as a sampling statement under RH (Zhu 2026), via Littlewood (1924) on gaps between ordinates and Beurling's sampling theorem (Seip 2004).
- Time and band limiting (Slepian and Pollak 1961; Landau and Pollak 1962; Landau and Widom 1980); verification of RH to height 3 times 10^12 (Platt and Trudgian 2021).

#### New results

Catalogued: the dictionary, the two parameter bound and four open problems; the tables are reported computations, not catalogued results.

- [Dictionary: Zhu's window form is Yoshida's Weil form and, under RH, a sampling functional of the Thorin measure](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#zhu_window_form_equals_yoshida_form_and_under_rh_is_thorin_sampling_functional) (Proposition 18.2.1, page 671; conditional on The Riemann Hypothesis, used only for the second set of identities (the sum over the zeros, the integral against the Thorin measure and the sampling reading of the least eigenvalue). The identity $Q(f)=\langle f,f\rangle=\mathcal{Y}(f*f)$ holds with no hypothesis on the zeros): On a window of half length $a$, Zhu's quadratic form equals Yoshida's Weil form of the autocorrelation $f*f$ with no hypothesis, and under RH it equals twice the sum of $|F|^2$ over the positive ordinates, so that the least even eigenvalue is the lower sampling constant of the Thorin measure of the clock for the real even Paley Wiener functions of type $a$. - [Two parameter bound: the damped least eigenvalue is at least the undamped one, and under RH at least $2\xi'(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha)$](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#two_parameter_bound_for_least_eigenvalue_of_damped_weil_form_on_a_window) (Theorem 18.5.2, page 682; conditional on The Riemann Hypothesis, used for part (ii) when $\alpha<1$, for the lower bound $2b_\alpha\ge4p_1(\alpha-\frac12)-4p_2(\alpha-\frac12)^3$ at every $\alpha>\frac12$ and for the closing maximum. Part (i), the bound $\lambda_{\min}(\alpha,a)\ge2b_\alpha$ for $\alpha\ge1$ and the upper bound $2b_\alpha\le4p_1(\alpha-\frac12)$ hold with no hypothesis on the zeros): The least eigenvalue of the damped Weil form on a window is at least the undamped one for every basepoint $\alpha>\frac12$ with no hypothesis, and under RH (or for $\alpha\ge1$) it is also at least $2\xi'(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha)$, a floor of order $\alpha-\frac12$. - [Open problem: the Landau Widom horizon as a theorem, the largest window on which Weil's form is positive when the zeros are controlled up to a height](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_problem_horizon_as_a_theorem_largest_window_from_zeros_verified_to_height_h) (Problem 18.1, page 684; open): Determine the largest half length $a(H,\delta_0)$ of a window on which Weil's form is positive when all zeros up to height $H$ lie on the critical line and the higher zeros lie within $\delta_0$ of it, and decide whether it is at least $\frac12\log\frac H{2\pi}-C(\delta_0)$ with a constant depending only on $\delta_0$. New in this book.
- [Open problem: derive Zhu's Landau Widom decay law for the least eigenvalue of Weil's form on a window from the Thorin side](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_problem_derive_zhu_decay_law_for_least_eigenvalue_from_thorin_side) (Problem 18.2, page 685; open): Derive Zhu's fitted decay law $-\log\lambda^{\mathrm{even}}_{\min}(\frac12,a)\approx C\,N(T_*)/\log N(T_*)$ with $T_*=2\pi e^{2a}$ for the least even eigenvalue of Weil's form on a window of half length $a$ from his product test function, and explain the constant through the Landau Widom plunge. New in this book.
- [Open problem: certified damped windows for basepoints between one half and one](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_problem_certified_damped_windows_for_basepoint_between_one_half_and_one) (Problem 18.3, page 685; open): Extend Zhu's computer assisted certificate of positivity of Weil's form on a window to the damped forms with basepoint $\alpha\in(\frac12,1)$, where under RH the margin is at least $2\xi'(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha)$ in place of the undamped least eigenvalue, and measure how large a window can be certified. New in this book.
- [Open problem: comb cancellation on average over Paley Wiener functions](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_problem_comb_cancellation_on_average_over_paley_wiener_functions) (Problem 18.4, page 685; open): Determine, as a function of $T$ and $a$, the supremum over Paley Wiener functions $F$ of type $a$ of the average of the prime comb against $|F|^2$ on the frequencies $|t|\ge T$, which is at most the pointwise supremum $A_a=(4+o(1))e^a$. chapters.title: Three families of generalised gamma convolutions and the deconvolution obstruction
chapters.summary:
This chapter asks where the difficulty of the Riemann Hypothesis (RH) sits in three one parameter families of generalized gamma convolutions (GGCs, Thorin measures) that contain the clock of Riemann's xi function as a boundary case: the Esscher tilt, the basepoint family of shifted clocks, whose Thorin density is a sum of Cauchy (Poisson) kernels over the zeros, and the de Bruijn Newman heat flow. It proves that the tilt is invertible and carries no information, that the basepoint family is a Poisson semigroup to the right of the zeros and fails to be one at the levels $\varepsilon\ge0$ with a zero to their right, at positive distance from the offsets of the zeros, and that RH is equivalent to deconvolving the Thorin density at such a basepoint into a positive measure, an unbounded operation. It gives the order $N^{\sigma_{\max}-\alpha}$ of the error of smoothed prime sums for Dirichlet L functions, sharp under GRH for $\alpha<\tfrac32$, and shows that no property preserved by Gaussian averaging and implying real zeros holds for any $H_t$. It derives the visibility curve of a hypothetical off line quadruple of zeros, in closed form in three lattice models, with about $\tfrac14\log(h/2\pi)$ levels needed at height $h$.

#### From the literature

The Thorin representation of generalized gamma convolutions (Thorin 1977; Bondesson 1992); Lagarias's positivity criterion for RH (Lagarias 1999); the explicit formula for a smoothed sum over primes (compare Davenport 2000); de Bruijn's theorem on strips of zeros under the heat flow (de Bruijn 1950); Newman's theorem $\Lambda>-\infty$ (Newman 1976), the nonnegativity of the de Bruijn Newman constant $\Lambda$ (Rodgers and Tao 2020), the bound $\Lambda\le0.2$ after Polymath 2019 and the verification of RH to height $3\times10^{12}$ (both Platt and Trudgian 2021); Lehmer pairs and $\Lambda$ (Csordas, Smith and Varga 1994); a zero free half plane $\operatorname{Re}s>\tfrac78$ announced in October 2026 and not yet refereed (OpenAI 2026).

#### New results

The visibility curve and the level counts concern a hypothetical off line quadruple of zeros, among the zeros of $\xi$ or in lattice models (no off line zero is known); the other results concern $\xi$ and $H_t$.

- [Tilt family of the clock: the Thorin property at one tilt is equivalent to RH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#tilt_family_of_the_clock_thorin_property_invariant_and_equivalent_to_rh) (Theorem 19.1.2, page 689; proved): The Esscher tilt of the clock of xi maps generalized gamma convolutions to generalized gamma convolutions in both directions and leaves the imaginary part of the point attached to each zero unchanged, so the Thorin property at one tilt is equivalent to the property at every tilt and to RH (the case of the rational field of the tilt theorem for Dedekind zeta functions). New in this book.
- [Poisson semigroup of the basepoint family and its converse](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#poisson_semigroup_of_basepoint_thorin_densities_and_its_converse) (Theorem 19.2.1, page 690; proved): The Thorin densities of the shifted clocks satisfy the Poisson semigroup identity from any level to the right of all zeros, with no hypothesis from level one half on, and the identity fails from every level $\varepsilon_0\ge0$ that has a zero to its right and lies at positive distance from the offsets of the zeros. New in this book.
- [Deconvolution form of RH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#deconvolution_form_of_rh_thorin_density_at_basepoint_is_smoothing_of_positive_measure) (Theorem 19.2.2, page 691; proved): RH holds if and only if the Thorin density at a basepoint to the right of all zeros is the Cauchy smoothing of a positive measure on the line, which is then the sum of unit point masses at the ordinates of the zeros, repeated according to multiplicity, and more generally the density deconvolves to a positive measure at level $\varepsilon_1$ exactly when no zero has offset $\beta-\tfrac12$ above $\varepsilon_1$. New in this book.
- [Thorin density near the critical line and Laguerre's quantity](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#thorin_density_near_the_critical_line_is_epsilon_times_laguerre_quantity) (Proposition 19.3.1, page 694; proved): For small epsilon the Thorin density at level epsilon equals epsilon over pi times Laguerre's quantity, the negative second derivative of the logarithm of the absolute value of Xi, up to $O(\varepsilon^3)$, and a hypothetical off line quadruple at distance delta contributes minus two over delta squared to that quantity at its own ordinate, up to $O(\gamma^{*-2})$. New in this book.
- [Visibility curve of a hypothetical off line quadruple and its closed forms in three lattice models](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#visibility_curve_of_off_line_quadruple_closed_forms_in_three_lattice_models) (Proposition 19.3.2, page 696; proved): At the ordinate of a hypothetical off line quadruple at distance delta, the Thorin density at level epsilon, when the other zeros contribute positively there, is negative exactly when epsilon is below delta and delta is below the visibility distance $\delta_{\mathrm{det}}(\varepsilon)$, which is given in closed form in three lattice models, increases with epsilon and exceeds epsilon by about Delta over pi at large epsilon; this is a theorem about a model with a hypothetical quadruple, not about the zeros of xi. New in this book.
- [Number of levels needed in the lattice models, one quarter of log h](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#number_of_levels_in_lattice_models_is_one_quarter_of_log_height) (Corollary 19.3.3, page 698; proved): In the lattice models a single hypothetical off line quadruple at any distance up to one half is detected at its ordinate by the sign of Laguerre's quantity together with K levels, no test of this kind uses fewer than K levels, and K equals one quarter of log(h over 2 pi) plus O(log log h) at height h; this is a statement about a model, not about the zeros of xi. New in this book.
- [No averaging stable property carries real zeros](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#no_averaging_stable_property_carries_real_zeros_for_the_heat_flow_functions) (Corollary 19.4.2, page 701; proved): A property of entire functions that is preserved by Gaussian averaging and implies that all zeros are real holds for no function $H_t$ of the de Bruijn Newman family, at no real time and in particular not at time zero. New in this book.
- [Question: a certificate with a few levels for the actual zeros](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#question_certificate_with_levels_for_the_actual_zeros) (Problem 19.1, page 702; open): The book asks for levels whose positivity, together with positivity of Laguerre's quantity, excludes all off line zeros of xi up to a given height, and whether the number of levels is still of order log of the height when several off line zeros, irregular spacing and minima off the ordinates are allowed. New in this book.
- [Question: stability with an a priori bound that comes from the Thorin structure](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#question_stability_with_an_a_priori_bound_from_the_thorin_structure) (Problem 19.2, page 702; open): The book asks whether the a priori bound that the three lines theorem needs on a zero free strip can come from the Thorin structure itself, for instance from positivity of the Thorin density at the levels already certified. New in this book.
- [Question: which positivity statements fail for negative heat time by a mechanism visible at finite height](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#question_seeing_the_boundary_of_the_heat_flow_at_negative_time) (Problem 19.3, page 702; open): The book asks which positivity statements, for instance the GGC property of the clock or the Pólya frequency property of the density of $Z\sqrt{2T}$, can be shown to fail for negative heat time by a mechanism visible at finite height, as Lehmer pairs make the de Bruijn Newman constant visible. New in this book.
- [Question: the window of levels below delta, its distribution over heights and the sine kernel](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#question_distribution_of_the_window_of_levels_below_delta_and_the_sine_kernel) (Problem 19.4, page 702; open): The book asks for the distribution over heights of the visibility distance and of the onset level at which a hypothetical off line quadruple at distance delta becomes visible, in terms of local zero statistics, compared with the prediction of the sine kernel. New in this book.

#### Key terms

generalized gamma convolution, generalised gamma convolution, GGC, Thorin measure, Thorin density, reciprocal xi function, Esscher tilt, basepoint family, shifted clock, Poisson semigroup, deconvolution, RH, GRH, zero free half plane, de Bruijn Newman constant, heat flow, Gaussian averaging, Laguerre quantity, visibility curve, off line zeros, lattice model, Lehmer pair, smoothed prime sums

chapters.title: Deconvolution as a damped Weil criterion
chapters.summary:
This chapter asks whether the deconvolution theorem for the Thorin density of the Riemann $\xi$ function can be carried out: RH holds exactly when the Thorin density at a basepoint to the right of the zeros is the Cauchy (Poisson) smoothing of a positive measure on the critical line. The deconvolved object always exists, with no hypothesis: it is Weil's distribution, the zero sum of Weil's explicit formula, computed from the gamma factor, the pole and the primes. Its Fourier dual is a damped Weil criterion: Weil's quadratic form damped by $e^{-\varepsilon|x|}$ is nonnegative exactly when no zero has real part above $\frac12+\varepsilon$, so $\varepsilon=0$ is Weil's criterion, $\varepsilon=\frac12$ holds unconditionally, and the zero free half plane $\operatorname{Re}s>\frac78$ announced in October 2026 (not refereed, not assumed here) is the case $\varepsilon=\frac38$. Restricting the test functions to support $[-a,a]$ gives a ladder of finite problems in the primes up to $e^{2a}$. If no zero has real part $\ge\frac12+\varepsilon$ and the Thorin density has a strict, nondegenerate global minimum at the origin, not approached at infinity (true at $\varepsilon=\frac12$, assumed below it), the least eigenvalue decreases to $2\xi'/\xi(\frac12+\varepsilon)$ at an algebraic rate in $a$; at $\varepsilon=0$, under RH, it falls faster than any power of $a$. The eigenvalue computations are numerical, not certificates.

#### From the literature

Weil's explicit formula and positivity criterion (Weil 1952; Iwaniec and Kowalski 2004); positivity of Weil's form on short windows where no prime enters (Yoshida 1992), other test functions of small support (Bombieri 2000), and a second proof of Yoshida's range (Connes and Consani 2021); a certified lower bound for the least eigenvalue on a short window, an empirical decay law, and under RH an upper bound $\exp(-ae^a)$ for large $a$ (Zhu 2026, preprint); low zeros from the lowest eigenvector of a truncated form (Connes, Consani and Moscovici 2025, preprint); the nonnegativity of the de Bruijn Newman constant (Rodgers and Tao 2020); the time and band limiting operator (Slepian and Pollak 1961); the Bochner Schwartz theorem (Gel'fand and Vilenkin 1964); the half plane $\operatorname{Re}s>\frac78$ (OpenAI 2026, announced, not refereed).

#### New results

The book proves the hypotheses of the ladder theorem only at $\varepsilon=\frac12$.

- [The deconvolved Thorin functional is Weil's distribution](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#deconvolved_thorin_functional_is_weil_distribution_no_hypothesis) (Theorem 20.1.1, page 706; proved): With no hypothesis on the zeros, deconvolving the Thorin density of the shifted clock by the Cauchy kernel gives a functional that does not depend on the basepoint and equals the sum of a test function over the zeros, which Weil's explicit formula computes from the gamma factor, the pole and the primes. New in this book.
- [Damped Weil criterion](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#damped_weil_criterion_no_zero_above_one_half_plus_epsilon) (Theorem 20.1.2, page 707; proved): For $0\le\varepsilon\le\frac12$, Weil's quadratic form damped by $e^{-\varepsilon|x|}$ is nonnegative on every test function exactly when no zero of $\zeta$ has real part above $\frac12+\varepsilon$, which is Weil's criterion for RH at $\varepsilon=0$, holds with no hypothesis at $\varepsilon=\frac12$, and at $\varepsilon=\frac38$ is equivalent to the half plane $\operatorname{Re}s>\frac78$ announced in October 2026 and not refereed. New in this book.
- [Ladder theorem: least eigenvalue of the damped Weil form on a window](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#ladder_theorem_least_eigenvalue_damped_weil_form_algebraic_rate_and_line_dichotomy) (Theorem 20.2.1, page 709; conditional on Parts (a) and (b), for a level $0<\varepsilon<\frac12$: that the closed half plane $\operatorname{Re}s\ge\frac12+\varepsilon$ contains no zero of $\zeta$ (that $\varepsilon$ is to the right of the zeros). This zero free half plane is not proved for any $\varepsilon<\frac12$; the half plane $\operatorname{Re}s>\frac78$ announced in October 2026 and not refereed would give it for $\varepsilon>\frac38$ only.; Parts (a) and (b), for a level $0<\varepsilon<\frac12$: that $v_{1/2+\varepsilon}(\theta)>v_{1/2+\varepsilon}(0)$ for every real $\theta\ne0$ and $v_{1/2+\varepsilon}''(0)>0$, that is, that the Thorin density has a strict, nondegenerate global minimum at the origin. The book certifies this only up to a finite height, and the strict minimum at the origin on every line $\frac12<\alpha<1$ at once is equivalent to RH.; Parts (a) and (b), for a level $0<\varepsilon<\frac12$: that $\liminf_{|\theta|\to\infty}v_{1/2+\varepsilon}(\theta)>v_{1/2+\varepsilon}(0)$, that is, that the minimum is not approached at infinity. This is not known for $0<\varepsilon<\frac12$ without RH, under which it holds.; Part (c), first half (the nonnegativity and the decay of $\lambda_{\min}(\frac12,a)$): the Riemann Hypothesis. All hypotheses of (a) and (b) hold at $\varepsilon=\frac12$ with no assumption on the zeros, and the second half of (c), the negativity for large $a$ if RH fails, needs no hypothesis. For $\varepsilon>\frac12$ the chapter does not discuss whether the hypotheses on $v_{1/2+\varepsilon}$ hold): At a level $\frac12+\varepsilon$ to the right of the zeros where the Thorin density has a strict, nondegenerate global minimum at the origin not approached at infinity (true at $\varepsilon=\frac12$, an assumption below it), the least eigenvalue of Weil's form damped by $e^{-\varepsilon|x|}$ on test functions supported in $[-a,a]$ decreases to $2\xi'/\xi(\frac12+\varepsilon)$ at a rate between $c/a^2$ and $(\pi^2v''(0)/4+o(1))/a^2$, with $v(\theta)=\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(\frac12+\varepsilon+i\theta)$, while at $\varepsilon=0$, under RH, it is nonnegative and $O(a^{-N})$ for every $N$, and if RH fails it is negative for all large $a$. New in this book.
- [Certified rungs of the ladder](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_certified_rungs_of_the_damped_weil_ladder_in_interval_arithmetic) (Problem 20.1, page 716; open): Certify in interval arithmetic that the least eigenvalue of Weil's damped form on test functions supported in $[-4,4]$ is positive at $\varepsilon=0.05$, $0.1$, $0.2$ and $0.375$, and find how far in the window a certificate can be pushed. New in this book.
- [The exact rate of the ladder](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_exact_rate_of_the_damped_weil_ladder_at_depth_epsilon) (Problem 20.2, page 716; open): Prove that the scaled excess of the least eigenvalue of the damped Weil form over its limit tends to the upper constant $\pi^2v''(0)/4$ of the ladder theorem, and find the next term; numerical fits are consistent with the limit and with a positive correction of order $1/a$, and neither is proved. New in this book.
- [The transition of the ladder at the line](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_transition_of_the_damped_weil_ladder_at_the_line) (Problem 20.3, page 716; open): Describe the least eigenvalue of the damped Weil form jointly as the window half length $a$ tends to infinity and the depth $\varepsilon$ tends to zero, where the rate is algebraic for fixed $\varepsilon>0$ under the hypotheses of the ladder theorem and faster than any power of $a$ at $\varepsilon=0$ under RH. New in this book.
- [Uniformity of the damped Weil form from structure](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_uniform_positivity_of_the_damped_weil_form_from_structure) (Problem 20.4, page 716; open): Find a structural reason, valid for all windows, why Weil's form damped by $e^{-\varepsilon|x|}$ is nonnegative on test functions supported in $[-a,a]$ for some fixed $\varepsilon<\frac12$, which by the damped Weil criterion would prove the zero free half plane $\operatorname{Re}s>\frac12+\varepsilon$. New in this book.

#### Key terms

Weil explicit formula, Weil positivity, Weil criterion, Weil distribution, damped Weil form, deconvolution, Cauchy smoothing, Thorin density, generalized gamma convolution, generalised gamma convolution, GGC, basepoint, zero free half plane, quasi Riemann hypothesis, Bochner Schwartz theorem, ladder, least eigenvalue, prolate spheroidal wave functions, time and band limiting operator

chapters.title: Thorin representations, Dirichlet L functions and the Linnik constant
chapters.summary:
Can the Thorin representation of the reciprocal of the Riemann xi function be carried to Dirichlet L functions and Dedekind zeta functions of number fields, and does it help with Linnik's constant $K$, the number of powers of two needed with two primes to represent every large even integer? The chapter proves that the reciprocal of a completed Dedekind zeta function, tilted by $u_0\ge0$, is a generalized gamma convolution (GGC) exactly when every nontrivial zero lies on the critical line or is a real zero within $\sqrt{u_0}$ of the centre (and there is no central zero at $u_0=0$), with Thorin measure the shifted zero counting measure. For all cyclotomic fields together, the Thorin property at the centre is equivalent to the generalized Riemann hypothesis (GRH) for all Dirichlet L functions with nonvanishing at the centre, which gives only the GRH value $K=7$. It also treats the centre clock of $\xi$ (moments, transfer function, negative moments), the sine squared lemma, real and complex characters, and mixtures of characters, not GGCs in general. Nothing here proves RH or lowers $K$.

#### From the literature

- Linnik's theorem (Linnik 1951, 1953) and the records $K=8$ unconditionally (Pintz and Ruzsa 2020) and $K=7$ under GRH (Heath-Brown and Puchta 2002; Pintz and Ruzsa 2003)
- Gallagher's circle method (Gallagher 1975); the zero free regions of Iwaniec and of Vinogradov (1958); symmetry types of families (Katz and Sarnak 1999)
- generalized gamma convolutions (Thorin 1977; Bondesson 1992, 2015); the Riemann zeta distribution (Khinchin 1938; Lin and Hu 2001); the mean value theorems of Carlson and Ingham (Titchmarsh 1986)
- the master theorem class (Chaudhry and Qadir 2012); an exponential Tauberian theorem (Kasahara 1978); Dedekind zeta functions with a zero at the centre (Armitage 1971)
- the Thorin framework (Polson 2018, 2026) and the sine squared lemma (Polson 2017, 2026); the sign criterion for RH (Lagarias 1999); RH as a Pólya frequency property (Schoenberg 1951; Konstantopoulos, Patie and Sarkar 2024)
- a zero free half plane $\operatorname{Re}s>\frac78$, announced and not refereed (OpenAI 2026)

#### New results

Statements are proved unless marked conditional (on RH, GRH, or GRH with nonvanishing at the centre); the Linnik constant corollary is weaker than the known result under GRH; the problems are open.

- [Thorin property of the tilted clock of a Dedekind zeta function at every tilt: equivalence with the position of the zeros](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#thorin_property_of_tilted_dedekind_zeta_clock_at_every_tilt) (Theorem 21.2.3, page 722; proved): For a number field and a tilt $u_0\ge0$, the tilted reciprocal of the completed Dedekind zeta function is a GGC exactly when every nontrivial zero lies on the critical line or is real at distance less than $\sqrt{u_0}$ from the centre (with no central zero when $u_0=0$), and its Thorin measure is then the zero counting measure shifted by $u_0$. New in this book.
- [The tilts: Thorin property of a Dedekind zeta clock at tilt zero and at tilts above one quarter, the Thorin threshold and the shift between tilts](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#thorin_property_of_dedekind_clock_at_tilt_zero_and_above_one_quarter_threshold_and_shift) (Corollary 21.2.4, page 723; proved): The Thorin property of a Dedekind zeta function holds at every tilt $u_0\ge\frac14$ exactly when all nontrivial zeros are on the critical line or the real axis, at tilt $0$ exactly when they are all on the critical line with $\zeta_F(\frac12)\ne0$, and, when all nonreal zeros are on the line, exactly above a threshold set by the real zero farthest from the centre, with the Thorin measures at two tilts shifts of one another. New in this book.
- [Closed form of the transfer function from the real axis to the critical line under RH, and its odd index power sum expansion](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#transfer_function_from_real_axis_to_critical_line_is_product_over_ordinates_under_rh) (Proposition 21.3.6, page 729; conditional on The Riemann Hypothesis: every nontrivial zero of the Riemann zeta function has real part $\frac12$): Under RH the transfer function $\xi(\frac12+it)/\xi(\frac12+|t|)$ equals $\prod_{\gamma>0}(\gamma^2-t^2)/(\gamma^2+t^2)$, is real, even, bounded by $1$ and vanishes exactly at the ordinates, and its logarithm near $0$ involves only the odd index power sums of the inverse squared ordinates. New in this book.
- [The odd index power sums of the inverse squared ordinates determine the zeros under RH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#odd_index_power_sums_of_inverse_squared_ordinates_determine_all_zeros_under_rh) (Proposition 21.3.7, page 729; conditional on The Riemann Hypothesis: every nontrivial zero of the Riemann zeta function has real part $\frac12$): Under RH the generating series of the odd index power sums $p_1,p_3,p_5,\dots$ of the inverse squared ordinates continues to a meromorphic function with poles at the points $\pm\gamma^2$, so these sums determine the ordinates with multiplicities and with them every power sum. New in this book.
- [The transfer function as a Blaschke product for the right half plane under RH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#transfer_function_is_blaschke_product_for_right_half_plane_under_rh) (Proposition 21.3.8, page 730; conditional on The Riemann Hypothesis: every nontrivial zero of the Riemann zeta function has real part $\frac12$): Under RH the function $\mathfrak B(z)=\prod_{\gamma>0}(\gamma^2-z)/(\gamma^2+z)$, with $\mathfrak T(t)=\mathfrak B(t^2)$ for the transfer function $\mathfrak T$, is a Blaschke product for the right half plane with zeros at the points $\gamma^2$ and no singular inner factor. New in this book.
- [Negative moments of the centre clock as a Mellin transform of the reciprocal of xi on the real axis](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#negative_moments_of_centre_clock_as_mellin_transform_of_reciprocal_xi) (Proposition 21.3.10, page 730; proved): For $\operatorname{Re}s>0$ the negative moment $\mathbb{E}[T^{-s}]$ of the centre clock of $\xi$ is the Mellin transform of $\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt u)$ divided by $\Gamma(s)$, with no hypothesis on the zeros. New in this book.
- [Growth of the gamma function times the reciprocal of xi on vertical strips under RH: the growth hypothesis of the master theorem class](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#growth_of_gamma_times_reciprocal_xi_on_vertical_strips_in_the_critical_strip_under_rh) (Lemma 21.4.1, page 733; conditional on The Riemann Hypothesis, used through the bound $1/\zeta(w)=O(|\operatorname{Im}w|^\eta)$ on $\operatorname{Re}w\ge\frac12+\sigma_1$ for every $\eta>0$): Under RH, on vertical strips $0<\sigma_1\le\operatorname{Re}s\le\sigma_2<\frac12$ the function $\Gamma(s)\,\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+s)$ is bounded by $C_\eta e^{-\pi|\tau|/4}|\tau|^{\sigma/2-9/4+\eta}$, which verifies the growth hypothesis of the master theorem class with exponential room, but a bound proved under RH cannot be an input to a proof of the Thorin property. New in this book.
- [Absolute convergence hypothesis of the master theorem route for the reciprocal of xi holds without RH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#absolute_convergence_hypothesis_of_master_theorem_route_holds_for_reciprocal_xi_without_rh) (Lemma 21.4.2, page 734; proved): With no hypothesis on the zeros, the series $\mathfrak R(w)=\sum_{k\ge1}b_kw^k$ built from $\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+k)$ is entire of order $\frac23$ and its integral against the density of the centre clock converges for every $z>0$, which is the absolute convergence needed to interchange sum and integral in the master theorem route. New in this book.
- [The reciprocal Xi function in the shifted variable lies in Hardy's class with no hypothesis on the zeros, so the master theorem carries no information on them](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#hardy_class_master_theorem_for_reciprocal_xi_in_shifted_variable_holds_and_is_empty) (Proposition 21.4.3, page 735; proved): The function $\xi(\frac32)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt{1+w})$ is analytic and bounded on $\operatorname{Re}w\ge-\delta$ for $0<\delta<1$, hence in Hardy's class unconditionally, and the image region contains no zero of $\xi$, so Ramanujan's master theorem in this variable says nothing about the zeros. New in this book.
- [Why the square root stays: reciprocal Xi function in the variable s is not a Laplace transform of a random variable, and its values on a vertical line are not a characteristic function](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#reciprocal_xi_is_not_laplace_transform_of_any_random_variable_and_not_characteristic_function) (Theorem 21.4.4, page 736; proved): For every real $\alpha$ the function $s\mapsto\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+s)$ is not the Laplace transform of any real random variable, whether or not RH holds, the function $t\mapsto\xi(\alpha+it)/\xi(\alpha)$ is a characteristic function that is never infinitely divisible, and $t\mapsto\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+it)$ is unbounded. New in this book.
- [Thorin representation of the reciprocal of the completed Dirichlet L function of a real primitive character under GRH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#thorin_representation_of_reciprocal_completed_l_function_of_real_character_under_grh) (Proposition 21.5.1, page 737; conditional on The generalized Riemann hypothesis for $L(s,\chi)$ (every nontrivial zero has real part $\frac12$) and $L(\frac12,\chi)\ne0$ (Chowla's conjecture for real characters, open)): For a real primitive character $\chi$, under GRH for $L(s,\chi)$ and $L(\frac12,\chi)\ne0$, the reciprocal $\xi(\frac12,\chi)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt u,\chi)$ is the Laplace transform of the GGC $\sum_{\gamma>0}e_\gamma/\gamma^2$ over the ordinates of the zeros, and the clock identities of the Riemann case carry over. New in this book.
- [Thorin representation for a complex character through the product of the completed L function with its conjugate, under GRH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#thorin_representation_of_product_of_conjugate_completed_l_functions_of_complex_character_under_grh) (Proposition 21.5.2, page 738; conditional on The generalized Riemann hypothesis for $L(s,\chi)$ (every nontrivial zero has real part $\frac12$) and $L(\frac12,\chi)\ne0$): For a complex primitive character $\chi$, the product $\xi(s,\chi)\xi(s,\bar\chi)$ is symmetric under $s\mapsto1-s$, and under GRH for $L(s,\chi)$ with $L(\frac12,\chi)\ne0$ the reciprocal of its ratio to the centre is the Laplace transform of the GGC $\sum e_\gamma/\gamma^2$ over all ordinates of $L(s,\chi)$ of both signs. New in this book.
- [Factorisation of the completed Dedekind zeta function of a quadratic field and clocks of cyclotomic fields as independent sums](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#completed_dedekind_zeta_of_quadratic_field_factors_and_clocks_of_cyclotomic_fields_add) (Proposition 21.5.3, page 739; conditional on The statement on cyclotomic fields assumes GRH for the Dirichlet $L$ functions of the nonprincipal primitive characters of conductor dividing $q$ and that their values at $\frac12$ are nonzero (the hypotheses of the propositions on real and complex characters). The factorisations of the completed functions hold without any hypothesis, and the statement for quadratic fields is an implication from the Thorin property of the two factors at the tilt considered): For a quadratic field the completed Dedekind zeta function is $2\xi(s)\xi(s,\chi)$ (times $q^{-1/2}$ for odd $\chi$), so at a tilt where both factors have the Thorin property the tilted clock is the independent sum of theirs and the Thorin measures add, and for cyclotomic fields, under GRH with nonzero central values, the clock is the independent sum of the clocks of $\zeta$ and of the nonprincipal primitive characters of conductor dividing $q$. New in this book.
- [Lévy decomposition of the logarithm of the completed Dedekind zeta function of any number field, with signs](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#signed_levy_decomposition_of_log_completed_dedekind_zeta_function_with_negative_density) (Proposition 21.5.4, page 740; proved): For $\alpha>1$ the compensated logarithm of $\xi_F(\alpha+s)/\xi_F(\alpha)$ is an integral against a signed Lévy measure whose arithmetic part has the positive weights $\Lambda_F(n)$ at $\log n$, plus gamma factor densities and the single negative density $-(1+e^x)$ coming from the factor $s(s-1)$. New in this book.
- [The sine squared lemma on the prime side for Dedekind zeta functions and real Dirichlet characters](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#sine_squared_lemma_for_dedekind_zeta_functions_and_real_dirichlet_characters) (Proposition 21.5.6, page 741; proved): For $\alpha>1$ and $f$ the completed Dedekind zeta function of a number field or the completed $L$ function of a real primitive character, the reciprocal $f(\alpha)/f(\alpha+\sqrt u)$ equals $\exp(-\int_0^\infty\log(1+u/b^2)\,v_\alpha(b)\,db/\pi)$ with $v_\alpha(b)=\operatorname{Re}(f'/f)(\alpha+ib)$ written through a sine squared transform of the Lévy measure (Polson's sine squared lemma applied to $f$), so that the density is determined by the primes with no reference to the zeros. New in this book.
- [The basepoint family of the sine squared lemma: Thorin property at a basepoint to the right of all zeros, failure when a zero lies to the right, and the Poisson form under GRH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#basepoint_family_thorin_property_for_dedekind_zeta_functions_and_real_characters_holds_left_of_all_zeros) (Theorem 21.5.8, page 742; conditional on Part (c) assumes GRH for $f$ (every zero has real part $\frac12$) and $f(\frac12)\ne0$. Parts (a) and (b) hold without any hypothesis, and part (a) holds unconditionally for every $\alpha\ge1$): For the completed Dedekind zeta function of a number field or the completed $L$ function of a real primitive character, the reciprocal $f(\alpha)/f(\alpha+\sqrt u)$ is a GGC with a positive Thorin density that is a sum over the zeros when every zero lies to the left of $\alpha$ (so unconditionally for $\alpha\ge1$), is not a GGC transform when a zero lies to the right, and under GRH the density is the Poisson smoothing of the zero counting measure at height $\alpha-\frac12$. New in this book.
- [GRH and nonvanishing at the centre from the Thorin property of the Dedekind zeta functions of quadratic and cyclotomic fields](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#thorin_property_of_quadratic_and_cyclotomic_dedekind_zeta_functions_implies_grh_and_central_nonvanishing) (Theorem 21.6.1, page 746; proved): If the tilted reciprocal of the Dedekind zeta function of a quadratic field is a GGC at tilt $1$, then RH holds and the zeros of the Dirichlet $L$ function are on the critical line or real; if it is a GGC at tilt $0$, then GRH holds for that $L$ function with $L(\frac12,\chi)\ne0$; and if this holds at tilt $0$ for every cyclotomic field, then GRH holds for all Dirichlet $L$ functions with all central values nonzero. New in this book.
- [Mixtures of clocks: a mixture of two GGC Laplace transforms with discrete unit atom Thorin measures is not a GGC transform when it vanishes off the atoms, in particular in the odd configuration](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#mixtures_of_ggc_laplace_transforms_with_unit_atom_thorin_measures_are_not_ggc_in_odd_configuration) (Proposition 21.6.3, page 749; proved): A mixture $\lambda\varphi_1+(1-\lambda)\varphi_2$ of two GGC Laplace transforms whose Thorin measures are sums of unit point masses is not a GGC transform if it vanishes at a negative point that is not an atom, and this happens for every weight $\lambda$ when two consecutive atoms of the union belong to different measures and an odd number of atoms lie at or below the first of them. New in this book.
- [The family of characters modulo 5: no mixture of the two clocks is a GGC, under GRH](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#family_modulo_five_mixture_of_clocks_is_not_ggc_under_grh) (Proposition 21.6.4, page 750; conditional on The generalized Riemann hypothesis for $L(s,\chi_5)$ and for $L(s,\psi)$ (every nontrivial zero has real part $\frac12$). The values $L(\frac12,\chi_5)$ and $L(\frac12,\psi)$ are certified nonzero, and the zeros below height $12$ are certified, in ball arithmetic; neither is assumed): Under GRH for the two members of the family of primitive characters modulo $5$, no mixture of their clocks, the uniform one included, is a GGC, because certified zero counts below height $12$ put their Thorin atoms in the odd configuration of the mixture criterion. New in this book.
- [A real zero of a Dirichlet L function makes the first rung of the twisted heat trace fail beyond an explicit time](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#real_zero_of_dirichlet_l_function_makes_first_rung_of_twisted_heat_trace_fail) (Proposition 21.6.6, page 752; proved): If $L(s,\chi)$ of a primitive real character has a real zero $\beta$ in $(\tfrac12,1)$ and all its nonreal zeros lie on the critical line, the twisted heat trace grows and is increasing beyond an explicit time $t_1$, so it is not completely monotone, already at order one. New in this book.
- [Linnik constant seven from the Thorin property of all cyclotomic fields (weaker than the known result under GRH)](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#seven_powers_of_two_from_thorin_property_of_all_cyclotomic_fields) (Corollary 21.7.1, page 753; conditional on The Thorin property at tilt $0$ for every cyclotomic field $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_q)$, $q\ge3$, which by the equivalence theorem of the chapter is GRH for all Dirichlet $L$ functions together with $L(\frac12,\chi)\ne0$ for every primitive character $\chi$. The proof uses only the GRH part, through the theorem of Heath-Brown and Puchta (2002) that GRH gives seven powers of two): If the centre clock of every cyclotomic field $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_q)$, $q\ge3$, is a GGC, then every sufficiently large even integer is a sum of two primes and at most seven powers of two, which is the value that GRH already gives, so the corollary is weaker than the theorem of Heath-Brown and Puchta (2002), also proved by Pintz and Ruzsa (2003), that GRH alone gives seven, because it assumes nonvanishing at the centre as well. New in this book.
- [Open problem: the Thorin property of the Riemann clock and of cyclotomic clocks without first knowing the zeros](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_problem_thorin_property_of_reciprocal_xi_and_cyclotomic_clocks_without_knowing_the_zeros) (Problem 21.1, page 754; open): Prove that the tilted reciprocal of the completed zeta function of $\mathbb{Q}$, or of a cyclotomic field, is the Laplace transform of a GGC without first knowing the zeros, in particular by settling the parabolic distortion in the master theorem route; for $\mathbb{Q}$ at the centre this is RH itself. New in this book.
- [Open problem: seven powers of two from GRH with possible real zeros, that is from the Thorin property at tilt one for cyclotomic fields](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_problem_seven_powers_of_two_from_grh_with_possible_real_zeros) (Problem 21.2, page 754; open): Show that every sufficiently large even integer is a sum of two primes and at most seven powers of two from the weaker hypothesis that every nontrivial zero of every Dirichlet $L$ function lies on the critical line or on the real axis, which would make real and Siegel zeros irrelevant to this value. New in this book.
- [Open problem: the anchored tail of the moment identity of the centre clock at large height and for Dirichlet L functions](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_problem_anchored_tail_of_the_moment_identity_at_large_height_and_for_l_functions) (Problem 21.3, page 755; open): Carry the anchored tail of the zero side of the moment identity of the centre clock to large height with tables of zeros of zeta, where the remaining integral of the zero count fluctuation sets the limit and calls for an explicit formula, and to Dirichlet $L$ functions. New in this book.
- [Open problem: the negative moment of the clock averaged over real characters of conductor in [Q,2Q] against the symplectic random matrix prediction](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_problem_negative_moment_of_the_clock_as_a_family_statistic_and_symplectic_prediction) (Problem 21.4, page 755; open): Compute the average of the negative moment $\mathbb{E}[T_\chi^{-1/2}]$ of the clock over real primitive characters of conductor in $[Q,2Q]$ and compare it with the prediction of the symplectic ensemble, noting that this moment is not a linear statistic of the zeros. New in this book.
- [Open problem: infinite divisibility of the family mixture of the clocks of the characters modulo q](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_problem_infinite_divisibility_of_the_family_mixture_of_clocks_of_dirichlet_characters) (Problem 21.5, page 756; open): Decide whether the clock of a uniformly chosen character of the family modulo $q$ is infinitely divisible, and whether some $q$ with two or more members avoids the odd configuration of the mixture criterion for every pair of members. New in this book.
- [Open problem: a sign definite explicit formula for primes in the progressions a modulo q with a not congruent to 1](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_problem_sign_definite_explicit_formula_for_primes_in_progressions_not_congruent_to_one) (Problem 21.6, page 756; open): Find a sign definite explicit formula for $\psi(x;q,a)$ with $a\not\equiv1\pmod q$ in terms of the zero counting measures of cyclotomic fields and their Poisson smoothings, for which the case $a\equiv1$ is already an integral against a nonnegative measure under the Thorin property. New in this book.
- [Open problem: certified backward continuation of the Thorin density of the basepoint family from the primes into the critical strip](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_problem_certified_backward_continuation_of_the_thorin_density_from_the_primes) (Problem 21.7, page 756; open): Determine how far into the critical strip positivity of the Thorin density $\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}(f'/f)(\alpha+ib)$ can be certified from smoothed prime sums alone before the ill posedness of the backward step takes over. New in this book.
- [Open problem: the exponential sum over primes on the minor arcs as an expectation against the GGC laws of the clocks](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_problem_exponential_sum_over_primes_on_the_minor_arcs_as_an_expectation_against_ggc_laws) (Problem 21.8, page 757; open): Decide whether the exponential sum over primes on the minor arcs of the circle method for Linnik's problem can be written as an expectation against the GGC laws of the clocks, which would give a different route to the supremum bound on the minor arcs. New in this book.
- [Open problem: the best minor arc exponent in Linnik's problem from a zero free half plane for all Dirichlet L functions](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_problem_best_minor_arc_exponent_in_linnik_problem_from_a_zero_free_half_plane) (Problem 21.9, page 757; open): Under a zero free half plane $\operatorname{Re}s>\theta_0$ for all Dirichlet $L$ functions, find the best minor arc exponent for the sum over primes in Linnik's problem, and decide whether the half plane improves the large deviation parameter for the powers of two or the major arc constant. New in this book.
- [Open problem: does a finite order of total positivity of the density force the zeros onto the line, in a class of even entire functions containing xi](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#open_problem_finite_order_total_positivity_forcing_real_zeros_in_a_class_of_entire_functions) (Problem 21.10, page 757; open): Decide whether some finite order of total positivity of the density $f_F$ forces every zero of $F$ onto the imaginary axis, for every $F$ in the class of even entire functions with the order, type and reflection symmetry of $\xi(\frac12+s)/\xi(\frac12)$ whose reciprocal is a characteristic function. New in this book.

#### Key terms

Thorin measure, generalized gamma convolution, GGC, Dirichlet L function, Dedekind zeta function, Linnik constant, primes and powers of two, circle method, generalized Riemann hypothesis, GRH, Siegel zero, cyclotomic field, tilt, basepoint, sine squared lemma, centre clock, Blaschke product, zero free half plane

chapters.title: Friable approximants of Xi after Miyatake and the cosh ladder
chapters.summary:
Which real zeros does the friable approximant of the Riemann Xi function share with Xi, and what does this test case say about computational criteria for the Riemann Hypothesis (RH)? Keep only the integers composed of the primes up to $P$ (the $P$ friable, or smooth, integers) in Riemann's theta series. The result, the friable approximant $\Xi_P$, differs from $\Xi$ by an exponentially small deficit, of size about $4\pi q^2e^{-\pi q^2}$ with $q$ the first prime left out, and yet has infinitely many zeros off the real line. The chapter proves that the folded kernel has a kink, that no summable reweighting of the theta series has infinitely many real zeros, that the deficit is positive and a sum of Lorentzians, and that real zeros live in the negative humps of $\Xi$ and are lost in pairs, with an exact count given the verification of RH to a finite height. A heuristic formula (checked by computation) puts the breakdown at height about $4q^2$. It then reads an identity of Miyatake probabilistically (Lévy's stochastic area, a Pólya Gamma clock, a logistic partition of unity), studies the exponential tail and the threshold $b=2$ of the transform of the kernel divided by $\cosh(bu)$, and places the bottom of the cosh ladder against the quasi Riemann abscissa, with a Hermite Biehler equivalence for the paired form. Nothing here proves RH.

#### From the literature

- Riemann's theta series representation of $\xi$ and the zeros of $\Xi$ on the critical line (Hardy 1914; Titchmarsh 1986)
- friable approximants and the symmetrised Pólya kernel (Miyatake 1951; Hejhal 1990), truncated theta series in incomplete gamma form (Haglund 2009)
- the cosh ladder: reciprocals of $\cosh(bu)$ times the kernel are generalised gamma convolutions for $b\ge\frac12$ (de Bruijn 1950; Lagarias 1999)
- the de Bruijn Newman constant is nonnegative (Rodgers and Tao 2020)
- verification of RH to height $3\cdot10^{12}$ (Platt and Trudgian 2021); the bound $|\zeta(\frac12+it)|\ll t^{1/6}\log t$ with explicit constant (Hiary 2016)
- the Biane Pitman Yor identity (Biane, Pitman and Yor 2001), the Pólya Gamma mixture (Polson, Scott and Windle 2013), Ingham's density estimate (Ingham 1940), Chebotarev's theorem (Chebotarev 1928), the Davenport Heilbronn function (Davenport and Heilbronn 1936)

#### New results

Statements are proved unless marked: the imaginary axis proposition is a computation on a grid, the count conjecture and the quasi Riemann abscissa conjecture are open; the zero count heuristic and the problems are not catalogued.

- [The friable approximant of Xi is exponentially close to Xi in a strip, with the accuracy set by the first omitted prime](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#friable_approximant_error_bound_in_strip_set_by_first_omitted_prime) (Theorem 22.2.1, page 763; proved): For $|\operatorname{Im}t|\le\frac32$ the friable approximant satisfies $|\Xi_P(t)-\Xi(t)|\le|t^2+\frac14|\,\delta_P$ with $\delta_P\le e^{-\pi q^2}/(\pi q^2(1-e^{-2\pi q}))$. New in this book.
- [Certified tracking: a Rouche criterion for a real zero of the friable approximant near a simple zero of Xi](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#certified_tracking_of_a_simple_zero_of_xi_by_a_real_zero_of_the_friable_approximant) (Corollary 22.2.2, page 763; proved): If a simple zero $\gamma$ of $\Xi$ has $|\Xi|>|t^2+\frac14|\delta_P$ on a circle of radius $r\le\frac32$ about it, then $\Xi_P$ has exactly one zero in the disc, it is real, and its shift from $\gamma$ is given to first order by $-(\Xi_P-\Xi)(\gamma)/\Xi'(\gamma)$. New in this book.
- [The folded kernel of the friable approximant has a kink of exact size c_P, so Xi_P tends to c_P on the real line and has finitely many real zeros](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#kink_constant_of_the_friable_approximant_and_finitely_many_real_zeros) (Theorem 22.2.3, page 764; proved): The folded kernel of $\Xi_P$ has a corner at the origin of size $c_P=\sum_{m\notin\mathcal F(P)}(4\pi m^2-1)e^{-\pi m^2}\sim4\pi q^2e^{-\pi q^2}>0$, so $\Xi_P(t)\to c_P$ along the real axis and $\Xi_P$ has finitely many real zeros. New in this book.
- [No reweighting of Riemann's theta series by summable weights has infinitely many real zeros](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#no_summable_reweighting_of_the_theta_series_has_infinitely_many_real_zeros) (Theorem 22.2.4, page 764; proved): For nonzero real weights $w_n$ with $\sum|w_n|n^{-\sigma}<\infty$ for every $\sigma>0$ (this includes the friable truncations), the reweighted function has finitely many real zeros and infinitely many nonreal zeros. New in this book.
- [The deficit Xi_P minus Xi is positive on the real line and decreases as the prime bound grows](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#deficit_of_the_friable_approximant_is_positive_and_decreasing_in_the_prime_bound) (Theorem 22.3.1, page 765; proved): For every prime $P$ and real $t$, $\Xi_P(t)-\Xi(t)>0$, and the deficit decreases strictly as $P$ increases, so $\Xi_P>\Xi_{P'}>\Xi$ on $\mathbb{R}$ for $P<P'$. New in this book.
- [Uniform Lorentzian bound: the deficit of the friable approximant is a sum of Lorentzians with an explicit uniform relative error](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#deficit_of_the_friable_approximant_is_a_sum_of_lorentzians_with_explicit_error) (Theorem 22.3.3, page 766; proved): For $a\ge9\pi$ the cosine transform $C_a$ of $e^{-ae^w}e^{w/4}$ equals the Lorentzian $\mathcal L_a(t)=e^{-a}b/(b^2+t^2/4)$ with relative error at most $\delta(a)\le5.61/a$, uniformly in real $t$, and the deficit $D_P$ is the corresponding sum over the omitted integers. New in this book.
- [Curvature: the logarithm of the deficit of the friable approximant is uniformly almost convex for t at least 14](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#uniform_curvature_bound_for_the_log_of_the_deficit_of_the_friable_approximant) (Theorem 22.3.4, page 766; proved): For every prime $P$ and $t\ge14$, $(\log D_P)''(t)\ge-0.0239$ for the deficit $D_P=\Xi_P-\Xi$, with an explicit bound in terms of the least omitted prime. New in this book.
- [Real zeros of the friable approximant live in the negative humps of Xi, in pairs, and surviving humps are nested in P](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#real_zeros_of_the_friable_approximant_live_in_negative_humps_of_xi_in_pairs) (Theorem 22.4.1, page 767; proved): Every real zero of $\Xi_P$ lies in a negative hump of $\Xi$ and each hump holds an even number of zeros; for humps below the verified height of RH and shorter than $18.29$, a hump holds none, one double or two simple zeros, according to the sign of $\max(|\Xi|-D_P)$ on it, and surviving humps are nested in $P$. New in this book.
- [Count: the number of positive real zeros of the friable approximant is twice the number of negative humps of Xi deeper than the deficit](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#count_of_real_zeros_of_the_friable_approximant_is_twice_the_number_of_deep_humps) (Theorem 22.4.2, page 768; proved): Under the hypotheses of the hump theorem the number $R_P$ of positive real zeros of $\Xi_P$ is twice the number of humps with $\max(|\Xi|-D_P)>0$, there is a unique height $\tau_P^+$ beyond which $\Xi_P>0$, and $R_P\le2\lceil N(\tau_P^+)/2\rceil$. New in this book.
- [Conjecture: the number of real zeros of the friable approximant is the zero count at the breakdown height plus a correction from the peaks of Hardy's function](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#conjecture_on_the_number_of_real_zeros_of_the_friable_approximant_and_the_peaks_of_hardys_function) (Conjecture 22.5.1, page 770; open): The number $R_P$ of positive real zeros of $\Xi_P$ is conjectured to equal $N(\tau_P^*)$ plus $\frac2{\pi^2}\log\frac{\tau_P^*}{2\pi}$ times the mean log peak of Hardy's function on negative humps near $\tau_P^*$, up to an error of order $\sqrt{\log q\,\log\log q}$. New in this book.
- [Kink budget: the limit of the friable approximant with a smooth even kernel replacing the pole term](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#kink_budget_when_the_pole_kernel_is_replaced_by_a_smooth_even_kernel) (Proposition 22.8.1, page 774; proved): If the pole kernel $e^{-u/2}$ in the folded kernel of $\Xi_P$ is replaced by an even smooth kernel $\kappa$ with derivatives $O(e^{-u/2})$, the limit of the modified function along the real axis is $c_P-\frac12-\kappa'(0+)$. New in this book.
- [Reweighting: among weights in [0,1] vanishing on a given set, the indicator of the complement has the smallest deficit](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#reweighting_with_weights_in_zero_one_has_smallest_deficit_for_the_indicator_of_the_complement) (Proposition 22.8.2, page 775; proved): For weights $0\le w_n\le w_n'\le1$ the deficits satisfy $D_w\ge D_{w'}\ge0$ with $D_{w'}>0$ unless all $w_n'=1$, so the friable truncation has the smallest deficit among weights in $[0,1]$ that vanish on the omitted set. New in this book.
- [The friable approximants for P = 2 and 3 are uniformly close to Xi on the imaginary axis and have no zero there](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#friable_approximant_is_uniformly_close_to_xi_on_the_imaginary_axis_for_p_2_and_3) (Proposition 22.9.1, page 776; computed): The relative error $\sup_y|\Xi_P(iy)/\Xi(iy)-1|$ is at most $6.8\times10^{-13}$ for $P=2$ and $3.4\times10^{-35}$ for $P=3$, so neither has a zero on the imaginary axis; the suprema of a proved bound were computed on a grid. New in this book.
- [Shift identity: Xi is the average of two shifts of the transform of Phi divided by cosh, which contains Miyatake's identity](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#shift_identity_xi_is_the_cosine_of_a_shift_applied_to_the_transform_of_phi_over_cosh) (Proposition 22.11.1, page 779; proved): For every $b>0$ and complex $z$, $\Xi(z)=\frac12\{g_b(z+ib)+g_b(z-ib)\}$, that is $\Xi=\cos(b\,d/dz)g_b$; Miyatake's identity is the case $b=\frac92$. New in this book.
- [Levy area, Polya Gamma clock and Thorin atoms: the transform of Phi over cosh is Xi smoothed by Levy's stochastic area](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#transform_of_phi_over_cosh_is_a_levy_area_smoothing_and_a_polya_gamma_mixture_of_the_flow) (Theorem 22.11.2, page 779; proved): The transform $g_b$ equals the expectation of $\Xi(x+2b\mathcal A)$ for Lévy's stochastic area $\mathcal A$, and the expectation of the de Bruijn Newman function at a Pólya Gamma random negative time, so $\Xi\mapsto g_b$ is convolution with an extended generalised gamma convolution with Thorin atoms at the odd multiples of $\pi/(2b)$. New in this book.
- [Logistic partition: 2 xi is the sum of two logistic weighted expectations of a power of a random variable](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#logistic_partition_of_unity_splits_xi_into_two_pieces_of_the_transform_over_cosh) (Proposition 22.11.3, page 780; proved): For $c>0$, $2\xi(s)$ is the sum of the expectations of $\Upsilon^s/(1+\Upsilon^c)$ and $\Upsilon^{s+c}/(1+\Upsilon^c)$, for the random variable $\Upsilon$ of the Biane Pitman Yor identity, and the logistic weight is a Pólya Gamma mixture. New in this book.
- [Exponential tail: the transform of Phi over cosh has a residue term C_b e^{-pi z/(2b)} exactly when b exceeds 2](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#exponential_tail_of_the_transform_of_phi_over_cosh_appears_exactly_above_b_equal_two) (Theorem 22.12.1, page 780; proved): For $b>2$ the transform $g_b$ equals $C_be^{-\pi z/(2b)}$ plus a faster decaying error, with $C_b=\frac{2\pi}b\Phi(\frac{i\pi}{2b})$, uniformly in horizontal strips; for $b<2$ there is no residue and $g_b(x)=O(e^{-\tau x})$ for every $\tau<\pi/4$. New in this book.
- [Cusp asymptotics: the residue constant C_b of the transform of Phi over cosh as b decreases to 2](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#cusp_asymptotics_of_the_residue_constant_as_b_decreases_to_two) (Theorem 22.12.2, page 781; proved): With $\delta=\pi(b-2)/(4b)$, as $b\downarrow2$ the constant $C_b$ is asymptotic to $-\frac{\pi^3}{32b}(2\delta)^{-1/2}\delta^{-4}e^{-\frac\pi8\cot\delta}$ and is negative and super exponentially small. New in this book.
- [For b above 2 with C_b nonzero the transform of Phi over cosh has finitely many real zeros and is not in the Laguerre Polya class](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#transform_of_phi_over_cosh_for_b_above_two_is_not_in_the_laguerre_polya_class) (Corollary 22.12.3, page 781; proved): For $b>2$ with $C_b\ne0$ the transform $g_b$ has finitely many real zeros and infinitely many nonreal zeros, so it is not in the Laguerre Pólya class; in particular Miyatake's transform ($b=\frac92$, $C_{9/2}>0$) is not. New in this book.
- [The bottom of the cosh ladder is at most the largest real part of a zero of zeta minus one half](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#bottom_of_the_cosh_ladder_is_bounded_by_the_quasi_riemann_abscissa) (Proposition 22.13.1, page 783; proved): The bottom rung $B_{\cosh}$ of the cosh ladder satisfies $B_{\cosh}\le\sigma_{\max}-\frac12$, where $\sigma_{\max}$ is the supremum of the real parts of the nontrivial zeros of zeta. New in this book.
- [Conjecture: the bottom of the cosh ladder lies between the asymptotic and the global quasi Riemann abscissa](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#conjecture_bottom_of_the_cosh_ladder_equals_the_asymptotic_quasi_riemann_abscissa) (Conjecture 22.13.2, page 784; open): The bottom rung of the cosh ladder is conjectured to satisfy $\sigma_{\max}^\infty-\frac12\le B_{\cosh}\le\sigma_{\max}-\frac12$ with $\sigma_{\max}^\infty=\limsup_{\gamma\to\infty}\beta$; the upper bound is proved. New in this book.
- [Paired form: zeta has no zero to the right of alpha exactly when the real and imaginary parts of xi on the line alpha interlace](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#paired_form_of_the_cosh_ladder_hermite_biehler_equivalence_with_zero_free_half_plane) (Theorem 22.13.3, page 785; proved): For $\alpha>\frac12$, zeta has no zero with real part at least $\alpha$ exactly when $E_\alpha(z)=\xi(\alpha-iz)$ is Hermite Biehler, exactly when the real and imaginary parts of $\xi(\alpha+it)$ have only real simple strictly interlacing zeros; hence RH holds if and only if this holds for every $\alpha>\frac12$. New in this book.
- [Real zeros of the real and imaginary parts of xi on a vertical line right of one half have asymptotically full density](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#density_of_real_zeros_of_the_real_and_imaginary_parts_of_xi_on_a_line_to_the_right_of_one_half) (Theorem 22.13.4, page 787; proved): For $\alpha>\frac12$ with no zero of zeta on the line, $\theta_\alpha(T)-\theta_\alpha(-T)=\pi(N^\pm(T)-2N^\pm_{>\alpha}(T))+O(\log T)$, so $\operatorname{Re}\xi(\alpha+it)$ and $\operatorname{Im}\xi(\alpha+it)$ each have at least $N^\pm(T)-2N^\pm_{>\alpha}(T)-O(\log T)$ real zeros in $[-T,T]$. New in this book.

#### Key terms

friable approximant, smooth number approximation of Xi, Riemann Xi function, theta series truncation, kink constant, Lorentzian, negative hump, Hardy function, cosh ladder, quasi Riemann hypothesis, quasi Riemann abscissa, Miyatake, Lévy area, Pólya Gamma, generalised gamma convolution, generalized gamma convolution, GGC, Thorin measure, Laguerre Pólya class, Hermite Biehler, de Bruijn Newman

chapters.title: Haseo Ki and the Thorin programme
chapters.summary:
What does the work of Haseo Ki and his coauthors say about the Thorin condition on the reciprocal of the Riemann Xi function? Ki and his coauthors studied Fourier transforms of rapidly decaying positive kernels, their zeros under the heat flow (the de Bruijn Newman flow) and under repeated differentiation, and zeta functions with the functional equation of $\zeta$ but no Euler product. The chapter reads this through the Thorin dictionary: a zero of an even entire function is an atom of the Thorin measure of its reciprocal, and the reciprocal is a generalized gamma convolution (GGC) exactly when the zeros are real. It proves that after any positive time the reciprocal of the flowed function is a GGC transform up to a finite rational factor (the theorem of Ki, Kim and Lee), with the atoms of the factor confined to confocal parabolas that shrink with time. With the theorem of Rodgers and Tao this gives an obstruction: no property of the Pólya density that survives a Gaussian tilt can imply RH. For repeated differentiation, the rescaled reciprocals converge to the Laplace transform of the exit time of Brownian motion from an interval, a GGC, and a conjecture gives the rate. Epstein type zeta functions and the Davenport Heilbronn functions indicate that a Thorin argument must use the Euler product. Nothing here proves RH.

#### From the literature

- the heat flow on Fourier transforms of positive kernels, the de Bruijn Newman constant, and the zeros of $\Xi_t$ (de Bruijn 1950; Newman 1976; Ki and Kim 2002, 2003; Ki, Kim and Lee 2009)
- the de Bruijn Newman constant is nonnegative (Rodgers and Tao 2020)
- Newman's characterisation of the Lee and Yang single spin laws by the Laguerre Pólya class (Newman 1974)
- Ki's theorem on repeated differentiation, the zeros of $\zeta'$, and approximation theorems for Epstein type zeta functions and the Davenport Heilbronn functions (Ki and coauthors)

#### New results

Statements are proved unless marked: the Edgeworth rate is an open conjecture supported by computation, and the remark on what a Thorin proof must use is a heuristic and is not catalogued.

- [Eventually Thorin: after any positive time the reciprocal of the flowed Xi function is a GGC transform times a finite rational factor](https://vsokolov.org/books/computing_rh/results.html#after_any_positive_time_the_reciprocal_of_the_flowed_function_is_a_ggc_transform_up_to_a_rational_factor) (Proposition 23.2.1, page 794; proved): For every $t>0$ the ratio $\Xi_t(0)/\Xi_t(i\sqrt s)$ equals a generalised gamma convolution Laplace transform times a finite product $\prod_{\eta\in E_t}(1+s/\eta)^{-1}$ over a conjugation invariant multiset off the positive axis, which is empty exactly when $\Xi_t$ has only real zeros. New in this book.
