results.supersedes: Proposition 29.5 of Polson (2026) proves that the shifted reciprocal zeta function is not a generalised gamma convolution for $\sigma\le\frac12$ only (for $\frac12<\sigma<1$ it is verified numerically and not proved), and has no clause on self decomposability.
results.label: rz:prop:onlyhalf

results.name: Laguerre Pólya class as integer atom GGCs
results.origin_text: First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
results.summary: A real even entire function $G$ of order below 2 lies in the Laguerre Pólya class exactly when $G(0)/G(i\sqrt s)$ is the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution whose Thorin measure has integer masses at the squared zeros.
results.statement: Let $G$ be a real even entire function of order less than $2$ with $G(0)\ne0$. Then $G$ is in the Laguerre Pólya class (the locally uniform limits of real polynomials with only real zeros, which for such $G$ means that all zeros of $G$ are real) if and only if $s\mapsto G(0)/G(i\sqrt s)$ is the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution whose Thorin measure is $\sum_km_k\delta_{\alpha_k^2}$ with integers $m_k\ge1$, where $\pm\alpha_k$ are the zeros of $G$ with multiplicities $m_k$.
results.label: rz:prop:lpthorin

results.name: Lee and Yang single spin laws as integer atom GGCs
results.origin_text: First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
results.summary: A symmetric law with Gaussian moments of all orders has the Lee and Yang property exactly when the reciprocal of its moment generating function at $\sqrt s$ is the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution with integer atoms at the squared zeros of its characteristic function.
results.statement: Let $\rho$ be a symmetric probability law on $\mathbb{R}$ with $\int e^{bt^2}\rho(dt)<\infty$ for every $b$. Say that $\rho$ has the Lee and Yang property if ferromagnetic systems of $\rho$ spins have partition function zeros only on the imaginary field axis; by a theorem of Newman this holds exactly when $z\mapsto\int e^{izt}\rho(dt)$ is in the Laguerre Pólya class. Then $\rho$ has the Lee and Yang property if and only if $s\mapsto1/\int e^{\sqrt s\,t}\rho(dt)$ is the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution with zero drift whose Thorin measure has integer atoms. The atoms are at the squares $\alpha_k^2$ of the zeros $\pm\alpha_k$ of $\int e^{izt}\rho(dt)$, with the multiplicities of the zeros.
results.label: rz:prop:newmanthorin

results.name: Random harmonic series and the strip of the Pólya kernel
results.origin_text: First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
results.summary: The random harmonic series $H_\kappa$ has a double exponential tail whose leading constant equals that of the Pólya kernel exactly at $\kappa^*=6.61845\ldots$, and its density is analytic in the strip $|\operatorname{Im}t|<\pi/4$, the strip of analyticity of the Pólya kernel.
results.statement: Let $\Phi(t)=2\sum_{n\ge1}\bigl(2\pi^2n^4e^{9t/2}-3\pi n^2e^{5t/2}\bigr)\exp(-\pi n^2e^{2t})$ be the Pólya kernel, an even function whose Fourier transform $\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Phi(t)\cos(\tau t)\,dt$ is $\xi(\frac12+i\tau)$, with $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$; it is analytic in the strip $|\operatorname{Im}t|<\pi/4$ and $\log\Phi(t)=-\pi e^{2t}+\frac92t+O(1)$ as $t\to+\infty$. For $\kappa>-1$ let $\varepsilon_k$ be independent fair signs $\pm1$ and $H_\kappa=\sum_{k\ge1}\varepsilon_k/(2(k+\kappa))$, with characteristic function $\hat f_\kappa(v)=\prod_{k\ge1}\cos\bigl(v/(2(k+\kappa))\bigr)$ and density $f_\kappa$. (i) As $s\to\infty$, $\log\mathbb{E}e^{sH_\kappa}=\frac s2\log s+A(\kappa)s+o(s)$ with $A(\kappa)=A(0)-\frac12\bigl(\psi(1+\kappa)+\gamma_E\bigr)$, where $\psi$ is the digamma function, $\gamma_E$ is Euler's constant and $A(0)=-0.1485757\ldots$. Hence $\log\Pr(H_\kappa>u)=-\frac12e^{2u-2A(\kappa)-1}(1+o(1))$ as $u\to\infty$, and the double exponential terms of $H_\kappa$ and of $\Phi$ agree exactly when $A(\kappa)=-\frac12(1+\log2\pi)$, that is at $\kappa^*=6.61845\ldots$. (ii) $\limsup_{|v|\to\infty}|v|^{-1}\log|\hat f_\kappa(v)|=-\pi/4$ for every $\kappa>-1$. Hence $f_\kappa$ is analytic in the strip $|\operatorname{Im}t|<\pi/4$, which is exactly the strip of analyticity of $\Phi$.
results.label: rz:prop:harmonic

results.name: The reciprocal Xi transform is a harmonic mean of Brownian exit time transforms
results.summary: The Laplace transform of the clock, the reciprocal Xi function, is the harmonic mean over the Pólya density of the Laplace transforms $1/\cosh(x\sqrt s)$ of scaled Brownian exit times, so by Jensen's inequality it is at most the Laplace transform of the corresponding scale mixture.
results.statement: Let $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$ be the completed Riemann zeta function. The Pólya variable $X$ is the symmetric real random variable with density $\Phi/\xi(\frac12)$, where $\Phi(t)=\sum_{n\ge1}(4\pi^2n^4e^{9t/2}-6\pi n^2e^{5t/2})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{2t})$, and moment generating function $\mathbb{E}e^{sX}=\xi(\frac12+s)/\xi(\frac12)$. The clock $T$ is the nonnegative random variable with $\mathbb{E}e^{-sT}=\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt s)$ for $s\ge0$ (it exists with no hypothesis on the zeros). Let $C$ be the exit time of standard Brownian motion from $(-1,1)$, so that $\mathbb{E}e^{-\theta C}=1/\cosh\sqrt{2\theta}$, and for $x\ne0$ let $L_x(s)=1/\cosh(x\sqrt s)=\mathbb{E}\exp(-\tfrac12x^2sC)$, the Laplace transform of $\tfrac12x^2C$ (the transform of a generalized gamma convolution with Thorin atoms $\pi^2(k-\frac12)^2/x^2$, $k\ge1$). Then, for $s\ge0$, $\mathbb{E}e^{-sT}=1/\mathbb{E}\bigl[1/L_X(s)\bigr]$: the reciprocal Xi transform is the harmonic mean, over the Pólya density, of the Brownian exit time transforms $L_x$. By Jensen's inequality, $\mathbb{E}e^{-sT}\le\mathbb{E}\exp(-\tfrac12sX^2C)$, with $C$ independent of $X$.
results.label: xg:prop:harm

results.name: A harmonic mean of two GGC transforms that is not a Laplace transform of a positive measure
results.summary: The harmonic mean of the Laplace transforms $(1+s)^{-2}$ and $(1+2s)^{-2}$ of two generalized gamma convolutions (GGC) is $1/(1+3s+\frac52s^2)$, whose inverse transform $2e^{-0.6t}\sin(0.2t)$ is negative on $(5\pi,10\pi)$, so a harmonic mean of GGC transforms need not be the Laplace transform of a positive measure.
results.statement: A generalized gamma convolution (GGC) is a law on $[0,\infty)$ whose Laplace transform is $\exp\bigl(-bs-\int_{(0,\infty)}\log(1+s/z)\,U(dz)\bigr)$ with drift $b\ge0$ and Thorin measure $U\ge0$; in particular $(1+s)^{-2}$ and $(1+2s)^{-2}$ are GGC transforms, those of Gamma(2) laws with scale $1$ and $2$. Their harmonic mean with equal weights, $\bigl(\tfrac12(1+s)^2+\tfrac12(1+2s)^2\bigr)^{-1}$, equals $1/(1+3s+\tfrac52s^2)$. It has poles at $s=-0.6\pm0.2i$, and its inverse Laplace transform is $2e^{-0.6t}\sin(0.2t)$, which is negative on $(5\pi,10\pi)$. So the harmonic mean is not the Laplace transform of a positive measure, and in particular not a GGC transform: a harmonic mean of GGC transforms need not even be a Laplace transform of a positive measure.
results.label: xg:ex:harm

results.name: A two point scale mixture of Gamma(2) that is infinitely divisible and not a GGC
results.summary: A scale mixture of a Gamma(2) variable by an independent variable equal to $1$ or to a positive $\lambda\ne1$ with probability one half each is infinitely divisible but not a generalized gamma convolution, because its Laplace transform has nonreal zeros.
results.statement: A generalized gamma convolution (GGC) is a law on $[0,\infty)$ whose Laplace transform is $\exp\bigl(-bs-\int_{(0,\infty)}\log(1+s/z)\,U(dz)\bigr)$ with drift $b\ge0$ and Thorin measure $U\ge0$; such a Laplace transform has no zeros outside $(-\infty,0]$. Let $\Gamma_2$ be a Gamma(2) variable (density $te^{-t}$ on $(0,\infty)$) and $Y\ge0$ a random variable independent of $\Gamma_2$. Every scale mixture $\Gamma_2Y$ is infinitely divisible (Kristiansen 1994), and it is a GGC if $Y$ is a GGC, since products of independent GGC variables are GGC (Bondesson 2015). Without a hypothesis on $Y$ it need not be a GGC: let $Y$ equal $1$ or $\lambda$, with $\lambda>0$ and $\lambda\ne1$, with probability $\frac12$ each. The Laplace transform $\mathbb{E}(1+sY)^{-2}$ of $\Gamma_2Y$ has numerator $(1+\lambda s)^2+(1+s)^2$ over the denominator $2(1+s)^2(1+\lambda s)^2$, and the numerator vanishes at nonreal $s$. Hence $\Gamma_2Y$ is infinitely divisible but not a GGC.
results.label: xg:ex:g2

results.name: The clock is not a Gamma scale mixture, for any shape
results.summary: The clock is not a scale mixture of Gamma($a$) laws for any shape $a>0$, because the Laplace transform of such a mixture is at least a constant times $s^{-a}$ for large $s$, while that of the clock is at most a constant times $e^{-x\sqrt s}$ for every $x>0$.
results.statement: Let $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$ be the completed Riemann zeta function and $T$ the clock, the nonnegative random variable with $\mathbb{E}e^{-sT}=\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt s)$ for $s\ge0$ (it exists with no hypothesis on the zeros). For $a>0$ let $\Gamma_a$ be a gamma variable with shape $a$ and unit scale, with density $t^{a-1}e^{-t}/\Gamma(a)$ on $(0,\infty)$. Then for no $a>0$ and no random variable $Y\ge0$ independent of $\Gamma_a$ does $T$ have the law of $\Gamma_aY$. The proof uses no hypothesis on the zeros of $\xi$.
results.label: xg:thm:nogamma

results.name: First order expansion of the zeros of the truncated lattice transforms
results.origin_text: First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
results.summary: Near each simple zero $\rho$ of $\xi$ the truncated transform $F_n$ has exactly one zero, equal to $\rho/2+\kappa(\rho)/n+O(n^{-2})$ for large $n$, with an explicit constant $\kappa(\rho)$.
results.statement: Let $e_k,e_k'$ ($k\ge1$) be independent standard exponential random variables, $\mathcal S_n=\sum_{k\le n}k^{-2}(e_k+e_k')$ and $F_n(w)=\mathbb{E}\,\mathcal S_n^{\,w}$ for $\operatorname{Re}w>-2$. As $n\to\infty$, $F_n\to F$ locally uniformly on $\operatorname{Re}w>-2$, where $F(w)=\mathbb{E}\bigl[(\sum_{k\ge1}k^{-2}(e_k+e_k'))^w\bigr]=2\pi^w\xi(2w)$ and $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$ is the completed zeta function, so the zeros of $F$ are the points $\rho/2$ for the nontrivial zeros $\rho$ of $\zeta$. Let $\rho$ be a simple zero of $\xi$ and put \[ \kappa(\rho)=\frac{\rho\,\xi(\rho-2)}{2\pi\,\xi'(\rho)}=\frac{\rho\,\xi(3-\rho)}{2\pi\,\xi'(\rho)} . \] There is a constant $C$ (depending on $\rho$) such that for all large $n$, $F_n$ has exactly one zero $w_n(\rho)$ in the disc $\bigl|w-\frac\rho2-\frac{\kappa(\rho)}n\bigr|<C/n^2$; thus $w_n(\rho)=\frac\rho2+\frac{\kappa(\rho)}n+O(n^{-2})$.
results.label: rz:prop:firstorder

results.name: Displacement constant of the truncated zeros in terms of Hardy's function
results.origin_text: First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
results.summary: For a simple zero on the critical line, the real and imaginary parts of the displacement constant $\kappa(\rho)$ are given in closed form by the derivative of Hardy's function $Z$ and the number $e^{i\theta(\gamma)}\zeta(\frac52+i\gamma)$.
results.statement: Let $\rho=\frac12+i\gamma$ be a simple zero of $\zeta$ on the critical line, $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$, and $\kappa(\rho)=\rho\,\xi(\rho-2)/(2\pi\,\xi'(\rho))$ the constant of the first order displacement of the zeros of the truncated lattice transforms $F_n(w)=\mathbb{E}\bigl[(\sum_{k\le n}k^{-2}(e_k+e_k'))^w\bigr]$, with $e_k,e_k'$ independent standard exponentials. Let $\theta(t)=\arg\Gamma(\frac14+\frac{it}2)-\frac t2\log\pi$ be the Riemann Siegel theta function, $Z(t)=e^{i\theta(t)}\zeta(\frac12+it)$ Hardy's function, and $a(\gamma)=e^{i\theta(\gamma)}\zeta(\frac52+i\gamma)$. Then \begin{align*} \operatorname{Re}\kappa(\rho)&=\frac{(\gamma^2-\frac{15}4)\operatorname{Im}a(\gamma)-4\gamma\operatorname{Re}a(\gamma)}{4\pi^2Z'(\gamma)},\\ \operatorname{Im}\kappa(\rho)&=\frac{4\gamma\operatorname{Im}a(\gamma)+(\gamma^2-\frac{15}4)\operatorname{Re}a(\gamma)}{4\pi^2Z'(\gamma)} . \end{align*}
results.label: rz:thm:kappaexact

results.name: Conjecture T is false for large n
results.origin_text: First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
results.summary: Conjecture T, that no truncated lattice transform $F_n$ has a zero with real part above $\frac14$, is false: for all large $n$ there is such a zero near $\rho_{213}/2$, certified with a ball arithmetic enclosure of the displacement constant.
results.statement: Let $e_k,e_k'$ be independent standard exponential variables and $F_n(w)=\mathbb{E}\bigl[\bigl(\sum_{k\le n}k^{-2}(e_k+e_k')\bigr)^w\bigr]$ for $\operatorname{Re}w>-2$. Conjecture T says that for every $n\ge1$, $F_n$ has no zeros with $\operatorname{Re}w>\frac14$ (which, if it held for infinitely many $n$, would imply the Riemann Hypothesis by Hurwitz's theorem, since $F_n\to2\pi^w\xi(2w)$). Conjecture T is false: for all sufficiently large $n$, $F_n$ has a zero with $\operatorname{Re}w>\frac14$ near $\rho_{213}/2$, where $\rho_{213}=\frac12+i\gamma_{213}$ and $\gamma_{213}=415.4552\ldots$ is the ordinate of the 213th zero of the zeta function in the upper half plane. The proof uses that the first $1.5\times10^9$ zeros lie on the critical line and are simple (van de Lune, te Riele and Winter), the first order displacement $\kappa(\rho)=\rho\,\xi(\rho-2)/(2\pi\,\xi'(\rho))$ of the zero of $F_n$ near $\rho/2$, and a ball arithmetic enclosure $233.95<\operatorname{Re}\kappa(\rho_{213})<233.96$. The statement is for all sufficiently large $n$ and gives no explicit $n$; the book notes that the first order regime requires $n$ large compared with $|\kappa(\rho_{213})|\approx2311$.
results.label: rz:cor:Tfalse

results.name: Symmetrised truncations: symmetry, limit and persistence of simple zeros on the line
results.origin_text: First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
results.summary: The symmetrised truncations $K_n$ are symmetric about the line $\operatorname{Re}w=\frac14$, converge to $4\xi(2w)$, and keep every simple zero of $\xi(2w)$ on the line as a zero exactly on the line for all large $n$.
results.statement: Let $e_k,e_k'$ be independent standard exponential variables, $F_n(w)=\mathbb{E}\bigl[\bigl(\sum_{k\le n}k^{-2}(e_k+e_k')\bigr)^w\bigr]$ for $\operatorname{Re}w>-2$, and define the symmetrised truncation and its restriction to the line by \[ K_n(w)=\pi^{-w}F_n(w)+\pi^{w-\frac12}F_n(\tfrac12-w),\qquad Z_n(y)=K_n(\tfrac14+iy). \] Then $K_n(\frac12-w)=K_n(w)$ and $K_n(\bar w)=\overline{K_n(w)}$, so $Z_n$ is real for real $y$ and the zeros of $K_n$ off the line $\operatorname{Re}w=\frac14$ come in quadruples. As $n\to\infty$, $K_n\to4\,\xi(2w)$ locally uniformly on $-\frac74<\operatorname{Re}w<\frac94$, where $\xi$ is the completed zeta function. Every simple zero $\frac14+i\frac\gamma2$ of $\xi(2w)$ on the line $\operatorname{Re}w=\frac14$ is, for all large $n$, the limit of a zero of $K_n$ lying exactly on that line.
results.label: rz:prop:symtrunc

results.name: Real rooted symmetrised truncations for infinitely many n imply the Riemann Hypothesis
results.origin_text: First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
results.summary: If for infinitely many $n$ all zeros of the symmetrised truncation $K_n$ in the strip $0<\operatorname{Re}w<\frac12$ lie on the line $\operatorname{Re}w=\frac14$, then the Riemann Hypothesis holds.
results.statement: Let $e_k,e_k'$ be independent standard exponential variables, $F_n(w)=\mathbb{E}\bigl[\bigl(\sum_{k\le n}k^{-2}(e_k+e_k')\bigr)^w\bigr]$ for $\operatorname{Re}w>-2$, and $K_n(w)=\pi^{-w}F_n(w)+\pi^{w-\frac12}F_n(\tfrac12-w)$. If for infinitely many $n$ all zeros of $K_n$ in the strip $0<\operatorname{Re}w<\frac12$ lie on the line $\operatorname{Re}w=\frac14$, then the Riemann Hypothesis holds.
results.label: rz:thm:symhurwitz

results.name: Single term bound: no off line zeros of the symmetrised truncation above explicit heights
results.origin_text: First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
results.summary: A single term bound shows that for $n=1$ to $6$, $8$ and $10$ the symmetrised truncation $K_n$ has no zero off the line in the strip above explicit heights $Y_n$ between $4.81$ and $21232$, which are obtained by evaluating the explicit bounds numerically.
results.statement: For $n\ge1$ let $\alpha_k,\beta_k$ ($k\le n$) be defined by the partial fraction expansion $\prod_{j\le n}(1+\lambda/j^2)^{-2}=\sum_{k\le n}k^{-2}\bigl\{\alpha_k(1+\lambda/k^2)^{-1}+\beta_k(1+\lambda/k^2)^{-2}\bigr\}$ (so $\beta_k=k^2\prod_{j\le n,\,j\ne k}(1-k^2/j^2)^{-2}$ and $\alpha_k=-2\beta_k\sum_{j\le n,\,j\ne k}k^2/(j^2-k^2)$), and put $Q_n(u)=\sum_{k\le n}k^{-2u}(\alpha_k+\beta_ku)$. Then $F_n(u-1)=\Gamma(u)Q_n(u)$ for $F_n(w)=\mathbb{E}\bigl[\bigl(\sum_{k\le n}k^{-2}(e_k+e_k')\bigr)^w\bigr]$ with $e_k,e_k'$ independent standard exponentials, and the symmetrised truncation is $K_n(w)=\pi^{-w}F_n(w)+\pi^{w-\frac12}F_n(\frac12-w)$. For $y>|\alpha_1|/|\beta_1|$ let \[ \delta_n(y)=\sum_{k=2}^nk^{-2}\frac{|\beta_k|y+|\alpha_k|}{|\beta_1|y-|\alpha_1|},\qquad \delta_n'(y)=\sum_{k=2}^nk^{-2}\frac{2\log k\,(|\beta_k|y+|\alpha_k|)+|\beta_k|}{|\beta_1|y-|\alpha_1|}+\delta_n(y)\,\frac{|\beta_1|}{|\beta_1|y-|\alpha_1|}, \] where $\delta_n'$ is a bound for a derivative used in the proof and is not the derivative of $\delta_n$. If $\delta_n(y)<1$ and \[ \log\frac y\pi-\frac1y-\frac{|\beta_1|}{|\beta_1|y-|\alpha_1|}-\frac{\delta_n'(y)}{1-\delta_n(y)}>0, \] then $K_n$ has no zeros off the line $\operatorname{Re}w=\frac14$ in $0<\operatorname{Re}w<\frac12$ at any height (imaginary part) at least $y$. The condition holds for all $y\ge Y_n$, with $Y_1=4.81$, $Y_2=5.85$, $Y_3=7.11$, $Y_4=9.08$, $Y_5=12.8$, $Y_6=20.8$, $Y_8=104.1$ and $Y_{10}=21232$ (values obtained by evaluating the bounds with the exact coefficients).
results.label: rz:thm:Yn

results.name: Conjecture S for n up to 6 and n = 8 above explicit heights
results.origin_text: First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
results.summary: Conjecture S is proved for $n=1$ to $6$ and $n=8$ above the explicit heights of the single term bound, which are evaluated numerically, and below those heights it is only checked numerically by floating point argument principle counts.
results.statement: Let $K_n(w)=\pi^{-w}F_n(w)+\pi^{w-\frac12}F_n(\frac12-w)$ be the symmetrised truncation, with $F_n(w)=\mathbb{E}\bigl[\bigl(\sum_{k\le n}k^{-2}(e_k+e_k')\bigr)^w\bigr]$ and $e_k,e_k'$ independent standard exponential variables. Conjecture S says that all zeros of $K_n$ in the strip $0<\operatorname{Re}w<\frac12$ lie on the line $\operatorname{Re}w=\frac14$. Proved: for $n=1,2,3,4,5,6,8$ the zeros of $K_n$ in the strip at height at least $Y_n$ lie on the line, with $Y_1=4.81$, $Y_2=5.85$, $Y_3=7.11$, $Y_4=9.08$, $Y_5=12.8$, $Y_6=20.8$, $Y_8=104.1$ (the heights of the single term bound). Below these heights the book verifies the same statement for these $n$ only numerically, by floating point argument principle counts and not by an enclosure (up to heights $6,7,8$ for $n=1,2,3$, up to $70$ for $4\le n\le6$ and up to $140$ for $n=8$); that part is not a certified result.
results.label: rz:cor:Ssmall

results.name: Torus bound for the symmetrised truncations
results.origin_text: First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
results.summary: Explicit inequalities on the extremes of the Dirichlet polynomial $P_n$ and its logarithmic derivative over the torus of prime phases imply that the symmetrised truncation $K_n$ has no zero off the line $\operatorname{Re}w=\frac14$ in the strip $0<\operatorname{Re}w<\frac12$ at a given height or above.
results.statement: Let $\alpha_k,\beta_k$ ($k\le n$) be defined by $\prod_{j\le n}(1+\lambda/j^2)^{-2}=\sum_{k\le n}k^{-2}\bigl\{\alpha_k(1+\lambda/k^2)^{-1}+\beta_k(1+\lambda/k^2)^{-2}\bigr\}$, so that $F_n(u-1)=\Gamma(u)Q_n(u)$ with $Q_n(u)=\sum_{k\le n}k^{-2u}(\alpha_k+\beta_ku)=uP_n(u)+R_n(u)$, $P_n(u)=\sum_{k\le n}\beta_kk^{-2u}$, $R_n(u)=\sum_{k\le n}\alpha_kk^{-2u}$, for $F_n(w)=\mathbb{E}\bigl[\bigl(\sum_{k\le n}k^{-2}(e_k+e_k')\bigr)^w\bigr]$ with $e_k,e_k'$ independent standard exponentials, and let $K_n(w)=\pi^{-w}F_n(w)+\pi^{w-\frac12}F_n(\frac12-w)$. For real $x$ and $\omega=(\omega_p)_{p\le n}$ in the torus $\mathbb{T}^{\pi(n)}$ of phases indexed by the primes $p\le n$, put $P_n(x,\omega)=\sum_{k\le n}\beta_kk^{-2x}\exp\bigl(-i\sum_{p\le n}v_p(k)\,\omega_p\bigr)$, where $v_p(k)$ is the exponent of $p$ in $k$, let $P_n'(x,\omega)=-\sum_{k\le n}2\log k\,\beta_kk^{-2x}\exp\bigl(-i\sum_{p\le n}v_p(k)\,\omega_p\bigr)$, $r(x)=\sum_{k\le n}|\alpha_k|k^{-2x}$ and $r'(x)=\sum_{k\le n}2\log k\,|\alpha_k|k^{-2x}$. Let $m_n=\min|P_n(x,\omega)|$, $M_n=\max\{-\operatorname{Re}(P_n'/P_n)(x,\omega)\}$ and $\ell_n=\max|P_n'/P_n|(x,\omega)$ over $\omega\in\mathbb{T}^{\pi(n)}$ and the band $1.2\le x\le1.3$, and \[ B_n(y)=\max_{0.3\le\sigma\le\frac12,\ \omega}\ \frac{\log\bigl(|P_n(\tfrac32-\sigma,\omega)|+r(\tfrac32-\sigma)/y\bigr)-\log\bigl(|P_n(1+\sigma,\omega)|-r(1+\sigma)/y\bigr)}{2\sigma-\frac12}. \] If $m_n>r(1.2)/y$, \[ \log\frac y\pi-\frac2y-M_n-\frac{\ell_n\,r(1.2)+r'(1.2)+r(1.2)/y}{y\,\bigl(m_n-r(1.2)/y\bigr)}>0\quad\text{and}\quad\log\frac y\pi-\frac1y>B_n(y), \] then $K_n$ has no zeros off the line $\operatorname{Re}w=\frac14$ in $0<\operatorname{Re}w<\frac12$ at height $y$, and the same holds at every larger height.
results.label: rz:thm:torus

results.name: Conjecture S for n up to 24, 32 and 36 above explicit thresholds
results.origin_text: Corrects a statement of Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
results.summary: Conjecture S is proved for $n=7$, $9$ to $24$, $32$ and $36$ above explicit height thresholds by torus bounds certified in ball arithmetic, and below the thresholds it is only checked numerically; with the small $n$ results it covers every $n\le24$ and $n=32,36$.
results.statement: Let $K_n(w)=\pi^{-w}F_n(w)+\pi^{w-\frac12}F_n(\frac12-w)$ be the symmetrised truncation, with $F_n(w)=\mathbb{E}\bigl[\bigl(\sum_{k\le n}k^{-2}(e_k+e_k')\bigr)^w\bigr]$ and $e_k,e_k'$ independent standard exponential variables. Conjecture S says that all zeros of $K_n$ in the strip $0<\operatorname{Re}w<\frac12$ lie on the line $\operatorname{Re}w=\frac14$. Proved, by torus bounds whose final boxes are enclosed in ball arithmetic: for $n=16,17,\dots,24,32,36$ the zeros of $K_n$ in the strip at height at least the threshold lie on the line, with thresholds $30,34,37,41,46,50,56,62,69$ for $n=16,\dots,24$ and $213$, $558$ for $n=32$, $36$; and the same holds for $n=7$ and $9\le n\le15$ above the thresholds $14,24,31,41,57,84,131,229$ for $n=7,9,10,11,12,13,14,15$. For all these $n$ the statement is also verified numerically below the thresholds, by floating point argument principle counts, which are not certified. Together with the case $n=1,\dots,6,8$ above explicit heights, this covers every $n\le24$ and $n=32,36$. The torus bounds behind the thresholds are proved in the book; in Polson's 2026 book On Hilbert's 8th Problem the corresponding corollary supposes that the extremes of the torus function, estimated by global optimisation and not enclosed, are bounds.
results.supersedes: Corollary 30.11 of Polson (2026) is conditional: it supposes that the torus extremes, estimated by global optimisation and not enclosed, are bounds.
results.label: rz:cor:Storus

results.name: Thorin positivity of R is Weil's criterion
results.origin_text: Corrects a statement of Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
results.summary: The reciprocal Xi function $R$ is the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution exactly when Weil's distribution is positive definite, by combining Polson's rigidity theorem with Weil's criterion, so Thorin positivity of $R$ is Weil's criterion in other coordinates and gives no new criterion.
results.statement: Let $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$ and $R(s)=\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt s)$. Let $D(x)=\sum_\rho e^{(\rho-\frac12)x}$ be Weil's distribution, summed over the nontrivial zeros $\rho$ of $\zeta$, whose action on a test function $h$ is $\sum_\rho\hat h(\gamma_\rho)$ with $\gamma_\rho=-i(\rho-\frac12)$ and $\hat h$ the Fourier transform of $h$. Then $R$ is the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution (whose Thorin measure is then $\sum_{\gamma>0}\delta_{\gamma^2}$ over the ordinates of the zeros) if and only if $D$ is positive definite, that is, $\sum_\rho\hat h(\gamma_\rho)\ge0$ for every $h=g*\tilde g$ with $g$ smooth and compactly supported and $\tilde g(x)=\overline{g(-x)}$. Both conditions are equivalent to the Riemann Hypothesis: the first by Proposition 3.4 of Polson's 2026 book On Hilbert's 8th Problem, the second by Weil's criterion (Weil 1952; Bombieri 2000). The proposition combines the two; the correspondence between Thorin measures and Weil's distribution behind it is formal.
results.supersedes: Theorem 30.13 of Polson (2026) states the correspondence between Thorin positivity of $R$ and positive definiteness of Weil's distribution as a theorem.
results.label: rz:thm:weil

results.name: Weil positivity on the Bernstein cone
results.origin_text: Corrects a statement of Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
results.summary: Unconditionally, Weil's functional $\sum_\rho\hat h(\gamma_\rho)$ is positive for every test function $\hat h$ that is a Laplace transform in $r^2$ of a nonnegative weight under an integrability condition, including Thorin type products, $\operatorname{sech}(cr)$ and $(1+r^2/a)^{-m}$; it integrates the positivity of the heat trace of the zeros (Polson 2026, Theorem A), for which the book gives a second proof certified with the verification of RH to height 50 and interval enclosures.
results.statement: For $y>0$ let $W(y)=\frac12\sum_\rho e^{y(\rho-\frac12)^2}$, the sum over all nontrivial zeros $\rho$ of the Riemann zeta function (the heat trace of the zeros), and put $\gamma_\rho=-i(\rho-\frac12)$. Let $\hat h(r)=\int_0^\infty e^{-yr^2}g(y)\,dy$ with $g\ge0$, $g\not\equiv0$ and $\int_0^1g(y)\,y^{-1/2}\bigl(1+\log(1/y)\bigr)\,dy+\int_1^\infty g(y)\,dy<\infty$, so that $\hat h$ is a completely monotone function of $r^2$. Then \[ \sum_\rho\hat h(\gamma_\rho)=2\int_0^\infty W(y)\,g(y)\,dy>0, \] the sum being over all nontrivial zeros. In particular Weil's functional $\sum_\rho\hat h(\gamma_\rho)$ is positive for every test function of Thorin type $\hat h(r)=\prod_k(1+r^2/t_k)^{-1}$ (a nonempty product with $t_k>0$ and $\sum_k1/t_k<\infty$), for $\hat h(r)=\operatorname{sech}(cr)$ with $c>0$, and for $\hat h(r)=(1+r^2/a)^{-m}$ with $a>0$ and $m>\frac12$. No hypothesis on the zeros is made. The positivity of $W(y)$ for every $y>0$, which with the identity gives the result, is Theorem A of Polson's 2026 book On Hilbert's 8th Problem; the book gives a second proof of it, which uses the verification of the Riemann Hypothesis up to height $50$ and interval enclosures, and corrects the integrability condition and the examples of Theorem 30.14 of that book.
results.supersedes: Theorem 30.14 of Polson (2026) has the integrability condition with $\log(1/y)$ in place of $1+\log(1/y)$, Thorin products without nonemptiness or $\sum_k1/t_k<\infty$, and $(1+r^2/a)^{-m}$ without $m>\frac12$, and its proof uses the verification of the Riemann Hypothesis to height $3\times10^{12}$.
results.label: rz:thm:bernsteincone

results.name: The de Bruijn Newman flow as a path of GGCs
results.origin_text: First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
results.summary: For every $t$ at least the de Bruijn Newman constant, $R_t=H_t(0)/H_t(2i\sqrt s)$ is the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution with atoms at the squared half zeros of $H_t$, so it is a GGC for every $t\ge0.2$ unconditionally, and the Riemann Hypothesis holds exactly when $R_t$ is a GGC for arbitrarily small $t>0$.
results.statement: Let $\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(u)=\sum_{n\ge1}\bigl(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u}-3\pi n^2e^{5u}\bigr)\exp(-\pi n^2e^{4u})$, $H_t(z)=\int_0^\infty e^{tu^2}\Phi_{\mathrm{dBN}}(u)\cos(zu)\,du$ (so that $H_0(z)=\frac18\xi(\frac12+\frac{iz}2)$ for the completed zeta function $\xi$) and $R_t(s)=H_t(0)/H_t(2i\sqrt s)$, so that $R_0(s)=\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt s)=R(s)$. Let $\Lambda$ be the de Bruijn Newman constant, so that $H_t$ has only real zeros exactly when $t\ge\Lambda$. Then for every $t\ge\Lambda$, $R_t$ is the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution with Thorin measure $\sum_k\delta_{(z_k(t)/2)^2}$, where $z_k(t)>0$ are the positive zeros of $H_t$ listed with multiplicity. In particular $R_t$ is a GGC for every $t\ge0.2$, unconditionally (using the bound $\Lambda\le0.2$ of Platt and Trudgian, which improves the bound $0.22$ of the Polymath project). The Riemann Hypothesis holds if and only if $R_t$ is a GGC for arbitrarily small $t>0$ (and, since $\Lambda\ge0$ by Rodgers and Tao, if and only if $\Lambda=0$).
results.label: rz:thm:dbn

results.name: No GGC multiplier can create the positivity of R
results.origin_text: Corrects a statement of Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
results.summary: Multiplying $R$ by the Laplace transform of any generalised gamma convolution gives a generalised gamma convolution exactly when the Riemann Hypothesis holds, so no such multiplier can manufacture the positivity; for the normalised reciprocal zeta function only one direction holds for every multiplier.
results.statement: Let $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$, $R(s)=\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt s)$, $G(s)=\Gamma(\frac14+\frac{\sqrt s}2)\,\pi^{-\sqrt s/2}/\Gamma(\frac14)$ and $\varphi(s)=R(s)G(s)=\zeta(\frac12)/\bigl((1-4s)\zeta(\frac12+\sqrt s)\bigr)$, and let $c=\frac12(\log\pi-\psi(\frac14))\approx2.68609$ with $\psi$ the digamma function. Let $V$ be the Laplace transform of any generalised gamma convolution (GGC). Then $V\cdot R$ is the Laplace transform of a GGC if and only if the Riemann Hypothesis holds. For $\varphi$ only one direction holds for every $V$: if $V\cdot\varphi$ is the Laplace transform of a GGC, then the Riemann Hypothesis holds. The converse depends on $V$: it fails for $V\equiv1$ (since $\varphi$ is not a GGC, unconditionally), and holds for $V(s)=e^{-c\sqrt s}/G(s)$, which is the Laplace transform of a GGC and for which $V\varphi=e^{-c\sqrt s}R$ is the floor of the reciprocal Xi function. In Polson's 2026 book On Hilbert's 8th Problem the same is claimed with $\varphi$ in place of $R$, that is, both directions for every multiplier, which fails for $V\equiv1$; the book keeps one direction.
results.supersedes: Proposition 30.16 of Polson (2026) states that the same is true with $\varphi$ in place of $R$, that is, both directions for every generalised gamma convolution multiplier, which fails for the multiplier $1$ by Theorem 28.9 of that book.
results.label: rz:prop:nomult

results.name: Conjecture S for infinitely many n
results.origin_text: First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
results.summary: The book asks for a proof that the symmetrised truncations $K_n$ have all their zeros in the strip $0<\operatorname{Re}w<\frac12$ on the line $\operatorname{Re}w=\frac14$ for infinitely many $n$, which would imply the Riemann Hypothesis.
results.statement: Let $e_k,e_k'$ be independent standard exponential variables, $F_n(w)=\mathbb{E}\bigl[\bigl(\sum_{k\le n}k^{-2}(e_k+e_k')\bigr)^w\bigr]$ for $\operatorname{Re}w>-2$, and $K_n(w)=\pi^{-w}F_n(w)+\pi^{w-\frac12}F_n(\frac12-w)$ the symmetrised truncation. Conjecture S: for every $n\ge1$ all zeros of $K_n$ in the strip $0<\operatorname{Re}w<\frac12$ lie on the line $\operatorname{Re}w=\frac14$. Problem: prove that this holds for infinitely many $n$; by a Hurwitz argument this would imply the Riemann Hypothesis. The book proves it above explicit heights for $n\le24$ and $n=32,36$ and checks it numerically below those heights. Since the one sided Conjecture T (no zero of $F_n$ with $\operatorname{Re}w>\frac14$) and the Hermite Biehler inequality for $\pi^{-w}F_n(w)$ fail for large $n$, a proof must establish real rootedness without a one sided inequality, for instance by an interlacing argument in $n$, or by following the zeros of $K_n(\frac14+iy)$ continuously in a parameter interpolating between $n$ and $n+1$ and excluding collisions of zeros on the line.
results.label: rz:prob:S

results.name: Torus method beyond n = 36
results.origin_text: First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
results.summary: The book asks for an extension of the torus bound for the symmetrised truncations with narrower bands around $x=\frac54$, and for the first $n$ at which the torus function $P_n$ has zeros with $x\ge\frac54$.
results.statement: Let $\alpha_k,\beta_k$ ($k\le n$) be the partial fraction coefficients of the Laplace transform $\prod_{j\le n}(1+\lambda/j^2)^{-2}$ of $\sum_{k\le n}k^{-2}(e_k+e_k')$, with $\beta_k=k^2\prod_{j\le n,\,j\ne k}(1-k^2/j^2)^{-2}$, and let $P_n(x,\omega)=\sum_{k\le n}\beta_kk^{-2x}\exp\bigl(-i\sum_{p\le n}v_p(k)\,\omega_p\bigr)$ be the torus function of the Dirichlet polynomial $P_n(u)=\sum_{k\le n}\beta_kk^{-2u}$ (phases $\omega_p$ indexed by the primes $p\le n$, $v_p(k)$ the exponent of $p$ in $k$). The torus method proves Conjecture S, that all zeros of the symmetrised truncation $K_n$ in $0<\operatorname{Re}w<\frac12$ lie on $\operatorname{Re}w=\frac14$, above explicit heights for $n=7$, $9\le n\le24$ and $n=32,36$ (the cases $n\le6$ and $n=8$ come from a single term bound); at $n=40$ the threshold, estimated by optimisation and not certified, is already near $4900$, and with the band $1.2\le x\le1.3$ the method ends between $n=40$ and $n=44$, where the torus minimum of $|P_n|$ in the band reaches zero. Problem: extend the torus bound with narrower bands around $x=\frac54$, and find the first $n$ at which $P_n$ has torus zeros with $x\ge\frac54$.
results.label: rz:prob:torus

results.name: From finite order to all orders for the floor
results.origin_text: First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
results.summary: The book asks whether the argument that proves $(-1)^nk^{(n)}(y)>0$ for the canonical function $k$ of the floor of the reciprocal Xi function up to order $10^{10}$ extends to every order, which would imply the Riemann Hypothesis; the signs are already known to order $10^{17}$ (Polson 2017, version 24 of 2026) and, by the book's heat trace estimates, to order $1.16\times10^{25}$.
results.statement: Let $W(y)=\frac12\sum_\rho e^{y(\rho-\frac12)^2}$, the sum over the nontrivial zeros $\rho$ of the Riemann zeta function, let $c=\frac12(\log\pi-\psi(\frac14))\approx2.68609$, and let $k(y)=W(y)+c/(2\sqrt{\pi y})$ be the canonical function of the floor $e^{-c\sqrt s}\,\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt s)$ of the reciprocal Xi function. The book proves, by a two range argument, that $(-1)^nk^{(n)}(y)>0$ for every $y>0$ and every $n\le10^{10}$, the bound on $n$ in that argument coming only from the height $3\times10^{12}$ to which the Riemann Hypothesis is verified, and the small $y$ branch of the proof holds for every $n$ on $(0,0.05/n]$. This is a separate proof of a smaller range: the same signs hold for every $n\le10^{17}$ by Theorem 7.10 of Polson's arXiv paper 1708.02653 (version 24, 2026), which proves them for $W$, and the book proves them for every $n\le1.16\times10^{25}$ by sharper estimates of the heat trace; the signs for every $n$ would make $k$ completely monotone, which is equivalent to the Riemann Hypothesis. Problem: can the two regimes be made to overlap for all $n$? This asks for a prime side estimate for $(-1)^nk^{(n)}(y)$ on a range $y\le y_n$ with $y_n$ growing at least linearly in $n$. In the proof the obstruction is the factor $2^n$ in the Cauchy estimate on the circle of radius $y/2$; a circle of radius close to $y$ loses only a factor of order $n$, but that argument also stops at a finite order.
results.label: rz:prob:allorders

results.name: Beyond the Bernstein cone
results.origin_text: First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
results.summary: The book asks for the largest cone of test functions, closed under the operations that preserve the Thorin structure, on which Weil positivity can be proved unconditionally, and for how far such a cone can localise in height.
results.statement: Weil's functional $\sum_\rho\hat h(\gamma_\rho)$, with $\gamma_\rho=-i(\rho-\frac12)$ for the nontrivial zeros $\rho$ of the Riemann zeta function, is unconditionally positive for every test function $\hat h$ completely monotone in $r^2$ under an integrability condition (the Bernstein cone). Problem: find the largest cone of test functions, closed under the operations that preserve the Thorin structure, on which positivity of Weil's functional can be proved unconditionally, and determine how far it can localise in height.
results.label: rz:prob:cone

results.name: Deforming the binary product
results.origin_text: First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
results.summary: The book asks where and how the positivity of the interference pattern of arithmetic progressions in the pseudo spectral trace formula can fail along the path from the binary product at $\sigma=0$ to the critical line.
results.statement: With the necklace weights $b_n(q)$ of the Vere-Jones factorisation, each Euler factor $(1-p^{-\sigma-u})^{-1}$ of $\zeta(\sigma+u)$ equals $\prod_{n\ge1}(1+p^{-nu})^{b_n(p^{-\sigma})}$, with integer multiplicities $0$ and $1$ at $\sigma=0$ (Euler's binary product) and necklace multiplicities $b_n(p^{-1/2})$ at $\sigma=\frac12$. The pseudo spectral trace formula writes the heat trace of the zeros of $\zeta$ (under the Riemann Hypothesis $\sum_{\gamma>0}e^{-x\gamma^2}$, and in general $\frac12\sum_\rho e^{x(\rho-\frac12)^2}$), net of its smooth part, as $e^{x/4}$ plus the sum over primes $p$ and $n\ge1$ of $b_n(p^{-1/2})$ times the heat trace $\sum_{k\ge0}e^{-x((2k+1)\pi/(n\log p))^2}$ of the arithmetic progression $(2k+1)\pi/(n\log p)$, net of its mean $n\log p/(4\sqrt{\pi x})$. Problem: follow this formula along the path $q=p^{-\sigma}$, $0\le\sigma\le\frac12$, and determine where and how the positivity of the interference pattern of the progressions can fail.
results.label: rz:prob:binary

results.name: Regularising the autocorrelation of the Pólya kernel
results.origin_text: Corrects a statement of Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
results.summary: The book asks for the regularised form of the Meixner characteristic function convolved with the positive lattice measure $\mathcal A$, and whether it has a Thorin or Lee and Yang structure in $v$.
results.statement: Let $p(\tau)=|\Gamma(\frac14+\frac{i\tau}2)|^2/(2^{3/2}\pi^{3/2})$ be the Meixner density, $\Phi$ the Pólya kernel (an even function with Fourier transform $\Xi(\tau)=\xi(\frac12+i\tau)$) and $\mathcal C(v)=\int p(\tau)\,|\zeta(\frac12+i\tau)|^2e^{iv\tau}\,d\tau$. Then $(\Phi*\Phi)(v)=2^{-3/2}\bigl(\frac{d^2}{dv^2}-\frac14\bigr)^2\mathcal C(v)$. Formally $\mathcal C=\operatorname{sech}(\cdot)^{1/2}*\mathcal A$, where $\operatorname{sech}(v)^{1/2}$ is the characteristic function of the Meixner law and $\mathcal A=\sum_{m,n\ge1}(mn)^{-1/2}\delta_{\log(m/n)}$ is a positive, positive definite measure. The lattice series diverges: truncated at $m,n\le X$ it grows linearly in $X$, through the square of the pole term of the partial sums of $\zeta$, and the factor $(\frac{d^2}{dv^2}-\frac14)^2$ does not remove this growth. Problem: find the regularised form of $\operatorname{sech}(\cdot)^{1/2}*\mathcal A$ and decide whether it has a Thorin or Lee and Yang structure in $v$. In Polson's 2026 book On Hilbert's 8th Problem the problem is posed up to a logarithmic divergence removed by the pole; the book finds linear growth that the factor does not remove.
results.supersedes: Open Problem 30.22 of Polson (2026) poses the problem up to a logarithmic divergence removed by the pole.
results.label: rz:prob:meixner

results.name: Unimodality of w and of the density f
results.origin_text: Corrects a statement of Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
results.summary: The book asks for proofs that the canonical function $w$ of the normalised reciprocal zeta function and the density $f$ of its law are unimodal, which is supported only by numerical evidence.
results.statement: Let $w(x)=e^{x/4}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{4\pi x}}\sum_{n\ge2}\Lambda(n)\,n^{-1/2}e^{-(\log n)^2/4x}$ be the canonical function of the normalised reciprocal zeta function $\varphi(s)=\zeta(\frac12)/\bigl((1-4s)\zeta(\frac12+\sqrt s)\bigr)$ and $f$ the density of the law with Laplace transform $\varphi$, which satisfies Steutel's equation $xf(x)=\int_0^xf(x-y)\,w(y)\,dy$. The book proves that $w'>0$ on $(0,0.004]$ and $w'<0$ on $[4.52,\infty)$; a grid evaluation (computed, not proved) finds exactly one sign change of $w'$ on $[0.004,4.6]$, at $x_m=0.015851\ldots$, and numerically $f$ rises from $0.365089$ to its maximum $0.366883$ at $x=0.024046$ and then decreases. Problem: prove that $w$ is unimodal, and prove that $f$ is unimodal with mode near $0.0240$, for instance from Steutel's equation and the unimodality of $w$. Yamazato's theorem, that every self decomposable law is unimodal, does not apply to the law of $\varphi$, which is infinitely divisible and not self decomposable. In Polson's 2026 book On Hilbert's 8th Problem the unimodality of $w$ is stated as a theorem, whose proof uses a bound on $w''$ that is not derived, and the problem asks only for the unimodality of $f$; the book proves only the two end ranges of $w'$ and asks for both.
results.supersedes: Theorem 28.12 of Polson (2026) states that $w$ is unimodal, with a proof that uses a bound on $w''$ not derived there, and Open Problem 30.23 asks only for the unimodality of $f$.
results.label: rz:prob:unimodal

results.name: Infinite divisibility across the strip
results.summary: The book asks whether $w_\sigma(x)>0$ for every $\sigma$ in $(0,1)$ and every $x>0$, that is whether the shifted reciprocal zeta function is infinitely divisible on every vertical line of the critical strip.
results.statement: For $\sigma\in(0,1)$ let $\varphi_\sigma(s)=\zeta(\sigma)/\bigl((1-s/(1-\sigma)^2)\zeta(\sigma+\sqrt s)\bigr)$ and $w_\sigma(x)=e^{(1-\sigma)^2x}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{4\pi x}}\sum_{n\ge2}\Lambda(n)\,n^{-\sigma}e^{-(\log n)^2/4x}$, its canonical function, with $\Lambda$ the von Mangoldt function. Problem: is $w_\sigma(x)>0$ for every $\sigma\in(0,1)$ and every $x>0$? Positivity gives infinite divisibility of $\varphi_\sigma$ with Lévy density $w_\sigma(x)/x$. The book proves $w_{1/2}>0$ and checks $w_\sigma>0$ numerically only for $x\le10^3$ and at nine values of $\sigma$. For $\frac12<\sigma<1$ the method of the case $\sigma=\frac12$ may apply, since the terms of the zeros below the verified height are Poisson kernels of positive width, so the question reduces to the sign of the explicit pole and archimedean terms at large $x$, whose limit is governed by $\zeta'(\sigma)/\zeta(\sigma)>0$. For the completed functions $R_\sigma(s)=\xi(\sigma)/\xi(\sigma+\sqrt s)$ the answer is known: $R_\sigma$ is infinitely divisible for every $\sigma>\frac12$ with no hypothesis; since $\varphi_\sigma$ differs from $R_\sigma$ by the gamma factor and elementary factors in $\sqrt s$, this does not settle the question for $w_\sigma$.
results.label: rz:prob:strip

results.name: Meixner Pollaczek truncations with real zeros
results.origin_text: First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
results.summary: The book asks for a weighting of the coefficients of the symmetric Meixner Pollaczek expansion of $(\tau^2+\frac14)Z(\tau)$, or a Jensen type construction from them, whose polynomials are real rooted with zeros converging to the ordinates of the zeta zeros.
results.statement: Let $Z$ be Hardy's function and $p(\tau)=|\Gamma(\frac14+\frac{i\tau}2)|^2/(2^{3/2}\pi^{3/2})$ the Meixner density. The truncations of the expansion of the real even function $(\tau^2+\frac14)Z(\tau)$ in the even Meixner Pollaczek polynomials $P^{(1/4)}_{2m}(\tau/2;\frac\pi2)$, which are orthogonal for $p$, are real even polynomials. The symmetric expansion captures the first ordinate at degree $40$ but converges slowly, and the real zeros of its truncations do not track the ordinates of the zeros of the zeta function. Problem: is there a weighting of its coefficients, or a Jensen type construction from them, whose polynomials are real rooted and whose zeros converge to the ordinates?
results.label: rz:prob:mptrunc

results.name: Nyman Beurling criterion and the sech expansion
results.origin_text: First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
results.summary: The book asks how the completeness question of Lai and Vere-Jones for dilates of $\operatorname{sech}$ relates to the Nyman Beurling criterion, and whether the sech expansion of $1/\zeta(\frac12+\sqrt s)$ has an $L^2$ version on the boundary.
results.statement: For $\operatorname{Re}\sqrt s>\frac12$ the book writes $1/\zeta(\frac12+\sqrt s)=1+\sum_{N\ge2}A_N\operatorname{sech}(\sqrt s\log N)$ with explicit Möbius type weights $A_N$ supported on the powers $N=n^m$ with $n$ squarefree and $m$ odd, and $A_N=\mu(N)/(2\sqrt N)$ for squarefree $N$ ($\mu$ the Möbius function). Problem: relate the completeness question of Lai and Vere-Jones for the dilates $\{\operatorname{sech}(\lambda x)\}$ to the Nyman Beurling criterion for the Riemann Hypothesis, and decide whether the sech expansion admits an $L^2$ version on the boundary $\operatorname{Re}\sqrt s=\frac12$.
results.label: rz:prob:nymanbeurling

results.name: Product representations of the law of R
results.origin_text: First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert's 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
results.summary: The book asks whether the compensation in the formal deconvolution of the reciprocal zeta law into the reciprocal Xi law can be absorbed into a product of independent generalised gamma convolution variables, since an unconditional representation of that kind would prove the Riemann Hypothesis.
results.statement: Let $X_R$ be a random variable with Laplace transform $R(s)=\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt s)$ and $X_\varphi$ one with Laplace transform $\varphi(s)=\zeta(\frac12)/\bigl((1-4s)\zeta(\frac12+\sqrt s)\bigr)$. The class of generalised gamma convolutions (GGC) is closed under independent sums, independent products and weak limits, so an unconditional representation of $X_R$ built from independent GGC variables by sums, products and weak limits would make $R$ a GGC and prove the Riemann Hypothesis; for $X_\varphi$ the book proves that no such representation exists, and the harmonic mean is not a closure operation of the class. The factorisation of $\varphi$ into $R$ and the gamma factor $\Gamma(\frac14+\frac{\sqrt s}2)\pi^{-\sqrt s/2}/\Gamma(\frac14)$ gives, formally, $X_R$ as $X_\varphi$ minus a positive stable law of index $\frac12$ and a compensated series of independent variables $Y_{c_n}$, where $\mathbb{E}e^{-sY_\kappa}=\kappa/(\kappa+\sqrt s)$ and $c_n=2n+\frac12$ for $n\ge0$. Question: can the compensation be absorbed into a product?
results.label: rz:prob:xrproduct

results.name: Möbius series for the density of the clock with no hypothesis, with terms g_n a convolution of one fixed function with a first passage kernel
results.summary: With no hypothesis the density $f$ of the clock equals $\sum_n\mu(n)n^{-1/2}g_n(t)$, $g_n=g_1*q_{\log n}$, an absolutely convergent series (faster than any power of $n$) whose terms are bounded through an erfc factor; $g_1$ grows like $2\xi(\frac12)e^{t/4}$, so for large $t$ the series rests on the prime number theorem, and for small $t$ it converges very fast.
results.statement: Write $\xi=\eta\zeta$ with $\eta(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(\frac s2)$ and $\phi_\eta(u)=\xi(\frac12)/\eta(\frac12+\sqrt u)$. Let $c>\frac14$, $g_1$ the inverse Laplace transform of $\phi_\eta$ along $\operatorname{Re}u=c$, $q_\lambda(x)=\frac{\lambda}{2\sqrt\pi}x^{-3/2}e^{-\lambda^2/4x}$ for $x>0$, both extended by $0$ to $x\le0$. Then for every $t>0$, $f(t)=\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{\mu(n)}{\sqrt n}g_n(t)$ with $g_n=g_1*q_{\log n}$ and $|g_n(t)|\le\sup_{0<x\le t}|g_1(x)|\operatorname{erfc}\big(\frac{\log n}{2\sqrt t}\big)$, so the series converges absolutely, faster than any power of $n$. Moreover $g_1(t)=2\xi(\frac12)e^{t/4}+O(e^{\varepsilon t})$ as $t\to\infty$ for every $\varepsilon>0$, so $g_1$ is not a density and for large $t$ the series rests on $\sum_n\mu(n)/n=0$. Numerically (Talbot inversion at 30 digits) the terms with $n\le5$ reproduce $f$ to at least $20$ digits at $t=0.008,\dots,0.04$.
results.label: tx3:prop:mobius

results.name: Lower tail of the clock: P(T at most y) is at most exp of minus (log 1/y) squared over 16 y, so the density vanishes to infinite order at the origin
results.summary: With no hypothesis $P(T\le y)\le\exp\{-(1+o(1))(\log\frac1y)^2/16y\}$ as $y\downarrow0$, by Chernoff's bound with $\log G(u)\sim\frac{\sqrt u}4\log u$ optimised at $\sqrt u\approx\log(1/y)/4y$; so the density vanishes to infinite order at the origin.
results.statement: Let $T$ be the clock, $\mathbb{E}e^{-uT}=1/G(u)$, $G(u)=\xi(\frac12+\sqrt u)/\xi(\frac12)$. With no hypothesis, $P(T\le y)\le\exp\{-(1+o(1))(\log\frac1y)^2/16y\}$ as $y\downarrow0$, so the density of $T$ vanishes to infinite order at the origin. The proof is Chernoff's bound $P(T\le y)\le e^{uy}/G(u)$, with $\log G(u)\sim\frac{\sqrt u}4\log u$ by Stirling's formula for $\xi$, optimised at $\sqrt u\approx\log(1/y)/4y$. The saddlepoint exponent has the same leading term but converges slowly: at $y=0.006$ it gives $-272$ against $-33.0$ for the exact $\log f$.
results.label: tx3:res:lowertail

results.name: RH holds if and only if the density of the clock is a Pólya frequency function of infinite order
results.summary: RH is equivalent to the density $f$ of the clock being a Pólya frequency function of infinite order, the one sided form of the two sided criterion: under RH $f$ is the density of $\sum_\gamma e_\gamma/\gamma^2$, and conversely Schoenberg's theorem forces $G$ to have only real zeros.
results.statement: RH holds if and only if the density $f$ of the clock $T$ is a Pólya frequency function of infinite order, that is $\det[f(x_i-y_j)]_{i,j\le r}\ge0$ for every $r$ and all $x_1<\cdots<x_r$, $y_1<\cdots<y_r$. Under RH $f$ is the density of $\sum_\gamma e_\gamma/\gamma^2$, exponential densities are Pólya frequency functions, and the class is closed under convolution and weak limits. Conversely, by Schoenberg's theorem the bilateral Laplace transform of an integrable Pólya frequency function of infinite order is $1/\Psi$ with $\Psi(u)=Ce^{-cu^2+bu}\prod_k(1+\lambda_ku)e^{-\lambda_ku}$, $\lambda_k$ real; here the transform is $1/G$, so $G(u)=\xi(\frac12+\sqrt u)/\xi(\frac12)$ has only real zeros $u=-a_k$, which forces $\rho-\frac12$ real or purely imaginary, and $\xi$ has no real zeros, so every $\rho$ is on the critical line. The book adds, as necessary conditions tested in floating point and not proved, $(\log f)''<0$ on $91$ points of $[0.006,0.08]$ with maximum $-0.026$.
results.label: tx2:prop:pf

results.name: The clock is not a Brownian first passage time to an independent random level
results.summary: The clock variable of the Riemann xi function is not, for any constant drift and any independent random level, the first passage time of Brownian motion with that drift to that level, and the proof uses no hypothesis on the zeros.
results.statement: Let $\xi(s)=\tfrac12 s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$ be Riemann's completed zeta function, and let $T$ be the clock variable, the nonnegative random variable whose Laplace transform is $\mathbb{E}e^{-uT}=\xi(\tfrac12)/\xi(\tfrac12+\sqrt{u})$ for $u\ge0$ (it exists with no hypothesis on the zeros of $\xi$). For a drift $c\ge0$ and a level $a>0$, the first passage time of standard Brownian motion with drift $c$ (unit variance per unit time) to the level $a$ has the inverse Gaussian law, with Laplace transform $\exp\{a(c-\sqrt{c^2+2u})\}$. Then for no drift $c\ge0$ and no probability law $F$ on $(0,\infty)$ is $T$ equal in law to the first passage time of Brownian motion with drift $c$ to an independent random level $A$ with law $F$. For a drift $c<0$ the first passage time is infinite with probability $1-\mathbb{E}e^{2cA}>0$, so equality is impossible as well.
results.label: prop:nogo

results.name: Keiper Li coefficients as values of the Thorin functional
results.summary: With no hypothesis on the zeros, each Keiper Li coefficient is the Thorin functional of the zeros paired with an explicit rational function that is nonnegative on the positive axis, so Li's criterion is nonnegativity of that functional on the cone spanned by these functions.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be Riemann's completed zeta function and, for $n\ge1$, let $\lambda_n=\sum_\rho\big[1-(1-1/\rho)^n\big]$ be the Keiper Li coefficient, the sum over the zeros $\rho$ of $\xi$ taken in conjugate pairs. Let $U$ be the Thorin functional of the zeros, which gives a unit point mass at $-(\rho-\tfrac12)^2$ to each pair $\{\rho,1-\rho\}$ of zeros of $\xi$, on the critical line or off it, so that $\langle U,\varphi\rangle=\sum_{\{\rho,1-\rho\}}\varphi\big(-(\rho-\tfrac12)^2\big)$. With no hypothesis on the zeros, $\lambda_n=\langle U,\varphi_n\rangle$, where $\varphi_n(z)=2-\Big(\frac{2\sqrt z+i}{2\sqrt z-i}\Big)^n-\Big(\frac{2\sqrt z-i}{2\sqrt z+i}\Big)^n$ is a rational function of $z$ with a pole of order $n$ at $z=-\tfrac14$ and $\varphi_n(z)\sim n^2/z$ as $z\to\infty$; for example $\varphi_1(z)=(z+\tfrac14)^{-1}$ and $\varphi_2(z)=4z(z+\tfrac14)^{-2}$. For $z>0$, $\varphi_n(z)=4\sin^2\big(n\arctan\tfrac1{2\sqrt z}\big)\ge0$. Consequently, by Li's criterion, the Riemann Hypothesis holds if and only if $\langle U,\varphi_n\rangle\ge0$ for every $n\ge1$.
results.label: prop:ch20:thorin

results.name: Critical point lower bound for the collision time of zeros under the backward heat flow
results.summary: While all zeros stay real and simple, a gap between two zeros of a real polynomial cannot close under the backward heat flow before the time one over Laguerre's quantity at the critical point of the gap, and z squared minus a squared attains the bound.
results.statement: Let $f_s$, $s\ge0$, be real entire functions of genus at most one, smooth in $(z,s)$, with $\partial_sf_s=\partial_z^2f_s$; for a real polynomial $p$ and $D=d/dz$ one such family is $f_s=e^{sD^2}p=\sum_{k\ge0}s^kp^{(2k)}/k!$. For a real entire function $f$ of genus at most one with zeros $z_j$, Laguerre's quantity is $\mathcal{L}_f(x)=-\frac{d^2}{dx^2}\log|f(x)|=\big(f'(x)^2-f(x)f''(x)\big)/f(x)^2=\sum_j(x-z_j)^{-2}$, a real sum because nonreal zeros come in conjugate pairs. Fix a gap between two adjacent simple real zeros $z_k(s)<z_{k+1}(s)$ of $f_s$, which move continuously until they meet, if they do. When all zeros of $f_s$ are real, $f_s'/f_s$ falls from $+\infty$ to $-\infty$ across the gap and vanishes at exactly one point $c(s)$, the critical point of the gap; put $\ell(s)=\mathcal{L}_{f_s}(c(s))$. Let $S>0$. If all zeros of $f_\sigma$ are real and simple for $0\le\sigma<S$, then $\dot\ell\le\ell^2$ on $[0,S)$ and $\ell(\sigma)\le\ell(0)/(1-\sigma\ell(0))$ for $0\le\sigma<\min(S,1/\ell(0))$. In particular, if $p$ is a real polynomial with only real simple zeros, and the first collision of any two zeros of $e^{sD^2}p$ happens at $s=s_1$, between the two zeros that bound the gap $(z_k,z_{k+1})$ of $p$ at $s=0$, then $s_1\ge1/\mathcal{L}_p(c_k)$, where $c_k$ is the critical point of $p$ in that gap. The bound is attained by $p(z)=z^2-a^2$.
results.label: thm:wigbiane:riccati

results.name: Biane form lower bound for the collision time of zeros under the backward heat flow
results.summary: While all zeros of a real polynomial stay real and simple, a gap between two adjacent zeros cannot close under the backward heat flow before the time one over the minimum of Laguerre's quantity over the gap, a bound at least as strong as the one from the critical point and attained by z squared minus a squared.
results.statement: Let $f_s$, $s\ge0$, be real entire functions of genus at most one, smooth in $(z,s)$, with $\partial_sf_s=\partial_z^2f_s$; for a real polynomial $p$ and $D=d/dz$ one such family is $f_s=e^{sD^2}p=\sum_{k\ge0}s^kp^{(2k)}/k!$. For a real entire function $f$ of genus at most one with zeros $z_j$, Laguerre's quantity is $\mathcal{L}_f(x)=-\frac{d^2}{dx^2}\log|f(x)|=\big(f'(x)^2-f(x)f''(x)\big)/f(x)^2=\sum_j(x-z_j)^{-2}$, a real sum because nonreal zeros come in conjugate pairs. Fix a gap between two adjacent simple real zeros $z_k(s)<z_{k+1}(s)$ of $f_s$, which move continuously until they meet, if they do. The quantity $\mathcal{L}_{f_s}$ tends to $+\infty$ at both ends of the gap; let $m(s)$ be its minimum over the gap and $D^+m$ the upper right Dini derivative of $m$. Let $S>0$. If all zeros of $f_\sigma$ are real and simple for $0\le\sigma<S$, then $D^+m\le m^2$ on $[0,S)$ and $m(\sigma)\le m(0)/(1-\sigma m(0))$ for $0\le\sigma<\min(S,1/m(0))$. In particular, if $p$ is a real polynomial with only real simple zeros, and the first collision of any two zeros of $e^{sD^2}p$ happens at $s=s_1$, between the two zeros that bound the gap $(z_k,z_{k+1})$ of $p$ at $s=0$, then $s_1\ge1/\min_{(z_k,z_{k+1})}\mathcal{L}_p$. This bound is at least as strong as the critical point bound $1/\mathcal{L}_p(c_k)$, where $c_k$ is the critical point of $p$ in the gap, because the minimum does not exceed the value at $c_k$, and it is attained by $p(z)=z^2-a^2$.
results.label: thm:wigbiane:biane2

results.name: Local lower bound for the closing of a gap with a correction from the nonreal zeros
results.summary: For the minimum m of Laguerre's quantity over a gap between real zeros, the upper right Dini derivative is at most one plus an explicit correction, computed from the nonreal zeros, times m squared, which bounds the time at which the gap closes from below.
results.statement: Let $f_s$, $s\ge0$, be real entire functions of genus at most one, smooth in $(z,s)$, with $\partial_sf_s=\partial_z^2f_s$, for example $f_s=e^{sD^2}p$ with $D=d/dz$ and $p$ a real polynomial. Let $\mathcal{L}(x)=-\frac{d^2}{dx^2}\log|f_s(x)|=\sum_j(x-z_j)^{-2}$, over the zeros $z_j$ of $f_s$, be Laguerre's quantity (a real sum, because nonreal zeros come in conjugate pairs). Fix a gap between two adjacent simple real zeros of $f_s$, which move continuously until they meet, if they do; $\mathcal{L}\to+\infty$ at both ends of the gap. Let $m(s)$ be the minimum of $\mathcal{L}$ over the gap, $D^+m$ its upper right Dini derivative, and at a time $s$ let $u$ be a point of the gap where the minimum is attained, with $m=m(s)=\mathcal{L}(u)>0$. For the conjugate pairs $a\pm ib$, $b>0$, of nonreal zeros of $f_s$, each pair counted once, put $B_p=\sum b^2|u-a|^{-p}$, and assume that $B_4$, $B_5$ and $B_6$ are finite. Then $\mathcal{L}''(u)-3m^2\le\eta m^2$, where $\eta=\big(36\,mB_4+108\,B_4^2+72\,(m+6B_4)^{1/2}B_5+120\,B_6\big)/m^2$, and $D^+m(s)\le(1+\eta)m^2$. Hence, if the two zeros bounding the gap meet at a time $s_c$, and $m>0$ and $\eta\le\bar\eta$ on $[0,s_c)$ for a constant $\bar\eta$ (with $\eta$ evaluated at a minimiser at each time), then $s_c\ge1/\big((1+\bar\eta)\,m(0)\big)$. All of this holds with the coefficient $72$ in $\eta$ replaced by $36$, by the sharp inequality $S_4\le\tfrac12S_2^2+\tfrac12S_2^{1/2}|S_3|$ for the power sums $S_k=\sum_jx_j^k$ of a real square summable sequence $(x_j)$.
results.label: thm:wigbiane:local

results.name: Lower bound for the closing of a gap from the quantity delta, with no knowledge of the nonreal zeros
results.summary: A quantity delta computed from the function and its first four derivatives at the minimiser of Laguerre's quantity over a gap between real zeros controls the growth of that minimum under the backward heat flow, and when delta stays at most zero until the collision the gap cannot close before Biane's time, one over the initial minimum of Laguerre's quantity, even when nonreal zeros are present.
results.statement: Let $f_s$, $s\ge0$, be real entire functions of genus at most one, smooth in $(z,s)$, with $\partial_sf_s=\partial_z^2f_s$, for example $f_s=e^{sD^2}p$ with $D=d/dz$ and $p$ a real polynomial, and let $\mathcal{L}(x)=-\frac{d^2}{dx^2}\log|f_s(x)|$ be Laguerre's quantity. Fix a gap between two adjacent simple real zeros of $f_s$, let $m(s)$ be the minimum of $\mathcal{L}$ over the gap, $D^+m$ its upper right Dini derivative, and at a time $s$ let $u$ be a point of the gap where the minimum is attained, with $m=m(s)=\mathcal{L}(u)>0$. For the conjugate pairs $a\pm ib$, $b>0$, of nonreal zeros of $f_s$, each pair counted once, put $B_p=\sum b^2|u-a|^{-p}$, assume that $B_4$, $B_5$ and $B_6$ are finite, and put $\eta=\big(36\,mB_4+108\,B_4^2+72\,(m+6B_4)^{1/2}B_5+120\,B_6\big)/m^2$. Put $\delta=\mathcal{L}''(u)/m^2-3$, computed from $f_s$ and its first four derivatives at $u$. Then $D^+m(s)\le(1+\delta)m^2$ and $\delta\le\eta$, and $\delta\le0$ when all zeros of $f_s$ are real. Hence, if the two zeros bounding the gap meet at a time $s_c$, and $m>0$ and $\delta\le\bar\delta$ on $[0,s_c)$ for a constant $\bar\delta>-1$, then $s_c\ge1/\big((1+\bar\delta)\,m(0)\big)$; if $\delta\le0$ throughout, the collision cannot come before Biane's time $1/m(0)$, exactly as for functions with only real zeros.
results.label: cor:wigbiane:delta

results.name: Upper bound (deadline) for the closing time of a gap between real zeros
results.summary: If the share Q of the other zeros and the sum W over the nonreal zeros stay below constants rho and W bar for which 3 rho plus the square root of 9 rho squared plus 6 W bar is less than the initial minimum of Laguerre's quantity over a gap between two real zeros, the gap closes, by a collision of one of its bounding zeros with another zero, no later than an explicit logarithmic time.
results.statement: Let $f_s$, $s\ge0$, be real entire functions of genus at most one, smooth in $(z,s)$, with $\partial_sf_s=\partial_z^2f_s$, for example $f_s=e^{sD^2}p$ with $D=d/dz$ and $p$ a real polynomial, and let $\mathcal{L}(x)=-\frac{d^2}{dx^2}\log|f_s(x)|=\sum_j(x-z_j)^{-2}$ be Laguerre's quantity (a real sum, because nonreal zeros come in conjugate pairs). Fix a gap between two adjacent simple real zeros $z_k<z_{k+1}$ of $f_s$, let $m(s)$ be the minimum of $\mathcal{L}$ over the gap, and let $u$ be a point where it is attained, so $m=\mathcal{L}(u)$. Write $m=P+Q$, where $P=(u-z_k)^{-2}+(u-z_{k+1})^{-2}$ is the share of the two zeros bounding the gap and $Q=\sum(u-z)^{-2}$ over all the other zeros $z$ of $f_s$, and let $W=\sum|u-z|^{-4}$ over the nonreal zeros $z$ of $f_s$. While the two zeros bounding the gap are real, the right derivative $m'(s^+)$ exists and is the least value of $\mathcal{L}''(u)-2m^2$ over the minimisers $u$, and at every minimiser $\mathcal{L}''(u)-2m^2\ge m^2-6mQ+3Q^2-6W$. Suppose that, for constants $\rho$ and $\bar W$ with $9\rho^2+6\bar W>0$, $Q\le\rho$ and $W\le\bar W$ at every minimiser for as long as the two zeros bounding the gap are real, and that $m(0)>r_1$, where $r_{1,2}=3\rho\pm(9\rho^2+6\bar W)^{1/2}$. Then the gap closes, one of the two zeros bounding it meeting another zero, at a time $s_c\le s^*=\frac{1}{r_1-r_2}\log\frac{m(0)-r_2}{m(0)-r_1}$. If all zeros are real, then $W=0$, so $\bar W=0$ may be taken, and for $\rho>0$ one has $s^*=(6\rho)^{-1}\log\big(m(0)/(m(0)-6\rho)\big)=1/m(0)+3\rho/m(0)^2+12\rho^2/m(0)^3+\cdots$.
results.label: thm:wigbiane:upper

results.name: Deadline for the closing of a gap in terms of the quantity kappa
results.summary: The deadline for the closing of a gap holds with six times the bound on W replaced by the largest negative part of a quantity kappa, computed from the function at the minimiser and the two zeros bounding the gap, and this form is never weaker.
results.statement: Let $f_s$, $s\ge0$, be real entire functions of genus at most one, smooth in $(z,s)$, with $\partial_sf_s=\partial_z^2f_s$, and let $\mathcal{L}(x)=-\frac{d^2}{dx^2}\log|f_s(x)|=\sum_j(x-z_j)^{-2}$ be Laguerre's quantity. Fix a gap between two adjacent simple real zeros $z_k<z_{k+1}$ of $f_s$, let $m(s)$ be the minimum of $\mathcal{L}$ over the gap, let $u$ be a point where it is attained, and put $x_j=1/(u-z_j)$ for the zeros $z_j$ of $f_s$, $P=x_k^2+x_{k+1}^2$, $Q=\sum_{j\ne k,k+1}x_j^2$, so that $m=P+Q$, and $W=\sum|x_j|^4$ over the nonreal zeros. Put $\kappa=\mathcal{L}''(u)-3P^2$, computed from $f_s$ at $u$ and the two zeros bounding the gap. Then $\kappa=3\big(x_k^2-x_{k+1}^2\big)^2+6\sum_{j\ne k,k+1}x_j^4\ge-6W$, with $\kappa\ge0$ when all zeros are real. Put $\bar\kappa=\max\big(0,\sup(-\kappa)\big)$, the supremum over the minimisers at the times before the collision. If $Q\le\rho$ at every minimiser for as long as the two zeros bounding the gap are real, with $9\rho^2+\bar\kappa>0$, and $m(0)>r_1$, where $r_{1,2}=3\rho\pm(9\rho^2+\bar\kappa)^{1/2}$, then the gap closes, one of the two zeros bounding it meeting another zero, at a time $s_c\le\frac{1}{r_1-r_2}\log\frac{m(0)-r_2}{m(0)-r_1}$. This bound is never weaker than the same bound with $6\bar W$ in place of $\bar\kappa$, where $\bar W$ is a constant with $W\le\bar W$ at every minimiser for as long as the two zeros bounding the gap are real, since then $\bar\kappa\le6\bar W$.
results.label: cor:wigbiane:kappa

results.name: Control of the nonreal zeros of the de Bruijn Newman function at negative times
results.summary: No bound is known, computed from the de Bruijn Newman function at time zero, for how far its nonreal zeros travel at negative times or how close to a gap between real zeros they come, and such control would make the lower and upper bounds for the closing time of a gap unconditional statements about that function.
results.statement: For real $t$ let $H_t(z)=\int_0^\infty e^{tu^2}\Phi(u)\cos(zu)\,du$ be the de Bruijn Newman function, with $\Phi(u)=\sum_{n\ge1}\big(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u}-3\pi n^2e^{5u}\big)\exp(-\pi n^2e^{4u})$, so that $H_0(z)=\tfrac18\Xi(z/2)$ with $\Xi(\theta)=\xi(\tfrac12+i\theta)$ for Riemann's completed zeta function $\xi$. As $t$ decreases from $0$ the zeros of $H_t$ move by the backward heat flow, and the book bounds from below and from above, in terms of $H_0$ alone, the time at which a gap between two adjacent real zeros closes, under hypotheses along the flow that the computation checks on a grid of times but cannot yet guarantee in advance. Problem: find a bound for how far the nonreal zeros of $H_t$, $t<0$, travel, and for how close to a gap between real zeros they come. No such bound is known, and such control would make the lower and upper bounds for the closing time of a gap unconditional statements about $H_t$, computed from $H_0$ alone.
results.label: prob:wigbiane:control

results.name: Shielding deficit identity for a pair of adjacent real zeros of the de Bruijn Newman function (Newton 2026, Zenodo)
results.summary: A telescoping identity (Newton 2026, Zenodo) expresses the shielding deficit of a pair of adjacent real zeros as a sum over the exterior gaps of the relative deviations of those gaps from the pair's gap, when all zeros are real and the exterior zeros tend to infinity.
results.statement: Let $a<b$ be adjacent simple real zeros of an entire function with zeros $\rho$ (here the de Bruijn Newman function $H_t$), with gap $g=b-a$, and put $S_{a,b}=\sum_{\rho\ne a,b}\frac{1}{(a-\rho)(b-\rho)}$ and $\mathrm{Def}=2-g^2S_{a,b}$. On each side of the pair number the exterior gaps outward, write them $g(1+\varepsilon_m)$ with $\varepsilon_m>-1$, and put $D_0=0$, $D_m=\sum_{j\le m}\varepsilon_j$, so that the $m$th exterior zero on that side is at distance $g(m+D_m)$ from the nearer end of the pair. Then on one side, for every $N\ge1$, $1-\sum_{m=1}^N\frac{1}{(m+D_m)(m+1+D_m)}=\sum_{m=1}^N\frac{\varepsilon_m}{(m+D_{m-1})(m+D_m)}+\frac{1}{N+1+D_N}$. If all zeros are real and the exterior zeros tend to infinity on both sides, then $\mathrm{Def}=\sum_{\text{sides}}\sum_{m\ge1}\frac{\varepsilon_m}{(m+D_{m-1})(m+D_m)}$. The result is due to Newton (2026, Zenodo).
results.label: nw:thm:shield

results.name: Consequences of the shielding deficit identity: lattice, truncated lattice, single enlarged gap, one sided bound and monotonicity of the smallest gap (Newton 2026, Zenodo)
results.summary: Five consequences of the shielding deficit identity: the lattice has zero deficit, a truncated lattice with $R$ exterior zeros per side has deficit $2/(R+1)$, a single enlarged gap contributes $\delta/(j(j+\delta))$, the positive part of the deficit is at most $g^{-1}\sum_j j^{-2}$ times the excess of the exterior gaps over $g$, and a smallest gap of a configuration does not shrink forward in time.
results.statement: In the setting of the shielding deficit identity (adjacent simple real zeros $a<b$ with gap $g$, $\mathrm{Def}=2-g^2S_{a,b}$, exterior gaps $g(1+\varepsilon_m)$ on each side, $\varepsilon_m>-1$, and the flow $\frac{d(g^2)}{dt}=4\,\mathrm{Def}$ for the de Bruijn Newman function): (a) if all $\varepsilon_m=0$ then $\mathrm{Def}=0$ and $g$ is constant, as for the lattice of zeros of $e^{\kappa^2t}\sin\kappa z$; (b) keeping $R$ exterior zeros on each side of a regular lattice of gap $g$ leaves $\mathrm{Def}=2/(R+1)$; (c) a single enlarged exterior gap $g(1+\delta)$ at position $j$ contributes exactly $\delta/(j(j+\delta))$; (d) with $d_{\nu,j}$ the exterior gaps on the sides $\nu=L,R$ and $[x]_+=\max(x,0)$, $[\mathrm{Def}]_+\le g^{-1}\sum_{j\ge1}j^{-2}\big[(d_{L,j}-g)_++(d_{R,j}-g)_+\big]$, and by (c) the constant $j^{-2}$ is optimal to first order; (e) if the configuration has a smallest gap $g>0$ (a finite configuration or a lattice) and $g$ is that gap, then every $\varepsilon_m\ge0$, so $\mathrm{Def}\ge0$ and the smallest gap does not shrink forward in time, with equality only for the lattice. The book notes that (e) does not apply to $H_t$, which has no smallest gap. The result is due to Newton (2026, Zenodo).
results.label: nw:cor:shield

results.name: The de Bruijn Newman function as a Gaussian average and the reciprocal transform of the tilted clock as a Gaussian smoothing of xi
results.summary: For $t>0$ the de Bruijn Newman function $H_t$ is the Gaussian average $\mathbb{E}H_0(z+i\sqrt{2t}Z)$ of $H_0$, and $1/R_t(\sigma^2)$, the reciprocal of the Laplace transform of the tilted clock when $t$ is at least the de Bruijn Newman constant, is the Gaussian smoothing of $\xi(\frac12+\sigma)$ with variance $t/2$, normalised at $\sigma=0$.
results.statement: Let $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$ be Riemann's completed zeta function, $\Phi(u)=\sum_{n\ge1}\bigl(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u}-3\pi n^2e^{5u}\bigr)\exp(-\pi n^2e^{4u})$, $H_t(z)=\int_0^\infty e^{tu^2}\Phi(u)\cos(zu)\,du$ for real $t$ (so that $H_0(z)=\frac18\xi(\frac12+\frac{iz}2)$) and $R_t(s)=H_t(0)/H_t(2i\sqrt s)$ for $s\ge0$. The function $R_0(s)=\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt s)$ is the Laplace transform of the clock $T$, which exists with no hypothesis on the zeros, and for $t$ at least the de Bruijn Newman constant $\Lambda$, $R_t$ is the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution $T_t$, the tilted clock. Let $Z$ be a standard normal variable. Then for every $t>0$, $H_t(z)=\mathbb{E}\,H_0\bigl(z+i\sqrt{2t}\,Z\bigr)$ for all $z\in\mathbb{C}$, and $\dfrac1{R_t(\sigma^2)}=\dfrac{\mathbb{E}\,\xi\bigl(\frac12+\sigma+\sqrt{t/2}\,Z\bigr)}{\mathbb{E}\,\xi\bigl(\frac12+\sqrt{t/2}\,Z\bigr)}$ for $\sigma\ge0$. So for $t>0$ the tilt is Gaussian convolution, along the real axis of $\sigma$, of the even function $\sigma\mapsto\xi(\frac12+\sigma)$, with variance $t/2$, normalised at $\sigma=0$.
results.label: xg:prop:gauss

results.name: Large tilt of the clock: the limit is twice the Brownian exit time
results.summary: As the tilt $t\to\infty$, the tilted clock divided by the square of the mode $u_t$ of the tilted kernel converges in law to twice the exit time of Brownian motion from $(-1,1)$, its Laplace transform tends to $1/\cosh(2\sqrt s)$, and $u_t$ times the $j$th positive zero of $H_t$ tends to $\pi(j-\frac12)$.
results.statement: Let $\Phi(u)=\sum_{n\ge1}\bigl(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u}-3\pi n^2e^{5u}\bigr)\exp(-\pi n^2e^{4u})$, $H_t(z)=\int_0^\infty e^{tu^2}\Phi(u)\cos(zu)\,du$ (so that $H_0(z)=\frac18\xi(\frac12+\frac{iz}2)$ for Riemann's completed zeta function $\xi$) and $R_t(s)=H_t(0)/H_t(2i\sqrt s)$. Let $\Lambda$ be the de Bruijn Newman constant, so that $H_t$ has only real zeros exactly when $t\ge\Lambda$. For $t\ge\Lambda$, in particular for $t\ge0.2$ (the bound $\Lambda\le0.2$ of Platt and Trudgian 2021), let $0<z_1(t)\le z_2(t)\le\cdots$ be the positive zeros of $H_t$; then $R_t$ is the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution $T_t$, the tilted clock, with Thorin atoms $z_j(t)^2/4$. For large $t$ let $u_t$ be the mode of $u\mapsto e^{tu^2}\Phi(u)$ on $(0,\infty)$, so that $e^{4u_t}\sim tu_t/(2\pi)$ as $t\to\infty$. Let $C$ be the exit time of standard Brownian motion from $(-1,1)$, with $\mathbb{E}e^{-\theta C}=1/\cosh\sqrt{2\theta}$. Then as $t\to\infty$, $R_t(s/u_t^2)\to1/\cosh(2\sqrt s)$ for every $s\ge0$, $T_t/u_t^2$ converges in law to $2C$ (whose Laplace transform is $1/\cosh(2\sqrt s)$), and $u_tz_j(t)\to\pi(j-\frac12)$ for every $j\ge1$.
results.label: xg:prop:large

results.name: Gaussian smoothing of a reciprocal GGC transform is again one
results.summary: Gaussian smoothing in the variable $\sqrt s$ of the reciprocal of the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution (GGC) with discrete Thorin measure and no drift is again the reciprocal of such a transform, the Thorin atoms obey, while they are simple, the motion equation of the de Bruijn Newman flow, and the mean of the GGC satisfies $\frac{d}{d\lambda}\mathbb{E}S_\lambda=(\mathbb{E}S_\lambda)^2-\frac32\operatorname{Var}S_\lambda$.
results.statement: A generalized gamma convolution (GGC) with Thorin measure $U\ge0$ and no drift is a law on $[0,\infty)$ with Laplace transform $\exp\bigl(-\int_{(0,\infty)}\log(1+s/z)\,U(dz)\bigr)$. Let $a_j>0$ with $\sum_ja_j^{-1}<\infty$, and let $M(\sigma)=\prod_j(1+\sigma^2/a_j)$, an even entire function of genus zero in $\sigma^2$, so that $1/M(\sqrt s)$ is the Laplace transform of the GGC with the discrete Thorin measure $\sum_j\delta_{a_j}$. Let $Z$ be a standard normal variable and, for $c>0$, $M_c(\sigma)=\mathbb{E}\,M(\sigma+cZ)\big/\mathbb{E}\,M(cZ)$. Then $M_c(\sigma)=\prod_j(1+\sigma^2/a_j(c))$ with real $a_j(c)>0$, so that $1/M_c(\sqrt s)$ is the Laplace transform of a GGC $S_\lambda$ with the Thorin measure $\sum_j\delta_{a_j(c)}$, where $\lambda=2c^2$. While the atoms are simple they obey, as functions of $\lambda$, the motion equation $\dfrac{da_j}{d\lambda}=\dfrac12+2\sum_{k\ne j}\dfrac{a_j}{a_j-a_k}$, and $\dfrac{d}{d\lambda}\mathbb{E}S_\lambda=(\mathbb{E}S_\lambda)^2-\dfrac32\operatorname{Var}S_\lambda$.
results.label: xg:thm:smooth

results.name: Concentration of the Laguerre expressions at the origin along the whole de Bruijn Newman flow, with positivity of $L_{n,t}$ on every window for large $n$ (Newton 2026, Zenodo)
