Let $\mathcal{B}$ be the space of even functions $\varphi(\theta)=\frac1{2\pi}\int\hat\varphi(x)e^{-i\theta x}\,dx$ with $\hat\varphi$ of compact support, Lipschitz, and with $\hat\varphi'$ of bounded variation; each such $\varphi$ is entire of exponential type, with $\varphi(\theta+is)=O(\theta^{-2})$ uniformly for $|s|\le1$. For $a\ge0$ let $P_a^{-1}\varphi\in\mathcal{B}$ be the function with Fourier transform $\hat\varphi(x)e^{a|x|}$. Let $\varepsilon_0$ be to the right of the zeros and, for $\varphi\in\mathcal{B}$, put $D(\varphi)=\int\varrho_{\varepsilon_0}(\theta)\,(P_{\varepsilon_0}^{-1}\varphi)(\theta)\,d\theta$. Then $D(\varphi)$ does not depend on $\varepsilon_0$, and with $g(x)=\hat\varphi(x)/2\pi$, so that $\varphi(\theta)=\int g(x)e^{i\theta x}dx=\hat g(\theta)$, \[ D(\varphi)=\sum_\rho\varphi(\gamma_\rho)=\hat g(\tfrac i2)+\hat g(-\tfrac i2)-(\gamma_E+\log\pi)\,g(0)+\int_0^\infty\frac{2\big(e^{-2x}g(0)-e^{-x/2}g(x)\big)}{1-e^{-2x}}\,dx-2\sum_{n\ge2}\frac{\Lambda(n)}{\sqrt n}\,g(\log n), \] where the sum over $\rho$ runs over all zeros with multiplicity, in conjugate pairs, and converges absolutely, $\gamma_E$ is Euler's constant and $\Lambda$ the von Mangoldt function. The second expression is Weil's explicit formula on $\mathcal{B}$, so $D$ is computed from the gamma factor, the pole and the primes $n$ with $\log n$ in the support of $g$; it is the action on $g$ of Weil's distribution $\sum_\rho e^{(\rho-1/2)x}$, that is, $\langle D,g\rangle=\sum_\rho\hat g(\gamma_\rho)$. Moreover, through the $x$ form of its archimedean term, the Thorin functional $U$ of the clock (the linear functional with $\langle U,\psi\rangle=\sum_k\psi(a_k)$ over the exponents $a_k=-(\rho_k-\frac12)^2$, one for each pair of zeros $\{\rho,1-\rho\}$, defined by the explicit formula, in which no zero appears) extends to $\mathcal{B}$, and then $D(\varphi)=2\langle U,\varphi(\sqrt{\cdot})\rangle$.
results.label: dc:thm:weil

results.name: Damped Weil criterion
results.summary: For $0\le\varepsilon\le\frac12$, Weil's quadratic form damped by $e^{-\varepsilon|x|}$ is nonnegative on every test function exactly when no zero of $\zeta$ has real part above $\frac12+\varepsilon$, which is Weil's criterion for RH at $\varepsilon=0$, holds with no hypothesis at $\varepsilon=\frac12$, and at $\varepsilon=\frac38$ is equivalent to the half plane $\operatorname{Re}s>\frac78$ announced in October 2026 and not refereed.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be the completed Riemann zeta function with nontrivial zeros $\rho=\beta+i\gamma$ counted with multiplicity, $\gamma_\rho=-i(\rho-\frac12)$, and for $\varepsilon>0$ let $\varrho_\varepsilon(\theta)=\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(\frac12+\varepsilon+i\theta)$, the Poisson smoothing of the zeros. Weil's distribution $D$ acts on an even Lipschitz function $g$ of compact support with $g'$ of bounded variation by $\langle D,g\rangle=\sum_\rho\hat g(\gamma_\rho)$, where $\hat g(t)=\int g(x)e^{itx}\,dx$ (Weil's explicit formula computes this from the gamma factor, the pole of $\zeta$ and the primes), and on a function that is not even through its even part. For a bounded function $h$ of bounded variation and compact support let $\tilde h(x)=\overline{h(-x)}$, so that $h*\tilde h$ is Lipschitz with $\widehat{h*\tilde h}=|\hat h|^2$, and for $\varepsilon\ge0$ put $Q_\varepsilon(h)=\langle D,e^{-\varepsilon|x|}(h*\tilde h)\rangle$, Weil's form damped by $e^{-\varepsilon|x|}$. Call $\varepsilon>0$ to the right of the zeros if $\beta<\frac12+\varepsilon$ for every zero. Let $0\le\varepsilon\le\frac12$. Then $Q_\varepsilon(h)\ge0$ for every $h\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb{R})$ (real $h$ suffice) if and only if no nontrivial zero of $\zeta$ has $\beta>\frac12+\varepsilon$. When $\varepsilon>0$ is to the right of the zeros, $Q_\varepsilon(h)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}|\hat h(\theta)|^2\varrho_\varepsilon(\theta)\,d\theta$ for every bounded $h$ of bounded variation and compact support. In particular: at $\varepsilon=0$ this is Weil's criterion for the Riemann Hypothesis; at $\varepsilon=\frac12$ it holds with no hypothesis on the zeros; and the zero free half plane $\operatorname{Re}s>\frac78$ announced in October 2026, which has not been refereed, is equivalent to $Q_{3/8}\ge0$.
results.label: dc:thm:damped

results.name: Ladder theorem: least eigenvalue of the damped Weil form on a window
results.status_text: conditional on Parts (a) and (b), for a level $0<\varepsilon<\frac12$: that the closed half plane $\operatorname{Re}s\ge\frac12+\varepsilon$ contains no zero of $\zeta$ (that $\varepsilon$ is to the right of the zeros). This zero free half plane is not proved for any $\varepsilon<\frac12$; the half plane $\operatorname{Re}s>\frac78$ announced in October 2026 and not refereed would give it for $\varepsilon>\frac38$ only.; Parts (a) and (b), for a level $0<\varepsilon<\frac12$: that $v_{1/2+\varepsilon}(\theta)>v_{1/2+\varepsilon}(0)$ for every real $\theta\ne0$ and $v_{1/2+\varepsilon}''(0)>0$, that is, that the Thorin density has a strict, nondegenerate global minimum at the origin. The book certifies this only up to a finite height, and the strict minimum at the origin on every line $\frac12<\alpha<1$ at once is equivalent to RH.; Parts (a) and (b), for a level $0<\varepsilon<\frac12$: that $\liminf_{|\theta|\to\infty}v_{1/2+\varepsilon}(\theta)>v_{1/2+\varepsilon}(0)$, that is, that the minimum is not approached at infinity. This is not known for $0<\varepsilon<\frac12$ without RH, under which it holds.; Part (c), first half (the nonnegativity and the decay of $\lambda_{\min}(\frac12,a)$): the Riemann Hypothesis. All hypotheses of (a) and (b) hold at $\varepsilon=\frac12$ with no assumption on the zeros, and the second half of (c), the negativity for large $a$ if RH fails, needs no hypothesis. For $\varepsilon>\frac12$ the chapter does not discuss whether the hypotheses on $v_{1/2+\varepsilon}$ hold
results.conditions: Parts (a) and (b), for a level $0<\varepsilon<\frac12$: that the closed half plane $\operatorname{Re}s\ge\frac12+\varepsilon$ contains no zero of $\zeta$ (that $\varepsilon$ is to the right of the zeros). This zero free half plane is not proved for any $\varepsilon<\frac12$; the half plane $\operatorname{Re}s>\frac78$ announced in October 2026 and not refereed would give it for $\varepsilon>\frac38$ only.; Parts (a) and (b), for a level $0<\varepsilon<\frac12$: that $v_{1/2+\varepsilon}(\theta)>v_{1/2+\varepsilon}(0)$ for every real $\theta\ne0$ and $v_{1/2+\varepsilon}''(0)>0$, that is, that the Thorin density has a strict, nondegenerate global minimum at the origin. The book certifies this only up to a finite height, and the strict minimum at the origin on every line $\frac12<\alpha<1$ at once is equivalent to RH.; Parts (a) and (b), for a level $0<\varepsilon<\frac12$: that $\liminf_{|\theta|\to\infty}v_{1/2+\varepsilon}(\theta)>v_{1/2+\varepsilon}(0)$, that is, that the minimum is not approached at infinity. This is not known for $0<\varepsilon<\frac12$ without RH, under which it holds.; Part (c), first half (the nonnegativity and the decay of $\lambda_{\min}(\frac12,a)$): the Riemann Hypothesis. All hypotheses of (a) and (b) hold at $\varepsilon=\frac12$ with no assumption on the zeros, and the second half of (c), the negativity for large $a$ if RH fails, needs no hypothesis. For $\varepsilon>\frac12$ the chapter does not discuss whether the hypotheses on $v_{1/2+\varepsilon}$ hold.
results.summary: At a level $\frac12+\varepsilon$ to the right of the zeros where the Thorin density has a strict, nondegenerate global minimum at the origin not approached at infinity (true at $\varepsilon=\frac12$, an assumption below it), the least eigenvalue of Weil's form damped by $e^{-\varepsilon|x|}$ on test functions supported in $[-a,a]$ decreases to $2\xi'/\xi(\frac12+\varepsilon)$ at a rate between $c/a^2$ and $(\pi^2v''(0)/4+o(1))/a^2$, with $v(\theta)=\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(\frac12+\varepsilon+i\theta)$, while at $\varepsilon=0$, under RH, it is nonnegative and $O(a^{-N})$ for every $N$, and if RH fails it is negative for all large $a$.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be the completed Riemann zeta function with nontrivial zeros $\rho=\beta+i\gamma$ counted with multiplicity and $\gamma_\rho=-i(\rho-\frac12)$. For real $\alpha$ and $\theta$ put $v_\alpha(\theta)=\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(\alpha+i\theta)$ and $b_\alpha=v_\alpha(0)=\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(\alpha)$. Weil's distribution $D$ acts on an even Lipschitz function $g$ of compact support with $g'$ of bounded variation by $\langle D,g\rangle=\sum_\rho\hat g(\gamma_\rho)$, where $\hat g(t)=\int g(x)e^{itx}\,dx$ (Weil's explicit formula computes this from the gamma factor, the pole of $\zeta$ and the primes). For a bounded real function $h$ of bounded variation and compact support let $\tilde h(x)=h(-x)$ and, for $\varepsilon\ge0$, $Q_\varepsilon(h)=\langle D,e^{-\varepsilon|x|}(h*\tilde h)\rangle$; for $a>0$ let $\lambda_{\min}(\frac12+\varepsilon,a)$ be the infimum of $Q_\varepsilon(h)/\|h\|_2^2$ over all such $h\ne0$ supported in $[-a,a]$ (only the prime powers $n\le e^{2a}$ enter $Q_\varepsilon(h)$ for these $h$). Let $\varepsilon>0$ be to the right of the zeros, that is, $\beta<\frac12+\varepsilon$ for every zero, and suppose that $v_{1/2+\varepsilon}(\theta)>v_{1/2+\varepsilon}(0)$ for every $\theta\ne0$ (a strict global minimum at the origin), that $v_{1/2+\varepsilon}''(0)>0$ (nondegenerate), and that $\liminf_{|\theta|\to\infty}v_{1/2+\varepsilon}(\theta)>v_{1/2+\varepsilon}(0)$ (not approached at infinity). Then: (a) $\lambda_{\min}(\frac12+\varepsilon,a)$ is nonincreasing in $a$, and $\lambda_{\min}(\frac12+\varepsilon,a)\ge2b_{1/2+\varepsilon}>0$ for every $a>0$; (b) $\lambda_{\min}(\frac12+\varepsilon,a)\to2b_{1/2+\varepsilon}$ as $a\to\infty$, and there are constants $c,a_0>0$ such that for all $a\ge a_0$, $\frac c{a^2}\le\lambda_{\min}(\frac12+\varepsilon,a)-2b_{1/2+\varepsilon}\le\frac{\pi^2v_{1/2+\varepsilon}''(0)/4+o(1)}{a^2}$, where $o(1)\to0$ as $a\to\infty$; (c) at $\varepsilon=0$, with none of the hypotheses above: if the Riemann Hypothesis holds, then $\lambda_{\min}(\frac12,a)\ge0$ for every $a$ and, for every $N$, $\lambda_{\min}(\frac12,a)=O(a^{-N})$ as $a\to\infty$, so that $\lambda_{\min}(\frac12,a)\to0$; if the Riemann Hypothesis fails, then $\lambda_{\min}(\frac12,a)<0$ for all large $a$.
results.label: dc:thm:ladder

results.name: Certified rungs of the ladder
results.summary: Certify in interval arithmetic that the least eigenvalue of Weil's damped form on test functions supported in $[-4,4]$ is positive at $\varepsilon=0.05$, $0.1$, $0.2$ and $0.375$, and find how far in the window a certificate can be pushed.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be the completed Riemann zeta function with zeros $\rho$ and $\gamma_\rho=-i(\rho-\frac12)$. Weil's distribution $D$ acts on an even Lipschitz function $g$ of compact support with $g'$ of bounded variation by $\langle D,g\rangle=\sum_\rho\hat g(\gamma_\rho)$, $\hat g(t)=\int g(x)e^{itx}\,dx$ (Weil's explicit formula computes this from the gamma factor, the pole and the primes). For bounded real $h$ of bounded variation and compact support let $\tilde h(x)=h(-x)$ and $Q_\varepsilon(h)=\langle D,e^{-\varepsilon|x|}(h*\tilde h)\rangle$, and for $a>0$ let $\lambda_{\min}(\frac12+\varepsilon,a)$ be the infimum of $Q_\varepsilon(h)/\|h\|_2^2$ over all such $h\ne0$ supported in $[-a,a]$. Certify, in interval arithmetic, that $\lambda_{\min}(\frac12+\varepsilon,a)>0$ for $\varepsilon\in\{0.05,0.1,0.2,0.375\}$ and $a=4$, which by monotonicity in $a$ covers every $a\le4$, and determine how far in $a$ a certificate can be pushed at fixed $\varepsilon$. Each certificate would be unconditional, and at $\varepsilon=\frac38$ it would agree with what the announced zero free half plane $\operatorname{Re}s>\frac78$ gives, namely $\lambda_{\min}\ge0$, and could be checked independently of it. Certifying one rung needs a lower bound for the bottom of the spectrum, not the variational upper bounds and extrapolated values the book computes; the book has not done this.
results.label: dc:prob:cert

results.name: The exact rate of the ladder
results.summary: Prove that the scaled excess of the least eigenvalue of the damped Weil form over its limit tends to the upper constant $\pi^2v''(0)/4$ of the ladder theorem, and find the next term; numerical fits are consistent with the limit and with a positive correction of order $1/a$, and neither is proved.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be the completed Riemann zeta function with zeros $\rho=\beta+i\gamma$ and $\gamma_\rho=-i(\rho-\frac12)$, and put $v_\alpha(\theta)=\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(\alpha+i\theta)$ and $b_\alpha=v_\alpha(0)=\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(\alpha)$. Weil's distribution $D$ acts on an even Lipschitz function $g$ of compact support with $g'$ of bounded variation by $\langle D,g\rangle=\sum_\rho\hat g(\gamma_\rho)$, $\hat g(t)=\int g(x)e^{itx}\,dx$. For bounded real $h$ of bounded variation and compact support let $\tilde h(x)=h(-x)$ and $Q_\varepsilon(h)=\langle D,e^{-\varepsilon|x|}(h*\tilde h)\rangle$, and for $a>0$ let $\lambda_{\min}(\frac12+\varepsilon,a)$ be the infimum of $Q_\varepsilon(h)/\|h\|_2^2$ over all such $h\ne0$ supported in $[-a,a]$. Let $\varepsilon>0$ be to the right of the zeros ($\beta<\frac12+\varepsilon$ for every zero), and suppose that $v_{1/2+\varepsilon}(\theta)>v_{1/2+\varepsilon}(0)$ for every $\theta\ne0$, that $v_{1/2+\varepsilon}''(0)>0$, and that $\liminf_{|\theta|\to\infty}v_{1/2+\varepsilon}(\theta)>v_{1/2+\varepsilon}(0)$. Prove that $a^2\big(\lambda_{\min}(\frac12+\varepsilon,a)-2b_{1/2+\varepsilon}\big)\to\pi^2v_{1/2+\varepsilon}''(0)/4$ as $a\to\infty$, and find the next term. Under these hypotheses the book proves only that this scaled excess is at most $\pi^2v_{1/2+\varepsilon}''(0)/4+o(1)$ and at least a positive constant $c$. The book's numerical fits of converged, extrapolated values are consistent with the limit and with a positive correction of order $1/a$, so that $\pi^2v_{1/2+\varepsilon}''(0)/4$ would not be an upper bound at finite $a$; neither the limit nor the order of the correction is proved.
results.label: dc:prob:rate

results.name: The transition of the ladder at the line
results.summary: Describe the least eigenvalue of the damped Weil form jointly as the window half length $a$ tends to infinity and the depth $\varepsilon$ tends to zero, where the rate is algebraic for fixed $\varepsilon>0$ under the hypotheses of the ladder theorem and faster than any power of $a$ at $\varepsilon=0$ under RH.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be the completed Riemann zeta function with zeros $\rho$ and $\gamma_\rho=-i(\rho-\frac12)$, and put $b_\alpha=\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(\alpha)$ for real $\alpha$ and $V_\xi=(\log\xi)''(\frac12)$. Weil's distribution $D$ acts on an even Lipschitz function $g$ of compact support with $g'$ of bounded variation by $\langle D,g\rangle=\sum_\rho\hat g(\gamma_\rho)$, $\hat g(t)=\int g(x)e^{itx}\,dx$. For bounded real $h$ of bounded variation and compact support let $\tilde h(x)=h(-x)$ and $Q_\varepsilon(h)=\langle D,e^{-\varepsilon|x|}(h*\tilde h)\rangle$, and for $a>0$ let $\lambda_{\min}(\frac12+\varepsilon,a)$ be the infimum of $Q_\varepsilon(h)/\|h\|_2^2$ over all such $h\ne0$ supported in $[-a,a]$. Describe $\lambda_{\min}(\frac12+\varepsilon,a)$ jointly as $a\to\infty$ and $\varepsilon\to0$. For fixed $\varepsilon>0$, under the hypotheses of the ladder theorem (the level $\varepsilon$ to the right of the zeros, and the Thorin density $\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(\frac12+\varepsilon+i\theta)$ having a strict, nondegenerate global minimum at $\theta=0$ that is not approached at infinity), the limit is $2b_{1/2+\varepsilon}$, which is at most $2V_\xi\,\varepsilon$ and asymptotic to it as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$, and the rate is algebraic; at $\varepsilon=0$, under RH, the decay is faster than any power of $a$. The questions are: on which curves $\varepsilon=\varepsilon(a)\to0$ does $\lambda_{\min}(\frac12+\varepsilon,a)$ stay comparable to $2b_{1/2+\varepsilon}$, and does the crossover occur at $\varepsilon$ of the order of the mean spacing of the zeros at height $e^{2a}$?
results.label: dc:prob:transition

results.name: Uniformity of the damped Weil form from structure
results.summary: Find a structural reason, valid for all windows, why Weil's form damped by $e^{-\varepsilon|x|}$ is nonnegative on test functions supported in $[-a,a]$ for some fixed $\varepsilon<\frac12$, which by the damped Weil criterion would prove the zero free half plane $\operatorname{Re}s>\frac12+\varepsilon$.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be the completed Riemann zeta function with zeros $\rho$ and $\gamma_\rho=-i(\rho-\frac12)$. Weil's distribution $D$ acts on an even Lipschitz function $g$ of compact support with $g'$ of bounded variation by $\langle D,g\rangle=\sum_\rho\hat g(\gamma_\rho)$, $\hat g(t)=\int g(x)e^{itx}\,dx$ (Weil's explicit formula computes this from the gamma factor, the pole and the primes). For bounded real $h$ of bounded variation and compact support let $\tilde h(x)=h(-x)$ and $Q_\varepsilon(h)=\langle D,e^{-\varepsilon|x|}(h*\tilde h)\rangle$. Find a structural reason, valid for all $a$, why $Q_\varepsilon(h)\ge0$ for every such $h$ supported in $[-a,a]$ (that is, $Q_\varepsilon\ge0$ on $L^2[-a,a]$) for some fixed $\varepsilon<\frac12$, using properties of the archimedean and pole terms that dominate the primes up to $e^{2a}$ uniformly in $a$. By the damped Weil criterion, any such argument proves the zero free half plane $\operatorname{Re}s>\frac12+\varepsilon$.
results.label: dc:prob:uniform

results.name: Thorin property of the tilted clock of a Dedekind zeta function at every tilt: equivalence with the position of the zeros
results.summary: For a number field and a tilt $u_0\ge0$, the tilted reciprocal of the completed Dedekind zeta function is a GGC exactly when every nontrivial zero lies on the critical line or is real at distance less than $\sqrt{u_0}$ from the centre (with no central zero when $u_0=0$), and its Thorin measure is then the zero counting measure shifted by $u_0$.
results.statement:
Let $F$ be a number field with $r_1$ real and $r_2$ complex places, discriminant $d_F$ and Dedekind zeta function $\zeta_F$. Put $\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s)=\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)$, $\Gamma_{\mathbb{C}}(s)=2(2\pi)^{-s}\Gamma(s)$ and $\xi_F(s)=s(s-1)|d_F|^{s/2}\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s)^{r_1}\Gamma_{\mathbb{C}}(s)^{r_2}\zeta_F(s)$; this is an entire function of order one, real on the real axis, with $\xi_F(s)=\xi_F(1-s)$, and for $F=\mathbb{Q}$ it equals $2\xi(s)$ with $\xi$ Riemann's xi function. Its zeros are the nontrivial zeros of $\zeta_F$; write them as $ho= rac12+w_ho$, put $z_ho=w_ho^2$ (one value for each pair $\{ho,1-ho\}$, with multiplicity), and let $2m_F$ be the order of vanishing of $\xi_F$ at $ rac12$. A generalized gamma convolution (GGC) is a probability law on $[0,\infty)$ whose Laplace transform is $\exp ig(-bs-\int_{(0,\infty)}\log(1+s/t)\,U(dt) ig)$ with drift $b\ge0$ and a nonnegative Thorin measure $U$. For $u_0\ge0$ with $\xi_F( rac12+\sqrt{u_0})
e0$ put $\varphi_{F,u_0}(s)=\xi_F( rac12+\sqrt{u_0})/\xi_F( rac12+\sqrt{u_0+s})$, $s\ge0$. For $u_0\ge0$ the following are equivalent. (i) $\xi_F( rac12+\sqrt{u_0})
e0$ and $\varphi_{F,u_0}$ is the Laplace transform of a GGC. (ii) Every $z_ho$ is real with $z_ho<u_0$, and $m_F=0$ if $u_0=0$; equivalently, every nontrivial zero of $\zeta_F$ lies on the critical line or is a real zero $ eta$ with $| eta- rac12|<\sqrt{u_0}$, and $\zeta_F( rac12)
e0$ when $u_0=0$. When they hold, $b=0$ and the Thorin measure is $U_{F,u_0}=\sum_{\gamma>0}\delta_{u_0+\gamma^2}+m_F\,\delta_{u_0}+\sum_ eta\delta_{u_0-( eta- rac12)^2}$, where $ rac12+i\gamma$ runs over the zeros on the critical line with $\gamma>0$ and $ eta$ over the real zeros in $( rac12,1)$, all with multiplicity.
results.label: gl:thm:family

results.name: The tilts: Thorin property of a Dedekind zeta clock at tilt zero and at tilts above one quarter, the Thorin threshold and the shift between tilts
results.summary: The Thorin property of a Dedekind zeta function holds at every tilt $u_0\ge\frac14$ exactly when all nontrivial zeros are on the critical line or the real axis, at tilt $0$ exactly when they are all on the critical line with $\zeta_F(\frac12)\ne0$, and, when all nonreal zeros are on the line, exactly above a threshold set by the real zero farthest from the centre, with the Thorin measures at two tilts shifts of one another.
results.statement: Let $F$ be a number field with $r_1$ real and $r_2$ complex places, discriminant $d_F$ and Dedekind zeta function $\zeta_F$, and $\xi_F(s)=s(s-1)|d_F|^{s/2}\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s)^{r_1}\Gamma_{\mathbb{C}}(s)^{r_2}\zeta_F(s)$ with $\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s)=\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)$ and $\Gamma_{\mathbb{C}}(s)=2(2\pi)^{-s}\Gamma(s)$, an entire function, real on the real axis, with $\xi_F(s)=\xi_F(1-s)$ (it equals $2\xi$ for $F=\mathbb{Q}$). For $u_0\ge0$ put $\varphi_{F,u_0}(s)=\xi_F(\frac12+\sqrt{u_0})/\xi_F(\frac12+\sqrt{u_0+s})$, and say that the Thorin property holds at tilt $u_0$ if $\xi_F(\frac12+\sqrt{u_0})\ne0$ and $\varphi_{F,u_0}$ is the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution (GGC); its Thorin measure is then written $U_{F,u_0}$ (the drift is $0$). (a) At $u_0=0$: $\xi_F(\frac12)/\xi_F(\frac12+\sqrt s)$ is a GGC Laplace transform if and only if all nontrivial zeros of $\zeta_F$ lie on the critical line and $\zeta_F(\frac12)\ne0$. (b) For every $u_0\ge\frac14$, in particular at $u_0=\frac14$ and $u_0=1$, where $\xi_F$ is read from $1$ and from $\frac32$: $\varphi_{F,u_0}$ is a GGC Laplace transform if and only if every nontrivial zero of $\zeta_F$ lies on the critical line or on the real axis. (c) Define the Thorin threshold $u^*_F=\max(\beta-\frac12)^2$ over the real zeros $\beta\in[\frac12,1)$ of $\xi_F$, with $u^*_F=0$ if there are none. If all nonreal zeros lie on the critical line, the Thorin property holds at tilt $u_0$ exactly for $u_0>u^*_F$, and also at $u_0=0$ when there are no real zeros at all. (d) When the Thorin property holds at two tilts $u_1<u_0$, the measures are shifts of one another, $U_{F,u_0}(A)=U_{F,u_1}(A-(u_0-u_1))$ for Borel sets $A$ (each atom moves to the right by $u_0-u_1$), and $\varphi_{F,u_1}(s)=\varphi_{F,u_0}(s-(u_0-u_1))/\varphi_{F,u_0}(-(u_0-u_1))$, the exponential tilt of a GGC.
results.label: gl:cor:basepoints

results.name: Closed form of the transfer function from the real axis to the critical line under RH, and its odd index power sum expansion
results.status_text: conditional on The Riemann Hypothesis: every nontrivial zero of the Riemann zeta function has real part $\frac12$
results.conditions: The Riemann Hypothesis: every nontrivial zero of the Riemann zeta function has real part $\frac12$.
results.summary: Under RH the transfer function $\xi(\frac12+it)/\xi(\frac12+|t|)$ equals $\prod_{\gamma>0}(\gamma^2-t^2)/(\gamma^2+t^2)$, is real, even, bounded by $1$ and vanishes exactly at the ordinates, and its logarithm near $0$ involves only the odd index power sums of the inverse squared ordinates.
results.statement: Assume the Riemann Hypothesis. Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function, let $\gamma>0$ run over the ordinates of the zeros $\frac12+i\gamma$ of $\xi$ with multiplicity, let $\gamma_1$ be the smallest of them, and put $p_j=\sum_{\gamma>0}\gamma^{-2j}$. For all real $t$, $\mathfrak T(t):=\frac{\xi(\frac12+it)}{\xi(\frac12+|t|)}=\prod_{\gamma>0}\frac{\gamma^2-t^2}{\gamma^2+t^2}$, and $\mathfrak T$ is real, even, bounded by $1$ in modulus, and vanishes exactly at $t=\pm\gamma$. For $|t|<\gamma_1$, $\log\mathfrak T(t)=-2\sum_{\gamma>0}\operatorname{artanh}\big(\frac{t^2}{\gamma^2}\big)=-2\sum_{m\ge1}\frac{p_{2m-1}}{2m-1}\,t^{4m-2}$, which involves only the odd index power sums $p_1,p_3,p_5,\dots$.
results.label: gl:prop:transfer

results.name: The odd index power sums of the inverse squared ordinates determine the zeros under RH
results.status_text: conditional on The Riemann Hypothesis: every nontrivial zero of the Riemann zeta function has real part $\frac12$
results.conditions: The Riemann Hypothesis: every nontrivial zero of the Riemann zeta function has real part $\frac12$.
results.summary: Under RH the generating series of the odd index power sums $p_1,p_3,p_5,\dots$ of the inverse squared ordinates continues to a meromorphic function with poles at the points $\pm\gamma^2$, so these sums determine the ordinates with multiplicities and with them every power sum.
results.statement: Assume the Riemann Hypothesis. Let $\gamma>0$ run over the ordinates of the zeros $\frac12+i\gamma$ of Riemann's xi function with multiplicity, let $\gamma_1$ be the smallest of them, and put $p_j=\sum_{\gamma>0}\gamma^{-2j}$. The series $\sum_{m\ge1}p_{2m-1}z^{2m-1}$ converges for $|z|<\gamma_1^2$ and continues to the meromorphic function $\frac12\sum_{\gamma>0}\Big(\frac{1}{1-z/\gamma^2}-\frac{1}{1+z/\gamma^2}\Big)$, whose poles are the points $\pm\gamma^2$, each with residue $-\frac12\gamma^2$ times the multiplicity of $\gamma$. Hence the odd index power sums $\{p_{2m-1}\}$ determine the ordinates $\{\gamma\}$ with multiplicities, and with them every $p_j$.
results.label: gl:prop:odd

results.name: The transfer function as a Blaschke product for the right half plane under RH
results.status_text: conditional on The Riemann Hypothesis: every nontrivial zero of the Riemann zeta function has real part $\frac12$
results.conditions: The Riemann Hypothesis: every nontrivial zero of the Riemann zeta function has real part $\frac12$.
results.summary: Under RH the function $\mathfrak B(z)=\prod_{\gamma>0}(\gamma^2-z)/(\gamma^2+z)$, with $\mathfrak T(t)=\mathfrak B(t^2)$ for the transfer function $\mathfrak T$, is a Blaschke product for the right half plane with zeros at the points $\gamma^2$ and no singular inner factor.
results.statement: Assume the Riemann Hypothesis. Let $\gamma>0$ run over the ordinates of the zeros $\frac12+i\gamma$ of Riemann's xi function with multiplicity, and put $\mathfrak B(z)=\prod_{\gamma>0}(\gamma^2-z)/(\gamma^2+z)$, so that the transfer function $\mathfrak T(t)=\xi(\frac12+it)/\xi(\frac12+|t|)$ equals $\mathfrak B(t^2)$. Then $\mathfrak B$ is a Blaschke product for the right half plane: the product converges there, $|\mathfrak B(z)|<1$ for $\operatorname{Re}z>0$, $|\mathfrak B(z)|=1$ for $\operatorname{Re}z=0$, its zeros are the points $\gamma^2$, and it has no singular inner factor.
results.label: gl:prop:inner

results.name: Negative moments of the centre clock as a Mellin transform of the reciprocal of xi on the real axis
results.summary: For $\operatorname{Re}s>0$ the negative moment $\mathbb{E}[T^{-s}]$ of the centre clock of $\xi$ is the Mellin transform of $\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt u)$ divided by $\Gamma(s)$, with no hypothesis on the zeros.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function and let $T$ be the centre clock, the positive self decomposable random variable with Laplace transform $\mathbb{E}[e^{-uT}]=\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt u)$ for $u\ge0$ (it exists without any hypothesis on the zeros). For $\operatorname{Re}s>0$, with no hypothesis on the zeros, $\mathbb{E}[T^{-s}]=\frac{1}{\Gamma(s)}\int_0^\infty u^{s-1}\,\frac{\xi(\frac12)}{\xi(\frac12+\sqrt u)}\,du=\frac{2\,\xi(\frac12)}{\Gamma(s)}\int_0^\infty\frac{w^{2s-1}}{\xi(\frac12+w)}\,dw$.
results.label: gl:prop:negmom

results.name: Growth of the gamma function times the reciprocal of xi on vertical strips under RH: the growth hypothesis of the master theorem class
results.status_text: conditional on The Riemann Hypothesis, used through the bound $1/\zeta(w)=O(|\operatorname{Im}w|^\eta)$ on $\operatorname{Re}w\ge\frac12+\sigma_1$ for every $\eta>0$
results.conditions: The Riemann Hypothesis, used through the bound $1/\zeta(w)=O(|\operatorname{Im}w|^\eta)$ on $\operatorname{Re}w\ge\frac12+\sigma_1$ for every $\eta>0$.
results.summary: Under RH, on vertical strips $0<\sigma_1\le\operatorname{Re}s\le\sigma_2<\frac12$ the function $\Gamma(s)\,\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+s)$ is bounded by $C_\eta e^{-\pi|\tau|/4}|\tau|^{\sigma/2-9/4+\eta}$, which verifies the growth hypothesis of the master theorem class with exponential room, but a bound proved under RH cannot be an input to a proof of the Thorin property.
results.statement: Assume the Riemann Hypothesis. Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function, $F(s;0)=\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+s)$, $0<\sigma_1\le\sigma_2<\frac12$ and $\eta>0$. Then for $s=\sigma+i\tau$ with $\sigma_1\le\sigma\le\sigma_2$ and $|\tau|\ge1$, $|\Gamma(s)\,F(s;0)|\le C_\eta\,e^{-\pi|\tau|/4}\,|\tau|^{\sigma/2-9/4+\eta}$, uniformly in $\sigma$ and $\tau$ in this range. In particular the growth condition $|\Gamma(s)F(s;0)|\le C|\tau|^{\kappa(\sigma-\delta)}$ with $\kappa=1$ and $\delta=\frac12$, the growth condition of the class $Q_\infty(1,\frac12)$ (the extension by Chaudhry and Qadir (2012) of Hardy's class for Ramanujan's master theorem), holds on such strips, with exponential room. By the functional equation the same argument gives, for $-\sigma_2\le\sigma\le-\sigma_1$, the exponent $\frac32\sigma-\frac94+\eta$, which is smaller.
results.label: gl:lem:stirling

results.name: Absolute convergence hypothesis of the master theorem route for the reciprocal of xi holds without RH
results.summary: With no hypothesis on the zeros, the series $\mathfrak R(w)=\sum_{k\ge1}b_kw^k$ built from $\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+k)$ is entire of order $\frac23$ and its integral against the density of the centre clock converges for every $z>0$, which is the absolute convergence needed to interchange sum and integral in the master theorem route.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function, let $T$ be the centre clock, the self decomposable random variable with Laplace transform $\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt u)$ (it exists without any hypothesis on the zeros), and let $g$ be its density. Put $b_k=\frac{1}{\Gamma(k)}\,\frac{\xi(\frac12)}{\xi(\frac12+k)}$ and $\mathfrak R(w)=\sum_{k\ge1}b_kw^k$. With no hypothesis on the zeros, $\mathfrak R$ is entire of order $\frac23$, and $\int_0^\infty g(y)\,\mathfrak R(z/y)\,dy<\infty$ for every $z>0$.
results.label: gl:lem:fubini

results.name: The reciprocal Xi function in the shifted variable lies in Hardy's class with no hypothesis on the zeros, so the master theorem carries no information on them
results.summary: The function $\xi(\frac32)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt{1+w})$ is analytic and bounded on $\operatorname{Re}w\ge-\delta$ for $0<\delta<1$, hence in Hardy's class unconditionally, and the image region contains no zero of $\xi$, so Ramanujan's master theorem in this variable says nothing about the zeros.
results.statement: Let $\xi(s)=(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(1+\frac s2)\zeta(s)$ be the completed Riemann zeta function and $0<\delta<1$. Hardy's class consists of the functions $\varphi$ analytic on $\operatorname{Re}w\ge-\delta$ with $|\varphi(v+i\tau)|\le Ce^{Pv+A|\tau|}$ for some constants $C,P$ and $A<\pi$; for them $\int_0^\infty x^{w-1}\sum_{k\ge0}(-x)^k\varphi(k)/k!\,dx=\Gamma(w)\varphi(-w)$ for $0<\operatorname{Re}w<\delta$. The function $\varphi(w)=\xi(\frac32)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt{1+w})$, with the principal square root, is analytic and bounded on $\operatorname{Re}w\ge-\delta$. Hence, with no hypothesis on the zeros, it lies in Hardy's class with $P=0$ and any $A$. The image of $\operatorname{Re}w\ge-\delta$ under $w\mapsto\frac12+\sqrt{1+w}$ lies in $\{\sigma+i\tau:\sigma-\frac12\ge\sqrt{1-\delta+\tau^2}\}$, which contains no zero of $\xi$, so the master theorem identity in this variable carries no information on the zeros.
results.label: tx:prop:hardy

results.name: Why the square root stays: reciprocal Xi function in the variable s is not a Laplace transform of a random variable, and its values on a vertical line are not a characteristic function
results.summary: For every real $\alpha$ the function $s\mapsto\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+s)$ is not the Laplace transform of any real random variable, whether or not RH holds, the function $t\mapsto\xi(\alpha+it)/\xi(\alpha)$ is a characteristic function that is never infinitely divisible, and $t\mapsto\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+it)$ is unbounded.
results.statement: Let $\xi(s)=(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(1+\frac s2)\zeta(s)$ be the completed Riemann zeta function, and let $L$ be the class of the functions $s\mapsto\mathbb{E}e^{-sX}$, $X$ a real random variable, finite on an interval. Let $\Phi(u)=2\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u/2}-3\pi n^2e^{5u/2})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{2u})$ be the Pólya kernel, so that $\xi(\frac12+iz)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Phi(u)e^{izu}\,du$. (a) For every real $\alpha$, $s\mapsto\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+s)$ is not in $L$, whether or not RH holds. (b) For every real $\alpha$, $t\mapsto\xi(\alpha+it)/\xi(\alpha)$ is, unconditionally, the characteristic function of the probability density $\Phi(u)e^{(\alpha-\frac12)u}/\xi(\alpha)$, but it is never infinitely divisible, hence never the law of an exponential generalised gamma convolution. At $\alpha=\frac12$ it is $\Xi(t)/\Xi(0)$, where $\Xi(t)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Phi(u)\cos(tu)\,du=\xi(\frac12+it)$. (c) For every real $\alpha$, $t\mapsto\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+it)$ is unbounded, so it is not a characteristic function.
results.label: tx:thm:nosqrt

results.name: Thorin representation of the reciprocal of the completed Dirichlet L function of a real primitive character under GRH
results.status_text: conditional on The generalized Riemann hypothesis for $L(s,\chi)$ (every nontrivial zero has real part $\frac12$) and $L(\frac12,\chi)\ne0$ (Chowla's conjecture for real characters, open)
results.conditions: The generalized Riemann hypothesis for $L(s,\chi)$ (every nontrivial zero has real part $\frac12$) and $L(\frac12,\chi)\ne0$ (Chowla's conjecture for real characters, open).
results.summary: For a real primitive character $\chi$, under GRH for $L(s,\chi)$ and $L(\frac12,\chi)\ne0$, the reciprocal $\xi(\frac12,\chi)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt u,\chi)$ is the Laplace transform of the GGC $\sum_{\gamma>0}e_\gamma/\gamma^2$ over the ordinates of the zeros, and the clock identities of the Riemann case carry over.
results.statement:
Let $\chi$ be a real primitive character modulo $q>1$ of parity $a\in\{0,1\}$ (so $\chi(-1)=(-1)^a$) and $\xi(s,\chi)=(q/\pi)^{(s+a)/2}\Gamma( rac{s+a}2)L(s,\chi)$ the completed Dirichlet $L$ function, an entire function of order one, real on the real axis, with $\xi(s,\chi)=\xi(1-s,\chi)$. Assume GRH for $L(s,\chi)$ and $L( rac12,\chi)
e0$, and write the zeros as $ rac12\pm i\gamma$ with $\gamma>0$, counted with multiplicity. Then $T_\chi\stackrel{d}{=}\sum_{\gamma>0}e_\gamma/\gamma^2$, with $e_\gamma$ independent standard exponential variables, is a GGC with $\xi( rac12,\chi)/\xi( rac12+\sqrt u,\chi)=\mathbb{E}[e^{-uT_\chi}]$ for $u\ge0$ and cumulants $(j-1)!\,p_j(\chi)$, $p_j(\chi)=\sum_{\gamma>0}\gamma^{-2j}$. The analogues for $\xi(\cdot,\chi)$ of the statements for Riemann's $\xi$ under RH on the transfer function from the real axis to the critical line, the odd index power sums of the inverse squared ordinates, the Blaschke product of the transfer function and the negative moments of the clock hold, with GRH for $L(s,\chi)$ and $L( rac12,\chi)
e0$ in place of RH and $\xi( rac12)
e0$. At the tilt $u_0= rac14$, $\sum_{\gamma>0} rac{1}{\gamma^2+1/4}= rac{\xi'}{\xi}(1,\chi)= rac12\log rac q\pi+ rac12\,\psi ig( rac{1+a}{2} ig)+ rac{L'}{L}(1,\chi)$, with $\psi$ the digamma function, and $\mathbb{E}[e^{-T_\chi/4}]=\xi( rac12,\chi)/\xi(1,\chi)$.
results.label: gl:prop:Lreal

results.name: Thorin representation for a complex character through the product of the completed L function with its conjugate, under GRH
results.status_text: conditional on The generalized Riemann hypothesis for $L(s,\chi)$ (every nontrivial zero has real part $\frac12$) and $L(\frac12,\chi)\ne0$
results.conditions: The generalized Riemann hypothesis for $L(s,\chi)$ (every nontrivial zero has real part $\frac12$) and $L(\frac12,\chi)\ne0$.
results.summary: For a complex primitive character $\chi$, the product $\xi(s,\chi)\xi(s,\bar\chi)$ is symmetric under $s\mapsto1-s$, and under GRH for $L(s,\chi)$ with $L(\frac12,\chi)\ne0$ the reciprocal of its ratio to the centre is the Laplace transform of the GGC $\sum e_\gamma/\gamma^2$ over all ordinates of $L(s,\chi)$ of both signs.
results.statement: Let $\chi$ be a complex primitive character modulo $q>1$ of parity $a\in\{0,1\}$ and $\xi(s,\chi)=(q/\pi)^{(s+a)/2}\Gamma(\frac{s+a}2)L(s,\chi)$ the completed Dirichlet $L$ function, an entire function of order one with $\xi(s,\chi)=W_\chi\,\xi(1-s,\bar\chi)$ and $|W_\chi|=1$. Put $\xi_{\chi\bar\chi}(s)=\xi(s,\chi)\,\xi(s,\bar\chi)$. Then $\xi_{\chi\bar\chi}(s)=\xi_{\chi\bar\chi}(1-s)$ and $\xi_{\chi\bar\chi}(\sigma)=|\xi(\sigma,\chi)|^2$ for real $\sigma$. If GRH holds for $L(s,\chi)$ and $L(\frac12,\chi)\ne0$, then $\xi_{\chi\bar\chi}(\frac12)/\xi_{\chi\bar\chi}(\frac12+\sqrt u)=\mathbb{E}[e^{-uT_{\chi\bar\chi}}]$ for $u\ge0$, where $T_{\chi\bar\chi}\stackrel{d}{=}\sum_{\gamma\in\Gamma_\chi}e_\gamma/\gamma^2$, $\Gamma_\chi$ is the multiset of all ordinates $\gamma$, of both signs, of the zeros $\frac12+i\gamma$ of $L(s,\chi)$, and the $e_\gamma$ are independent standard exponential variables.
results.label: gl:prop:Lcomplex

results.name: Factorisation of the completed Dedekind zeta function of a quadratic field and clocks of cyclotomic fields as independent sums
results.status_text: conditional on The statement on cyclotomic fields assumes GRH for the Dirichlet $L$ functions of the nonprincipal primitive characters of conductor dividing $q$ and that their values at $\frac12$ are nonzero (the hypotheses of the propositions on real and complex characters). The factorisations of the completed functions hold without any hypothesis, and the statement for quadratic fields is an implication from the Thorin property of the two factors at the tilt considered
results.conditions: The statement on cyclotomic fields assumes GRH for the Dirichlet $L$ functions of the nonprincipal primitive characters of conductor dividing $q$ and that their values at $\frac12$ are nonzero (the hypotheses of the propositions on real and complex characters). The factorisations of the completed functions hold without any hypothesis, and the statement for quadratic fields is an implication from the Thorin property of the two factors at the tilt considered.
results.summary: For a quadratic field the completed Dedekind zeta function is $2\xi(s)\xi(s,\chi)$ (times $q^{-1/2}$ for odd $\chi$), so at a tilt where both factors have the Thorin property the tilted clock is the independent sum of theirs and the Thorin measures add, and for cyclotomic fields, under GRH with nonzero central values, the clock is the independent sum of the clocks of $\zeta$ and of the nonprincipal primitive characters of conductor dividing $q$.
results.statement: Let $\chi$ be a real primitive character of conductor $q$ and parity $a\in\{0,1\}$, with $\xi(s,\chi)=(q/\pi)^{(s+a)/2}\Gamma(\frac{s+a}2)L(s,\chi)$, let $F=\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt D)$ with $D=\chi(-1)q$ a fundamental discriminant (so $\zeta_F=\zeta\cdot L(\cdot,\chi)$, and $F$ is real quadratic for even $\chi$ and imaginary quadratic for odd $\chi$), let $\xi_F(s)=s(s-1)|d_F|^{s/2}\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s)^{r_1}\Gamma_{\mathbb{C}}(s)^{r_2}\zeta_F(s)$ be its completed Dedekind zeta function ($d_F$ the discriminant, $r_1$ and $r_2$ the numbers of real and complex places, $\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s)=\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)$, $\Gamma_{\mathbb{C}}(s)=2(2\pi)^{-s}\Gamma(s)$) and let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function. Then $\xi_F(s)=2\,\xi(s)\,\xi(s,\chi)$ when $\chi$ is even and $\xi_F(s)=2q^{-1/2}\,\xi(s)\,\xi(s,\chi)$ when $\chi$ is odd. For a function $f$ the tilted clock at tilt $u_0\ge0$ is the random variable with Laplace transform $f(\frac12+\sqrt{u_0})/f(\frac12+\sqrt{u_0+s})$, and the centre clock is the case $u_0=0$. Consequently, at any tilt $u_0\ge0$ at which $\xi$ and $\xi(\cdot,\chi)$ both have the Thorin property (this reciprocal is the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution), so does $\xi_F$, its tilted clock is the independent sum of the tilted clocks of $\xi$ and of $\xi(\cdot,\chi)$, and the Thorin measures add, $U_{F,u_0}=U_{\mathbb{Q},u_0}+U_{\chi,u_0}$, where $U_{\chi,u_0}$ is the Thorin measure of the tilted clock of $\xi(\cdot,\chi)$; at $u_0=0$ this reads $T_F\stackrel d=T_\zeta+T_\chi$ for the centre clocks, and the cumulants add, $p_j(F)=p_j(\zeta)+p_j(\chi)$ with $p_j=\sum_{\gamma>0}\gamma^{-2j}$ over the ordinates of the zeros. For the cyclotomic field $F_q=\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_q)$, $q\ge3$, under GRH for the Dirichlet $L$ functions of the nonprincipal primitive characters of conductor dividing $q$ and with their values at $\frac12$ nonzero, the centre clock $T_{F_q}$ is the independent sum of $T_\zeta$ (the centre clock of $\xi$), of $T_\chi$ (the centre clock of $\xi(\cdot,\chi)$) over the real primitive characters $\chi$ of conductor $f\mid q$ with $f>1$, and of $T_{\chi\bar\chi}$ (the centre clock of $\xi(s,\chi)\xi(s,\bar\chi)$) over the conjugate pairs of complex primitive characters of conductor dividing $q$.
results.label: gl:prop:dedekind

results.name: Lévy decomposition of the logarithm of the completed Dedekind zeta function of any number field, with signs
results.summary: For $\alpha>1$ the compensated logarithm of $\xi_F(\alpha+s)/\xi_F(\alpha)$ is an integral against a signed Lévy measure whose arithmetic part has the positive weights $\Lambda_F(n)$ at $\log n$, plus gamma factor densities and the single negative density $-(1+e^x)$ coming from the factor $s(s-1)$.
results.statement: Let $F$ be a number field with $r_1$ real and $r_2$ complex places and Dedekind zeta function $\zeta_F$, and $\xi_F(s)=s(s-1)|d_F|^{s/2}\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s)^{r_1}\Gamma_{\mathbb{C}}(s)^{r_2}\zeta_F(s)$ its completed Dedekind zeta function ($d_F$ the discriminant, $\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s)=\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)$, $\Gamma_{\mathbb{C}}(s)=2(2\pi)^{-s}\Gamma(s)$). Let $\Lambda_F(n)=\sum_{N\mathfrak p^r=n}\log N\mathfrak p\ge0$, the sum over prime ideals $\mathfrak p$ and integers $r\ge1$ with $N\mathfrak p^r=n$, and $h_s(x)=e^{-sx}-1+sx\ge0$. For $\alpha>1$ and $s\ge0$, $\log\frac{\xi_F(\alpha+s)}{\xi_F(\alpha)}-s\,\frac{\xi_F'}{\xi_F}(\alpha)=\int_0^\infty h_s(x)\,e^{-\alpha x}\,\frac{\nu_F(dx)}x$ with the signed measure $\nu_F(dx)=\Big(\frac{r_1}{1-e^{-2x}}+\frac{r_2}{1-e^{-x}}-1-e^x\Big)dx+\sum_{n\ge2}\Lambda_F(n)\,\delta_{\log n}(dx)$.
results.label: gl:prop:levyF

results.name: The sine squared lemma on the prime side for Dedekind zeta functions and real Dirichlet characters
results.summary: For $\alpha>1$ and $f$ the completed Dedekind zeta function of a number field or the completed $L$ function of a real primitive character, the reciprocal $f(\alpha)/f(\alpha+\sqrt u)$ equals $\exp(-\int_0^\infty\log(1+u/b^2)\,v_\alpha(b)\,db/\pi)$ with $v_\alpha(b)=\operatorname{Re}(f'/f)(\alpha+ib)$ written through a sine squared transform of the Lévy measure (Polson's sine squared lemma applied to $f$), so that the density is determined by the primes with no reference to the zeros.
results.statement:
Let $f$ be either $\xi_F(s)=s(s-1)|d_F|^{s/2}\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s)^{r_1}\Gamma_{\mathbb{C}}(s)^{r_2}\zeta_F(s)$, the completed Dedekind zeta function of a number field $F$ with discriminant $d_F$, $r_1$ real and $r_2$ complex places, $\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s)=\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)$ and $\Gamma_{\mathbb{C}}(s)=2(2\pi)^{-s}\Gamma(s)$, or $\xi(\cdot,\chi)$, the completed Dirichlet $L$ function $\xi(s,\chi)=(q/\pi)^{(s+a)/2}\Gamma( rac{s+a}2)L(s,\chi)$ of a real primitive character $\chi$ modulo $q>1$ of parity $a\in\{0,1\}$. Let $\alpha>1$, $h_w(x)=e^{-wx}-1+wx$, and let $
u$ be the signed Lévy measure of $f$, defined by $\log rac{f(\alpha+w)}{f(\alpha)}-w\, rac{f'}{f}(\alpha)=\int_0^\infty h_w(x)\,e^{-\alpha x}\, rac{
u(dx)}x$ for $w\ge0$: for $f=\xi_F$, $
u_F(dx)=\Big( rac{r_1}{1-e^{-2x}}+ rac{r_2}{1-e^{-x}}-1-e^x\Big)dx+\sum_{n\ge2}\Lambda_F(n)\,\delta_{\log n}(dx)$ with $\Lambda_F(n)=\sum_{N\mathfrak p^r=n}\log N\mathfrak p$; for $f=\xi(\cdot,\chi)$, $
u_\chi(dx)=\sum_{n\ge2}\chi(n)\Lambda(n)\,\delta_{\log n}(dx)+ rac{e^{(1-a)x}}{2\sinh x}\,dx$, where $\Lambda$ is the von Mangoldt function. Then, for $u\ge0$, $ rac{f(\alpha)}{f(\alpha+\sqrt u)}=\exp\Big(-\int_0^\infty\log\Big(1+ rac u{b^2}\Big)\, rac{v_\alpha(b)}\pi\,db\Big)$, where $v_\alpha(b)= rac{f'}{f}(\alpha)+\int_0^\infty2\sin^2\Big( rac{bx}2\Big)e^{-\alpha x}\,
u(dx)=\operatorname{Re} rac{f'}{f}(\alpha+ib)$.
results.label: gl:prop:sinsq

results.name: The basepoint family of the sine squared lemma: Thorin property at a basepoint to the right of all zeros, failure when a zero lies to the right, and the Poisson form under GRH
results.status_text: conditional on Part (c) assumes GRH for $f$ (every zero has real part $\frac12$) and $f(\frac12)\ne0$. Parts (a) and (b) hold without any hypothesis, and part (a) holds unconditionally for every $\alpha\ge1$
results.conditions: Part (c) assumes GRH for $f$ (every zero has real part $\frac12$) and $f(\frac12)\ne0$. Parts (a) and (b) hold without any hypothesis, and part (a) holds unconditionally for every $\alpha\ge1$.
results.summary: For the completed Dedekind zeta function of a number field or the completed $L$ function of a real primitive character, the reciprocal $f(\alpha)/f(\alpha+\sqrt u)$ is a GGC with a positive Thorin density that is a sum over the zeros when every zero lies to the left of $\alpha$ (so unconditionally for $\alpha\ge1$), is not a GGC transform when a zero lies to the right, and under GRH the density is the Poisson smoothing of the zero counting measure at height $\alpha-\frac12$.
results.statement:
Let $f$ be either $\xi_F(s)=s(s-1)|d_F|^{s/2}\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s)^{r_1}\Gamma_{\mathbb{C}}(s)^{r_2}\zeta_F(s)$, the completed Dedekind zeta function of a number field $F$ with discriminant $d_F$, $r_1$ real and $r_2$ complex places, where $\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s)=\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)$ and $\Gamma_{\mathbb{C}}(s)=2(2\pi)^{-s}\Gamma(s)$, or $\xi(s,\chi)=(q/\pi)^{(s+a)/2}\Gamma( rac{s+a}2)L(s,\chi)$, the completed Dirichlet $L$ function of a real primitive character $\chi$ modulo $q>1$ of parity $a\in\{0,1\}$ (each is entire and real on the real axis, with $f(s)=f(1-s)$), with zeros $ho= eta+i\gamma$ counted with multiplicity, and for $\alpha> rac12$ put $v_\alpha(b)=\operatorname{Re} rac{f'}{f}(\alpha+ib)$. Say that $f$ has the Thorin property at the basepoint $\alpha> rac12$ if $f(\alpha)
e0$ and $u\mapsto f(\alpha)/f(\alpha+\sqrt u)$ is the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution (GGC). (a) If every zero has $ eta<\alpha$, then $ rac{f(\alpha)}{f(\alpha+\sqrt u)}=\exp ig(-\int_0^\infty\log(1+u/b^2)\, rac{v_\alpha(b)}\pi\,db ig)$ for $u\ge0$, with $ rac{v_\alpha(b)}\pi= rac1\pi\sum_ho\operatorname{Re} rac{1}{\alpha+ib-ho}= rac1\pi\sum_ho rac{\alpha- eta}{(\alpha- eta)^2+(b-\gamma)^2}>0$, so $f$ has the Thorin property at the basepoint $\alpha$, with no drift and Thorin measure $U_\alpha(dt)=v_\alpha(\sqrt t)\,dt/(2\pi\sqrt t)$. Since every zero has $ eta<1$, this holds unconditionally for every $\alpha\ge1$. (b) If some zero has $ eta>\alpha$ and $f(\alpha)
e0$, then $f$ does not have the Thorin property at the basepoint $\alpha$. Hence $f$ has it at every basepoint $\alpha> rac12$ if and only if every zero lies on the critical line. (c) Under GRH for $f$ (every zero has real part $ rac12$), and if $f( rac12)
e0$, with $\varepsilon=\alpha- rac12$, $ rac{v_\alpha(b)}\pi=\sum_{\gamma>0} ig(P_\varepsilon(b-\gamma)+P_\varepsilon(b+\gamma) ig)$ with $P_\varepsilon(x)= rac{\varepsilon}{\pi(\varepsilon^2+x^2)}$, the Poisson smoothing at height $\varepsilon$ of the zero counting measure. As $\alpha\downarrow rac12$, $(v_\alpha(b)/\pi)\,db	o\sum_{\gamma>0}\delta_\gamma$ vaguely on $[0,\infty)$, and $U_\alpha$ tends to $\sum_{\gamma>0}\delta_{\gamma^2}$, the Thorin measure of the centre clock.
results.label: gl:thm:sinsq

results.name: GRH and nonvanishing at the centre from the Thorin property of the Dedekind zeta functions of quadratic and cyclotomic fields
results.summary: If the tilted reciprocal of the Dedekind zeta function of a quadratic field is a GGC at tilt $1$, then RH holds and the zeros of the Dirichlet $L$ function are on the critical line or real; if it is a GGC at tilt $0$, then GRH holds for that $L$ function with $L(\frac12,\chi)\ne0$; and if this holds at tilt $0$ for every cyclotomic field, then GRH holds for all Dirichlet $L$ functions with all central values nonzero.
results.statement: Let $\chi$ be a real primitive character of conductor $q$, $F=\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt D)$ with $D=\chi(-1)q$ the quadratic field of $\chi$ (so that $\zeta_F(s)=\zeta(s)L(s,\chi)$), $\xi_F(s)=s(s-1)|d_F|^{s/2}\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s)^{r_1}\Gamma_{\mathbb{C}}(s)^{r_2}\zeta_F(s)$ its completed Dedekind zeta function ($d_F$ the discriminant, $r_1$ and $r_2$ the numbers of real and complex places, $\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s)=\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)$, $\Gamma_{\mathbb{C}}(s)=2(2\pi)^{-s}\Gamma(s)$), and $\varphi_{F,u_0}(s)=\xi_F(\frac12+\sqrt{u_0})/\xi_F(\frac12+\sqrt{u_0+s})$ for $u_0\ge0$. (a) If $\varphi_{F,1}$ is the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution (GGC), then RH holds and every nontrivial zero of $L(s,\chi)$ lies on the critical line or is real. (b) If $\varphi_{F,0}$ is the Laplace transform of a GGC, equivalently $\varphi_{F,1}$ is one with Thorin measure in $(1,\infty)$, then $L(s,\chi)$ satisfies GRH (all its nontrivial zeros lie on the critical line) and $L(\frac12,\chi)\ne0$. If $\varphi_{F_q,0}$ is a GGC Laplace transform for every $q\ge3$, with $F_q=\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_q)$, then GRH holds for all Dirichlet $L$ functions, and $L(\frac12,\chi)\ne0$ for every primitive character $\chi$.
results.label: gl:thm:grh

results.name: Mixtures of clocks: a mixture of two GGC Laplace transforms with discrete unit atom Thorin measures is not a GGC transform when it vanishes off the atoms, in particular in the odd configuration
results.summary: A mixture $\lambda\varphi_1+(1-\lambda)\varphi_2$ of two GGC Laplace transforms whose Thorin measures are sums of unit point masses is not a GGC transform if it vanishes at a negative point that is not an atom, and this happens for every weight $\lambda$ when two consecutive atoms of the union belong to different measures and an odd number of atoms lie at or below the first of them.
results.statement: Let $\varphi_1,\varphi_2$ be Laplace transforms of generalized gamma convolutions (GGCs: laws on $[0,\infty)$ with Laplace transform $\exp(-bs-\int_{(0,\infty)}\log(1+s/t)\,U(dt))$, drift $b\ge0$ and Thorin measure $U$) with zero drift and Thorin measures $U_1,U_2$ that are sums of unit point masses, repeated according to multiplicity, so that $\varphi_i(s)=\prod_t t/(t+s)$, over the atoms $t$ of $U_i$, is meromorphic on $\mathbb{C}$ with poles at the points $-t$. Let $0<\lambda<1$ and $\varphi=\lambda\varphi_1+(1-\lambda)\varphi_2$. (a) If $\varphi(-x)=0$ for some $x>0$ that is not an atom of $U_1$ or $U_2$, then $\varphi$ is not the Laplace transform of a GGC. (b) Let $t_1<t_2$ be consecutive points of $\operatorname{supp}U_1\cup\operatorname{supp}U_2$ with $t_1$ an atom of only one of the measures and $t_2$ an atom of only the other. If $U_1+U_2$ has an odd number of atoms in $(0,t_1]$, counted with multiplicity, then $\varphi$ has a zero in $(-t_2,-t_1)$, so $\varphi$ is not the Laplace transform of a GGC, for any $\lambda$.
results.label: gl:prop:mixture

results.name: The family of characters modulo 5: no mixture of the two clocks is a GGC, under GRH
results.status_text: conditional on The generalized Riemann hypothesis for $L(s,\chi_5)$ and for $L(s,\psi)$ (every nontrivial zero has real part $\frac12$). The values $L(\frac12,\chi_5)$ and $L(\frac12,\psi)$ are certified nonzero, and the zeros below height $12$ are certified, in ball arithmetic; neither is assumed
results.conditions: The generalized Riemann hypothesis for $L(s,\chi_5)$ and for $L(s,\psi)$ (every nontrivial zero has real part $\frac12$). The values $L(\frac12,\chi_5)$ and $L(\frac12,\psi)$ are certified nonzero, and the zeros below height $12$ are certified, in ball arithmetic; neither is assumed.
results.summary: Under GRH for the two members of the family of primitive characters modulo $5$, no mixture of their clocks, the uniform one included, is a GGC, because certified zero counts below height $12$ put their Thorin atoms in the odd configuration of the mixture criterion.
results.statement: Let $\chi_5$ be the real primitive character modulo $5$ (the Legendre symbol, even) and $\psi$ the primitive character modulo $5$ with $\psi(2)=i$ (odd). For a primitive character $\chi$ modulo $q$ of parity $a\in\{0,1\}$ let $\xi(s,\chi)=(q/\pi)^{(s+a)/2}\Gamma(\frac{s+a}2)L(s,\chi)$, and put $\xi_{\psi\bar\psi}(s)=\xi(s,\psi)\,\xi(s,\bar\psi)$. A generalized gamma convolution (GGC) is a probability law on $[0,\infty)$ whose Laplace transform is $\exp\big(-bs-\int_{(0,\infty)}\log(1+s/t)\,U(dt)\big)$ with drift $b\ge0$ and a nonnegative Thorin measure $U$. Assume GRH for $L(s,\chi_5)$ and $L(s,\psi)$. Then for every $\lambda\in(0,1)$ the function $u\mapsto\lambda\,\xi(\frac12,\chi_5)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt u,\chi_5)+(1-\lambda)\,\xi_{\psi\bar\psi}(\frac12)/\xi_{\psi\bar\psi}(\frac12+\sqrt u)$, $u\ge0$, is not the Laplace transform of a GGC. In particular the case $\lambda=\frac12$, the clock of a uniformly chosen member of the family $\{\chi_5,\{\psi,\bar\psi\}\}$ of primitive characters modulo $5$, is not a GGC.
results.label: gl:prop:mod5

results.name: A real zero of a Dirichlet L function makes the first rung of the twisted heat trace fail beyond an explicit time
results.summary: If $L(s,\chi)$ of a primitive real character has a real zero $\beta$ in $(\tfrac12,1)$ and all its nonreal zeros lie on the critical line, the twisted heat trace grows and is increasing beyond an explicit time $t_1$, so it is not completely monotone, already at order one.
results.statement: Let $\chi$ be a primitive real Dirichlet character of conductor $q\ge3$, $L(s,\chi)$ its $L$ function, and $\xi(s,\chi)$ the completed $L$ function, an entire function with $\xi(s,\chi)=\xi(1-s,\chi)$. With zeros counted with multiplicity and $z_\rho=(\rho-\tfrac12)^2$, the twisted heat trace is $W(t;\chi)=\sum_{\operatorname{Im}\rho>0}e^{tz_\rho}+\tfrac12\sum_{\rho\text{ real}}e^{tz_\rho}$ for $t>0$. Let $\beta\in(\tfrac12,1)$ be the largest real zero of $L(s,\chi)$, suppose that every nonreal zero of $L(s,\chi)$ lies on the critical line, and put $c=(\beta-\tfrac12)^2$. Then $W(t;\chi)\to\infty$ as $t\to\infty$, and $-W'(t;\chi)<0$ for all $t>t_1=\max\{1,c^{-1}\log(C'\log q/c)\}$, where $C'$ is an absolute constant. Hence $W(\cdot\,;\chi)$ is not completely monotone, the first rung of the ladder $(-1)^kW^{(k)}>0$ failing at order $k=1$ beyond $t_1$. The book adds the following consequence, which rests on the unrefereed theorem of Banks and Kerr (October 2026) that there are absolute constants $q_0$ and $\delta_0>0$ with $(1-\beta)\log q\ge\delta_0$ for every real zero $\beta$ of every primitive real character of conductor $q\ge q_0$: for $q\ge q_0$ and $\eta=\delta_0/\log q$ one has $c\le\tfrac14-\eta(1-\eta)$, so the growth rate $c$ is at least $\eta(1-\eta)$ below the rate $\tfrac14$ of the pole term $e^{t/4}$ of $\zeta$. That consequence is conditional on the Banks and Kerr theorem and is not part of the proved status of this entry; the first part (the growth and the sign of $-W'$) uses only the bound $N(T,\chi)\ll(T+1)\log(q(T+2))$ for the number of zeros up to height $T$.
results.label: gl:prop:rung1

results.name: Linnik constant seven from the Thorin property of all cyclotomic fields (weaker than the known result under GRH)
results.status_text: conditional on The Thorin property at tilt $0$ for every cyclotomic field $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_q)$, $q\ge3$, which by the equivalence theorem of the chapter is GRH for all Dirichlet $L$ functions together with $L(\frac12,\chi)\ne0$ for every primitive character $\chi$. The proof uses only the GRH part, through the theorem of Heath-Brown and Puchta (2002) that GRH gives seven powers of two
results.conditions: The Thorin property at tilt $0$ for every cyclotomic field $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_q)$, $q\ge3$, which by the equivalence theorem of the chapter is GRH for all Dirichlet $L$ functions together with $L(\frac12,\chi)\ne0$ for every primitive character $\chi$. The proof uses only the GRH part, through the theorem of Heath-Brown and Puchta (2002) that GRH gives seven powers of two.
results.summary: If the centre clock of every cyclotomic field $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_q)$, $q\ge3$, is a GGC, then every sufficiently large even integer is a sum of two primes and at most seven powers of two, which is the value that GRH already gives, so the corollary is weaker than the theorem of Heath-Brown and Puchta (2002), also proved by Pintz and Ruzsa (2003), that GRH alone gives seven, because it assumes nonvanishing at the centre as well.
results.statement: Suppose that for every integer $q\ge3$ the function $\varphi_{F,0}(s)=\xi_F(\frac12)/\xi_F(\frac12+\sqrt s)$, with $\xi_F(s)=s(s-1)|d_F|^{s/2}\Gamma_{\mathbb{C}}(s)^{\varphi(q)/2}\zeta_F(s)$, $\Gamma_{\mathbb{C}}(s)=2(2\pi)^{-s}\Gamma(s)$, the completed Dedekind zeta function of the cyclotomic field $F=\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_q)$, a totally complex field of degree $\varphi(q)$ and discriminant $d_F$, is the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution. Then every sufficiently large even integer is a sum of two primes and at most seven powers of two.
results.label: gl:cor:K7

results.name: Open problem: the Thorin property of the Riemann clock and of cyclotomic clocks without first knowing the zeros
results.summary: Prove that the tilted reciprocal of the completed zeta function of $\mathbb{Q}$, or of a cyclotomic field, is the Laplace transform of a GGC without first knowing the zeros, in particular by settling the parabolic distortion in the master theorem route; for $\mathbb{Q}$ at the centre this is RH itself.
results.statement: Let $\xi_F(s)=s(s-1)|d_F|^{s/2}\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s)^{r_1}\Gamma_{\mathbb{C}}(s)^{r_2}\zeta_F(s)$ be the completed Dedekind zeta function of a number field $F$ ($d_F$ the discriminant, $r_1$ and $r_2$ the numbers of real and complex places, $\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s)=\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)$, $\Gamma_{\mathbb{C}}(s)=2(2\pi)^{-s}\Gamma(s)$) and $\varphi_{F,u_0}(s)=\xi_F(\frac12+\sqrt{u_0})/\xi_F(\frac12+\sqrt{u_0+s})$ its tilted reciprocal. Prove that $\varphi_{\mathbb{Q},u_0}$, or $\varphi_{F,u_0}$ for the cyclotomic fields $F$, is the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution (the first condition of the equivalence theorem on the Thorin property of the tilted clock), without first knowing the second condition, namely the position of the zeros. In the route through Ramanujan's master theorem, which expands $\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt u)$ term by term, settle the parabolic distortion (the Laplace variable is $u=s^2$, and the squaring map carries the strip $|\operatorname{Re}s|<1$ onto the region $\{|\operatorname{Im}u|<2\sqrt{1-\operatorname{Re}u}\}$), uniformly in the field, and find a substitute for the residue bookkeeping at the zeros. For $\mathbb{Q}$ at $u_0=0$ the statement to be proved is the Riemann Hypothesis, so a growth bound that is itself proved under RH cannot be an input to its proof.
results.label: gl:op:direct

results.name: Open problem: seven powers of two from GRH with possible real zeros, that is from the Thorin property at tilt one for cyclotomic fields
results.summary: Show that every sufficiently large even integer is a sum of two primes and at most seven powers of two from the weaker hypothesis that every nontrivial zero of every Dirichlet $L$ function lies on the critical line or on the real axis, which would make real and Siegel zeros irrelevant to this value.
results.statement: Show that every sufficiently large even integer is a sum of two primes and at most seven powers of two (the Linnik constant $K=7$) from the hypothesis that for every cyclotomic field $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_q)$, $q\ge3$, the tilted reciprocal $\varphi_{\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_q),1}$ of the completed Dedekind zeta function at tilt $u_0=1$ is the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution; by the equivalence theorem of the chapter this hypothesis says that every nontrivial zero of every Dirichlet $L$ function lies on the critical line or on the real axis, that is, GRH with possible real zeros. The book locates, by a heuristic estimate, the arcs of the circle method on which a real zero can make the minor arc bound of exponent $\frac34$ for the sum over primes fail; what remains is to move these arcs into the major arcs and to redo the main term of the major arc estimate with several real zeros, checking that its constant survives. If it works, real zeros, and with them Siegel zeros, become irrelevant to $K=7$.
results.label: gl:op:exceptional

results.name: Open problem: the anchored tail of the moment identity of the centre clock at large height and for Dirichlet L functions
results.summary: Carry the anchored tail of the zero side of the moment identity of the centre clock to large height with tables of zeros of zeta, where the remaining integral of the zero count fluctuation sets the limit and calls for an explicit formula, and to Dirichlet $L$ functions.
results.statement: Let $T$ be the centre clock of Riemann's xi function. Its moments are computed from the power sums $p_j=\sum_{\gamma>0}\gamma^{-2j}$ of the inverse squared ordinates of the zeros, summed over the first zeros and completed by a tail. With $N(t)$ the zero count, $N_0=\vartheta/\pi$ with $\vartheta$ the Riemann Siegel theta function, and $S(t)=N(t)-N_0(t)-1$, the tail beyond a height $H$ satisfies exactly $\sum_{\gamma>H}\gamma^{-2j}=\int_H^\infty t^{-2j}\,\frac{\vartheta'(t)}{\pi}\,dt+\big(N_0(H)+1-N(H)\big)H^{-2j}+2j\int_H^\infty S(t)\,t^{-2j-1}\,dt$, and the anchored tail keeps the first two terms. Carry the anchoring to large height with tables of zeros of the Riemann zeta function, where the remaining term, the integral of $S(t)\,t^{-2j-1}$ over the tail, sets the limit and calls for an explicit formula for $\int S$, and to Dirichlet $L(s,\chi)$ with tables of their zeros. The book reproduces the anchoring only for the first ordinates; large heights and the characters are open.
results.label: gl:op:numerics

results.name: Open problem: the negative moment of the clock averaged over real characters of conductor in [Q,2Q] against the symplectic random matrix prediction
results.summary: Compute the average of the negative moment $\mathbb{E}[T_\chi^{-1/2}]$ of the clock over real primitive characters of conductor in $[Q,2Q]$ and compare it with the prediction of the symplectic ensemble, noting that this moment is not a linear statistic of the zeros.
results.statement: For a real primitive character $\chi$ let $T_\chi$ be the clock (under GRH for $L(s,\chi)$ and $L(\frac12,\chi)\ne0$) with Laplace transform $\xi(\frac12,\chi)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt u,\chi)$, and $T$ the centre clock of Riemann's xi function. The negative moment $\mathbb{E}[T^{-1/2}]=\Gamma(\frac12)^{-1}\int_0^\infty u^{-1/2}\prod_{\gamma>0}(1+u/\gamma^2)^{-1}\,du$, the product being over the ordinates $\gamma>0$ of the zeros, is computed from $\xi$ alone, and the book finds it to be mostly a smooth statistic of the zeros, so that a single function says little and the natural comparison with random matrix theory is in families. Compute the average of $\mathbb{E}[T_\chi^{-1/2}]$ over the real primitive characters $\chi$ of conductor in $[Q,2Q]$ and compare it with the prediction of the symplectic ensemble. Since $\mathbb{E}[T^{-1/2}]$ is not a linear statistic of the zeros, the one level density of the family (Katz and Sarnak 1999) alone does not give this prediction, and all the correlation functions enter. The single function is computed in the book; the family average is open.
results.label: gl:op:negmoment

results.name: Open problem: infinite divisibility of the family mixture of the clocks of the characters modulo q
results.summary: Decide whether the clock of a uniformly chosen character of the family modulo $q$ is infinitely divisible, and whether some $q$ with two or more members avoids the odd configuration of the mixture criterion for every pair of members.
results.statement: Let $\mathcal F_q$ consist of the real primitive characters modulo $q$ together with one representative of each conjugate pair of complex primitive characters modulo $q$. Assume GRH for the members and that their central values are nonzero, so that their clocks exist: $T_\chi\stackrel d=\sum_{\gamma>0}e_\gamma/\gamma^2$ for a real member (the ordinates $\gamma>0$ of $L(s,\chi)$, with independent standard exponential variables $e_\gamma$) and $T_{\chi\bar\chi}\stackrel d=\sum_{\gamma\in\Gamma_\chi}e_\gamma/\gamma^2$ for a complex pair (all ordinates of both signs). Let $T^{(q)}$ be the clock of a uniformly chosen member. Is $T^{(q)}$ infinitely divisible? Does any $q$ for which $\mathcal F_q$ has two or more members avoid, for every pair of its members, the odd configuration of the mixture criterion (two clocks whose Thorin measures are sums of unit point masses, with consecutive atoms $t_1<t_2$ of the union belonging to different clocks and an odd number of atoms of the union in $(0,t_1]$)? It is settled that $T^{(q)}$ is not a GGC for $q=5$ and every weight, under GRH for the two members (their values at $\frac12$ are nonzero numerically), and, under the same hypotheses, for every $q$ whose family has exactly two members, when these are in the odd configuration; this does not decide whether $T^{(5)}$ is infinitely divisible.
results.label: gl:op:family

results.name: Open problem: a sign definite explicit formula for primes in the progressions a modulo q with a not congruent to 1
results.summary: Find a sign definite explicit formula for $\psi(x;q,a)$ with $a\not\equiv1\pmod q$ in terms of the zero counting measures of cyclotomic fields and their Poisson smoothings, for which the case $a\equiv1$ is already an integral against a nonnegative measure under the Thorin property.
results.statement: Let $F_q=\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_q)$ and $\psi(x;q,a)=\sum_{n\le x,\ n\equiv a\ (q)}\Lambda(n)$ with $\Lambda$ the von Mangoldt function. Suppose that the centre clock of the completed Dedekind zeta function $\xi_{F_q}(s)=s(s-1)|d_{F_q}|^{s/2}\Gamma_{\mathbb{C}}(s)^{\varphi(q)/2}\zeta_{F_q}(s)$, with $\Gamma_{\mathbb{C}}(s)=2(2\pi)^{-s}\Gamma(s)$ and $d_{F_q}$ the discriminant, is a generalized gamma convolution (equivalently, GRH for the Dirichlet $L$ functions of conductor dividing $q$ with nonzero central values). Then the explicit formula for $\psi(x;q,1)$, which up to the factor $\varphi(q)$ counts the prime ideals of $F_q$, becomes an integral against the nonnegative zero counting Thorin measure $U_{F_q,0}$, and the positive family $\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}(\xi_{F_q}'/\xi_{F_q})(\alpha+ib)$ of the basepoint family joins it to the primes. For $a\not\equiv1\pmod q$ the characters enter the explicit formula for $\psi(x;q,a)$ with the weights $\bar\chi(a)$, which are complex or negative, and no sign is available. These are zero counting measures and their Poisson smoothings, so any gain must come from structure beyond counting, such as monotonicity or log concavity of the associated GGC densities, transported to bounds on $L'/L$ near the line. Is there a sign definite explicit formula for $\psi(x;q,a)$ with $a\not\equiv1\pmod q$, in terms of such measures?
results.label: gl:op:signdefinite

results.name: Open problem: certified backward continuation of the Thorin density of the basepoint family from the primes into the critical strip
results.summary: Determine how far into the critical strip positivity of the Thorin density $\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}(f'/f)(\alpha+ib)$ can be certified from smoothed prime sums alone before the ill posedness of the backward step takes over.
results.statement: Let $f$ be the completed Dedekind zeta function $\xi_F(s)=s(s-1)|d_F|^{s/2}\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s)^{r_1}\Gamma_{\mathbb{C}}(s)^{r_2}\zeta_F(s)$ of a number field $F$ ($d_F$ the discriminant, $r_1$ and $r_2$ the numbers of real and complex places, $\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s)=\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)$, $\Gamma_{\mathbb{C}}(s)=2(2\pi)^{-s}\Gamma(s)$) or the completed Dirichlet $L$ function $\xi(s,\chi)=(q/\pi)^{(s+a)/2}\Gamma(\frac{s+a}2)L(s,\chi)$ of a real primitive character $\chi$ modulo $q>1$ of parity $a\in\{0,1\}$. The Thorin density $\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}(f'/f)(\alpha+ib)$ of the basepoint family is computable from the primes, with rigorous error bounds, for $\alpha>1$, and its positivity on every line $\operatorname{Re}s=\alpha'$ with $\alpha'>\alpha$ is a zero free half plane $\operatorname{Re}s>\alpha$. How far into the critical strip (that is, to which $\alpha<1$) can positivity be certified from the primes alone, using smoothed prime sums of the kind that locate the zeros of a Dirichlet $L$ function, before the ill posedness of the backward step takes over? The backward step is a deconvolution of the Poisson smoothing, which is unbounded, and the number of primes it needs grows without bound as $\alpha\downarrow\frac12$; for the heat flow the corresponding step is stable but cannot carry real zeros. What smoothed prime sums can certify below $\alpha=1$ is open; the book finds the output of the sine squared lemma not computable from the primes alone in practice for $\alpha\le1$ (a computation for a character modulo $4$ with the prime powers up to a finite cutoff), so that the minima it computes there come from the zeros.
results.label: gl:op:backward

results.name: Open problem: the exponential sum over primes on the minor arcs as an expectation against the GGC laws of the clocks
results.summary: Decide whether the exponential sum over primes on the minor arcs of the circle method for Linnik's problem can be written as an expectation against the GGC laws of the clocks, which would give a different route to the supremum bound on the minor arcs.
results.statement:
For $F=\mathbb{Q}$ let $
u_F$ be the signed Lévy measure of the completed zeta function $\xi_F$, defined by $\log rac{\xi_F(\alpha+w)}{\xi_F(\alpha)}-w rac{\xi_F'}{\xi_F}(\alpha)=\int_0^\infty(e^{-wx}-1+wx)\,e^{-\alpha x}\, rac{
u_F(dx)}x$ for $\alpha>1$ and $w\ge0$, that is $
u_F(dx)= ig( rac1{1-e^{-2x}}-1-e^x ig)dx+\sum_{n\ge2}\Lambda(n)\,\delta_{\log n}(dx)$ with $\Lambda$ the von Mangoldt function, and let the GGC laws of the clocks be the laws with Laplace transform $\xi_F(\alpha)/\xi_F(\alpha+\sqrt u)$, $u\ge0$, for $\alpha>1$. The atoms of $
u_F$ at the primes $p$ have mass $\log p$, the weights that enter the exponential sum $\mathcal S(\alpha)=\sum_{\varpi N<p\le N}e(p\alpha)$ of the circle method for Linnik's problem (with $e(x)=\exp(2\pi ix)$ and $\varpi>0$ small); the prime powers in $
u_F$ do not enter $\mathcal S(\alpha)$. Can $\mathcal S(\alpha)$ on the minor arcs be written as an expectation against the GGC laws of the clocks? Such a representation would be a different route to the supremum bound for $\mathcal S$ on the minor arcs; nothing in the chapter shows that it exists.
results.label: gl:op:arith

results.name: Open problem: the best minor arc exponent in Linnik's problem from a zero free half plane for all Dirichlet L functions
results.summary: Under a zero free half plane $\operatorname{Re}s>\theta_0$ for all Dirichlet $L$ functions, find the best minor arc exponent for the sum over primes in Linnik's problem, and decide whether the half plane improves the large deviation parameter for the powers of two or the major arc constant.
results.statement:
Consider the circle method for Linnik's problem of writing large even $N$ as $p_1+p_2+2^{k_1}+\cdots+2^{k_K}$, with $\mathcal S(\alpha)=\sum_{\varpi N<p\le N}e(p\alpha)$, $e(x)=\exp(2\pi ix)$. Assume $L(s,\chi)
e0$ for $\operatorname{Re}s>	heta_0$ and every Dirichlet character $\chi$. What is the best exponent $	heta(	heta_0)$ in the minor arc bound $\mathcal S(\alpha)\ll N^{	heta+o(1)}$ obtainable by combining the explicit formula with Vaughan's identity? A one line heuristic balance gives $	heta= rac12(1+	heta_0)$, which is better than the unconditional exponent $ rac{263}{308}$ exactly when $	heta_0< rac{109}{154}$, so it does nothing at $	heta_0= rac78$; it is not shown to be optimal. Does a hybrid bound, using the half plane only for the characters of small conductor, improve the parameter $\lambda$ of the large deviation estimate for the sum over powers of two (the measure of the set where $|\sum_{1\le
u\le L}e(2^
u\alpha)|\ge\lambda L$)? And does the half plane, which excludes exceptional zeros of large conductor, raise the constant of the major arc main term? The paper of Heath-Brown and Puchta (2002) suggests that it does not by itself: they state that zeros close to $\sigma=1$ play no role there; the constant is a sum over small divisors, and the restriction $q\le P=N^{45/154-4\varpi}$ of the major arcs comes from zero density estimates whose critical zeros have $\sigma\le rac34$ and are not removed by a half plane at $ rac78$.
results.label: gl:op:quasi

results.name: Open problem: does a finite order of total positivity of the density force the zeros onto the line, in a class of even entire functions containing xi
results.summary: Decide whether some finite order of total positivity of the density $f_F$ forces every zero of $F$ onto the imaginary axis, for every $F$ in the class of even entire functions with the order, type and reflection symmetry of $\xi(\frac12+s)/\xi(\frac12)$ whose reciprocal is a characteristic function.
results.statement: Let $T$ be the centre clock of Riemann's xi function, $Z$ an independent standard normal variable and $Y=\sqrt{2T}\,Z$. RH holds if and only if the density of $Y$ is a Pólya frequency function of infinite order, that is, every determinant $\det[f(x_i-y_j)]$ with $x_1<\dots<x_n$ and $y_1<\dots<y_n$ is nonnegative. For this one density the question whether a finite order already implies RH has a trivial answer: the orders decrease, so if RH holds every such implication is true, and if RH fails the property fails at some finite order, where the implication is vacuous. The question has content for a class of functions. Let $\mathcal E$ be the class of even entire functions $F$ with $F(0)=1$ and the order, type and reflection symmetry of $\xi(\frac12+s)/\xi(\frac12)$ for which $1/F$ is the characteristic function of a probability density $f_F$; the density of $Y$ is $f_F$ for $F=\xi(\frac12+\cdot)/\xi(\frac12)$. Is there a finite $k$ such that, for every $F\in\mathcal E$, the property that $f_F$ is a Pólya frequency function of order $k$ implies that every zero of $F$ lies on the imaginary axis?
results.label: gl:op:pf

results.name: The friable approximant of Xi is exponentially close to Xi in a strip, with the accuracy set by the first omitted prime
results.summary: For $|\operatorname{Im}t|\le\frac32$ the friable approximant satisfies $|\Xi_P(t)-\Xi(t)|\le|t^2+\frac14|\,\delta_P$ with $\delta_P\le e^{-\pi q^2}/(\pi q^2(1-e^{-2\pi q}))$.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function and $\Xi(t)=\xi(\frac12+it)$, an even entire function, real on $\mathbb{R}$, whose zeros are the ordinates of the nontrivial zeros of the zeta function. Let $\mathcal F(P)$ be the set of positive integers all of whose prime factors are at most $P$ (the $P$ friable integers), $\psi_P(x)=\sum_{n\in\mathcal F(P)}e^{-\pi n^2x}$, and let the friable approximant be $\Xi_P(t)=\frac12-2(t^2+\frac14)\int_0^\infty\psi_P(e^{2u})e^{u/2}\cos(tu)\,du$ (the same formula with all integers $n$ gives $\Xi$). Let $q$ be the least prime above $P$ and $D_P=\Xi_P-\Xi$ the deficit. Let $\delta_P=\sum_{m\notin\mathcal F(P)}e^{-\pi m^2}/(\pi m^2)$. For $|\operatorname{Im}t|\le\frac32$, $|\Xi_P(t)-\Xi(t)|\le|t^2+\frac14|\,\delta_P$, and $\delta_P\le e^{-\pi q^2}/(\pi q^2(1-e^{-2\pi q}))$.
results.label: mi:thm:approx

results.name: Certified tracking: a Rouche criterion for a real zero of the friable approximant near a simple zero of Xi
results.summary: If a simple zero $\gamma$ of $\Xi$ has $|\Xi|>|t^2+\frac14|\delta_P$ on a circle of radius $r\le\frac32$ about it, then $\Xi_P$ has exactly one zero in the disc, it is real, and its shift from $\gamma$ is given to first order by $-(\Xi_P-\Xi)(\gamma)/\Xi'(\gamma)$.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function and $\Xi(t)=\xi(\frac12+it)$, an even entire function, real on $\mathbb{R}$, whose zeros are the ordinates of the nontrivial zeros of the zeta function. Let $\mathcal F(P)$ be the set of positive integers all of whose prime factors are at most $P$ (the $P$ friable integers), $\psi_P(x)=\sum_{n\in\mathcal F(P)}e^{-\pi n^2x}$, and let the friable approximant be $\Xi_P(t)=\frac12-2(t^2+\frac14)\int_0^\infty\psi_P(e^{2u})e^{u/2}\cos(tu)\,du$ (the same formula with all integers $n$ gives $\Xi$). Let $q$ be the least prime above $P$ and $D_P=\Xi_P-\Xi$ the deficit. Let $\delta_P=\sum_{m\notin\mathcal F(P)}e^{-\pi m^2}/(\pi m^2)$. If $\gamma$ is a simple zero of $\Xi$ and $|\Xi(t)|>|t^2+\frac14|\delta_P$ on the circle $|t-\gamma|=r\le\frac32$, then $\Xi_P$ has exactly one zero $\gamma_P$ in the disc $|t-\gamma|<r$, it is real, and $\gamma_P-\gamma=-(\Xi_P-\Xi)(\gamma)/\Xi'(\gamma)\,(1+O(\eta))$, where $\eta$ is the ratio of $\max|\Xi_P-\Xi|$ on the disc to $\min|\Xi|$ on the circle.
results.label: mi:cor:rouche

results.name: The folded kernel of the friable approximant has a kink of exact size c_P, so Xi_P tends to c_P on the real line and has finitely many real zeros
results.summary: The folded kernel of $\Xi_P$ has a corner at the origin of size $c_P=\sum_{m\notin\mathcal F(P)}(4\pi m^2-1)e^{-\pi m^2}\sim4\pi q^2e^{-\pi q^2}>0$, so $\Xi_P(t)\to c_P$ along the real axis and $\Xi_P$ has finitely many real zeros.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function and $\Xi(t)=\xi(\frac12+it)$, an even entire function, real on $\mathbb{R}$, whose zeros are the ordinates of the nontrivial zeros of the zeta function. Let $\mathcal F(P)$ be the set of positive integers all of whose prime factors are at most $P$ (the $P$ friable integers), $\psi_P(x)=\sum_{n\in\mathcal F(P)}e^{-\pi n^2x}$, and let the friable approximant be $\Xi_P(t)=\frac12-2(t^2+\frac14)\int_0^\infty\psi_P(e^{2u})e^{u/2}\cos(tu)\,du$ (the same formula with all integers $n$ gives $\Xi$). Let $q$ be the least prime above $P$ and $D_P=\Xi_P-\Xi$ the deficit. Fold $\Xi_P$ as $\Xi_P(t)=(t^2+\frac14)\int_0^\infty k_P(u)\cos(tu)\,du$ with kernel $k_P(u)=e^{-u/2}-2e^{u/2}\psi_P(e^{2u})$ and put $c_P=-k_P'(0)$. Then $c_P=\sum_{m\notin\mathcal F(P)}(4\pi m^2-1)e^{-\pi m^2}=4\pi q^2e^{-\pi q^2}(1+O(q^{-2}))>0$, and $\Xi_P(t)=c_P+O_P(t^{-2})$ as $t\to\infty$ along $\mathbb{R}$. Hence $\Xi_P$ has finitely many real zeros.
results.label: mi:thm:kink

results.name: No reweighting of Riemann's theta series by summable weights has infinitely many real zeros
results.summary: For nonzero real weights $w_n$ with $\sum|w_n|n^{-\sigma}<\infty$ for every $\sigma>0$ (this includes the friable truncations), the reweighted function has finitely many real zeros and infinitely many nonreal zeros.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function and $\Xi(t)=\xi(\frac12+it)$, an even entire function, real on $\mathbb{R}$, whose zeros are the ordinates of the nontrivial zeros of the zeta function.
