For real weights $w=(w_n)\ne0$ with $\sum_n|w_n|n^{-\sigma}<\infty$ for every $\sigma>0$ (this includes the weights $1_{\mathcal F(P)}$, for which the sum is $\prod_{p\le P}(1-p^{-\sigma})^{-1}$, and so $\Xi_P$), put $\psi_w(x)=\sum_nw_ne^{-\pi n^2x}$ and $\Xi_w(t)=\frac12-2(t^2+\frac14)\int_0^\infty\psi_w(e^{2u})e^{u/2}\cos(tu)\,du$. Then $\Xi_w$ is even, entire of order at most one, and has finitely many real zeros and infinitely many nonreal zeros.
results.label: mi:thm:noproxy

results.name: The deficit Xi_P minus Xi is positive on the real line and decreases as the prime bound grows
results.summary: For every prime $P$ and real $t$, $\Xi_P(t)-\Xi(t)>0$, and the deficit decreases strictly as $P$ increases, so $\Xi_P>\Xi_{P'}>\Xi$ on $\mathbb{R}$ for $P<P'$.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function and $\Xi(t)=\xi(\frac12+it)$, an even entire function, real on $\mathbb{R}$, whose zeros are the ordinates of the nontrivial zeros of the zeta function. Let $\mathcal F(P)$ be the set of positive integers all of whose prime factors are at most $P$ (the $P$ friable integers), $\psi_P(x)=\sum_{n\in\mathcal F(P)}e^{-\pi n^2x}$, and let the friable approximant be $\Xi_P(t)=\frac12-2(t^2+\frac14)\int_0^\infty\psi_P(e^{2u})e^{u/2}\cos(tu)\,du$ (the same formula with all integers $n$ gives $\Xi$). Let $q$ be the least prime above $P$ and $D_P=\Xi_P-\Xi$ the deficit. For all real $t$, $D_P(t)>0$, and $D_P>D_{P'}$ when $P<P'$ are primes. Hence $\Xi_P>\Xi_{P'}>\Xi$ on $\mathbb{R}$.
results.label: mi:thm:positive

results.name: Uniform Lorentzian bound: the deficit of the friable approximant is a sum of Lorentzians with an explicit uniform relative error
results.summary: For $a\ge9\pi$ the cosine transform $C_a$ of $e^{-ae^w}e^{w/4}$ equals the Lorentzian $\mathcal L_a(t)=e^{-a}b/(b^2+t^2/4)$ with relative error at most $\delta(a)\le5.61/a$, uniformly in real $t$, and the deficit $D_P$ is the corresponding sum over the omitted integers.
results.statement: For $a\ge9\pi$ put $b=a-\frac14$, $f_a(w)=e^{-ae^w}e^{w/4}$, $C_a(t)=\int_0^\infty f_a(w)\cos(tw/2)\,dw$ and $\mathcal L_a(t)=e^{-a}b/(b^2+t^2/4)$. For all real $t$, $|C_a(t)-\mathcal L_a(t)|\le\delta(a)\mathcal L_a(t)$ with $\delta(a)=\frac1b\big[\frac{2ab^2}{(b-1)^3}+\frac{2ab}{(b-1)^2}+\frac{2a^2}{(b-2)^3}+\frac a{b-1}\big]\le5.61/a$. The deficit of the friable approximant $\Xi_P$ (the difference of $\Xi_P$ and Riemann's $\Xi$, for $\mathcal F(P)$ the integers with all prime factors at most $P$) is $D_P(t)=(t^2+\frac14)\sum_{m\notin\mathcal F(P)}C_{\pi m^2}(t)$, so it is a sum of Lorentzians of half widths about $2\pi m^2$ over the omitted integers $m$, with relative error $\delta(\pi q^2)$ for $q$ the least prime above $P$.
results.label: mi:thm:lorentz

results.name: Curvature: the logarithm of the deficit of the friable approximant is uniformly almost convex for t at least 14
results.summary: For every prime $P$ and $t\ge14$, $(\log D_P)''(t)\ge-0.0239$ for the deficit $D_P=\Xi_P-\Xi$, with an explicit bound in terms of the least omitted prime.
results.statement: Let $\mathcal F(P)$ be the set of positive integers all of whose prime factors are at most $P$ (the $P$ friable integers), $\psi_P(x)=\sum_{n\in\mathcal F(P)}e^{-\pi n^2x}$, and let the friable approximant be $\Xi_P(t)=\frac12-2(t^2+\frac14)\int_0^\infty\psi_P(e^{2u})e^{u/2}\cos(tu)\,du$ (the same formula with all integers $n$ gives $\Xi$). Let $q$ be the least prime above $P$ and $D_P=\Xi_P-\Xi$ the deficit. For $a\ge9\pi$ and $b=a-\frac14$ let $\delta=\delta(a)$ be the constant of the uniform Lorentzian bound, $r_1(a)=\frac1{2(1-\delta)b}\big(1+\frac{a^2}{(b-2)^2}+\frac a{(b-1)^2}+\frac{2a}{b-1}\big)$ and $r_2(a)=\frac1{4(1-\delta)b}\big(\frac4b+\frac{2a^2}{(b-2)^3}+\frac{2a}{(b-1)^3}+\frac{4a}{(b-1)^2}\big)$; these bound $|C_a'|/C_a$ and $|C_a''|/C_a$ uniformly in $t$, where $C_a$ is the cosine transform of $e^{-ae^w}e^{w/4}$ at $t/2$. For every prime $P$ and $t\ge14$, with $a_q=\pi q^2$, $(\log D_P)''(t)\ge-2/t^2-r_2(a_q)-r_1(a_q)^2\ge-0.0239$.
results.label: mi:thm:curv

results.name: Real zeros of the friable approximant live in the negative humps of Xi, in pairs, and surviving humps are nested in P
results.summary: Every real zero of $\Xi_P$ lies in a negative hump of $\Xi$ and each hump holds an even number of zeros; for humps below the verified height of RH and shorter than $18.29$, a hump holds none, one double or two simple zeros, according to the sign of $\max(|\Xi|-D_P)$ on it, and surviving humps are nested in $P$.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function and $\Xi(t)=\xi(\frac12+it)$, an even entire function, real on $\mathbb{R}$, whose zeros are the ordinates of the nontrivial zeros of the zeta function. Let $\mathcal F(P)$ be the set of positive integers all of whose prime factors are at most $P$ (the $P$ friable integers), $\psi_P(x)=\sum_{n\in\mathcal F(P)}e^{-\pi n^2x}$, and let the friable approximant be $\Xi_P(t)=\frac12-2(t^2+\frac14)\int_0^\infty\psi_P(e^{2u})e^{u/2}\cos(tu)\,du$ (the same formula with all integers $n$ gives $\Xi$). Let $q$ be the least prime above $P$ and $D_P=\Xi_P-\Xi$ the deficit. A negative hump is a maximal interval $I_j\subset(0,\infty)$ on which $\Xi<0$, of length $\ell_j$. (1) Every real zero of $\Xi_P$ lies in a negative hump, and $\Xi_P(\gamma)=D_P(\gamma)>0$ at every zero $\gamma$ of $\Xi$. (2) Each hump holds an even number of zeros of $\Xi_P$ counted with multiplicity, and the number $R_P$ of positive real zeros is even. (3) Suppose every zero of $\Xi$ whose real part lies within $\frac12$ of $I_j$ is real (by the verification of the Riemann Hypothesis of Platt and Trudgian (2021) this holds for every hump below $3\cdot10^{12}$) and $\ell_j<18.29$. Then $I_j$ holds no zero, one double zero or two simple zeros of $\Xi_P$, and two simple zeros exactly when $\max_{I_j}(|\Xi|-D_P)>0$. (4) If $I_j$ carries zeros of $\Xi_P$ then it carries zeros of $\Xi_{P'}$ for every prime $P'>P$.
results.label: mi:thm:humps

results.name: Count: the number of positive real zeros of the friable approximant is twice the number of negative humps of Xi deeper than the deficit
results.summary: Under the hypotheses of the hump theorem the number $R_P$ of positive real zeros of $\Xi_P$ is twice the number of humps with $\max(|\Xi|-D_P)>0$, there is a unique height $\tau_P^+$ beyond which $\Xi_P>0$, and $R_P\le2\lceil N(\tau_P^+)/2\rceil$.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function and $\Xi(t)=\xi(\frac12+it)$, an even entire function, real on $\mathbb{R}$, whose zeros are the ordinates of the nontrivial zeros of the zeta function. Let $\mathcal F(P)$ be the set of positive integers all of whose prime factors are at most $P$ (the $P$ friable integers), $\psi_P(x)=\sum_{n\in\mathcal F(P)}e^{-\pi n^2x}$, and let the friable approximant be $\Xi_P(t)=\frac12-2(t^2+\frac14)\int_0^\infty\psi_P(e^{2u})e^{u/2}\cos(tu)\,du$ (the same formula with all integers $n$ gives $\Xi$). Let $q$ be the least prime above $P$ and $D_P=\Xi_P-\Xi$ the deficit. Let $N(T)$ count the zeros of $\Xi$ in $(0,T]$ with multiplicity, $A(t)=\frac12(t^2+\frac14)\pi^{-1/4}|\Gamma(\frac14+\frac{it}2)|$, so that $\Xi=-AZ$ with $Z$ Hardy's function, and $I_j$ the negative humps of $\Xi$. Assume that for every hump meeting $(0,\tau_P^+)$ the local hypotheses hold (all zeros of $\Xi$ within $\frac12$ of the hump are real, by the verification of the Riemann Hypothesis of Platt and Trudgian (2021) below height $3\cdot10^{12}$, and its length is below $18.29$). Then $R_P=2\#\{j:\max_{I_j}(|\Xi|-D_P)>0\}$. Let $\tau_P^+$ solve $D_P(\tau)=0.63A(\tau)\tau^{1/6}\log\tau$; the solution is unique for $\tau\ge14$ and $\Xi_P>0$ on $(\tau_P^+,\infty)$ (this uses Hiary's bound $|\zeta(\frac12+it)|\le0.63t^{1/6}\log t$). Then $R_P\le2\lceil N(\tau_P^+)/2\rceil$.
results.label: mi:thm:count

results.name: Conjecture: the number of real zeros of the friable approximant is the zero count at the breakdown height plus a correction from the peaks of Hardy's function
results.summary: The number $R_P$ of positive real zeros of $\Xi_P$ is conjectured to equal $N(\tau_P^*)$ plus $\frac2{\pi^2}\log\frac{\tau_P^*}{2\pi}$ times the mean log peak of Hardy's function on negative humps near $\tau_P^*$, up to an error of order $\sqrt{\log q\,\log\log q}$.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function and $\Xi(t)=\xi(\frac12+it)$, an even entire function, real on $\mathbb{R}$, whose zeros are the ordinates of the nontrivial zeros of the zeta function. Let $\mathcal F(P)$ be the set of positive integers all of whose prime factors are at most $P$ (the $P$ friable integers), $\psi_P(x)=\sum_{n\in\mathcal F(P)}e^{-\pi n^2x}$, and let the friable approximant be $\Xi_P(t)=\frac12-2(t^2+\frac14)\int_0^\infty\psi_P(e^{2u})e^{u/2}\cos(tu)\,du$ (the same formula with all integers $n$ gives $\Xi$). Let $q$ be the least prime above $P$ and $D_P=\Xi_P-\Xi$ the deficit. Let $N(T)$ count the zeros of $\Xi$ in $(0,T]$, $R_P$ the number of positive real zeros of $\Xi_P$, $\tau_P^*$ the breakdown height, the solution of $A(\tau)=D_P(\tau)$ (about $4q^2$, a heuristic formula checked by computation) and $m_Z(T)$ the mean of $\log\max|Z|$ over the negative humps near $T$, for $Z$ Hardy's function. Conjecture: $R_P=N(\tau_P^*)+\frac2{\pi^2}\log\frac{\tau_P^*}{2\pi}\,m_Z(\tau_P^*)+O\big((\log q)^{1/2}(\log\log q)^{1/2}\big)$.
results.label: mi:conj:survey

results.name: Kink budget: the limit of the friable approximant with a smooth even kernel replacing the pole term
results.summary: If the pole kernel $e^{-u/2}$ in the folded kernel of $\Xi_P$ is replaced by an even smooth kernel $\kappa$ with derivatives $O(e^{-u/2})$, the limit of the modified function along the real axis is $c_P-\frac12-\kappa'(0+)$.
results.statement: Let $\mathcal F(P)$ be the set of positive integers all of whose prime factors are at most $P$ (the $P$ friable integers), $\psi_P(x)=\sum_{n\in\mathcal F(P)}e^{-\pi n^2x}$, and let the friable approximant be $\Xi_P(t)=\frac12-2(t^2+\frac14)\int_0^\infty\psi_P(e^{2u})e^{u/2}\cos(tu)\,du$ (the same formula with all integers $n$ gives $\Xi$). Let $q$ be the least prime above $P$ and $D_P=\Xi_P-\Xi$ the deficit. Let $c_P=\sum_{m\notin\mathcal F(P)}(4\pi m^2-1)e^{-\pi m^2}$ be the kink constant. Replace the pole kernel $e^{-u/2}$ in the folded kernel $k_P(u)=e^{-u/2}-2e^{u/2}\psi_P(e^{2u})$ by an even kernel $\kappa$, smooth on $[0,\infty)$ with all derivatives $O(e^{-u/2})$, and let $\Xi_P^\kappa(t)=(t^2+\frac14)\int_0^\infty(k_P+\kappa-e^{-u/2})(u)\cos(tu)\,du$. Then $\lim_{t\to\infty}\Xi_P^\kappa(t)=c_P-\frac12-\kappa'(0+)$ along $\mathbb{R}$.
results.label: mi:prop:kinkbudget

results.name: Reweighting: among weights in [0,1] vanishing on a given set, the indicator of the complement has the smallest deficit
results.summary: For weights $0\le w_n\le w_n'\le1$ the deficits satisfy $D_w\ge D_{w'}\ge0$ with $D_{w'}>0$ unless all $w_n'=1$, so the friable truncation has the smallest deficit among weights in $[0,1]$ that vanish on the omitted set.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function and $\Xi(t)=\xi(\frac12+it)$, an even entire function, real on $\mathbb{R}$, whose zeros are the ordinates of the nontrivial zeros of the zeta function. For weights $w=(w_n)$ let $\Xi_w(t)=\frac12-2(t^2+\frac14)\int_0^\infty\psi_w(e^{2u})e^{u/2}\cos(tu)\,du$ with $\psi_w(x)=\sum_nw_ne^{-\pi n^2x}$, and $D_w=\Xi_w-\Xi=(t^2+\frac14)\sum_n(1-w_n)C_{\pi n^2}$, where $C_a$ is the cosine transform of $e^{-ae^w}e^{w/4}$ at $t/2$. If $0\le w_n\le w_n'\le1$ for every $n$ then $D_w\ge D_{w'}\ge0$ on $\mathbb{R}$, with $D_{w'}>0$ unless every $w_n'=1$. So among weights in $[0,1]$ that vanish on a given set of integers, the indicator of its complement has the smallest deficit.
results.label: mi:prop:reweight

results.name: The friable approximants for P = 2 and 3 are uniformly close to Xi on the imaginary axis and have no zero there
results.summary: The relative error $\sup_y|\Xi_P(iy)/\Xi(iy)-1|$ is at most $6.8\times10^{-13}$ for $P=2$ and $3.4\times10^{-35}$ for $P=3$, so neither has a zero on the imaginary axis; the suprema of a proved bound were computed on a grid.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function and $\Xi(t)=\xi(\frac12+it)$, an even entire function, real on $\mathbb{R}$, whose zeros are the ordinates of the nontrivial zeros of the zeta function. Let $\mathcal F(P)$ be the set of positive integers all of whose prime factors are at most $P$ (the $P$ friable integers), $\psi_P(x)=\sum_{n\in\mathcal F(P)}e^{-\pi n^2x}$, and let the friable approximant be $\Xi_P(t)=\frac12-2(t^2+\frac14)\int_0^\infty\psi_P(e^{2u})e^{u/2}\cos(tu)\,du$ (the same formula with all integers $n$ gives $\Xi$). Let $q$ be the least prime above $P$ and $D_P=\Xi_P-\Xi$ the deficit. For $P=2$ and $P=3$, $\sup_{y\in\mathbb{R}}|\Xi_P(iy)/\Xi(iy)-1|$ is at most $6.8\times10^{-13}$ for $P=2$ and at most $3.4\times10^{-35}$ for $P=3$. In particular $\Xi_P$ has no zero on $i\mathbb{R}$. The bound rests on the proved estimate $|\Xi_P(iy)-\Xi(iy)|\le|y^2-\frac14|\sum_{m\notin\mathcal F(P)}(\pi m^2)^{-s}\Gamma(s,\pi m^2)$ with $s=\frac12(|y|+\frac12)$, whose supremum after division by $\Xi(iy)=\xi(\frac12+y)>0$ was computed at $30$ digits on a grid of step $0.1$ on $[0,40]$ and shown to decrease beyond it; it is a computation, not a certified enclosure.
results.label: mi:prop:axis

results.name: Shift identity: Xi is the average of two shifts of the transform of Phi divided by cosh, which contains Miyatake's identity
results.summary: For every $b>0$ and complex $z$, $\Xi(z)=\frac12\{g_b(z+ib)+g_b(z-ib)\}$, that is $\Xi=\cos(b\,d/dz)g_b$; Miyatake's identity is the case $b=\frac92$.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function and $\Xi(t)=\xi(\frac12+it)$, an even entire function, real on $\mathbb{R}$, whose zeros are the ordinates of the nontrivial zeros of the zeta function. Let $\Phi$ be Riemann's kernel, $\Phi(u)=2\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u/2}-3\pi n^2e^{5u/2})e^{-\pi n^2e^{2u}}$, so that $\Xi(t)=2\int_0^\infty\Phi(u)\cos(tu)\,du$ and $\Phi$ is positive and even. For $b>0$ put $g_b(z)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Phi(u)\operatorname{sech}(bu)\,e^{izu}\,du$ (the transform of $\Phi/\cosh(bu)$), an entire even function of order at most one, real on $\mathbb{R}$. For every $b>0$ and $z\in\mathbb{C}$, $\Xi(z)=\frac12\{g_b(z+ib)+g_b(z-ib)\}$, that is $\Xi=\cos(b\partial)g_b$ with $\partial=d/dz$. Miyatake's identity is the case $b=\frac92$ (with his transform $g(x)=g_{9/2}(2x)/(4\pi^2)$).
results.label: mi:prop:shiftb

results.name: Levy area, Polya Gamma clock and Thorin atoms: the transform of Phi over cosh is Xi smoothed by Levy's stochastic area
results.summary: The transform $g_b$ equals the expectation of $\Xi(x+2b\mathcal A)$ for Lévy's stochastic area $\mathcal A$, and the expectation of the de Bruijn Newman function at a Pólya Gamma random negative time, so $\Xi\mapsto g_b$ is convolution with an extended generalised gamma convolution with Thorin atoms at the odd multiples of $\pi/(2b)$.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function and $\Xi(t)=\xi(\frac12+it)$, an even entire function, real on $\mathbb{R}$, whose zeros are the ordinates of the nontrivial zeros of the zeta function. Let $\Phi$ be Riemann's kernel, $\Phi(u)=2\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u/2}-3\pi n^2e^{5u/2})e^{-\pi n^2e^{2u}}$, so that $\Xi(t)=2\int_0^\infty\Phi(u)\cos(tu)\,du$ and $\Phi$ is positive and even. For $b>0$ put $g_b(z)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Phi(u)\operatorname{sech}(bu)\,e^{izu}\,du$ (the transform of $\Phi/\cosh(bu)$), an entire even function of order at most one, real on $\mathbb{R}$. Let $\mathcal A=\frac12\int_0^1(W^1dW^2-W^2dW^1)$ be Lévy's stochastic area of a planar Brownian motion $(W^1,W^2)$, with $\mathbb{E}e^{i\lambda\mathcal A}=\operatorname{sech}(\lambda/2)$, let $\varpi$ be a Pólya Gamma variable $\mathrm{PG}(1,0)$ with $\mathbb{E}e^{-s\varpi}=\operatorname{sech}\sqrt{s/2}$, and $\mathcal H_\lambda(z)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Phi(u)e^{\lambda u^2}e^{izu}\,du$ the de Bruijn Newman family. For real $x$, $g_b(x)=\mathbb{E}\,\Xi(x+2b\mathcal A)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Xi(x-y)\frac1{2b}\operatorname{sech}\frac{\pi y}{2b}\,dy=\mathbb{E}_\varpi[\mathcal H_{-2b^2\varpi}(x)]$, and $2b\mathcal A\overset d=2b\sqrt\varpi\,\mathcal N\overset d=\sum_{k\ge1}\frac{2b}{(2k-1)\pi}L_k$ with $\mathcal N$ standard normal and $L_k$ independent standard Laplace variables. Hence $\Xi\mapsto g_b$ is convolution with an extended generalised gamma convolution whose Thorin measure has atoms at $\pm(2k-1)\pi/(2b)$.
results.label: mi:thm:levyarea

results.name: Logistic partition: 2 xi is the sum of two logistic weighted expectations of a power of a random variable
results.summary: For $c>0$, $2\xi(s)$ is the sum of the expectations of $\Upsilon^s/(1+\Upsilon^c)$ and $\Upsilon^{s+c}/(1+\Upsilon^c)$, for the random variable $\Upsilon$ of the Biane Pitman Yor identity, and the logistic weight is a Pólya Gamma mixture.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function and $\Upsilon=V^{1/2}$ with $V$ the random variable of the Biane Pitman Yor identity for $\xi$ (as defined in the book), and $\varpi\sim\mathrm{PG}(1,0)$ a Pólya Gamma variable. For $c>0$, $2\xi(s)=\mathbb{E}[\Upsilon^s/(1+\Upsilon^c)]+\mathbb{E}[\Upsilon^{s+c}/(1+\Upsilon^c)]$; with $c=2b$ and $s=\frac12+iz$ the two terms are $g_b(z+ib)$ and $g_b(z-ib)$, for $g_b$ the transform of $\Phi/\cosh(bu)$. The logistic weight is the Pólya Gamma mixture $\Upsilon^c/(1+\Upsilon^c)=\frac12\Upsilon^{c/2}\mathbb{E}_\varpi\exp(-\frac12\varpi c^2(\log\Upsilon)^2)$ (Polson, Scott and Windle 2013).
results.label: mi:prop:logistic

results.name: Exponential tail: the transform of Phi over cosh has a residue term C_b e^{-pi z/(2b)} exactly when b exceeds 2
results.summary: For $b>2$ the transform $g_b$ equals $C_be^{-\pi z/(2b)}$ plus a faster decaying error, with $C_b=\frac{2\pi}b\Phi(\frac{i\pi}{2b})$, uniformly in horizontal strips; for $b<2$ there is no residue and $g_b(x)=O(e^{-\tau x})$ for every $\tau<\pi/4$.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function and $\Xi(t)=\xi(\frac12+it)$, an even entire function, real on $\mathbb{R}$, whose zeros are the ordinates of the nontrivial zeros of the zeta function. Let $\Phi$ be Riemann's kernel, $\Phi(u)=2\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u/2}-3\pi n^2e^{5u/2})e^{-\pi n^2e^{2u}}$, so that $\Xi(t)=2\int_0^\infty\Phi(u)\cos(tu)\,du$ and $\Phi$ is positive and even. For $b>0$ put $g_b(z)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Phi(u)\operatorname{sech}(bu)\,e^{izu}\,du$ (the transform of $\Phi/\cosh(bu)$), an entire even function of order at most one, real on $\mathbb{R}$. Let $b>2$, $\pi/(2b)<\tau<\min(\pi/4,3\pi/(2b))$ and $Y>0$. Then, uniformly for $\operatorname{Re}z\ge0$ and $|\operatorname{Im}z|\le Y$, $g_b(z)=C_be^{-\pi z/(2b)}+O(e^{-\tau\operatorname{Re}z})$ with $C_b=\frac{2\pi}b\,\Phi(\frac{i\pi}{2b})$. For $b<2$ there is no residue and $g_b(x)=O(e^{-\tau x})$ for every $\tau<\pi/4$.
results.label: mi:thm:tail

results.name: Cusp asymptotics: the residue constant C_b of the transform of Phi over cosh as b decreases to 2
results.summary: With $\delta=\pi(b-2)/(4b)$, as $b\downarrow2$ the constant $C_b$ is asymptotic to $-\frac{\pi^3}{32b}(2\delta)^{-1/2}\delta^{-4}e^{-\frac\pi8\cot\delta}$ and is negative and super exponentially small.
results.statement: Let $\Phi$ be Riemann's kernel, $\Phi(u)=2\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u/2}-3\pi n^2e^{5u/2})e^{-\pi n^2e^{2u}}$, so that $\Xi(t)=2\int_0^\infty\Phi(u)\cos(tu)\,du$ and $\Phi$ is positive and even. For $b>2$ put $C_b=\frac{2\pi}b\Phi(\frac{i\pi}{2b})$ (the residue constant of the transform of $\Phi/\cosh(bu)$) and $\delta=\pi(b-2)/(4b)$. As $b\downarrow2$, $C_b=-\frac{\pi^3}{32b}(2\delta)^{-1/2}\delta^{-4}e^{-\frac\pi8\cot\delta}(1+O(b-2))$.
results.label: mi:thm:cusp

results.name: For b above 2 with C_b nonzero the transform of Phi over cosh has finitely many real zeros and is not in the Laguerre Polya class
results.summary: For $b>2$ with $C_b\ne0$ the transform $g_b$ has finitely many real zeros and infinitely many nonreal zeros, so it is not in the Laguerre Pólya class; in particular Miyatake's transform ($b=\frac92$, $C_{9/2}>0$) is not.
results.statement: Let $\Phi$ be Riemann's kernel, $\Phi(u)=2\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u/2}-3\pi n^2e^{5u/2})e^{-\pi n^2e^{2u}}$, so that $\Xi(t)=2\int_0^\infty\Phi(u)\cos(tu)\,du$ and $\Phi$ is positive and even. For $b>0$ put $g_b(z)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Phi(u)\operatorname{sech}(bu)\,e^{izu}\,du$ (the transform of $\Phi/\cosh(bu)$), an entire even function of order at most one, real on $\mathbb{R}$. For $b>2$ with $C_b=\frac{2\pi}b\Phi(\frac{i\pi}{2b})\ne0$, $g_b$ has finitely many real zeros, infinitely many nonreal zeros, and is not in the Laguerre Pólya class. In particular Miyatake's transform, for which $b=\frac92$ and $C_{9/2}>0$, is not.
results.label: mi:cor:notLP

results.name: The bottom of the cosh ladder is at most the largest real part of a zero of zeta minus one half
results.summary: The bottom rung $B_{\cosh}$ of the cosh ladder satisfies $B_{\cosh}\le\sigma_{\max}-\frac12$, where $\sigma_{\max}$ is the supremum of the real parts of the nontrivial zeros of zeta.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function and $\Xi(t)=\xi(\frac12+it)$, an even entire function, real on $\mathbb{R}$, whose zeros are the ordinates of the nontrivial zeros of the zeta function. For real $b$ let $F_b(z)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Phi(u)\cosh(bu)e^{izu}\,du=\frac12\{\Xi(z+ib)+\Xi(z-ib)\}$, so that $F_b(x)=\operatorname{Re}\xi(\frac12+b+ix)$ on $\mathbb{R}$. Let $B_{\cosh}=\inf\{b\ge0: F_b\text{ has only real zeros}\}$ (the bottom of the cosh ladder; $B_{\cosh}\le\frac12$ by de Bruijn's strip theorem) and $\sigma_{\max}=\sup\operatorname{Re}\rho$ over the nontrivial zeros $\rho$ of zeta. Then $B_{\cosh}\le\sigma_{\max}-\frac12$.
results.label: mi:prop:BTheta

results.name: Conjecture: the bottom of the cosh ladder lies between the asymptotic and the global quasi Riemann abscissa
results.summary: The bottom rung of the cosh ladder is conjectured to satisfy $\sigma_{\max}^\infty-\frac12\le B_{\cosh}\le\sigma_{\max}-\frac12$ with $\sigma_{\max}^\infty=\limsup_{\gamma\to\infty}\beta$; the upper bound is proved.
results.statement: With $F_b(z)=\int\Phi(u)\cosh(bu)e^{izu}\,du$, so that $F_b(x)=\operatorname{Re}\xi(\frac12+b+ix)$ on $\mathbb R$, the cosh ladder of Riemann's xi function, $B_{\cosh}=\inf\{b\ge0: F_b\text{ has only real zeros}\}$ its bottom rung, $\sigma_{\max}=\sup\operatorname{Re}\rho$ and $\sigma_{\max}^\infty=\limsup_{\gamma\to\infty}\beta$ over the nontrivial zeros $\rho=\beta+i\gamma$ of zeta: conjecturally $\sigma_{\max}^\infty-\frac12\le B_{\cosh}\le\sigma_{\max}-\frac12$. The upper bound is proved; the lower bound is conjectured. Under the conjecture, lowering the unconditional bound $B_{\cosh}\le\frac12$ is equivalent to a quasi Riemann hypothesis whenever $\sigma_{\max}$ is approached at large height.
results.label: mi:conj:quasi

results.name: Paired form: zeta has no zero to the right of alpha exactly when the real and imaginary parts of xi on the line alpha interlace
results.summary: For $\alpha>\frac12$, zeta has no zero with real part at least $\alpha$ exactly when $E_\alpha(z)=\xi(\alpha-iz)$ is Hermite Biehler, exactly when the real and imaginary parts of $\xi(\alpha+it)$ have only real simple strictly interlacing zeros; hence RH holds if and only if this holds for every $\alpha>\frac12$.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function, $\alpha>\frac12$, $E_\alpha(z)=\xi(\alpha-iz)$ and $E^\#(z)=\overline{E(\bar z)}$. The following are equivalent: (i) $\zeta(s)\ne0$ for $\operatorname{Re}s\ge\alpha$; (ii) $E_\alpha$ is Hermite Biehler, that is $|E_\alpha(z)|>|E_\alpha^\#(z)|$ for $\operatorname{Im}z>0$; (iii) $\operatorname{Re}\xi(\alpha+it)$ and $\operatorname{Im}\xi(\alpha+it)$, as entire functions of $t$, have only real simple zeros, and these strictly interlace. Hence the paired bottom rung, the infimum of the $\alpha-\frac12$ for which these hold, is exactly $\sigma_{\max}-\frac12$ (with $\sigma_{\max}$ the supremum of the real parts of the nontrivial zeros), and the Riemann Hypothesis holds if and only if (iii) holds for every $\alpha>\frac12$.
results.label: mi:thm:paired

results.name: Real zeros of the real and imaginary parts of xi on a vertical line right of one half have asymptotically full density
results.summary: For $\alpha>\frac12$ with no zero of zeta on the line, $\theta_\alpha(T)-\theta_\alpha(-T)=\pi(N^\pm(T)-2N^\pm_{>\alpha}(T))+O(\log T)$, so $\operatorname{Re}\xi(\alpha+it)$ and $\operatorname{Im}\xi(\alpha+it)$ each have at least $N^\pm(T)-2N^\pm_{>\alpha}(T)-O(\log T)$ real zeros in $[-T,T]$.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function, $N^\pm(T)$ the number of nontrivial zeros $\beta+i\gamma$ of zeta with $|\gamma|\le T$, $N^\pm_{>\alpha}(T)$ the number of them with $\beta>\alpha$, and $\theta_\alpha(t)=\arg\xi(\alpha+it)$. For $\alpha>\frac12$ with $\beta\ne\alpha$ for every zero, $\theta_\alpha(T)-\theta_\alpha(-T)=\pi(N^\pm(T)-2N^\pm_{>\alpha}(T))+O(\log T)$. Hence $\operatorname{Re}\xi(\alpha+it)$ and $\operatorname{Im}\xi(\alpha+it)$ each have at least $N^\pm(T)-2N^\pm_{>\alpha}(T)-O(\log T)$ real zeros in $[-T,T]$. If moreover $F_b$, for $b=\alpha-\frac12$ and $F_b(z)=\operatorname{Re}\xi(\alpha+iz)$, satisfies the Riemann von Mangoldt formula with error $O(\log T)$, its nonreal zeros with $|\operatorname{Re}z|\le T$ number at most $2N^\pm_{>\alpha}(T)+O(\log T)$.
results.label: mi:thm:density

results.name: Eventually Thorin: after any positive time the reciprocal of the flowed Xi function is a GGC transform times a finite rational factor
results.summary: For every $t>0$ the ratio $\Xi_t(0)/\Xi_t(i\sqrt s)$ equals a generalised gamma convolution Laplace transform times a finite product $\prod_{\eta\in E_t}(1+s/\eta)^{-1}$ over a conjugation invariant multiset off the positive axis, which is empty exactly when $\Xi_t$ has only real zeros.
results.statement: For real $t$ let $\Xi_t(\theta)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Phi(u)e^{tu^2/4}\cos(\theta u)\,du$ be the de Bruijn Newman flow of Riemann's kernel $\Phi$ (so $\Xi_0=\Xi$, Riemann's Xi function). For every $t>0$ there are a finite, conjugation invariant multiset $E_t\subset\mathbb{C}\setminus(0,\infty)$ and a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) Laplace transform $L_t$, with discrete Thorin measure on $(0,\infty)$ whose atoms are simple beyond a finite level, such that $\Xi_t(0)/\Xi_t(i\sqrt s)=L_t(s)\prod_{\eta\in E_t}(1+s/\eta)^{-1}$. The function $\Xi_t$ has only real zeros exactly when $E_t=\emptyset$. (This is the theorem of Ki, Kim and Lee on the zeros of $\Xi_t$, written through the Thorin dictionary.)
results.label: ki:prop:eventual

results.name: Shrinking parabolas: Thorin atoms of the flowed Xi function lie to the right of a parabola that collapses at t = 1/2
results.summary: For $0<t<\frac12$ every Thorin atom of $\Xi_t$ lies in the closed region to the right of the parabola $x=y^2/(4\Delta^2)-\Delta^2$ with $\Delta^2=\frac14-\frac t2$; the parabolas share the focus $0$ and collapse onto $[0,\infty)$ at $t=\frac12$.
results.statement: For real $t$ let $\Xi_t(\theta)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Phi(u)e^{tu^2/4}\cos(\theta u)\,du$ be the de Bruijn Newman flow of Riemann's kernel $\Phi$ (so $\Xi_0=\Xi$, Riemann's Xi function). For $0<t<\frac12$ put $\Delta(t)^2=\frac14-\frac t2$. Every Thorin atom of $\Xi_t$, that is every square of a zero of $\Xi_t$ and in particular every $\eta\in E_t$ of the eventually Thorin factorisation, lies in the closed region $\{x+iy:\ x\ge y^2/(4\Delta(t)^2)-\Delta(t)^2\}$ to the right of the parabola with focus $0$ and vertex $-\Delta(t)^2$. The parabolas are nested and collapse onto $[0,\infty)$ at $t=\frac12$, where de Bruijn's theorem takes over.
results.label: ki:cor:parab

results.name: No slack in the Gaussian direction: no class of kernels closed under Gaussian damping and containing Phi has only real zeros
results.summary: If a class of positive even kernels is closed under multiplication by $e^{-bu^2}$ for every $b>0$ and every member has a Fourier transform with only real zeros, then Riemann's kernel $\Phi$ is not in the class; this follows from the theorem of Rodgers and Tao that the de Bruijn Newman constant is nonnegative.
results.statement: Let $\Phi$ be Riemann's kernel, $\Phi(u)=2\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u/2}-3\pi n^2e^{5u/2})e^{-\pi n^2e^{2u}}$, so that $\Xi(t)=2\int_0^\infty\Phi(u)\cos(tu)\,du$ and $\Phi$ is positive and even. Let $\mathcal K$ be a class of positive even kernels closed under $K\mapsto Ke^{-bu^2}$ for every $b>0$. If every $K\in\mathcal K$ has a Fourier transform with only real zeros, then $\Phi\notin\mathcal K$. (The proof uses the theorem of Rodgers and Tao, $\Lambda\ge0$, for the de Bruijn Newman constant $\Lambda$.)
results.label: ki:prop:obstruction

results.name: Brownian exit time limit: the reciprocals of the even derivatives of Xi, rescaled, converge to 1 over cosh of the square root of 2s
results.summary: For $\psi_n(s)=\Xi^{(2n)}(0)/\Xi^{(2n)}(i\sqrt{2s}/m_n)$, $\psi_n(s)\to1/\cosh\sqrt{2s}$ locally uniformly off the poles, the Laplace transform of the exit time of Brownian motion from $(-1,1)$, whose Thorin atoms $c_k^2/2$ are approached by the smallest atoms of $\psi_n$; under RH each $\psi_n$ is a GGC transform and the clocks converge in law.
results.statement: Let $\Phi$ be Riemann's kernel, $\Phi(u)=2\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u/2}-3\pi n^2e^{5u/2})e^{-\pi n^2e^{2u}}$, so that $\Xi(t)=2\int_0^\infty\Phi(u)\cos(tu)\,du$ and $\Phi$ is positive and even. Let $X_n$ be the symmetric random variable with density proportional to $u^{2n}\Phi(u)$ and $m_n=\mathbb{E}|X_n|$, so that $\Xi^{(2n)}(\theta)/\Xi^{(2n)}(0)=\mathbb{E}\cos(\theta X_n)$ for the even derivatives of $\Xi$, and put $\psi_n(s)=\Xi^{(2n)}(0)/\Xi^{(2n)}(i\sqrt{2s}/m_n)=1/\mathbb{E}[\cosh(\sqrt{2s}X_n/m_n)]$. Then $\psi_n(s)\to1/\cosh\sqrt{2s}$ locally uniformly off the poles of the limit. The limit is $\mathbb{E}[e^{-sT}]$ for $T$ the exit time of standard Brownian motion from $(-1,1)$, a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) with Thorin measure $\sum_{k\ge1}\delta_{c_k^2/2}$, $c_k=(2k-1)\pi/2$. For each $K$ there is $n_K$ such that for $n\ge n_K$ the $K$ smallest Thorin atoms of $\psi_n$ are positive and simple and converge to $c_k^2/2$. If the Riemann Hypothesis holds, each $\psi_n$ is the Laplace transform of a GGC $T_n$ and $T_n\to T$ in law.
results.label: ki:prop:bm

results.name: Conjecture: the Edgeworth rate of convergence of the zeros and clocks of the derivatives of Xi
results.summary: The $k$th positive zero of $\Xi^{(2n)}$ is conjectured to satisfy $z_{k,n}m_n=c_k+\kappa_nc_k^3/(6m_n^3)(1+o(1))$ and the distance of $\psi_n$ from $1/\cosh\sqrt{2s}$ is $\sup_{x\le\sqrt{2S}}\frac{x^2}{2\cosh x}\cdot\sigma_n^2/m_n^2\,(1+o(1))$; the constant $0.53222$ is computed.
results.statement: Let $\Phi$ be Riemann's kernel, $\Phi(u)=2\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u/2}-3\pi n^2e^{5u/2})e^{-\pi n^2e^{2u}}$, so that $\Xi(t)=2\int_0^\infty\Phi(u)\cos(tu)\,du$ and $\Phi$ is positive and even. With $X_n$ the symmetric variable of density proportional to $u^{2n}\Phi(u)$, $m_n=\mathbb{E}|X_n|$, $V_n=|X_n|-m_n$, $\sigma_n^2=\mathbb{E}V_n^2$, $\kappa_n=\mathbb{E}V_n^3$, $c_k=(2k-1)\pi/2$ and $\psi_n(s)=1/\mathbb{E}[\cosh(\sqrt{2s}X_n/m_n)]$, conjecturally, as $n\to\infty$ and for each fixed $k$, the $k$th positive zero $z_{k,n}$ of $\Xi^{(2n)}$ satisfies $z_{k,n}m_n=c_k+\frac{\kappa_nc_k^3}{6m_n^3}(1+o(1))$, and for every $S>0$, $\sup_{0\le s\le S}|\psi_n(s)-1/\cosh\sqrt{2s}|=\big(\sup_{x\le\sqrt{2S}}\frac{x^2}{2\cosh x}\big)\frac{\sigma_n^2}{m_n^2}(1+o(1))$. For $S\ge2.133$ the constant is $\max_xx^2/(2\cosh x)=0.53222$, attained at $x=2.06534$, the root of $\tanh x=2/x$ (computed).
results.label: ki:conj:rate

results.name: The density of the reciprocal xi law is the limit of grouped residue sums, with no hypothesis on the zeros
results.summary: There are radii $R_n\in[n,2n]$ with $f(y)=\lim_{n\to\infty}\sum_{|u_\rho|<R_n}\operatorname{Res}_{u=u_\rho}e^{uy}/G(u)$ for every $y>0$, with an explicit error bound, whatever the zeros.
results.statement: Let $\zeta$ be the Riemann zeta function, $\rho=\frac12+\delta+i\gamma$ its nontrivial zeros, and for each zero in the upper half plane let $u_\rho=(\rho-\frac12)^2$ (equal to $-\gamma^2$ under the Riemann Hypothesis, RH). Let $G(u)=\prod_{\gamma>0}(1-u/u_\rho)$ (entire of order one half) and let $\mu$ be the law on $[0,\infty)$, the law of the clock $T$ of the book, with Laplace transform $1/G$ and density $f$; $\mu$ is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) if and only if RH holds, and then $T=\sum_{\gamma>0}e_\gamma/\gamma^2$ with independent standard exponential variables $e_\gamma$. Write $w_\gamma=1/G'(-\gamma^2)$ under RH, and $\gamma_1<\gamma_2<\gamma_3<\dots$ for the ordinates. There are radii $R_n\to\infty$ with $R_n\in[n,2n]$ such that for every $y>0$, $f(y)=\lim_{n\to\infty}\sum_{|u_\rho|<R_n}\operatorname{Res}_{u=u_\rho}e^{uy}/G(u)$, with no hypothesis on the zeros. A simple zero contributes $e^{u_\rho y}/G'(u_\rho)$, a zero of multiplicity $m$ contributes $e^{u_\rho y}P_\rho(y)$ with $P_\rho$ a polynomial of degree $m-1$, and a pair of zeros $\frac12\pm\delta+i\gamma$ off the line contributes $2\operatorname{Re}(e^{u_\rho y}/G'(u_\rho))$. For $y$ in a compact subset of $(0,\infty)$ the error after the $n$th group is at most $R_n\exp(-\frac12R_ny+C\sqrt{R_n}\log R_n)+\exp(-c\sqrt{R_n}\log R_n)$ for constants $c,C>0$.
results.label: ht:thm:grouped

results.name: Residue expansion: absolute convergence of the density series given a lower bound for the derivative of xi at the zeros
results.status_text: conditional on the zeros of the Riemann zeta function are simple and $|\xi'(\rho)|\ge e^{-C|\gamma|}$ for some constant $C$ and all zeros
results.conditions: the zeros of the Riemann zeta function are simple and $|\xi'(\rho)|\ge e^{-C|\gamma|}$ for some constant $C$ and all zeros
results.summary: If the zeros of $\zeta$ are simple and $|\xi'(\rho)|\ge e^{-C|\gamma|}$ for all zeros, the residue series for $f$ converges absolutely and locally uniformly, and under RH equals $\sum_{\gamma>0}w_\gamma e^{-\gamma^2y}$.
results.statement: Let $\zeta$ be the Riemann zeta function, $\rho=\frac12+\delta+i\gamma$ its nontrivial zeros, and for each zero in the upper half plane let $u_\rho=(\rho-\frac12)^2$ (equal to $-\gamma^2$ under the Riemann Hypothesis, RH). Let $G(u)=\prod_{\gamma>0}(1-u/u_\rho)$ (entire of order one half) and let $\mu$ be the law on $[0,\infty)$, the law of the clock $T$ of the book, with Laplace transform $1/G$ and density $f$; $\mu$ is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) if and only if RH holds, and then $T=\sum_{\gamma>0}e_\gamma/\gamma^2$ with independent standard exponential variables $e_\gamma$. Write $w_\gamma=1/G'(-\gamma^2)$ under RH, and $\gamma_1<\gamma_2<\gamma_3<\dots$ for the ordinates. Assume that the zeros of $\zeta$ are simple and that $|\xi'(\rho)|\ge e^{-C|\gamma|}$ for some constant $C$ and all zeros (a hypothesis not known to hold). Then $f(y)=\sum_{\gamma>0}e^{u_\rho y}/G'(u_\rho)$, $y>0$, converges absolutely and locally uniformly. Under RH it reads $f(y)=\sum_{\gamma>0}w_\gamma e^{-\gamma^2y}$ with $w_\gamma=\gamma^2\prod_{\gamma'\ne\gamma}(1-\gamma^2/\gamma'^2)^{-1}$.
results.label: ht:thm:res

results.name: Upper tail of the density of the reciprocal xi law: two exponential terms and an explicit remainder
results.summary: With no hypothesis, $f(y)=w_1e^{-\gamma_1^2y}+w_2e^{-\gamma_2^2y}+O(e^{-c_3y})$ as $y\to\infty$, with $c_3=\frac12(\gamma_2^2+\gamma_3^2)$ and the same bound for each derivative.
results.statement: Let $\zeta$ be the Riemann zeta function, $\rho=\frac12+\delta+i\gamma$ its nontrivial zeros, and for each zero in the upper half plane let $u_\rho=(\rho-\frac12)^2$ (equal to $-\gamma^2$ under the Riemann Hypothesis, RH). Let $G(u)=\prod_{\gamma>0}(1-u/u_\rho)$ (entire of order one half) and let $\mu$ be the law on $[0,\infty)$, the law of the clock $T$ of the book, with Laplace transform $1/G$ and density $f$; $\mu$ is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) if and only if RH holds, and then $T=\sum_{\gamma>0}e_\gamma/\gamma^2$ with independent standard exponential variables $e_\gamma$. Write $w_\gamma=1/G'(-\gamma^2)$ under RH, and $\gamma_1<\gamma_2<\gamma_3<\dots$ for the ordinates. Let $c_3=\frac12(\gamma_2^2+\gamma_3^2)$. With no hypothesis, $f(y)=w_1e^{-\gamma_1^2y}+w_2e^{-\gamma_2^2y}+O(e^{-c_3y})$ as $y\to\infty$, with the same bound for each derivative, where $w_1=1.01635\times10^4>0$ and $w_2=-1.17754\times10^6<0$.
results.label: ht:prop:tail

results.name: Kent's eigenfunction expansion is the residue expansion under RH with simple zeros
results.summary: Under RH with simple zeros the residue series is Kent's expansion with $\lambda_n=\gamma_n^2$ and $f$ is the density of the hitting time of a Krein string with Dirichlet spectrum $\{\gamma_n^2\}$; without these hypotheses the grouped expansion only continues Kent's formula to complex eigenvalues.
results.statement: Let $\zeta$ be the Riemann zeta function, $\rho=\frac12+\delta+i\gamma$ its nontrivial zeros, and for each zero in the upper half plane let $u_\rho=(\rho-\frac12)^2$ (equal to $-\gamma^2$ under the Riemann Hypothesis, RH). Let $G(u)=\prod_{\gamma>0}(1-u/u_\rho)$ (entire of order one half) and let $\mu$ be the law on $[0,\infty)$, the law of the clock $T$ of the book, with Laplace transform $1/G$ and density $f$; $\mu$ is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) if and only if RH holds, and then $T=\sum_{\gamma>0}e_\gamma/\gamma^2$ with independent standard exponential variables $e_\gamma$. Write $w_\gamma=1/G'(-\gamma^2)$ under RH, and $\gamma_1<\gamma_2<\gamma_3<\dots$ for the ordinates. If RH holds and the zeros are simple, the residue series $\sum_{\gamma>0}e^{u_\rho y}/G'(u_\rho)$ is Kent's expansion with $\lambda_n=\gamma_n^2$, and $f$ is the density of the hitting time of a Krein string with Dirichlet spectrum $\{\gamma_n^2\}$. Without these hypotheses the grouped expansion is the formal continuation of Kent's formula to complex eigenvalues: an off line pair contributes $2\operatorname{Re}(e^{u_\rho y}/G'(u_\rho))$, a multiple zero contributes a polynomial times an exponential, and no string has such a spectrum.
results.label: ht:prop:kent

results.name: The function xi(1/2+it) is not in Krein's class and the partial fraction series of 1/G diverges under RH
results.summary: $\xi(\frac12+it)$ is not in Krein's class, with or without RH, and under RH the partial fraction series of $1/G$ over the points $-\gamma_n^2$ does not converge absolutely.
results.statement: Let $\zeta$ be the Riemann zeta function, $\rho=\frac12+\delta+i\gamma$ its nontrivial zeros, and for each zero in the upper half plane let $u_\rho=(\rho-\frac12)^2$ (equal to $-\gamma^2$ under the Riemann Hypothesis, RH). Let $G(u)=\prod_{\gamma>0}(1-u/u_\rho)$ (entire of order one half) and let $\mu$ be the law on $[0,\infty)$, the law of the clock $T$ of the book, with Laplace transform $1/G$ and density $f$; $\mu$ is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) if and only if RH holds, and then $T=\sum_{\gamma>0}e_\gamma/\gamma^2$ with independent standard exponential variables $e_\gamma$. Write $w_\gamma=1/G'(-\gamma^2)$ under RH, and $\gamma_1<\gamma_2<\gamma_3<\dots$ for the ordinates. The function $\xi(\frac12+it)$ does not belong to Krein's class, whether or not RH holds. Moreover, under RH the partial fraction series of $1/G$ over the points $u_\rho=-\gamma_n^2$ does not converge absolutely.
results.label: ht:prop:krein

results.name: RH holds if and only if the reciprocal xi law is a weak limit of GGC laws
results.summary: RH holds if and only if there are GGC laws, for instance hitting times of strings, converging weakly to $\mu$.
results.statement: Let $\zeta$ be the Riemann zeta function, $\rho=\frac12+\delta+i\gamma$ its nontrivial zeros, and for each zero in the upper half plane let $u_\rho=(\rho-\frac12)^2$ (equal to $-\gamma^2$ under the Riemann Hypothesis, RH). Let $G(u)=\prod_{\gamma>0}(1-u/u_\rho)$ (entire of order one half) and let $\mu$ be the law on $[0,\infty)$, the law of the clock $T$ of the book, with Laplace transform $1/G$ and density $f$; $\mu$ is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) if and only if RH holds, and then $T=\sum_{\gamma>0}e_\gamma/\gamma^2$ with independent standard exponential variables $e_\gamma$. Write $w_\gamma=1/G'(-\gamma^2)$ under RH, and $\gamma_1<\gamma_2<\gamma_3<\dots$ for the ordinates. RH holds if and only if there are GGC laws, for instance hitting times of strings, converging weakly to $\mu$.
results.label: ht:prop:red

results.name: Truncations of the Hadamard product: GGC if and only if the first N zeros lie on the line, and GGC up to the verified height
results.summary: The law $\mu_N$ with transform $1/G_N$ (first $N$ zeros) is a GGC iff the first $N$ zeros are on the line, hence for every $N$ up to the zeros below $3\cdot10^{12}$; RH holds iff every $\mu_N$ is a GGC; under RH $0\le\log G-\log G_N\le u\tau_1(N)$ on $u\ge0$.
results.statement: Let $\zeta$ be the Riemann zeta function, $\rho=\frac12+\delta+i\gamma$ its nontrivial zeros, and for each zero in the upper half plane let $u_\rho=(\rho-\frac12)^2$ (equal to $-\gamma^2$ under the Riemann Hypothesis, RH). Let $G(u)=\prod_{\gamma>0}(1-u/u_\rho)$ (entire of order one half) and let $\mu$ be the law on $[0,\infty)$, the law of the clock $T$ of the book, with Laplace transform $1/G$ and density $f$; $\mu$ is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) if and only if RH holds, and then $T=\sum_{\gamma>0}e_\gamma/\gamma^2$ with independent standard exponential variables $e_\gamma$. Write $w_\gamma=1/G'(-\gamma^2)$ under RH, and $\gamma_1<\gamma_2<\gamma_3<\dots$ for the ordinates. Order the zeros in the upper half plane by height, let $G_N(u)=\prod_{n\le N}(1-u/u_{\rho_n})$, $\varphi_N=1/G_N$, $\varphi=1/G$, and let $\mu_N$ be the law with Laplace transform $\varphi_N$. (i) $\varphi_N\to\varphi$ pointwise on $[0,\infty)$, and for each fixed zero $1/G_N'(u_\rho)\to1/G'(u_\rho)$, with correction factor $\prod_{n>N}(1-u_\rho/u_{\rho_n})^{-1}\approx\exp(u_\rho\sum_{n>N}u_{\rho_n}^{-1})$, which under RH equals $\exp(\gamma^2\sum_{n>N}\gamma_n^{-2})>1$. (ii) $\mu_N$ is a GGC if and only if the first $N$ zeros lie on the line; in particular it is a GGC, unconditionally, for every $N\le N_0(H)$, the number of zeros below the verified height $H=3\cdot10^{12}$ (Platt and Trudgian). (iii) RH holds if and only if every $\mu_N$ is a GGC, and then $\mu$ is a GGC by Bondesson's continuity theorem. (iv) Under RH, for $u\ge0$, $0\le\log G(u)-\log G_N(u)\le u\,\tau_1(N)$ with $\tau_1(N)=\sum_{n>N}\gamma_n^{-2}\approx(\log(T_N/2\pi)+1)/(2\pi T_N)$, where $T_N$ is the height of the $N$th zero.
results.label: ht:prop:trunc

results.name: The density of the reciprocal xi law is strictly log concave on a half line, with no hypothesis
results.summary: There is $Y$ such that $f$ is strictly log concave on $[Y,\infty)$, with no hypothesis on the zeros.
results.statement: Let $\zeta$ be the Riemann zeta function, $\rho=\frac12+\delta+i\gamma$ its nontrivial zeros, and for each zero in the upper half plane let $u_\rho=(\rho-\frac12)^2$ (equal to $-\gamma^2$ under the Riemann Hypothesis, RH). Let $G(u)=\prod_{\gamma>0}(1-u/u_\rho)$ (entire of order one half) and let $\mu$ be the law on $[0,\infty)$, the law of the clock $T$ of the book, with Laplace transform $1/G$ and density $f$; $\mu$ is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) if and only if RH holds, and then $T=\sum_{\gamma>0}e_\gamma/\gamma^2$ with independent standard exponential variables $e_\gamma$. Write $w_\gamma=1/G'(-\gamma^2)$ under RH, and $\gamma_1<\gamma_2<\gamma_3<\dots$ for the ordinates. There is $Y$ such that $f$ is strictly log concave on $[Y,\infty)$, with no hypothesis.
results.label: ht:thm:lctail

results.name: Log concavity of the reciprocal xi density near the origin, given the saddle point approximation
results.status_text: conditional on the saddle point approximation of $\log f(y)$ holds as $y\to0$ together with two derivatives
results.conditions: the saddle point approximation of $\log f(y)$ holds as $y\to0$ together with two derivatives
results.summary: If the saddle point approximation of $\log f(y)$ holds as $y\to0$ together with two derivatives, then $f$ is strictly log concave on $(0,y_0]$ for some $y_0>0$.
results.statement: Let $\zeta$ be the Riemann zeta function, $\rho=\frac12+\delta+i\gamma$ its nontrivial zeros, and for each zero in the upper half plane let $u_\rho=(\rho-\frac12)^2$ (equal to $-\gamma^2$ under the Riemann Hypothesis, RH). Let $G(u)=\prod_{\gamma>0}(1-u/u_\rho)$ (entire of order one half) and let $\mu$ be the law on $[0,\infty)$, the law of the clock $T$ of the book, with Laplace transform $1/G$ and density $f$; $\mu$ is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) if and only if RH holds, and then $T=\sum_{\gamma>0}e_\gamma/\gamma^2$ with independent standard exponential variables $e_\gamma$. Write $w_\gamma=1/G'(-\gamma^2)$ under RH, and $\gamma_1<\gamma_2<\gamma_3<\dots$ for the ordinates. Let $\psi=\log G$, $\Lambda_f(y)=\sup_{u>0}(\psi(u)-uy)$ and $u_y$ the solution of $\psi'(u_y)=y$. Suppose the saddle point approximation $\log f(y)\approx-\Lambda_f(y)-\frac12\log(2\pi|\psi''(u_y)|)$ holds as $y\to0$ together with two derivatives (this is assumed, not proved). Then $f$ is strictly log concave on $(0,y_0]$ for some $y_0>0$.
results.label: ht:prop:lc0

results.name: The density of the reciprocal xi law is the sum of its first 120 residue terms up to an explicit exponentially small error
results.summary: For every $y>0$ and $j\ge0$, $|f^{(j)}(y)-\sum_{n\le120}w_n(-\gamma_n^2)^je^{-\gamma_n^2y}|\le M_je^{-cy}$ with $M_j=\frac1{2\pi}\int|{-c}+it|^j/|G(-c+it)|\,\mathrm dt$, and numerically $\log M_0=206.26$.
results.statement: Let $\zeta$ be the Riemann zeta function, $\rho=\frac12+\delta+i\gamma$ its nontrivial zeros, and for each zero in the upper half plane let $u_\rho=(\rho-\frac12)^2$ (equal to $-\gamma^2$ under the Riemann Hypothesis, RH). Let $G(u)=\prod_{\gamma>0}(1-u/u_\rho)$ (entire of order one half) and let $\mu$ be the law on $[0,\infty)$, the law of the clock $T$ of the book, with Laplace transform $1/G$ and density $f$; $\mu$ is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) if and only if RH holds, and then $T=\sum_{\gamma>0}e_\gamma/\gamma^2$ with independent standard exponential variables $e_\gamma$. Write $w_\gamma=1/G'(-\gamma^2)$ under RH, and $\gamma_1<\gamma_2<\gamma_3<\dots$ for the ordinates. With no hypothesis, for every $y>0$ and $j\ge0$, $|f^{(j)}(y)-\sum_{n\le120}w_n(-\gamma_n^2)^je^{-\gamma_n^2y}|\le M_je^{-cy}$, where $c$ is the constant of the book's contour shift beyond the 120th zero, $w_n$ and $\gamma_n$ are the weights and ordinates of the first $120$ zeros, and $M_j=\frac1{2\pi}\int_{-\infty}^\infty|{-c}+it|^j/|G(-c+it)|\,\mathrm dt$. Numerically $\log M_0=206.26$ and $M_{j+1}/M_j=1.0000185\,c$ for $j=0,1,2$ (computed).
results.label: ht:prop:explicit

results.name: Log concavity of the reciprocal xi density on [0.008, infinity) from computed constants
results.summary: Assuming the quadrature values of the constants $M_j$, $j\le8$, of the explicit truncation bound, $f$ is strictly log concave on $[0.008,\infty)$ with no hypothesis on the zeros.
results.statement: Let $\zeta$ be the Riemann zeta function, $\rho=\frac12+\delta+i\gamma$ its nontrivial zeros, and for each zero in the upper half plane let $u_\rho=(\rho-\frac12)^2$ (equal to $-\gamma^2$ under the Riemann Hypothesis, RH). Let $G(u)=\prod_{\gamma>0}(1-u/u_\rho)$ (entire of order one half) and let $\mu$ be the law on $[0,\infty)$, the law of the clock $T$ of the book, with Laplace transform $1/G$ and density $f$; $\mu$ is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) if and only if RH holds, and then $T=\sum_{\gamma>0}e_\gamma/\gamma^2$ with independent standard exponential variables $e_\gamma$. Write $w_\gamma=1/G'(-\gamma^2)$ under RH, and $\gamma_1<\gamma_2<\gamma_3<\dots$ for the ordinates. Assume the values of the constants $M_j$, $j\le8$, of the explicit truncation bound for $f$ with its first $120$ residue terms (computed by quadrature). Then, with no hypothesis on the zeros, $f$ is strictly log concave on $[Y_*,\infty)$ with $Y_*=0.008$.
results.label: ht:thm:lc

results.name: If the density of the reciprocal xi law were HCM then RH would hold
results.summary: If $f$ is hypergeometrically completely monotone (HCM) then $\mu$ is a GGC and RH holds.
results.statement: Let $\zeta$ be the Riemann zeta function, $\rho=\frac12+\delta+i\gamma$ its nontrivial zeros, and for each zero in the upper half plane let $u_\rho=(\rho-\frac12)^2$ (equal to $-\gamma^2$ under the Riemann Hypothesis, RH). Let $G(u)=\prod_{\gamma>0}(1-u/u_\rho)$ (entire of order one half) and let $\mu$ be the law on $[0,\infty)$, the law of the clock $T$ of the book, with Laplace transform $1/G$ and density $f$; $\mu$ is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) if and only if RH holds, and then $T=\sum_{\gamma>0}e_\gamma/\gamma^2$ with independent standard exponential variables $e_\gamma$. Write $w_\gamma=1/G'(-\gamma^2)$ under RH, and $\gamma_1<\gamma_2<\gamma_3<\dots$ for the ordinates. If the density $f$ of $\mu$ is HCM (hyperbolically completely monotone), then $\mu$ is a GGC and RH holds.
results.label: ht:prop:hcm

results.name: No HCM: sums of exponentials are not HCM, and the continued reciprocal xi density has a computed zero in the right half plane
results.status_text: conditional on for part (ii), an explicit remainder bound for the omitted terms on a sector containing $z_*$
results.conditions: for part (ii), an explicit remainder bound for the omitted terms on a sector containing $z_*$
results.summary: No density of a sum of $n\ge2$ independent exponentials with distinct rates is HCM (proved); the continuation of $f$ from its first 120 residue terms vanishes at $z_*=0.01383187+0.02000180i$ (computed), which proves $f$ is not HCM once the omitted terms are controlled on a sector containing $z_*$.
results.statement: Let $\zeta$ be the Riemann zeta function, $\rho=\frac12+\delta+i\gamma$ its nontrivial zeros, and for each zero in the upper half plane let $u_\rho=(\rho-\frac12)^2$ (equal to $-\gamma^2$ under the Riemann Hypothesis, RH). Let $G(u)=\prod_{\gamma>0}(1-u/u_\rho)$ (entire of order one half) and let $\mu$ be the law on $[0,\infty)$, the law of the clock $T$ of the book, with Laplace transform $1/G$ and density $f$; $\mu$ is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) if and only if RH holds, and then $T=\sum_{\gamma>0}e_\gamma/\gamma^2$ with independent standard exponential variables $e_\gamma$. Write $w_\gamma=1/G'(-\gamma^2)$ under RH, and $\gamma_1<\gamma_2<\gamma_3<\dots$ for the ordinates. (i) No density of a sum of $n\ge2$ independent exponential variables with distinct rates is HCM. (ii) With the first $120$ terms of the residue series for $f$, the continuation of $f$ to $\operatorname{Re}z>0$ vanishes at $z_*=0.013831874754506+0.020001801712034\,i$ (computed). If the omitted terms are controlled by an explicit remainder bound on a sector containing $z_*$, this proves that $f$ is not HCM.
results.label: ht:thm:nohcm

results.name: Jensen polynomial laws mu_d of the reciprocal xi function: convergence, existence if and only if RH, and existence up to degree 2e17
results.summary: $J_d\to G$ locally uniformly; if $J_d$ has only real zeros then $1/J_d$ is the transform of a GGC law $\mu_d$ (a pure birth chain passage time); RH iff $\mu_d$ exists for all $d$, and then $\mu_d\Rightarrow\mu$; $\mu_d$ exists for $d\le2\cdot10^{17}$ unconditionally (quoted); $\mu_d$ has mean $c_1$ and variance exceeding that of $\mu$ by $2c_2/d$.
results.statement: Let $\zeta$ be the Riemann zeta function, $\rho=\frac12+\delta+i\gamma$ its nontrivial zeros, and for each zero in the upper half plane let $u_\rho=(\rho-\frac12)^2$ (equal to $-\gamma^2$ under the Riemann Hypothesis, RH). Let $G(u)=\prod_{\gamma>0}(1-u/u_\rho)$ (entire of order one half) and let $\mu$ be the law on $[0,\infty)$, the law of the clock $T$ of the book, with Laplace transform $1/G$ and density $f$; $\mu$ is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) if and only if RH holds, and then $T=\sum_{\gamma>0}e_\gamma/\gamma^2$ with independent standard exponential variables $e_\gamma$. Write $w_\gamma=1/G'(-\gamma^2)$ under RH, and $\gamma_1<\gamma_2<\gamma_3<\dots$ for the ordinates. Write $G(u)=\sum_{k\ge0}c_ku^k$, so that $G(u)=\mathbb E\cosh(\sqrt u\,V)$ with $V$ symmetric with density $\Phi/\Xi(0)$ ($\Phi$ Riemann's kernel, $\Xi(z)=\xi(\frac12+iz)$) and $c_k=\mathbb E V^{2k}/(2k)!>0$. For $d\ge1$ let $J_d(u)=\sum_{k=0}^d\binom dk\frac{k!}{d^k}c_ku^k=\sum_{k=0}^dc_k\prod_{j<k}(1-\frac jd)u^k$ (up to scaling the Jensen polynomial of degree $d$ and shift $0$ of Griffin, Ono, Rolen and Zagier). (1) $J_d\to G$ uniformly on compact sets, without any hypothesis. (2) If $J_d$ has only real zeros, they are negative, $J_d(u)=\prod_{j\le d}(1+u/\ell_{d,j})$, and $1/J_d$ is the Laplace transform of the GGC law $\mu_d$ of $\sum_{j\le d}e_j/\ell_{d,j}$, the time a pure birth chain with rates $\ell_{d,1},\dots,\ell_{d,d}$ takes to pass through $d$ states. (3) RH holds if and only if $\mu_d$ exists for every $d$, and then $\mu_d\Rightarrow\mu$. (4) $\mu_d$ exists for every $d\le2\cdot10^{17}$, unconditionally (quoted from Griffin, Ono, Rolen and Zagier, who quote Chass\'e). (5) Every $\mu_d$ has the same mean $c_1$ as $\mu$, and its variance exceeds that of $\mu$ by $2c_2/d$.
results.label: ht:prop:jensen

results.name: Density of a sum of independent exponentials as a Laplace transform of a B spline, the Dirichlet mean form
results.summary: For $0<\lambda_1<\dots<\lambda_N$ the density of $\sum e_k/\lambda_k$ is $(\prod\lambda_k)\frac{y^{N-1}}{(N-1)!}\int M(x;\lambda)e^{-xy}\,dx$ with $M$ the Curry and Schoenberg B spline, the density of the Dirichlet mean $\sum W_k\lambda_k$.
results.statement: Let $0<\lambda_1<\dots<\lambda_N$, let $e_k$ be independent standard exponential variables and $f_N$ the density of $\sum_{k\le N}e_k/\lambda_k$. Then $f_N(y)=(\prod_{k\le N}\lambda_k)\frac{y^{N-1}}{(N-1)!}\int M(x;\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_N)e^{-xy}\,\mathrm dx$, where $M(\cdot;\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_N)$ is the Curry and Schoenberg B spline with knots $\lambda_k$, normalised to integral one. Equivalently $M$ is the density of the Dirichlet mean $D_N=\sum_kW_k\lambda_k$ with $(W_k)$ uniform on the simplex, and the formula is the case of Dirichlet parameter $N$ of the density formula of James, Roynette and Yor.
results.label: ht:prop:bspline

results.name: A sum of exponentials is a linear functional of the Gumbel extremal process
results.summary: For $0<\lambda_1\le\lambda_2\le\cdots$ with $\sum1/\lambda_k<\infty$ and $b_k=k/\lambda_k$, $\sum e_k/\lambda_k\overset d=\sum_kb_k(G_k-G_{k+1})$, rearranged to $b_1G_1+\sum_{k\ge2}(b_k-b_{k-1})G_k$ if $k\log k/\lambda_k\to0$; under RH $\mu$ is $\sum k\gamma_k^{-2}(G_k-G_{k+1})$.
results.statement: Let $e_k$ be independent standard exponential variables and $G_1>G_2>\cdots$ the points of the Gumbel extremal process of the book. For any $0<\lambda_1\le\lambda_2\le\cdots$ with $\sum1/\lambda_k<\infty$, and $b_k=k/\lambda_k$, $\sum_ke_k/\lambda_k\overset d=\sum_{k\ge1}b_k(G_k-G_{k+1})$, and if moreover $k\log k/\lambda_k\to0$ the series may be rearranged: $\sum_{k\ge1}b_k(G_k-G_{k+1})=b_1G_1+\sum_{k\ge2}(b_k-b_{k-1})G_k$. In particular, under RH, the reciprocal xi law $\mu$ is the law of $\sum_kk\gamma_k^{-2}(G_k-G_{k+1})$. For finite $N$ the truncation $\mu_N$ is the L statistic $\sum_{k\le N}b_k(e_{(N-k+1)}-e_{(N-k)})$ of $N$ exponentials, with $e_{(0)}=0$.
results.label: ht:thm:extremal

results.name: Truncated Euler products give GGC laws Y_P, and first passage to the mean level decomposes as Y_P plus the first passage to the log of N_P
results.summary: For every $\alpha>0$ and $P$, $e^{-B\sqrt{2u}}\zeta_P(\alpha)/\zeta_P(\alpha+\sqrt{2u})$ is the Laplace transform of a GGC law $Y_P$ with zero drift and an explicit nonnegative Thorin density, in particular unconditionally at $\alpha=\frac12$; and $T_{\mathbb E\log N_P}\overset d=Y_P+T_{\log N_P}$.
results.statement: For $P\ge2$ let $\zeta_P(z)=\prod_{p\le P}(1-p^{-z})^{-1}$, fix $\alpha>0$, and let $N_P$ be the random integer with $\Pr(N_P=n)=n^{-\alpha}/\zeta_P(\alpha)$ for $n$ composed of primes up to $P$. Let $L=\log N_P$, $B_{\alpha,P}=\mathbb EL=\sum_{p\le P}\log p\,p^{-\alpha}/(1-p^{-\alpha})$, and $T_a$ the first passage time of standard Brownian motion to the level $a$. For every $\alpha>0$ and every $P$ the function $\Phi_{\alpha,P}(u)=e^{-B_{\alpha,P}\sqrt{2u}}/\mathbb Ee^{-\sqrt{2u}L}=\frac{\zeta_P(\alpha)}{\zeta_P(\alpha+\sqrt{2u})}e^{-B_{\alpha,P}\sqrt{2u}}$ is the Laplace transform of a GGC law $Y_P$ with zero drift, whose Thorin measure has density in the ordinate $\tau$ (atom positions $\tau^2/2$) equal to $\frac1\pi\sum_{p\le P}\sum_{k\ge1}\log p\,p^{-k\alpha}(1-\cos(k\tau\log p))\ge0$. In particular this holds on the critical line $\alpha=\frac12$, unconditionally. If $Y_P$ is independent of $N_P$ and of the Brownian motion, then $T_{\mathbb E\log N_P}\overset d=Y_P+T_{\log N_P}$.
results.label: ht:thm:trunc

results.name: The Euler hitting times converge after scaling to a spectrally positive stable law of index 3/2
results.summary: As $P\to\infty$, $Z_P=(Y_P-\kappa_2(P))/\kappa_3(P)^{2/3}\Rightarrow Z$ with $\log\mathbb Ee^{-sZ}=(2s)^{3/2}/6$, with the bound $|\log\mathbb Ee^{-sZ_P}-(2s)^{3/2}/6|\le\frac{|s|^2}6\rho_4(P)$ for $\operatorname{Re}s\ge0$ and $\rho_4(P)\to0$.
results.statement: Take $\alpha=\frac12$ in the truncated Euler product laws: $Y_P$ is the GGC law with transform $\zeta_P(\frac12)e^{-B\sqrt{2u}}/\zeta_P(\frac12+\sqrt{2u})$, $L_P=\log N_P$, $\kappa_j(P)$ the $j$th cumulant of $L_P$ (so $K_P(w)=\log\mathbb Ee^{-w(L_P-\mathbb EL_P)}=\sum_{p\le P}\sum_{m\ge1}\frac{p^{-m/2}}m(e^{-wm\log p}-1+wm\log p)$), and $\rho_j(P)=\kappa_j(P)/\kappa_3(P)^{j/3}$; $Y_P$ has mean $\kappa_2(P)=\operatorname{Var}L_P$. As $P\to\infty$, $Z_P=(Y_P-\kappa_2(P))/\kappa_3(P)^{2/3}\Rightarrow Z$, $\log\mathbb Ee^{-sZ}=(2s)^{3/2}/6$ for $\operatorname{Re}s\ge0$, a spectrally positive stable law of index $\frac32$. More precisely, for $\operatorname{Re}s\ge0$, $|\log\mathbb Ee^{-sZ_P}-(2s)^{3/2}/6|\le\frac{|s|^2}6\rho_4(P)$, and $\rho_4(P)\to0$.
results.label: ht:thm:32

results.name: Thorin rigidity: any factorisation of the reciprocal xi law into two GGC laws forces RH and splits the zeros
results.summary: If $\mu=\mu_1*\mu_2$ with both factors GGC, then RH holds and the Thorin measures are $\sum a_\gamma\delta_{\gamma^2}$ and $\sum(m_\gamma-a_\gamma)\delta_{\gamma^2}$ with $0\le a_\gamma\le m_\gamma$; no GGC law with drift or a nonzero absolutely continuous Thorin part is a GGC factor with a GGC cofactor.
results.statement: Let $\zeta$ be the Riemann zeta function, $\rho=\frac12+\delta+i\gamma$ its nontrivial zeros, and for each zero in the upper half plane let $u_\rho=(\rho-\frac12)^2$ (equal to $-\gamma^2$ under the Riemann Hypothesis, RH). Let $G(u)=\prod_{\gamma>0}(1-u/u_\rho)$ (entire of order one half) and let $\mu$ be the law on $[0,\infty)$, the law of the clock $T$ of the book, with Laplace transform $1/G$ and density $f$; $\mu$ is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) if and only if RH holds, and then $T=\sum_{\gamma>0}e_\gamma/\gamma^2$ with independent standard exponential variables $e_\gamma$. Write $w_\gamma=1/G'(-\gamma^2)$ under RH, and $\gamma_1<\gamma_2<\gamma_3<\dots$ for the ordinates. If $\mu=\mu_1*\mu_2$ with $\mu_1$ and $\mu_2$ GGC laws, then RH holds and the Thorin measures are $U_1=\sum_{\gamma>0}a_\gamma\delta_{\gamma^2}$ and $U_2=\sum_{\gamma>0}(m_\gamma-a_\gamma)\delta_{\gamma^2}$ with $0\le a_\gamma\le m_\gamma$, where $m_\gamma$ is the multiplicity of the zero ($m_\gamma=1$ for simple zeros), and $\mu_1$ is the law of $\sum_\gamma g_\gamma/\gamma^2$ with independent gamma variables $g_\gamma$ of shapes $a_\gamma$. No GGC law with drift or with a nonzero absolutely continuous Thorin part is a GGC factor of $\mu$ with a GGC cofactor.
results.label: ht:thm:rigid

results.name: Small time enclosure of the inverse first passage boundary of the reciprocal xi law, independent of RH
results.summary: With $F(t)=\mu(0,t]$ and $m(t)=\inf_{s\le t}b(s)$, $\sqrt t\bar\Phi_N^{-1}(F(t))\le b(t)$ and $m(t)\le\sqrt t\bar\Phi_N^{-1}(\frac12F(t))$; $-\log F(t)\sim\log^2(1/t)/(16t)$, so $\liminf b/\log(1/t)\ge1/(2\sqrt2)\ge\limsup m/\log(1/t)$, and $b\sim\log(1/t)/(2\sqrt2)$ if $b$ is nonincreasing near $0$; no use of RH.
results.statement: Let $\mu$ be the reciprocal xi law of the book, with Laplace transform $1/G$, $G(u)=\prod_{\gamma>0}(1-u/u_\rho)$ over the zeros of the Riemann zeta function, and let $b$ be the boundary of the inverse first passage problem for $\mu$: $b$ is such that $\tau_b=\inf\{t>0:W_t\ge b(t)\}$ for a standard Brownian motion $W$ has law $\mu$. Write $F(t)=\mu(0,t]$ and $m(t)=\inf_{0<s\le t}b(s)$, and let $\Phi_{\mathrm N}$ be the standard normal distribution function, $\bar\Phi_{\mathrm N}=1-\Phi_{\mathrm N}$. For every $t>0$, $\sqrt t\,\bar\Phi_{\mathrm N}^{-1}(F(t))\le b(t)$ and $m(t)\le\sqrt t\,\bar\Phi_{\mathrm N}^{-1}(\frac12F(t))$. Moreover $-\log F(t)\sim(\log(1/t))^2/(16t)$ as $t\downarrow0$, so $\liminf_{t\downarrow0}b(t)/\log(1/t)\ge\frac1{2\sqrt2}$ and $\limsup_{t\downarrow0}m(t)/\log(1/t)\le\frac1{2\sqrt2}$, and if $b$ is nonincreasing near $0$ then $b(t)\sim\log(1/t)/(2\sqrt2)$. None of this depends on RH.
results.label: ht:prop:smallb

results.name: Moving a pair of zeros off the line by delta multiplies the Laplace transform by 1+6 delta^2 s/gamma^4 to first order
results.summary: Moving the pair at height $\gamma$ off the line by $\delta$ multiplies the Laplace transform, relative to the control, by $1+6\delta^2s/\gamma^4+O(\delta^2s^2/\gamma^6)$ for $|s|\ll\gamma^2$, which to first order shifts the mean by $-6\delta^2/\gamma^4$.
results.statement: Let $\mu$ be the reciprocal xi law, with Laplace transform $1/G$, $G(u)=\prod_{\gamma>0}(1-u/u_\rho)$ over the zeros of the Riemann zeta function (the control being the case of all zeros on the line). Moving the pair of zeros at height $\gamma$ off the line by $\delta$ multiplies the Laplace transform, relative to the control, by $1+6\delta^2s/\gamma^4+O(\delta^2s^2/\gamma^6)$ for $|s|\ll\gamma^2$. To first order this is the shift $\tau\mapsto\tau-6\delta^2/\gamma^4$ of the mean $\tau$.
results.label: ht:prop:resp

results.name: The reciprocal xi law as the reciprocal of an expected cosh under the size biased Biane Pitman Yor measure
results.summary: Under the size biased measure with density $Y^{1/2}/\mathbb EY^{1/2}$, $U=\log Y$ is symmetric with density $\Phi/\Xi(0)$, and $\mathbb Ee^{-s\tau}=\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt s)=1/\mathbb E^*\cosh(\sqrt sU)$, which is $1/\mathbb E^*[\mathbb E[e^{-sT}|U]^{-1}]$ for $T$ the exit time of Brownian motion from $(-|U|/\sqrt2,|U|/\sqrt2)$.
results.statement: Let $Y=\sqrt{2/\pi}(\max_ub_u-\min_ub_u)$ for a standard Brownian bridge $b$, so that $\mathbb EY^s=2\xi(s)$, and let $\tau$ be the clock with $\mathbb Ee^{-s\tau}=\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt s)$. Let $\mathbb P^*$ have density $Y^{1/2}/\mathbb EY^{1/2}$ with respect to $\mathbb P$ and let $U=\log Y$. Under $\mathbb P^*$ the variable $U$ is symmetric with density $\Phi/\Xi(0)$, where $\Xi(z)=\xi(\frac12+iz)$ and $\Phi$ is the kernel of Riemann and P\'olya; equivalently $U/2$ has density $2\Phi(2u)/\Xi(0)$. Moreover $\mathbb Ee^{-s\tau}=\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt s)=1/\mathbb E^*\cosh(\sqrt sU)=1/\mathbb E^*[\mathbb E[e^{-sT}|U]^{-1}]$, where, given $U$, $T$ is the exit time of a standard Brownian motion from $(-|U|/\sqrt2,|U|/\sqrt2)$.
results.label: ht:prop:bpy

results.name: The Davenport Heilbronn theta function is positive, giving a symmetric variable and a positive Polya kernel for a function violating RH
results.summary: With $a_n$ periodic mod $5$, $(a_0,\dots,a_4)=(0,1,\kappa,-\kappa,-1)$, $\kappa=0.2840790438$, $\theta_{DH}(x)=\sum a_nn\,e^{-\pi n^2x/5}>0$ for all $x>0$, so there are a probability law with Mellin transform proportional to $\xi_{DH}$, a symmetric $U_{DH}$ with $\mathbb E^*e^{wU_{DH}}=\xi_{DH}(\frac12+w)/\xi_{DH}(\frac12)$, and a positive Polya kernel $\Phi_{DH}$.
results.statement: Let $a_n$ be the Davenport and Heilbronn coefficients, periodic modulo $5$ with $(a_0,\dots,a_4)=(0,1,\kappa,-\kappa,-1)$ and $\kappa=0.2840790438$, let $\xi_{DH}$ be the completed Davenport and Heilbronn function (a function with a functional equation and an off line zero, as in the book), and $\theta_{DH}(x)=\sum_{n\ge1}a_nn\,e^{-\pi n^2x/5}$. Then $\theta_{DH}(x)>0$ for every $x>0$. Consequently there is a probability law on $(0,\infty)$ whose Mellin transform is a constant multiple of $\xi_{DH}$, a symmetric $U_{DH}$ with $\mathbb E^*e^{wU_{DH}}=\xi_{DH}(\frac12+w)/\xi_{DH}(\frac12)$, and a positive P\'olya kernel $\Phi_{DH}$.
results.label: ht:prop:dhtheta

results.name: Wiener and Gamma representation of the base point laws, and RH as monotonicity of the smoothed zero counting functions N_alpha
results.summary: For $\mu^{(\alpha)}$ with transform $\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+\sqrt s)$ and $h_\alpha(u)=N_\alpha^{-1}(u)^{-2}$, $X_\alpha=\int h_\alpha\,d\gamma_u$ has law $\mu^{(\alpha)}$ for every $\alpha\ge\sup_\rho\operatorname{Re}\rho$ (so every $\alpha\ge1$); RH holds iff $N_\alpha$ is nondecreasing for every $\alpha>\frac12$. (The convergence as $\alpha\downarrow\frac12$ under RH is only sketched in the book and is not entered.)
results.statement: For $\alpha>\frac12$ let $\mu^{(\alpha)}$ be the base point law with Laplace transform $\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+\sqrt s)$ and $N_\alpha'(t)=\frac1\pi\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(\alpha+it)=\frac1\pi\sum_\rho\frac{\alpha-\beta}{(\alpha-\beta)^2+(t-\gamma)^2}$ ($\beta=\operatorname{Re}\rho$), $N_\alpha(0)=0$, and $h_\alpha(u)=N_\alpha^{-1}(u)^{-2}$. On one gamma process $\gamma$, set $X_\alpha=\int_0^\infty h_\alpha(u)\,\mathrm d\gamma_u$. Then $X_\alpha$ has law $\mu^{(\alpha)}$ for every $\alpha\ge\sup_\rho\operatorname{Re}\rho$, in particular for every $\alpha\ge1$. RH holds if and only if $N_\alpha$ is nondecreasing for every $\alpha>\frac12$.
results.label: ht:prop:wg

results.name: Partial complete monotonicity of the canonical function of the reciprocal xi law up to an order growing with x, from the verified zeros
results.summary: With $T=3\cdot10^{12}$, for every $x\ge1/T$ and every integer $0\le n\le((T^2-\gamma_1^2-1)x-5)/\log(T^2/\gamma_1^2)$, $(-1)^n\Theta^{(n)}(x)>0$ (numerically $n\le1.7\cdot10^{23}x$); RH holds iff the bound can be replaced by $n<\infty$ for every $x>0$.
results.statement: Let $\gamma_1$ be the first ordinate, $s_\rho=(\rho-\frac12)^2$ and $\Theta(x)=\sum_{\gamma>0}e^{s_\rho x}$ the canonical function of the reciprocal xi law. Let $T=3\cdot10^{12}$, so that every zero with $0<\gamma\le T$ is on the line (Platt and Trudgian). For every $x\ge1/T$ and every integer $0\le n\le\frac{(T^2-\gamma_1^2-1)x-5}{\log(T^2/\gamma_1^2)}$ we have $(-1)^n\Theta^{(n)}(x)>0$. Numerically the bound is $n\le1.7\cdot10^{23}x$. RH holds if and only if the bound can be replaced by $n<\infty$ for every $x>0$.
results.label: ht:thm:partialcm

results.name: Equivalent forms of the quasi Riemann hypothesis QRH(alpha) through the prime counting error, the prime Dirichlet series and the base point laws
results.summary: For $\frac12\le\alpha<1$ the following are equivalent: QRH($\alpha$); $\psi(x)=x+O(x^{\alpha+\varepsilon})$; $\sum(\Lambda(n)-1)n^{-s}$ converges for $\operatorname{Re}s>\alpha$; $\operatorname{Re}\xi'/\xi(s)>0$ for $\operatorname{Re}s>\alpha$; the base point laws $\mu^{(\beta)}$ are GGCs for every $\beta>\alpha$.
results.statement: Write $\mathrm{QRH}(\alpha)$ for the statement that every nontrivial zero of $\zeta$ has real part at most $\alpha$, $\frac12\le\alpha<1$. Let $\psi$ be the Chebyshev function, $\Lambda$ the von Mangoldt function, and $\mu^{(\beta)}$ the base point law with Laplace transform $\xi(\beta)/\xi(\beta+\sqrt s)$. For $\frac12\le\alpha<1$ the following are equivalent. (1) $\mathrm{QRH}(\alpha)$. (2) $\psi(x)=x+O(x^{\alpha+\varepsilon})$ for every $\varepsilon>0$. (3) The Dirichlet series $D(s)=\sum_{n\ge1}(\Lambda(n)-1)n^{-s}$ converges for $\operatorname{Re}s>\alpha$, so that $-\zeta'/\zeta=\zeta+D$ there. (4) $\operatorname{Re}\xi'/\xi(s)>0$ for $\operatorname{Re}s>\alpha$. (5) The base point laws $\mu^{(\beta)}$ are GGCs, that is diffusion hitting times, for every $\beta>\alpha$.
results.label: ht:prop:qrh

results.name: The function 1/xi(beta+w) is never a Laplace transform of a positive measure in w
results.summary: For no real $\beta$ is $w\mapsto1/\xi(\beta+w)$ the one sided or two sided Laplace transform of a positive measure.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function. For no real $\beta$ is $w\mapsto1/\xi(\beta+w)$ the one or two sided Laplace transform of a positive measure.
results.label: ht:lem:landau

results.name: Prime built GGC hitting times converge to the base point laws for theta < beta < 2 - theta under QRH(theta)
results.status_text: conditional on the quasi Riemann hypothesis QRH($\theta$) for some $\theta<1$ (every nontrivial zero has real part at most $\theta$)
results.conditions: the quasi Riemann hypothesis QRH($\theta$) for some $\theta<1$ (every nontrivial zero has real part at most $\theta$)
results.summary: Assume QRH($\theta$) and $\theta<\beta<2-\theta$. Then $|d_X(t)-\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}\xi'/\xi(\beta+it)|\ll_\beta X^{\theta-\beta}\log(t+2)$ uniformly in $t$, $d_X\ge0$ for $X\ge X_0(\beta,\theta)$, the GGC laws $\mu^{(\beta)}_X$ with Thorin density $d_X$ converge weakly to $\mu^{(\beta)}$, and conversely nonnegativity of $d_X(t)$ for large $X$ at one $\beta$ gives QRH($\beta$).
results.statement: Assume $\mathrm{QRH}(\theta)$ for some $\theta<1$ (every nontrivial zero of $\zeta$ has real part at most $\theta$) and let $\theta<\beta<2-\theta$. Let $w(u)=(1-u)_+^3$ with Mellin transform $W(z)=6/(z(z+1)(z+2)(z+3))$, and for $\beta>\theta$ let $d_X(t)=\frac1\pi(\operatorname{Re}A(\beta+it)-\operatorname{Re}\sum_{n\le X}\Lambda(n)n^{-\beta-it}(1-n/X)^3+\operatorname{Re}X^{1-\beta-it}W(1-\beta-it))$, where $A$ is the archimedean (gamma function) term of the explicit formula as defined in the book, so that $d_X$ uses only the primes up to $X$. Then $|d_X(t)-\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}\xi'/\xi(\beta+it)|\ll_\beta X^{\theta-\beta}\log(t+2)$ uniformly in $t$, and there is $X_0(\beta,\theta)$ such that for $X\ge X_0$ the function $d_X$ is nonnegative. The GGC laws $\mu^{(\beta)}_X$ with Thorin density $d_X$ in the variable $z=t^2$ are then hitting times built from the primes up to $X$, and $\mu^{(\beta)}_X\Rightarrow\mu^{(\beta)}$ as $X\to\infty$, where $\mu^{(\beta)}$ has Laplace transform $\xi(\beta)/\xi(\beta+\sqrt s)$. Conversely, if for some $\beta$ and every $t$ the values $d_X(t)$ are nonnegative for all large $X$, then $\mathrm{QRH}(\beta)$ holds. The unconditional range $1<\beta<2$ is not covered.
results.label: ht:thm:primebuilt

results.name: The Taylor coefficients of xi(1/2+sqrt s) are a Polya frequency sequence if and only if RH, and unconditionally PF2
results.summary: RH holds iff $(c_n)$ is a P\'olya frequency sequence (all minors of the Toeplitz matrix $(c_{i-j})$ nonnegative), and unconditionally $(c_n)$ is PF$_2$: $c_n^2\ge c_{n-1}c_{n+1}$ for $n\ge1$.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function, $F(s)=\xi(\frac12+\sqrt s)/\xi(\frac12)=\sum_{n\ge0}c_ns^n$, so that $c_n=\mathbb EV^{2n}/(2n)!>0$ for the symmetric variable $V$ with density $\Phi/\Xi(0)$ ($\Phi$ Riemann's kernel), $c_0=1$, and let $s_\rho=(\rho-\frac12)^2$ for the zeros $\rho$ of $\zeta$ in the upper half plane, with $\theta_\rho\in[0,\pi)$ the angle between $s_\rho$ and the negative real axis ($\theta_\rho=0$ for a zero on the line). A sequence is PF$_k$ if all minors of its Toeplitz matrix of order at most $k$ are nonnegative, and a P\'olya frequency (PF) sequence if it is PF$_k$ for every $k$. (i) RH holds if and only if $(c_n)$ is a P\'olya frequency sequence, that is, every minor of the Toeplitz matrix $(c_{i-j})$ is nonnegative. (ii) Unconditionally, $(c_n)$ is PF$_2$: $c_n^2\ge c_{n-1}c_{n+1}$ for all $n\ge1$.
results.label: ht:thm:coef

results.name: A three term quadratic coefficient sequence is PF_k if and only if its angle is at most pi/(k+1)
results.summary: For $r>0$ and $0\le\theta<\pi$ the sequence $(1,2r^{-1}\cos\theta,r^{-2})$, the coefficients of $(1+s/re^{i\theta})(1+s/re^{-i\theta})$, is PF$_k$ if and only if $\theta\le\pi/(k+1)$.
results.statement: A sequence is PF$_k$ if all minors of order at most $k$ of its Toeplitz matrix are nonnegative. For $r>0$ and $0\le\theta<\pi$, the sequence $(1,\,2r^{-1}\cos\theta,\,r^{-2})$, the coefficient sequence of $(1+s/re^{i\theta})(1+s/re^{-i\theta})$, is PF$_k$ if and only if $\theta\le\pi/(k+1)$.
results.label: ht:lem:three

results.name: Angle theorem: if every zero has angle at most pi/(k+1) then the coefficient sequence of xi is PF_k
results.summary: If every zero of $\zeta$ satisfies $\theta_\rho\le\pi/(k+1)$, then the Taylor coefficients $(c_n)$ of $F(s)=\xi(\frac12+\sqrt s)/\xi(\frac12)$ form a PF$_k$ sequence.

A sequence is PF$_k$ if all minors of its Toeplitz matrix of order at most $k$ are nonnegative, and a P\'olya frequency (PF) sequence if it is PF$_k$ for every $k$. If every zero of $\zeta$ satisfies $\theta_\rho\le\pi/(k+1)$, then the Taylor coefficients $(c_n)$ of $F$ form a PF$_k$ sequence.

results.name: Unconditional rung count: the coefficient sequence of xi is PF_k for every k up to about 9.4e12
results.summary: Unconditionally $(c_n)$ is PF$_k$ for every $k\le\lfloor\pi H\rfloor-1=9424777960768$, $H=3\cdot10^{12}$; more generally PF$_K$ as soon as every zero with $\gamma\le(K+1)/\pi$ is on the line.
results.statement: Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function, $F(s)=\xi(\frac12+\sqrt s)/\xi(\frac12)=\sum_{n\ge0}c_ns^n$, so that $c_n=\mathbb EV^{2n}/(2n)!>0$ for the symmetric variable $V$ with density $\Phi/\Xi(0)$ ($\Phi$ Riemann's kernel), $c_0=1$, and let $s_\rho=(\rho-\frac12)^2$ for the zeros $\rho$ of $\zeta$ in the upper half plane, with $\theta_\rho\in[0,\pi)$ the angle between $s_\rho$ and the negative real axis ($\theta_\rho=0$ for a zero on the line). A sequence is PF$_k$ if all minors of its Toeplitz matrix of order at most $k$ are nonnegative, and a P\'olya frequency (PF) sequence if it is PF$_k$ for every $k$. Unconditionally, $(c_n)$ is PF$_k$ for every $k\le\lfloor\pi H\rfloor-1=9424777960768$, where $H=3\cdot10^{12}$ is the height to which all zeros are known to lie on the line (Platt and Trudgian). More generally, $(c_n)$ is PF$_K$ as soon as every zero with $\gamma\le(K+1)/\pi$ lies on the line.
results.label: ht:cor:rungs
